leads.summary: These two units share 19 motifs: the escaped remnant shall again take root downward and bear fruit upward; a remnant goes out from zion, the king tears his clothes, puts on sackcloth and goes into the temple in crisis, king spreads the enemy's threatening letter before god in the temple, the enemy is said to reproach (harref) 'the living god'….

evidence.text: Passages are shown for the 10 rarest of 19 shared motifs; the full list follows.

Shared motifs, rarest first: The escaped remnant shall again take root downward and bear fruit upward; a remnant goes out from Zion (weight 6.7); The king tears his clothes, puts on sackcloth and goes into the temple in crisis (weight 6.7); King spreads the enemy's threatening letter before God in the temple (weight 6.7); The enemy is said to reproach (harref) 'the living God' (weight 6.7); Sign: this year eat aftergrowth, next year what springs of itself, the third year sow and reap (weight 6.7); God puts a spirit in the invader so that he hears a rumor and returns home (weight 6.7); The arrogant king boasts of climbing the heights of Lebanon and cutting its cedars, drying up rivers with his feet (weight 6.7); The 'virgin daughter of Zion' laughs at and wags her head after the enemy (weight 6.7); The angel of YHWH strikes 185,000 in the enemy camp in one night; at dawn all are corpses (weight 6.7); Royal parricides flee to the land of Ararat (weight 6.7); Proverb of crisis: children have come to the birth-stool and there is no strength to deliver (weight 6.7); God says the conqueror's victories were planned by him long ago; the conqueror is only his instrument (weight 6.7); God's angels strike the enemy army [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.3); Enemy king is murdered by his own sons while worshipping in his god's temple (weight 6.3); God defends the city for his own sake and for the sake of David his servant (weight 6.0); Conquered nations' gods were burned because they were no gods, only wood and stone made by hands (weight 5.8); Taunt: Where are the gods of the conquered nations? Could they save their lands from my hand? (weight 5.8); God will put his hook in the enemy king's nose and his bit in his lips and lead him back (weight 5.8); God addressed as enthroned (yoshev) on the cherubim (weight 5.4). Shared motifs, rarest first: God's power to make water sweet or bitter [contrast between the texts] (weight 6.3); Bitter water made drinkable by throwing in a piece of wood God shows the leader (weight 6.0). Pair score 12.3.

Only in Elisha heals Jericho's water; the bears of Bethel: Small boys jeer 'Go up, baldhead!'; the prophet curses them and two she-bears maul forty-two of them; Prophet throws salt from a new bowl into the spring and heals the deadly, miscarriage-causing water 'to this day'.

Only in The Companions of the Left in smoke and samum; who creates semen, crops, rain and fire?; the hidden Book; the soul at the throat: The damned eat of Zaqqum to fill their bellies and drink boiling water like thirst-crazed camels (al-him); A noble Quran in a hidden Book which none touch but the purified; The 'hospitality' (nuzul) of the deniers is boiling water and roasting in hell; The damned had lived in luxury and persisted in the great sin (al-hinth al-'azim); 'I swear by the positions (setting-places) of the stars, a mighty oath if you knew'; Have you seen the water you drink? Did you send it down from the rain-clouds? We could make it bitter (ujaj); For those brought near: rest (rawh), fragrance (rayhan) and a garden of bliss; The Companions of the Left are in scorching wind (samum), boiling water and the shade of black smoke (yahmum), neither cool nor kind; 'This is the certain truth' (haqq al-yaqin); Have you seen what you sow? Do you make it grow, or are we the grower? We could make it chaff; Fire kindled from a tree that God made grow [divergence between the texts]; The scripture exists with God in the 'Mother of the Book' (umm al-kitab), a heavenly archetype; and 7 more.
Elisha heals Jericho's water; the bears of Bethel: tagged by Claude (model), reading the Hebrew.
The Companions of the Left in smoke and samum; who creates semen, crops, rain and fire?; the hidden Book; the soul at the throat: tagged by Claude (model), reading the Arabic.

leads.title: Hezekiah's illness, the shadow on the steps and the Babylonian envoys ↔ Hezekiah's illness, the shadow on the steps of Ahaz, and Hezekiah's psalm
leads.summary: These two units share 8 motifs: a cake of figs laid on a boil heals the king, given a choice of signs, the king picks the harder (shadow going backward), prophet tells the sick king 'set your house in order, for you shall die', dying man turns his face to the wall and prays, weeping….

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: A cake of figs laid on a boil heals the king (weight 6.7); Given a choice of signs, the king picks the harder (shadow going backward) (weight 6.7); Prophet tells the sick king 'Set your house in order, for you shall die' (weight 6.7); Dying man turns his face to the wall and prays, weeping (weight 6.7); In answer to prayer God adds fifteen years to the king's life [contrast between the texts] (weight 6.3); In answer to prayer God adds fifteen years to the king's life (weight 6.3); As a sign the shadow goes back ten steps on the stairway (dial) of Ahaz (weight 6.3); At a leader's command the sun and moon stand still until the battle is won (weight 6.0). evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: A lost book of the law is found in the temple during repairs (weight 6.7); Royal officials consult a woman prophet on behalf of the king (weight 6.7); Because the king humbled himself, he will die in peace and not see the coming disaster (weight 6.7); Workmen handling sacred funds are not audited because they deal faithfully (weight 6.3); Men tear their garments in grief or dismay (weight 4.9). Pair score 31.3.

Only in Josiah's temple repair, the finding of the book and Huldah's oracle: A newly found sacred book is read aloud before the king, who tears his clothes; The king organizes the collection of silver for repairing the temple; A child of eight to twelve years becomes king.

Only in Temple repair, finding of the book of the Torah, Huldah's oracle and covenant: Prophet announces that the curses written in the found book will come upon the land; King stands at his place and makes the covenant before God; Levites skilled in music oversee the burden-bearers and workmen; The scribe reads the found book aloud before the king; Money collected by the Levites is given to the workmen to repair the temple; The book of the covenant is read aloud to the people; King and people enter a covenant to seek or serve YHWH in a public ceremony.

leads.title: Josiah's covenant, purge of the cults and Passover; death at Megiddo ↔ The moving shadow, the night garment, the two seas and the constellations
leads.summary: These two units share 1 motifs: worship of the constellations or zodiac signs (mazzalot).

passages.note: Worship of the constellations or zodiac signs (mazzalot)
passages.text: וְהִשְׁבִּ֣ית אֶת הַכְּמָרִ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֤ר נָֽתְנוּ֙ מַלְכֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֔ה וַיְקַטֵּ֤ר בַּבָּמוֹת֙ בְּעָרֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֔ה וּמְסִבֵּ֖י יְרוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וְאֶת הַֽמְקַטְּרִ֣ים לַבַּ֗עַל לַשֶּׁ֤מֶשׁ וְלַיָּרֵ֨חַ֙ וְלַמַּזָּל֔וֹת וּלְכֹ֖ל צְבָ֥א הַשָּׁמָֽיִם

passages.note: Worship of the constellations or zodiac signs (mazzalot) (burūj as God's work, not objects of worship)

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: Worship of the constellations or zodiac signs (mazzalot) (weight 6.7). Pair score 6.7.

Only in Josiah's covenant, purge of the cults and Passover; death at Megiddo: Idolatrous cult objects are burned and their dust carried away or thrown on graves; Despite the righteous king's reform, God does not turn from his anger over a predecessor's sins; Horses dedicated to the sun at the temple entrance and chariots of the sun burned; The high places Solomon built on the 'mount of destruction' (Mount of Olives) for Ashtoreth, Chemosh and Milcom; The righteous king is killed at Megiddo by Pharaoh Necho; Priests of the high places are slaughtered on their own altars; An old prophecy (naming the future king) is fulfilled generations later; The bones of a prophet are left undisturbed when other graves are desecrated; Priests of the high places may not serve at the altar but eat unleavened bread among their brothers; The Tophet in the valley of Ben-hinnom is defiled so no one may burn children to Molech; A Passover such as had not been kept since the days of the judges; Women weave 'houses' (garments, hangings) for Asherah in the temple precinct; and 11 more.

Only in The moving shadow, the night garment, the two seas and the constellations: God extends the shadow, makes the sun its guide, then draws it back gently; God created humans from water and gave them kinship by blood and by marriage; Told to prostrate to the Merciful, the pagans ask 'What is al-Raḥmān?'; What God does after creating in six days [divergence between the texts]; God has inscribed a circle on the face of the waters at the boundary between light and darkness; God made the night a garment, sleep a rest, and the day a rising (nushūr); As a sign the shadow goes back ten steps on the stairway (dial) of Ahaz; God set constellations (buruj) in the sky and adorned it for beholders; God the Ever-Living, the Self-Subsisting (al-hayy al-qayyum); God let loose the two seas, one sweet, one salt, with a barrier (barzakh) and partition between them; God makes winds his messengers (angels) and flaming fire his ministers; A solid firmament (raqia) separates upper waters from lower waters; and 6 more.

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/07-hb-quran.yaml): parallel. The biblical exception: a prophet's word authorizes felling good trees: wə-ḵol ʿēṣ ṭôḇ tappîlû wə-ḵol maʿyənê mayim tistōmû (Elisha's oracle, carried out in 3:25) vs. mā qaṭaʿtum min līnatin ... fa-bi-idhni llāh. In both the destruction of the enemy's trees is licensed by a divine word; both run against Deut 20:19.
Shared motifs, rarest first: Do not cut down fruit trees during a siege: is the tree of the field a man? (weight 6.3). Pair score 6.3.

Only in Jehoram's campaign against Mesha of Moab: Besieged king offers his firstborn heir as a burnt offering on the city wall, and 'great wrath' falls on Israel, who withdraw; Prophet calls for a musician; as he plays, the hand of YHWH comes upon him; Prophet says he would not even look at the wicked king were it not for the righteous ally; Invaders fell every good tree, stop every spring and ruin every good field with stones; Allied kings on a seven-day detour run out of water for army and beasts and despair; A sheep-breeding vassal king pays tribute of a hundred thousand lambs and the wool of a hundred thousand rams; At sunrise the water looks red as blood; the enemy thinks the kings have slain each other and rushes to plunder; Dry wadi fills with water though no wind or rain is seen; Standard regnal formula: age at accession, length of reign, mother's name, evaluation, burial, successor; Nations burn their sons and daughters in fire to their gods.

Only in Al-Hashr: the first gathering and exile of the Banu Nadir, the cut palms, and the law of fay': The expelled demolish their houses with their own hands and the hands of the believers; Had God not decreed exile (jala') for them, he would have punished them in this world; God expelled the unbelieving People of the Book (the Banu Nadir) from their homes at 'the first gathering' (li-awwal al-hashr); Whatever palm trees (lina) you cut down or left standing on their roots was by God's leave; Later believers pray: forgive us and our brethren who preceded us in faith, and put no rancor in our hearts; Whether the enemy's trees may be cut down in a siege [contrast between the texts]; How spoil taken from the enemy is distributed [divergence between the texts]; Fay' (booty gained without cavalry or camels) goes to God, the messenger, kin, orphans, the poor and the wayfarer, so wealth does not circulate only among the rich; They thought their fortresses would protect them from God, but God came from where they did not expect and cast terror into their hearts; The poor emigrants and the hosts who prefer others over themselves even in need; whoever is saved from his own greed succeeds; Cities 'great and fortified up to heaven'; Spoils divided half to warriors, half to community, with a levy for God; and 2 more.

leads.title: Nathan's parable of the ewe lamb and David's punishment ↔ David's mountains, the two litigants and the ninety-nine ewes
leads.summary: These two units share 5 motifs: david's repentance and what follows it [divergence between the texts], the king confesses 'i have sinned' and the prophet announces forgiveness with a remaining penalty, a man with many sheep takes another's only ewe [divergence between the texts], a case about a ewe is brought to david for judgment [divergence between the texts]….

passages.note: David's repentance and what follows it [divergence between the texts] (Verdict, recognition and outcome. Sam: David burns with anger, ben-māweṯ hā-ʾîš, fourfold restitution; Nathan: ʾattâ hā-ʾîš; David: ḥāṭāʾṯî la-YHWH; pardon with a penalty, gam ha-bbēn ha-yyillôḏ ləḵā môṯ yāmûṯ, and the sword never leaves his house (12:10). Q: a calm verdict, la-qad ẓalamaka bi-suʾāli naʿjatika ilā niʿājihi; no 'you are the man'. Pair score 33.0.

Only in Nathan's parable of the ewe lamb and David's punishment: A child born of the sin dies as punishment for the father; A child is given a second name by a prophet at God's word; Father fasts and lies on the ground praying for a dying child; God reminds the king he gave him his predecessor's house and wives; 'I shall go to him, but he will not return to me'; After the death the mourner unexpectedly rises, washes, anoints himself and eats; A poor man's only ewe lamb, raised like a daughter, taken by a rich man for a guest; Punishment: the sword will never depart from the king's house; Five oxen for a stolen ox and four sheep for a stolen sheep; Punishment: the king's wives will be lain with publicly 'before the sun'.

Only in David's mountains, the two litigants and the ninety-nine ewes: Two litigants scale the wall of David's prayer-chamber (mihrab) and frighten him; A man with ninety-nine ewes demands his brother's single ewe and overpowers him in argument; 'O David, we made you a vicegerent (khalifa) on earth; judge between people with truth and do not follow desire'; David realizes he was being tested, asks forgiveness, falls down bowing and turns in repentance; God strengthened David's kingdom and gave him wisdom and decisive judgment (fasl al-khitab); Shall God treat believers like those who spread corruption, the godfearing like the wicked?; Mountains and birds are made to glorify God together with David; God did not create the heavens and earth and what is between them in play (la'ibin) but in truth.

evidence.text: Passages are shown for the 10 rarest of 16 shared motifs; the full list follows.

Shared motifs, rarest first: God rewards the speaker according to his righteousness and clean hands (weight 6.7); 'By my God I leap over a wall' (weight 6.7); God trains the king's hands for war so his arms bend a bow of bronze (weight 6.7); God shows steadfast love to his anointed and his seed forever (weight 6.7); Enemies beaten fine as dust and trampled like mire of the streets (weight 6.7); God reaches from on high and draws the sufferer out of many waters (weight 6.7); Foreigners come cringing and trembling to submit to the king (weight 6.7); Smoke rises from God's nostrils and devouring fire from his mouth (weight 6.7); God hears the cry from his (heavenly) temple (weight 6.7); God shows himself loyal to the loyal and crooked to the crooked (weight 6.7); God rides on a cherub and flies on the wings of the wind (weight 6.7); God is called the speaker's lamp who lights his darkness (weight 6.3); God makes the speaker's feet like hinds' feet and sets him on the heights (weight 6.3); The psalmist is engulfed by breakers of death and cords of Sheol (weight 6.3); God shoots his arrows at the people or enemies (weight 5.6); At God's coming the earth quakes, heavens drip and mountains flow (weight 5.2). Pair score 103.2.

Only in David's song of deliverance (= Psalm 18): Leader and people sing a victory song after the enemy's destruction; Theophany with thunder, lightning, thick cloud and a loud trumpet; God called the Rock (tsur).

Only in Psalm 18 - David's song of deliverance and the storm theophany: God makes darkness his hiding place and dark waters and clouds his canopy; The king gives thanks for God's deliverance from all his enemies (song also in 2 Sam 22); At God's rebuke the channels of the sea are seen and the foundations of the world laid bare; 'Who is God except YHWH, and who is a rock besides our God?'; God answers the distressed when he calls and removes the evil; God's words are pure, silver refined in a furnace, purified seven times; God addressed with a string of protective epithets: rock, fortress, deliverer, shield, horn of salvation, stronghold; God sends hail mingled with fire and thunder from heaven; Thunder is the roaring voice of God; On that day a great earthquake shakes the land; fish, birds, beasts, creeping things and all humans quake before God, mountains are thrown down and every wall falls; Superscription sets the psalm in a specific episode of David's life.

leads.summary: These two units share 1 motifs: god gave david the psalms (zabur).

passages.note: God gave David the Psalms (Zabur)
passages.text: إِنَّآ أَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَيْكَ كَمَآ أَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَىٰ نُوحٍ وَٱلنَّبِيِّۦنَ مِنۢ بَعْدِهِۦ وَأَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَىٰٓ إِبْرَٰهِيمَ وَإِسْمَٰعِيلَ وَإِسْحَٰقَ وَيَعْقُوبَ وَٱلْأَسْبَاطِ وَعِيسَىٰ وَأَيُّوبَ وَيُونُسَ وَهَٰرُونَ وَسُلَيْمَٰنَ وَءَاتَيْنَا دَاوُۥدَ زَبُورًا

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/02-hb-quran.yaml): echo. David as an inspired psalmist. Q: wa-ātaynā Dāwūda zabūran. 2Sam: nəʿîm zəmirôt Yiśrāʾēl; rûaḥ YHWH dibber-bî û-millātô ʿal-ləšônî. zabūr is often linked to Hebrew zəmīrāh/mizmôr (etymology disputed).
Shared motifs, rarest first: God gave David the Psalms (Zabur) (weight 6.0). Pair score 6.0.

Only in The last words of David: A just ruler is like the morning sun on a cloudless day; Poem opening with 'Oracle (ne'um) of the man...' formula; The spirit of God speaks through the king's tongue; The wicked are thorns that cannot be handled and are burned; God has made an everlasting covenant with the king's house.

Only in The chain of revelation; Jesus, word and spirit; 'say not three': The angels brought near (al-muqarrabūn) to God; God spoke to Moses directly (kallama taklīman); Jesus is God's word cast to Mary and a spirit from him; Catalogue of prophets who received revelation, from Noah to Jesus; People of the Book, do not go to excess (lā taghlū) in your religion; The Messiah does not disdain to be a servant of God, nor do the angels brought near; Do not say 'three'; God is only one god (rejection of a triad); First servant song: God's chosen servant with his spirit brings justice to the nations without crying out; a bruised reed he will not break; Of the messengers before you, some we have related to you and some we have not; God speaks to the prophet face to face, as a man speaks to his friend; Whether God has a son, or calls his anointed king his begotten son [contrast between the texts]; Denial that God has taken a son (walad); and 2 more.

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/02-hb-quran.yaml): parallel. Q: an yuqattalū aw yuṣallabū aw tuqaṭṭaʿa aydīhim wa-arjuluhum min khilāfin. 2Sam: wa-yyahargûm wa-yqaṣṣəṣû ʾet-yədêhem wə-ʾet-raglêhem wa-yyitlû ʿal-hab-bərēkhāh. Hands and feet cut off and the body exposed. In 2Sam it is the king's one-off sentence on assassins; in Q a standing law for those who wage war on God and his Messenger, with 'opposite sides' and an alternative of exile (yunfaw).

Only in The son of Mary as an example and sign of the Hour; the Garden with golden dishes; Malik of hell: The guilty remain in the punishment of Gehenna forever; it is not lightened for them and they despair (mublisun); On that day intimate friends become enemies to one another, except the God-fearing; In paradise they are served with golden platters and cups, with all that souls desire and eyes delight in; 'If the Merciful had a son, I would be the first of worshippers'; Jesus is only a servant whom God favored and made an example for the Children of Israel; When the son of Mary is cited as an example, the opponents clamor and ask whether their gods or he are better; Jesus came with wisdom to make clear some of what they disputed and called them to worship God, 'my Lord and your Lord'; Jesus (or the revelation) is knowledge/a sign of the Hour; The damned call on Malik, the keeper of hell, to ask God to end them, and he answers 'You will remain'; Those invoked besides God have no power of intercession, except one who bore witness to the truth; The righteous enter the Garden with their spouses, made joyful; The prophet is told to turn away from the scoffers and say 'Peace' (salam), for they will come to know; and 11 more.

Only in Cows of Bashan; 'yet you did not return'; prepare to meet your God: The wealthy women of Samaria are called 'cows of Bashan' who oppress the poor and say to their husbands 'Bring, let us drink'; Hymnic doxology: he who forms the mountains, creates the wind, makes dawn into darkness, treads the heights; YHWH of hosts is his name; Captives will be dragged away with hooks and fishhooks; Ironic summons: 'Come to Bethel and transgress, to Gilgal and multiply transgression'; 'Prepare to meet your God, O Israel'; God makes it rain on one city and not on another, one field and not another; Israel was like a brand plucked from the burning; The evil diseases of Egypt removed from the obedient or brought on the disobedient; The 'overturned cities' (al-mu'tafikat), Lot's towns; Locusts brought by an east wind devour all vegetation left after the hail; God swears by himself; God rains sulfur and fire from heaven on cities.

Only in One community split into sects; the heedless rich and the God-fearing: Nation pictured as a body beaten from sole of foot to head, with untended wounds and sores; Humanity was one community (umma) but split its affair into sects; Whether a prophet takes payment for his message [contrast between the texts]; Were there gods besides God in heaven and earth, both would have been ruined; False prophets prophesy 'from their own heart', following their own spirit, having seen nothing; Speaker is troubled by the prosperity and ease of the wicked (theodicy); God did not send the prophets who promise peace; they prophesy a lying vision, divination and the deceit of their heart; God burdens no soul beyond its capacity; Officers call the visiting prophet 'this madman' (meshugga'); The Prophet asks no wage for the message; God keeps a book in which names are written and from which sinners are blotted.

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/06-hb-quran.yaml): parallel. wə-rabbîm mî-yšēnê ʾaḏmaṯ-ʿāp̄ār yāqîṣû ʾēlleh lə-ḥayyê ʿôlām wə-ʾēlleh la-ḥărāp̄ôṯ lə-ḏirʾôn ʿôlām vs. man baʿathanā min marqadinā ... wa-mtāzū l-yawma ayyuhā l-mujrimūn: the dead as sleepers who wake from their resting place and are split into two groups. Daniel raises 'many'; the Quran gathers all (jamīʿun ladaynā muḥḍarūn, 36:53).

Shared motifs, rarest first: The resurrected cry 'Woe to us, who has raised us from our sleeping place (marqad)?' (weight 6.7); Your dead shall live, their corpses rise; dwellers in the dust shall awake and sing (weight 4.9). Pair score 11.6.

Only in Michael arises, the resurrection, and the sealed book: Two figures stand on either bank of the river, with a linen-clad figure above the waters; Secret reckonings: 1,290 days from the abolition of the daily offering, and blessed is he who waits for 1,335 days; Many shall run to and fro and knowledge shall increase; The seer is told he will rest and rise to his allotted portion at the end of days; A time of trouble such as never was since nations existed; The wise shine like the brightness of the firmament and those who turn many to righteousness like the stars forever; On judgment day each receives a book of his deeds spread open, leaving nothing small or great unrecorded [divergence between the texts]; God raises his hand to heaven and swears: as I live forever; Into how many groups humankind is sorted at the end [divergence between the texts]; A heavenly being or the seer asks 'Until when (ad matai)?' the desolation will last; Persecution lasts 'a time, times and half a time' (three and a half periods); An abomination that makes desolate (shiqquts meshomem) is set up in the sanctuary; and 7 more.

Only in The trumpet, the sleepers raised, the Garden and the witnessing limbs: The people of the Garden recline with their spouses in shade on couches (ara'ik), with fruit and whatever they ask; God's covenant with the children of Adam: do not serve Satan; serve me, this is a straight path; Whomever God gives long life he reverses in creation (returns to weakness); 'Peace': a word from a merciful Lord to the blessed; God did not teach the prophet poetry, nor is it fitting for him; it is a reminder and a clear Quran; 'Separate yourselves today, you guilty ones!'; What the dead say when they wake from the dust [divergence between the texts]; A horn blown on the last day, and whom it gathers [divergence between the texts]; The prophet heard or dismissed as a poet or singer [divergence between the texts]; If God willed he would blot out their eyes or transform them (maskh) in their places so they could neither go on nor return; On judgment day tongues, hands and feet testify against people; No host from heaven was needed: a single Shout (sayha) and they were extinguished; and 1 more.

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml): parallel. Cognate key word: Dan 4:24 wa-ḥăṭāyāk bĕ-ṣidqâ pĕruq wa-ʿăwāyātāk bĕ-miḥan ʿănāyin 'break off your sins by ṣidqâ and your iniquities by mercy to the poor'; Q 2:271 in tubdū ṣ-ṣadaqāti ... wa-tuʾtūhā l-fuqarāʾa fa-huwa khayrun lakum wa-yukaffiru ʿankum min sayyiʾātikum: alms (ṣadaqāt) given to the poor expiate sins. Aramaic ṣidqâ ('righteousness', here almsgiving) and Arabic ṣadaqa. Daniel advises a pagan king; the Quran makes it a rule for believers and prefers secret giving.
Shared motifs, rarest first: Advice to break off sins by righteousness/almsgiving (tsidqah) and iniquities by mercy to the poor (weight 6.7). Pair score 6.7.

Only in Nebuchadnezzar's letter, the great tree dream and his madness: Dream of an immense tree whose top reaches heaven, visible to the ends of the earth, sheltering beasts and birds; The sentence is 'by the decree of the watchers and the word of the holy ones'; The king boasts 'Is not this great Babylon which I have built by my might?'; The king's reason returns when he lifts his eyes to heaven and he is restored to his throne after praising God; No one can stay God's hand or say to him 'What are you doing?'; The seer is dismayed and terrified when he grasps the meaning of the dream; 'Seven times' (periods) pass over the punished king; The felled tree's stump is left in the earth bound with a band of iron and bronze; While the words are still in his mouth a voice falls from heaven pronouncing the king's sentence; A 'watcher' ('ir), a holy one, descends from heaven and decrees the judgment; Take alms from their wealth to purify them; the prophet's prayer is a comfort to them; A king is driven from human society to live with beasts, eating grass like oxen, wet with dew, with hair like eagles' feathers and nails like birds' claws; and 7 more.

Only in Parables of charity: Charity voided by reminders of generosity and injury, like dust on a rock washed bare by rain; Spending for God's pleasure is like a garden on a height that yields double with heavy rain or even with dew; Spending in God's way is like a grain sprouting seven ears with a hundred grains each; Deserving poor, restrained in God's way, thought rich by the ignorant for their restraint, known by their mark; Satan threatens you with poverty and commands indecency; He who gives to the poor will not lack, but he who hides his eyes will get many curses; Patriarch reaps a hundredfold in one year; An old man with weak children loses his garden of palms and vines to a fiery whirlwind; Giving charity openly is good, but giving it secretly to the poor is better and expiates sins; God gives wisdom to whom he wills; whoever is given wisdom is given much good; One scatters and yet increases; the generous soul is made fat and who waters will be watered.

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml): parallel. Same formula (malkû / mulk; lĕ-man dî yiṣbēʾ / man tashāʾ). Daniel's is a verdict on a proud king (Nebuchadnezzar); the Quran's a prayer addressed to God.
Shared motifs, rarest first: The Most High rules the kingdom of men, gives it to whom he wills and sets over it the lowliest of men (weight 6.7). Pair score 6.7.

Only in Nebuchadnezzar's letter, the great tree dream and his madness: Dream of an immense tree whose top reaches heaven, visible to the ends of the earth, sheltering beasts and birds; The sentence is 'by the decree of the watchers and the word of the holy ones'; The king boasts 'Is not this great Babylon which I have built by my might?'; The king's reason returns when he lifts his eyes to heaven and he is restored to his throne after praising God; No one can stay God's hand or say to him 'What are you doing?'; The seer is dismayed and terrified when he grasps the meaning of the dream; 'Seven times' (periods) pass over the punished king; The felled tree's stump is left in the earth bound with a band of iron and bronze; While the words are still in his mouth a voice falls from heaven pronouncing the king's sentence; A 'watcher' ('ir), a holy one, descends from heaven and decrees the judgment; Take alms from their wealth to purify them; the prophet's prayer is a comfort to them; Advice to break off sins by righteousness/almsgiving (tsidqah) and iniquities by mercy to the poor; and 7 more.

Only in Owner of sovereignty: On the day each soul finds what good and evil it did present before it, wishing a far distance from its evil; Believers may not take unbelievers as allies, unless guarding against them (tuqat); God warns you of himself (yuhadhdhirukum allahu nafsahu); God makes night enter day and day night, brings the living from the dead and the dead from the living; O God, owner of sovereignty, you give it to whom you will and take it from whom you will; you exalt and abase; God changes times and seasons, deposes kings and sets up kings; God gives justice to the poor and seats kings (or the lowly) on the throne; God provides for whom he wills without reckoning (bi-ghayri hisab); Hymn of reversals: the barren bears seven, the mighty broken, the poor raised from the dung-heap.

Only in The striking day: moths, wool and the scales: The one whose scales are light: 'his mother is Hawiya (the abyss)', a blazing fire; On the striking day (al-qari'a) people will be like scattered moths; On the day the mountains will be like (carded, dyed) wool ('ihn); Deeds are weighed on judgment day; heavy scales mean salvation, light scales loss; Spies seem like grasshoppers in their own eyes and the giants'; Hell given proper names: Laza (scalp-stripper), Saqar (scorcher, leaves nothing), al-Hutama (the crusher), Hawiya (the abyss); Rhetorical formula 'And what will make you know what X is?' passages.text: ٱللَّهُ لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ ٱلْحَىُّ ٱلْقَيُّومُ لَا تَأْخُذُهُۥ سِنَةٌ وَلَا نَوْمٌ لَّهُۥ مَا فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ مَن ذَا ٱلَّذِى يَشْفَعُ عِندَهُۥٓ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِهِۦ يَعْلَمُ مَا بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَمَا خَلْفَهُمْ وَلَا يُحِيطُونَ بِشَىْءٍ مِّنْ عِلْمِهِۦٓ إِلَّا بِمَا شَآءَ وَسِعَ كُرْسِيُّهُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضَ وَلَا يَـُٔودُهُۥ حِفْظُهُمَا وَهُوَ ٱلْعَلِىُّ ٱلْعَظِيمُ

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml): parallel. Cognate pair of titles: Dan 6:27 dî hûʾ ʾĕlāhāʾ ḥayyāʾ wĕ-qayyām lĕ-ʿālmîn 'the living God, enduring forever'; Q 2:255 allāhu lā ilāha illā huwa l-ḥayyu l-qayyūm. Aramaic ḥayyāʾ wĕ-qayyām = Arabic al-ḥayy al-qayyūm. In Daniel the title is spoken by a pagan king's decree; in the Quran it opens the Throne Verse.
Shared motifs, rarest first: Israel's God is called 'the living God, enduring forever, whose kingdom shall never be destroyed' (weight 6.3). Pair score 6.3.

Only in Daniel in the lions' den: The accusers, with their wives and children, are thrown to the lions and crushed before they reach the bottom; God sends his angel and shuts the lions' mouths so they do not harm the innocent; For thirty days no one may petition any god or man except the king; Darius the Mede receives the kingdom at age sixty-two; A stone is placed on the mouth of the pit and sealed with the king's signet and those of his nobles; A royal decree written by the law of the Medes and Persians cannot be revoked, even by the king; The king spends a sleepless night fasting, without entertainment, worrying over the hero; The pious kneels on his knees to pray; The faithful prays facing Jerusalem through open windows; Rivals can find no fault in the hero except in the matter of the law of his God; The king appoints 120 satraps over the kingdom with three presidents above them, one of them the hero; The hero is thrown into a pit of lions; and 8 more.

Only in Ranks of the messengers and the Throne Verse: God's footstool or seat (kursi) extends over the heavens and the earth; No compulsion in religion; Neither slumber nor sleep overtakes God; God's throne in relation to heaven and earth [divergence between the texts]; Whoever rejects false gods (taghut) and believes in God grasps the firmest handhold that never breaks; God does not slumber or sleep [divergence between the texts]; The guardian of Israel neither slumbers nor sleeps; A day comes with no trade, no friendship and no intercession; The temple as a house of rest for the ark and the footstool of God's feet; Jesus son of Mary given clear signs and supported with the holy spirit (ruh al-qudus); God ranked some messengers above others; to some God spoke; God the Ever-Living, the Self-Subsisting (al-hayy al-qayyum); and 4 more.

Dan's court judges empires; Q's book belongs to each person.
Shared motifs, rarest first: The heavenly court sits in judgment and the books are opened (weight 6.0). Pair score 6.0.

Only in The four beasts, the Ancient of Days and one like a son of man: Thrones are set and the Ancient of Days sits, his garment white as snow and his hair like pure wool; The seer asks one of the attendants or an angel, who explains the vision to him; A bear raised on one side with three ribs in its mouth is told 'Arise, devour much flesh'; The arch-enemy beast is slain and its body given over to burning fire; A heavenly figure or the holy ones are given everlasting dominion, glory and kingdom which all peoples serve; God's throne is flames of fire with wheels of burning fire; Four great beasts rise from the sea, each different, symbolizing successive kingdoms; A leopard with four wings and four heads is given dominion; The four winds of heaven stir up the great sea, out of which monstrous beasts arise; The holy ones of the Most High (qaddishe 'elyonin) receive and possess the kingdom forever; The horn makes war against the holy ones and prevails until the Ancient of Days comes; A little horn with human eyes and a mouth speaking great things uproots three horns; and 15 more.

Only in The bird on the neck, the open book and individual responsibility (Surah 17:9-21): When God would destroy a town he commands its affluent ones; they transgress and it is destroyed; The hereafter is greater in degrees and in preference than this world; Every human's 'bird' (ta'ir, fate or omen) is fastened to his neck; How many generations God destroyed after Noah; Man prays for evil as he prays for good; man is ever hasty; Those who want the hasty world get some of it and then hell; those who strive for the hereafter are thanked; On judgment day each receives a book of his deeds spread open, leaving nothing small or great unrecorded; On judgment day each receives a book of his deeds spread open, leaving nothing small or great unrecorded [divergence between the texts]; Night and day are two signs; the sign of night is effaced and that of day made bright for reckoning years; God does not punish a people before sending a messenger, lest they plead they had none; Each person dies for his own sin; Sun and moon are set to rule day and night and mark signs and seasons.

passages.note: One mighty in power (shadid al-quwa) taught him, stood poised on the highest horizon, then drew near and descended (A heavenly being flies down to a praying man to instruct him: wə-hā-ʾîš gaḇrîʾēl ... muʿāp̄ bîʿāp̄ nōḡēaʿ ʾēlay ... wa-yyāḇen wa-yḏabbēr ʿimmî ... yāṣāʾṯî lə-haśkîləḵā ḇînâ vs. ʿallamahu shadīdu l-quwā dhū mirratin fa-stawā wa-huwa bi-l-ufuqi l-aʿlā thumma danā fa-tadallā ... fa-awḥā ilā ʿabdihi mā awḥā. Daniel names him Gabriel; Q 53 does not name the 'mighty in power' (tradition identifies him as Jibrīl, cf. Q 2:97). Daniel's angel explains a vision; the Quran's figure transmits revelation (waḥy).)
passages.text: וְע֛וֹד אֲנִ֥י מְדַבֵּ֖ר בַּתְּפִלָּ֑ה וְהָאִ֣ישׁ גַּבְרִיאֵ֡ל אֲשֶׁר֩ רָאִ֨יתִי בֶחָז֤וֹן בַּתְּחִלָּה֙ מֻעָ֣ף בִּיעָ֔ף נֹגֵ֣עַ אֵלַ֔י כְּעֵ֖ת מִנְחַת עָֽרֶב

Daniel names him Gabriel; Q 53 does not name the 'mighty in power' (tradition identifies him as Jibrīl, cf. Q 2:97). Daniel's angel explains a vision; the Quran's figure transmits revelation (waḥy).)

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/07-hb-quran.yaml): echo. A heavenly being flies down to a praying man to instruct him: wə-hā-ʾîš gaḇrîʾēl ... muʿāp̄ bîʿāp̄ nōḡēaʿ ʾēlay ... wa-yyāḇen wa-yḏabbēr ʿimmî ... yāṣāʾṯî lə-haśkîləḵā ḇînâ vs. ʿallamahu shadīdu l-quwā dhū mirratin fa-stawā wa-huwa bi-l-ufuqi l-aʿlā thumma danā fa-tadallā ... fa-awḥā ilā ʿabdihi mā awḥā. Daniel names him Gabriel; Q 53 does not name the 'mighty in power' (tradition identifies him as Jibrīl, cf. Q 2:97). Daniel's angel explains a vision; the Quran's figure transmits revelation (waḥy).
Shared motifs, rarest first: One mighty in power (shadid al-quwa) taught him, stood poised on the highest horizon, then drew near and descended (weight 6.7). Pair score 6.7.

Only in Daniel's penitential prayer and the seventy weeks: The angel arrives in swift flight at the time of the evening offering, while the seer is still praying; An anointed one (mashiah) is cut off and has nothing; The curse and oath written in the Torah of Moses has been poured out on the people; Communal confession: 'To you, Lord, belongs righteousness and to us shame of face'; We present our pleas not because of our righteous deeds but because of your great mercy; The seer studies the books (sefarim) to understand a prophecy; Seventy 'weeks' (seventy sevens) decreed to finish transgression, atone iniquity, bring everlasting righteousness and anoint a most holy; The seer is addressed as 'greatly beloved' (ish hamudot); Prayer accompanied by fasting, sackcloth and ashes; Muhammad is not the father of any of your men but the messenger of God and the seal of the prophets (khatam al-nabiyyin); An abomination that makes desolate (shiqquts meshomem) is set up in the sanctuary; The angel Gabriel is named and sent to explain the vision; and 3 more.

Only in Al-Najm: the star that sets, the mighty one on the horizon two bow-lengths away, and the Lote-Tree of the Boundary: The heart did not falsify what it saw; the gaze did not swerve nor transgress; When there covered the Lote-Tree that which covered it (an ineffable phenomenon); Oath 'By the star when it sets/falls (idha hawa)'; He saw him at a second descent by the Lote-Tree of the Boundary (sidrat al-muntaha), near the Garden of Refuge; The heavenly figure came within two bow-lengths or nearer (qaba qawsayn aw adna) and revealed to his servant; Leaders see God with a sapphire-like pavement under his feet; He saw some of the greatest signs of his Lord; Your companion has not erred; he does not speak from desire; it is only revelation revealed; Whether a prophet speaks from his own heart or desire, or by revelation [contrast between the texts]; What or whom the visionaries saw: God himself or his messenger [divergence between the texts]; No human can see God's face and live; A tree whose fruit gives eternal life.

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/08-hb-quran.yaml): echo. wa-jibrīlu wa-ṣāliḥu l-muʾminīna wa-l-malāʾikatu baʿda dhālika ẓahīr ~ we-hā-ʾîš Gavrîʾēl ʾăšer rāʾîtî ve-ḥāzôn. The only named angel shared by both books; in Daniel he comes to explain the vision, in Q 66:4 he is the prophet's ally (ẓahīr) in a household dispute.
Shared motifs, rarest first: The angel Gabriel is named and sent to explain the vision (weight 6.0). Pair score 6.0.

Only in Daniel's penitential prayer and the seventy weeks: The angel arrives in swift flight at the time of the evening offering, while the seer is still praying; An anointed one (mashiah) is cut off and has nothing; The curse and oath written in the Torah of Moses has been poured out on the people; Communal confession: 'To you, Lord, belongs righteousness and to us shame of face'; We present our pleas not because of our righteous deeds but because of your great mercy; The seer studies the books (sefarim) to understand a prophecy; Seventy 'weeks' (seventy sevens) decreed to finish transgression, atone iniquity, bring everlasting righteousness and anoint a most holy; The seer is addressed as 'greatly beloved' (ish hamudot); Prayer accompanied by fasting, sackcloth and ashes; One mighty in power (shadid al-quwa) taught him, stood poised on the highest horizon, then drew near and descended; Muhammad is not the father of any of your men but the messenger of God and the seal of the prophets (khatam al-nabiyyin); An abomination that makes desolate (shiqquts meshomem) is set up in the sanctuary; and 3 more.

Only in Al-Tahrim: the prohibited thing and the divulged secret; fire fed with stones; the wives of Noah and Lot, Pharaoh's wife and Mary daughter of 'Imran: If he divorced them, God might give him in exchange better wives: submitting, believing, devout, repentant, worshipping, fasting/wandering (sa'ihat), previously married and virgins; A Fire whose fuel is people and stones, over which are harsh, stern angels who never disobey God; If two wives back each other against him, God is his protector, and Gabriel, the righteous believers and the angels; Mary, daughter of 'Imran, guarded her chastity; God breathed into it of his spirit, and she believed the words of her Lord and his books; Pharaoh's wife prays 'My Lord, build me a house with you in the Garden and save me from Pharaoh and his deeds'; The believers pray on the day: 'Our Lord, perfect our light for us and forgive us'; 'O Prophet, why do you forbid what God made lawful for you, seeking to please your wives?'; God has ordained the dissolution of oaths; Turn to God in sincere repentance (tawba nasuh); The prophet confided a secret to one of his wives; she divulged it, and God informed him; The wives of Noah and Lot, married to righteous servants, betrayed them and are told to enter the Fire; Father or husband may annul a woman's vow on the day he hears it; A man's vow or oath must be fulfilled as uttered [contrast between the texts]; and 10 more.

leads.title: Setting of Moses' speech; appointment of judges ↔ Ha-Mim 'Ayn-Sin-Qaf: revelation, the angels' intercession and the one religion of the prophets
leads.summary: These two units share 1 motifs: judges must not show partiality, 'for the judgment is god's'.

passages.note: Judges must not show partiality, 'for the judgment is God's'
passages.text: וָאֲצַוֶּה֙ אֶת שֹׁ֣פְטֵיכֶ֔ם בָּעֵ֥ת הַהִ֖וא לֵאמֹ֑ר שָׁמֹ֤עַ בֵּין אֲחֵיכֶם֙ וּשְׁפַטְתֶּ֣ם צֶ֔דֶק בֵּֽין אִ֥ישׁ וּבֵין אָחִ֖יו וּבֵ֥ין גֵּרֽוֹ

passages.note: Judges must not show partiality, 'for the judgment is God's'
passages.text: לֹֽא תַכִּ֨ירוּ פָנִ֜ים בַּמִּשְׁפָּ֗ט כַּקָּטֹ֤ן כַּגָּדֹל֙ תִּשְׁמָע֔וּן לֹ֤א תָג֨וּרוּ֙ מִפְּנֵי אִ֔ישׁ כִּ֥י הַמִּשְׁפָּ֖ט לֵאלֹהִ֣ים ה֑וּא וְהַדָּבָר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יִקְשֶׁ֣ה מִכֶּ֔ם תַּקְרִב֥וּן אֵלַ֖י וּשְׁמַעְתִּֽיו

passages.note: Judges must not show partiality, 'for the judgment is God's' (whatever you differ over, its judgment is God's)
passages.text: وَمَا ٱخْتَلَفْتُمْ فِيهِ مِن شَىْءٍ فَحُكْمُهُۥٓ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ ذَٰلِكُمُ ٱللَّهُ رَبِّى عَلَيْهِ تَوَكَّلْتُ وَإِلَيْهِ أُنِيبُ

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: Judges must not show partiality, 'for the judgment is God's' (weight 6.7). Pair score 6.7.

Only in Setting of Moses' speech; appointment of judges: Eleven days' journey from Horeb to Kadesh-barnea (yet it took forty years); People multiplied 'like the stars of heaven'; Moses 'expounds this Torah' in Moab on the first of the eleventh month of the fortieth year; Blessing: may God make you a thousand times as many; Officers over thousands, hundreds, fifties and tens; hard cases to the leader; Leader protests he did not conceive or bear the people to carry them like a nurse; Ideal borders of the promised land traced from the Brook of Egypt to Lebo-Hamath; The defeat of Sihon of Heshbon and Og of Bashan recalled.

Only in Ha-Mim 'Ayn-Sin-Qaf: revelation, the angels' intercession and the one religion of the prophets: Whoever seeks the tillage (harth) of the hereafter has it increased; whoever seeks the tillage of this world gets some of it and no share hereafter; Perhaps the Hour is near; unbelievers mock and ask to hasten it, believers fear it; The prophet's only requested 'wage' is affection among kin (al-mawadda fi l-qurba); 'There is nothing like him' (laysa ka-mithlihi shay'), yet he is the Hearing, the Seeing; Abraham kept God's charge, commandments, statutes and laws (torot) before Sinai; Angels glorify God and ask forgiveness for those on earth; God sent down the Book with the truth and the Balance (al-mizan); Earlier communities split into factions only after knowledge came to them, out of rivalry (baghy) among themselves; God expands provision (rizq) for whom he wills and restricts it; The heavens almost burst apart from above (at God's majesty or at a blasphemy); To God belong the keys (maqalid) of the heavens and the earth; Whether humans bear God's likeness, or nothing is like him [contrast between the texts]; and 11 more.

Only in The chosen place; profane slaughter; blood prohibition: Do not inquire how the nations served their gods in order to imitate them; Every man doing what is right in his own eyes; Meat may be slaughtered and eaten anywhere, like gazelle and deer, when far from the sanctuary; Rejoice before God with sons, daughters, slaves and the Levite; Blood is the life; do not eat it but pour it on the ground like water; After crossing the sea the people see idol-worshipers and ask the prophet for a god like theirs; God causes his name to dwell at the chosen place; Sacrifice only at the place God will choose to make his name dwell; Command to smash altars, standing stones and Asherah poles and burn idols; Nations burn their sons and daughters in fire to their gods; Pagan worship on high mountains, hills and under every green tree.

Only in Abraham, the Ancient House and the rites of pilgrimage and sacrifice: Abraham is told to proclaim the pilgrimage; people come on foot and on lean camels from every deep ravine; Pilgrims finish their grooming, fulfill vows and circle the Ancient House (al-bayt al-ʿatīq); Neither the flesh nor the blood of sacrifices reaches God, only the piety of the offerer; Simile: the polytheist is like one who falls from the sky and is snatched by birds or flung far by the wind; The Sacred Mosque is appointed for all people alike, the resident and the visitor from the desert; Sacrificial camels (budn) are slaughtered standing in ranks; when their sides fall, eat of them; God settled Abraham at the site of the House and told him to purify it for those who circle, stand, bow and prostrate; Nazirite brings burnt, sin and well-being offerings with unleavened bread when his term ends; Eat of the sacrificial animals and feed the wretched poor and the needy; God appointed for every community a rite of sacrifice (mansak); A place recognized as the house of God and gate of heaven; Offer to God a sacrifice of thanksgiving (todah) and pay your vows to Elyon; and 5 more.

leads.title: Idolater's trial; witnesses; high court; law of the king ↔ The debt verse
leads.summary: These two units share 2 motifs: how many witnesses are required [divergence between the texts], no one put to death on the testimony of a single witness.

passages.note: How many witnesses are required [divergence between the texts] (Deut 17:6 ʿal pî šĕnayim ʿēdîm ʾô šĕlōšâ ʿēdîm yûmat ha-mmēt: two or three witnesses for a capital case; Q 4:15 fa-stashhidū ʿalayhinna arbaʿatan minkum: four witnesses required for a charge of indecency (fāḥisha). The number is raised for sexual offences.)
passages.text: עַל פִּ֣י שְׁנַ֣יִם עֵדִ֗ים א֛וֹ שְׁלֹשָׁ֥ה עֵדִ֖ים יוּמַ֣ת הַמֵּ֑ת לֹ֣א יוּמַ֔ת עַל פִּ֖י עֵ֥ד אֶחָֽד

passages.note: Limits on how many wives the leader may take [divergence between the texts] (A limit on the leader's wives. Deut: wə-lōʾ yarbeh-lô nāšîm wə-lōʾ yāsûr ləḇāḇô, a general cap on number, for fear his heart turns. Q: first an enumerated permission (innā aḥlalnā laka azwājaka ... khāliṣatan laka min dūni l-muʾminīn), then a freeze: lā yaḥillu laka n-nisāʾu min baʿdu wa-lā an tabaddala bihinna min azwājin wa-law aʿjabaka ḥusnuhunna. Deut does not let the number grow; the Quran grants a special privilege and then closes it.)

passages.note: Whether and when to call the enemy to peace [contrast between the texts] (Calling for peace in war. Deuteronomy: kî ṯiqraḇ ʾel ʿîr lə-hillāḥēm ʿālêhā wə-qārāʾṯā ʾēlêhā lə-šālôm (offer peace first; if accepted, forced labor). Quran: fa-lā tahinū wa-tadʿū ilā s-salmi wa-antumu l-aʿlawna wa-llāhu maʿakum (do not weaken and call for peace while you have the upper hand). Same expression, qārāʾṯā ... lə-šālôm / tadʿū ilā s-salm, with opposite advice; the settings differ (before a siege; in a war already being won).)

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/07-hb-quran.yaml): contrast. The fainthearted man at the call to war, with opposite rulings. Deuteronomy sends him home: mî hā-ʾîš hay-yārēʾ wə-raḵ hal-lēḇāḇ yēlēḵ wə-yāšōḇ lə-ḇêṯô wə-lōʾ yimmas ʾeṯ ləḇaḇ ʾeḥâw. The Quran rebukes him: raʾayta lladhīna fī qulūbihim maraḍun yanẓurūna ilayka naẓara l-maghshiyyi ʿalayhi mina l-mawt ... fa-awlā lahum; ṭāʿatun wa-qawlun maʿrūf. Deuteronomy: kî ṯiqraḇ ʾel ʿîr lə-hillāḥēm ʿālêhā wə-qārāʾṯā ʾēlêhā lə-šālôm (offer peace first; if accepted, forced labor). Quran: fa-lā tahinū wa-tadʿū ilā s-salmi wa-antumu l-aʿlawna wa-llāhu maʿakum (do not weaken and call for peace while you have the upper hand). Same expression, qārāʾṯā ... lə-šālôm / tadʿū ilā s-salm, with opposite advice; the settings differ (before a siege; in a war already being won).

leads.title: Rules of war: exemptions, peace terms, fruit trees ↔ Al-Hashr: the first gathering and exile of the Banu Nadir, the cut palms, and the law of fay'
leads.summary: These two units share 2 motifs: whether the enemy's trees may be cut down in a siege [contrast between the texts], do not cut down fruit trees during a siege: is the tree of the field a man?.

passages.note: Whether the enemy's trees may be cut down in a siege [contrast between the texts] (Cutting the enemy's trees during a siege: opposite rulings. Deuteronomy: kî ṯāṣûr ʾel ʿîr ... lōʾ ṯašḥîṯ ʾeṯ ʿēṣāh ... kî mimmennû ṯōʾḵēl, only non-fruit trees may be cut (raq ʿēṣ ʾăšer tēḏaʿ kî lōʾ ʿēṣ maʾăḵāl hûʾ). Quran: mā qaṭaʿtum min līnatin aw taraktumūhā qāʾimatan ʿalā uṣūlihā fa-bi-idhni llāhi wa-li-yukhziya l-fāsiqīn (whatever palms you cut or left standing was by God's leave). Date palms are fruit trees; the Quran sanctions what Deuteronomy forbids, for a given siege.)
passages.text: כִּֽי תָצ֣וּר אֶל עִיר֩ יָמִ֨ים רַבִּ֜ים לְֽהִלָּחֵ֧ם עָלֶ֣יהָ לְתָפְשָׂ֗הּ לֹֽא תַשְׁחִ֤ית אֶת עֵצָהּ֙ לִנְדֹּ֤חַ עָלָיו֙ גַּרְזֶ֔ן כִּ֚י מִמֶּ֣נּוּ תֹאכֵ֔ל וְאֹת֖וֹ לֹ֣א תִכְרֹ֑ת כִּ֤י הָֽאָדָם֙ עֵ֣ץ הַשָּׂדֶ֔ה לָבֹ֥א מִפָּנֶ֖יךָ בַּמָּצֽוֹר

Same reasoning for keeping the unwilling out of the army: they would weaken the rest. law kharajū fīkum mā zādūkum illā khabālan ... yabghūnakumu l-fitnata vs wᵉlōʾ yimmas ʾet-lᵉbab ʾeḥāyw kilbābô. In Deut the officers send them home; in Q God himself holds them back (kariha llāhu nbiʿāthahum fa-thabbaṭahum wa-qīla qʿudū maʿa l-qāʿidīn).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Who is excused from going out to war [contrast between the texts] (weight 6.7); The fearful are sent home before battle (weight 6.3). Pair score 13.0.

passages.note: A heifer and a killing whose perpetrator is unknown [divergence between the texts] (Deut 21:1, 3 kî yimmāṣēʾ ḥālāl ... lōʾ nôdaʿ mî hikkāhû ... ʿeglat bāqār ʾăšer lōʾ ʿubbad bāh ʾăšer lōʾ māšĕkâ bĕ-ʿōl: an unsolved killing and an unworked heifer; Q 2:71-72 lā dhalūlun tuthīru l-arḍa ... wa-idh qataltum nafsan fa-ddāraʾtum fīhā: a heifer not used for ploughing and a killing over which people dispute. The ending is reversed: in Deut the killer stays unknown, the neck is broken (wĕ-ʿārĕpû) and the elders declare yādênû lōʾ šāpĕkû ʾet ha-ddām ha-zzeh, the blood atoned; in the Quran the cow is slaughtered (fa-dhabaḥūhā) and God brings out what was hidden (wa-llāhu mukhrijun mā kuntum taktumūn): the dead man is revived and the killer known.)

passages.text: ٱلزَّانِيَةُ وَٱلزَّانِى فَٱجْلِدُوا۟ كُلَّ وَٰحِدٍ مِّنْهُمَا مِا۟ئَةَ جَلْدَةٍ وَلَا تَأْخُذْكُم بِهِمَا رَأْفَةٌ فِى دِينِ ٱللَّهِ إِن كُنتُمْ تُؤْمِنُونَ بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلْيَوْمِ ٱلْءَاخِرِ وَلْيَشْهَدْ عَذَابَهُمَا طَآئِفَةٌ مِّنَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml): contrast, divergence. Both punish man and woman alike, but differently: û-mētû gam šənêhem hā-ʾîš ... wə-hā-ʾiššâ ~ az-zāniyatu wa-z-zānī fa-jlidū kulla wāḥidin minhumā miʾata jaldatin: death in Deuteronomy, a hundred lashes in the Quran. Note also the order: the Quran names the woman first. Punishing the false accuser of a woman: Deut 22:18-19 the husband who brought out an evil name (hôṣîʾ šēm rāʿ) is chastised (wə-yissərû ʾōtô), fined a hundred silver and may never divorce her; Q 24:4 anyone who accuses chaste women (al-muḥṣanāt) without four witnesses gets eighty lashes, and his testimony is never accepted again. In the Quran the husband's case goes to the oath procedure of 24:6-9.

Shared motifs, rarest first: Husband who falsely accuses his bride is flogged, fined 100 silver, and may never divorce her (weight 6.7); The penalty for adultery or fornication [contrast between the texts] (weight 6.7); The penalty for falsely accusing a woman of unchastity [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); Adulterer and adulteress both put to death (weight 6.3). Pair score 26.4.

Only in Lost property, bird's nest, mixtures, tassels, virginity and sexual offences: Betrothed girl lain with in the city dies for not crying out; in the field only the man dies; Woman must not wear man's gear, nor man a woman's garment; Help lift a brother's fallen ox or donkey; Prohibition of mixed seeds in a vineyard; Bride found not a virgin stoned at the door of her father's house; Do not plough with an ox and a donkey together; Build a parapet on a new roof so no one falls; Return a brother's lost animal or property; you may not hide yourself; Man who lies with an unbetrothed virgin pays her father fifty silver and must marry her without divorce; Send away the mother bird before taking the young, for long life; Tassels (gedilim) on the four corners of the garment; Parents display the bride's virginity cloth before the elders; and 2 more.

Only in Lashes for fornication, four witnesses and the mutual cursing oath: The fornicating woman and man each receive a hundred lashes, witnessed by a party of believers; A fornicator may marry only a fornicator or an idolater; such marriage is forbidden to believers; A husband accusing his wife without witnesses swears four times by God and a fifth time invokes God's curse on himself if lying; she averts punishment by four counter-oaths and a fifth invoking God's wrath; Whether the husband who accuses his wife bears any liability [contrast between the texts]; Wife suspected of adultery drinks 'water of bitterness' as an ordeal; Whoever accuses a chaste woman without four witnesses is flogged eighty lashes and his testimony is never accepted; Who is barred from marrying an unchaste woman [divergence between the texts]; Judges told to let no pity hold them back from carrying out a fixed punishment; How many lashes a flogging may have [contrast between the texts]; A man accused swears a curse-oath before the altar, and God judges guilty and innocent; Who swears, and how, when a husband suspects his wife of adultery without witnesses [divergence between the texts]; Adultery done in secret with no witness and not caught in the act; and 4 more.

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/07-hb-quran.yaml): echo. kabbēḏ ʾeṯ ʾāḇîḵā wə-ʾeṯ ʾimmeḵā kaʾăšer ṣiwwəḵā YHWH ... ləmaʿan yîṭaḇ lāḵ vs. wa-waṣṣaynā l-insāna bi-wālidayhi iḥsānan. Deuteronomy's 'as YHWH commanded you' (ṣiwwəḵā) matches the Quran's 'we enjoined' (waṣṣaynā), both from the root ṣ-w-y.
Shared motifs, rarest first: Honor father and mother, with the promise of long life (weight 5.3). Pair score 5.3.

Only in The Decalogue restated and the people's fear at Horeb: The covenant is made with those alive today, not only with the fathers; Worship of God alone joined to duty to parents [divergence between the texts]; Whether God should speak to the people directly [contrast between the texts]; Mountain burns with fire to the heart of heaven amid darkness and cloud; The people answer as one: all that YHWH has spoken we will do [response between the texts]; Who was present at the revelation on the mountain, and who knows it only by report [contrast between the texts]; God heard as a voice out of fire with no visible form; People fear to hear God directly and ask the prophet to mediate; The people's answer to the covenant ('we hear ...') [response between the texts]; Sabbath grounded in the memory of slavery in Egypt; Honor father and mother, with the promise of long life [divergence between the texts]; Believers' confession 'we hear and we obey' (sami'na wa-ata'na); and 10 more.

Only in Kindness to parents, thirty months of bearing and weaning, the prayer at forty and the son who says 'Uff': God enjoins humans to be good to their parents; On reaching full strength at forty, a man prays to be grateful for favor on himself and his parents and for righteous offspring; A son says 'Uff!' to his parents who plead with him, scorning resurrection as 'tales of the ancients'; His mother bore him with hardship and delivered him with hardship; bearing and weaning take thirty months; The damned are told: you used up your good things in your worldly life and enjoyed them; today you are repaid with humiliation; The mother's pain in bearing children: penalty, or ground of gratitude [divergence between the texts]; For all there are degrees (darajat) according to what they did; The ground and the reward of the duty to parents [divergence between the texts]; A son who rejects his parents: the charge and the penalty [divergence between the texts]; Stubborn and rebellious son, glutton and drunkard, stoned by the men of his city; Whoever does good does it for his own soul; whoever does evil, it is against it; Unbelievers dismiss the revelation as 'tales of the ancients' (asatir al-awwalin) they could equal.

leads.title: The Decalogue restated and the people's fear at Horeb ↔ The recited commandments (the Quranic decalogue)

passages.note: Honor father and mother, with the promise of long life [divergence between the texts] (Deut: kabbēd ʾet-ʾāvîkhā wə-ʾet-ʾimmekhā ... ləmaʿan yaʾărîkhūn yāmêkhā û-ləmaʿan yîṭav lākh ʿal-hā-ʾădāmāh. Q: wa-bi-l-wālidayni iḥsānan. 'Honour' becomes 'kindness', and the promise of long life in the land is dropped.)

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/02-hb-quran.yaml): divergence, parallel. Deut: kabbēd ʾet-ʾāvîkhā wə-ʾet-ʾimmekhā ... ləmaʿan yaʾărîkhūn yāmêkhā û-ləmaʿan yîṭav lākh ʿal-hā-ʾădāmāh. Q: wa-bi-l-wālidayni iḥsānan. 'Honour' becomes 'kindness', and the promise of long life in the land is dropped. Deut: lōʾ tirṣāḥ; wə-lōʾ tinʾāf; wə-lōʾ-taʿăneh və-rēʿăkhā ʿēd šāwʾ, absolute. Q qualifies and widens: wa-lā taqtulū l-nafsa llatī ḥarrama llāhu illā bi-l-ḥaqqi (with an exception); wa-lā taqrabū l-fawāḥisha mā ẓahara minhā wa-mā baṭana (all indecency, not only adultery); wa-idhā qultum fa-ʿdilū wa-law kāna dhā qurbā (just speech even against kin). Theft is absent. Deut, right after the Decalogue: lōʾ tāsurû yāmîn û-śəmōʾl bə-khol-ha-dderekh ... tēlēkhû. Q, right after its list: wa-anna hādhā ṣirāṭī mustaqīman fa-ttabiʿūhu wa-lā tattabiʿū l-subula fa-tafarraqa bikum. The single road versus side paths, placed at the same point.

Shared motifs, rarest first: Honor father and mother, with the promise of long life [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.0); Keep the law, turning neither to the right nor to the left (weight 5.8); Prohibitions of murder, adultery, theft and false witness [divergence between the texts] (weight 5.8); The Ten Commandments (Decalogue) (weight 5.4); Honor father and mother, with the promise of long life (weight 5.3); Prohibitions of murder, adultery, theft and false witness (weight 5.1). Pair score 33.4.

Only in The Decalogue restated and the people's fear at Horeb: The covenant is made with those alive today, not only with the fathers; Worship of God alone joined to duty to parents [divergence between the texts]; Whether God should speak to the people directly [contrast between the texts]; Mountain burns with fire to the heart of heaven amid darkness and cloud; The people answer as one: all that YHWH has spoken we will do [response between the texts]; Who was present at the revelation on the mountain, and who knows it only by report [contrast between the texts]; God heard as a voice out of fire with no visible form; People fear to hear God directly and ask the prophet to mediate; The people's answer to the covenant ('we hear ...') [response between the texts]; Sabbath grounded in the memory of slavery in Egypt; Believers' confession 'we hear and we obey' (sami'na wa-ata'na); Prohibition of coveting the neighbor's wife and property; and 5 more.

Only in The recited commandments (the Quranic decalogue): List of commandments introduced 'Come, I will recite what your Lord has forbidden you'; Lest you say scripture was sent only to two groups before us; This is my straight path; follow it and not other ways that scatter you; God gave Moses the book complete and detailing everything; Do not kill your children for fear of poverty; God provides for them and you; The Ten Commandments (Decalogue) [divergence between the texts]; Stand firm for justice as witnesses for God even against yourselves, parents and kin, rich or poor; Guardians must keep orphans' property intact and hand it over when they come of age; I set before you life and death, blessing and curse: choose life; God burdens no soul beyond its capacity; Honest balances, weights, ephah and hin are commanded.

passages.note: Those who remember God standing, sitting and on their sides and reflect on creation (Deut 6:7 wĕ-dibbartā bām bĕ-šibtĕkā bĕ-bêtekā û-bĕ-lektĕkā ba-dderek û-bĕ-šokbĕkā û-bĕ-qûmekā: speak of these words sitting, walking, lying down and rising; Q 3:191 alladhīna yadhkurūna llāha qiyāman wa-quʿūdan wa-ʿalā junūbihim: who remember God standing, sitting and lying on their sides. Same set of bodily postures for constant attention; the object is the commandments in Deut, God himself and his creation in the Quran.)
passages.text: וְשִׁנַּנְתָּ֣ם לְבָנֶ֔יךָ וְדִבַּרְתָּ֖ בָּ֑ם בְּשִׁבְתְּךָ֤ בְּבֵיתֶ֨ךָ֙ וּבְלֶכְתְּךָ֣ בַדֶּ֔רֶךְ וּֽבְשָׁכְבְּךָ֖ וּבְקוּמֶֽךָ

passages.note: Those who remember God standing, sitting and on their sides and reflect on creation
passages.text: فَإِذَا قَضَيْتُمُ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ فَٱذْكُرُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ قِيَٰمًا وَقُعُودًا وَعَلَىٰ جُنُوبِكُمْ فَإِذَا ٱطْمَأْنَنتُمْ فَأَقِيمُوا۟ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ إِنَّ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ كَانَتْ عَلَى ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ كِتَٰبًا مَّوْقُوتًا

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/02-hb-quran.yaml): echo. God is to be remembered in every posture. Q: fa-dhkurū llāha qiyāman wa-quʿūdan wa-ʿalā junūbikum. Deut: bə-šivtəkhā bə-vêtekhā û-və-lekhtəkhā vaddérekh û-və-šokhbəkhā û-və-qûmekhā.
Shared motifs, rarest first: Those who remember God standing, sitting and on their sides and reflect on creation (weight 6.0). Pair score 6.0.

Only in The Shema and the instruction to teach: When your son asks what the laws mean, recite the exodus story; Swear only by God's name; Teach the words to your children when sitting, walking, lying down and rising; Words bound as a sign on the hand and between the eyes (phylacteries); Do not put God to the test as at Massah; When you eat and are full, beware lest you forget God; Words written on doorposts and gates (mezuzah); Israel will inherit cities, houses, cisterns, vineyards and olives they did not build or plant; Love God with all your heart, soul and might; Hear O Israel: YHWH our God, YHWH is one; Promised land described as flowing with milk and honey.

Only in Shortened prayer and prayer in shifts under arms: If you suffer, they suffer as you do, but you hope from God what they do not; Prayer is prescribed for believers at fixed times (kitāban mawqūtan); Prayer may be shortened when travelling in danger; In war the congregation prays in shifts, one group standing guard with weapons.

leads.title: The Shema and the instruction to teach ↔ The chain of revelation; Jesus, word and spirit; 'say not three'
leads.summary: These two units share 1 motifs: hear o israel: yhwh our god, yhwh is one.

passages.note: Hear O Israel: YHWH our God, YHWH is one
passages.text: שְׁמַ֖ע יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵ֖ינוּ יְהוָ֥ה אֶחָֽד

passages.note: Hear O Israel: YHWH our God, YHWH is one (Q: wa-lā taqūlū thalāthatun ... innamā llāhu ilāhun wāḥidun. Deut: šəmaʿ Yiśrāʾēl YHWH ʾĕlōhênû YHWH ʾeḥād. Q turns the oneness formula against the Christians' 'three'.)
passages.text: يَٰٓأَهْلَ ٱلْكِتَٰبِ لَا تَغْلُوا۟ فِى دِينِكُمْ وَلَا تَقُولُوا۟ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ إِلَّا ٱلْحَقَّ إِنَّمَا ٱلْمَسِيحُ عِيسَى ٱبْنُ مَرْيَمَ رَسُولُ ٱللَّهِ وَكَلِمَتُهُۥٓ أَلْقَىٰهَآ إِلَىٰ مَرْيَمَ وَرُوحٌ مِّنْهُ فَـَٔامِنُوا۟ بِٱللَّهِ وَرُسُلِهِۦ وَلَا تَقُولُوا۟ ثَلَٰثَةٌ ٱنتَهُوا۟ خَيْرًا لَّكُمْ إِنَّمَا ٱللَّهُ إِلَٰهٌ وَٰحِدٌ سُبْحَٰنَهُۥٓ أَن يَكُونَ لَهُۥ وَلَدٌ لَّهُۥ مَا فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ وَكَفَىٰ بِٱللَّهِ وَكِيلًا

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/02-hb-quran.yaml): parallel. Q: wa-lā taqūlū thalāthatun ... innamā llāhu ilāhun wāḥidun. Deut: šəmaʿ Yiśrāʾēl YHWH ʾĕlōhênû YHWH ʾeḥād. Q turns the oneness formula against the Christians' 'three'.
Shared motifs, rarest first: Hear O Israel: YHWH our God, YHWH is one (weight 5.4). Pair score 5.4.

Only in The Shema and the instruction to teach: When your son asks what the laws mean, recite the exodus story; Swear only by God's name; Teach the words to your children when sitting, walking, lying down and rising; Words bound as a sign on the hand and between the eyes (phylacteries); Do not put God to the test as at Massah; When you eat and are full, beware lest you forget God; Words written on doorposts and gates (mezuzah); Israel will inherit cities, houses, cisterns, vineyards and olives they did not build or plant; Love God with all your heart, soul and might; Those who remember God standing, sitting and on their sides and reflect on creation; Promised land described as flowing with milk and honey.

Only in The chain of revelation; Jesus, word and spirit; 'say not three': The angels brought near (al-muqarrabūn) to God; God spoke to Moses directly (kallama taklīman); Jesus is God's word cast to Mary and a spirit from him; Catalogue of prophets who received revelation, from Noah to Jesus; People of the Book, do not go to excess (lā taghlū) in your religion; The Messiah does not disdain to be a servant of God, nor do the angels brought near; Do not say 'three'; God is only one god (rejection of a triad); First servant song: God's chosen servant with his spirit brings justice to the nations without crying out; a bruised reed he will not break; Of the messengers before you, some we have related to you and some we have not; God gave David the Psalms (Zabur); God speaks to the prophet face to face, as a man speaks to his friend; Whether God has a son, or calls his anointed king his begotten son [contrast between the texts]; and 2 more.

leads.title: Dispossession of the seven nations; Israel the treasured people ↔ Address to the Children of Israel
leads.summary: These two units share 2 motifs: if the people keep god's covenant, god keeps his covenant with them, israel chosen as god's treasured people (am segullah) out of all peoples.

passages.note: If the people keep God's covenant, God keeps his covenant with them (Deut 7:12 wĕ-hāyâ ʿēqeb tišmĕʿûn ... wĕ-šāmar YHWH ʾĕlōhêkā lĕkā ʾet ha-bĕrît, 7:9 šōmēr ha-bĕrît wĕ-ha-ḥesed lĕ-ʾōhăbāyw; Q 2:40 wa-awfū bi-ʿahdī ūfi bi-ʿahdikum 'fulfil my covenant and I will fulfil yours': the covenant kept on both sides, addressed to Israel.)
passages.text: וְיָ֣דַעְתָּ֔ כִּֽי יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ ה֣וּא הָֽאֱלֹהִ֑ים הָאֵל֙ הַֽנֶּאֱמָ֔ן שֹׁמֵ֧ר הַבְּרִ֣ית וְהַחֶ֗סֶד לְאֹהֲבָ֛יו וּלְשֹׁמְרֵ֥י מצותו מִצְוֺתָ֖יו לְאֶ֥לֶף דּֽוֹר

passages.text: וְהָיָ֣ה עֵ֣קֶב תִּשְׁמְע֗וּן אֵ֤ת הַמִּשְׁפָּטִים֙ הָאֵ֔לֶּה וּשְׁמַרְתֶּ֥ם וַעֲשִׂיתֶ֖ם אֹתָ֑ם וְשָׁמַר֩ יְהוָ֨ה אֱלֹהֶ֜יךָ לְךָ֗ אֶֽת הַבְּרִית֙ וְאֶת הַחֶ֔סֶד אֲשֶׁ֥ר נִשְׁבַּ֖ע לַאֲבֹתֶֽיךָ

passages.note: Israel chosen as God's treasured people (am segullah) out of all peoples
passages.text: כִּ֣י עַ֤ם קָדוֹשׁ֙ אַתָּ֔ה לַיהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֶ֑יךָ בְּךָ֞ בָּחַ֣ר יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֗יךָ לִהְי֥וֹת לוֹ֙ לְעַ֣ם סְגֻלָּ֔ה מִכֹּל֙ הָֽעַמִּ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֖ר עַל פְּנֵ֥י הָאֲדָמָֽה

passages.note: Israel chosen as God's treasured people (am segullah) out of all peoples (preferred over the worlds)
passages.text: يَٰبَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ ٱذْكُرُوا۟ نِعْمَتِىَ ٱلَّتِىٓ أَنْعَمْتُ عَلَيْكُمْ وَأَنِّى فَضَّلْتُكُمْ عَلَى ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml): parallel. Deut 7:12 wĕ-hāyâ ʿēqeb tišmĕʿûn ... wĕ-šāmar YHWH ʾĕlōhêkā lĕkā ʾet ha-bĕrît, 7:9 šōmēr ha-bĕrît wĕ-ha-ḥesed lĕ-ʾōhăbāyw; Q 2:40 wa-awfū bi-ʿahdī ūfi bi-ʿahdikum 'fulfil my covenant and I will fulfil yours': the covenant kept on both sides, addressed to Israel. Deut 7:6 bĕkā bāḥar YHWH ... lĕ-ʿam sĕgullâ mi-kkōl hā-ʿammîm; Q 2:47 wa-annī faḍḍaltukum ʿalā l-ʿālamīn. The Quran grants the election, but in the past tense, set inside a warning (2:48) rather than as a status.

Shared motifs, rarest first: If the people keep God's covenant, God keeps his covenant with them (weight 6.7); Israel chosen as God's treasured people (am segullah) out of all peoples (weight 5.3). Pair score 12.0.

Only in Dispossession of the seven nations; Israel the treasured people: God chose Israel not for their numbers, being the fewest of peoples, but from love; Silver and gold on idols must not be taken; it is abomination and herem; Obedience brings fertility: none barren among people or cattle; Enemies driven out little by little lest wild beasts multiply; Why God chose Israel: love, or knowledge and testing [divergence between the texts]; The evil diseases of Egypt removed from the obedient or brought on the disobedient; God sends the hornet to drive out the inhabitants; Ban on marrying outside the community and its criterion [divergence between the texts]; List of the seven nations of Canaan to be dispossessed; God visits the fathers' sin on the third and fourth generation, but keeps steadfast love for thousands; Prohibition of intermarriage with the peoples of the land lest they turn sons to other gods; Command to smash altars, standing stones and Asherah poles and burn idols; and 1 more.

Only in Address to the Children of Israel: God's choosing of Israel among the peoples [divergence between the texts]; On that day no soul will avail another, no intercession or ransom accepted, no help given; Refrain to the Children of Israel: 'remember my favor which I bestowed on you'; God rebukes the wicked who recites his statutes and covenant yet consorts with thieves and adulterers; Whether payment may substitute for a life [contrast between the texts]; People of the Book cast God's book behind their backs; No man can ransom his brother or give God a ransom (kofer) for him; the redemption of life is too costly; Each person dies for his own sin.

leads.title: Dispossession of the seven nations; Israel the treasured people ↔ Wine, gambling, orphans, mixed marriage and menstruation
leads.summary: These two units share 2 motifs: ban on marrying outside the community and its criterion [divergence between the texts], prohibition of intermarriage with the peoples of the land lest they turn sons to other gods.

passages.note: Ban on marrying outside the community and its criterion [divergence between the texts] (Deut 7:3-4 wĕ-lōʾ titḥattēn bām ... kî yāsîr ʾet binkā mē-ʾaḥăray wĕ-ʿābĕdû ʾĕlōhîm ʾăḥērîm: no marriage with the peoples of Canaan, for they will turn your son to other gods; Q 2:221 wa-lā tankiḥū l-mushrikāti ḥattā yuʾminna ... ulāʾika yadʿūna ilā n-nāri: no marriage with polytheist women or men 'until they believe', for they call to the Fire. Same reason (being drawn to other gods), but the bar is belief, removable by conversion, not nationhood; and the Quran adds a believing slave is better than a free polytheist.)

leads.title: Superscription, 'vapor of vapors' and the endless cycles of nature ↔ Signs of the dead earth, night, sun, moon and the laden ship
leads.summary: These two units share 1 motifs: the sun runs to its resting place (mustaqarr).

passages.note: The sun runs to its resting place (mustaqarr) (wə-zāraḥ ha-ššemeš û-ḇāʾ ha-ššāmeš wə-ʾel-məqômô šôʾēp̄ zôrēaḥ hûʾ šām vs. wa-sh-shamsu tajrī li-mustaqarrin lahā dhālika taqdīru l-ʿazīzi l-ʿalīm. The sun hurries back to its place (māqôm / mustaqarr). For Qohelet this is the weary round of hevel; for the Quran it is the decree (taqdīr) of the Mighty and is a sign (āya).)
passages.text: וְזָרַ֥ח הַשֶּׁ֖מֶשׁ וּבָ֣א הַשָּׁ֑מֶשׁ וְאֶ֨ל מְקוֹמ֔וֹ שׁוֹאֵ֛ף זוֹרֵ֥חַֽ ה֖וּא שָֽׁם

passages.note: The sun runs to its resting place (mustaqarr)
passages.text: وَٱلشَّمْسُ تَجْرِى لِمُسْتَقَرٍّ لَّهَا ذَٰلِكَ تَقْدِيرُ ٱلْعَزِيزِ ٱلْعَلِيمِ

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/06-hb-quran.yaml): parallel. wə-zāraḥ ha-ššemeš û-ḇāʾ ha-ššāmeš wə-ʾel-məqômô šôʾēp̄ zôrēaḥ hûʾ šām vs. wa-sh-shamsu tajrī li-mustaqarrin lahā dhālika taqdīru l-ʿazīzi l-ʿalīm. The sun hurries back to its place (māqôm / mustaqarr). For Qohelet this is the weary round of hevel; for the Quran it is the decree (taqdīr) of the Mighty and is a sign (āya).
Shared motifs, rarest first: The sun runs to its resting place (mustaqarr) (weight 6.7). Pair score 6.7.

Only in Superscription, 'vapor of vapors' and the endless cycles of nature: Endless cycles: the sun rises and pants back to its place, the wind circles, rivers run to the sea which is never full; All things are wearisome; the eye is not sated with seeing nor the ear filled with hearing; A generation goes and a generation comes, but the earth stands forever; There is no remembrance of former people nor will there be of those yet to come; What has been is what will be; there is nothing new under the sun; The speaker Qohelet ('the assembler') is presented as son of David and king over Israel in Jerusalem (royal fiction); What profit (yitron) has a man from all his toil under the sun?; 'Hevel havalim': vapor of vapors, all is vapor (vanity, futility, transience).

Only in Signs of the dead earth, night, sun, moon and the laden ship: The night is a sign: God strips (naslakh) the day from it and they are in darkness; A sign: God carried their offspring in the laden ship, and made for them similar things to ride; God measured stations (manazil) for the moon until it returns like an old dried palm-stalk; Asked to spend, unbelievers retort 'shall we feed one whom God could feed if he willed?'; God made the flood ship (or its survivors) a sign for all the worlds; The hero is saved with those with him in the laden ark (al-fulk al-mashḥūn); The sun comes forth like a bridegroom from his chamber and rejoices like a strong man to run his course; God made the sun a radiance and the moon a light with measured stations, to count years and reckoning; Sun and moon each swim in an orbit (falak); God created humans (and things) in pairs, male and female; Scoffers ask the prophet to hasten the punishment; it is held back only by an appointed term and will come suddenly; Sun and moon are set to rule day and night and mark signs and seasons; and 1 more.

leads.title: Cast your bread upon the waters; rejoice in youth ↔ God's signs, the inexhaustible words, and the five things only God knows
leads.summary: These two units share 1 motifs: god alone knows the hour, sends rain, knows what is in wombs; no soul knows what it will earn tomorrow or in what land it will die.

passages.note: God alone knows the Hour, sends rain, knows what is in wombs; no soul knows what it will earn tomorrow or in what land it will die (ka-ʿăṣāmîm bə-ḇeṭen ha-mməlēʾâ kāḵâ lōʾ ṯēḏaʿ ʾeṯ-maʿăśēh hā-ʾĕlōhîm vs. wa-yaʿlamu mā fī l-arḥām: what grows in the womb is hidden from humans and known to God. Qohelet joins it to the way of the wind (ha-rûaḥ), the Quran to the Hour and the rain.)
