evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/06-hb-quran.yaml): parallel. ka-ʿăṣāmîm bə-ḇeṭen ha-mməlēʾâ kāḵâ lōʾ ṯēḏaʿ ʾeṯ-maʿăśēh hā-ʾĕlōhîm vs. wa-yaʿlamu mā fī l-arḥām: what grows in the womb is hidden from humans and known to God. Qohelet joins it to the way of the wind (ha-rûaḥ), the Quran to the Hour and the rain.
Shared motifs, rarest first: God alone knows the Hour, sends rain, knows what is in wombs; no soul knows what it will earn tomorrow or in what land it will die (weight 6.3). Pair score 6.3.

Only in Cast your bread upon the waters; rejoice in youth: As you do not know the way of the wind (or spirit), or how bones grow in the womb of the pregnant, so you do not know the work of God; Send out your bread on the face of the waters, for after many days you will find it; Give a portion to seven or even to eight, for you do not know what disaster may come; Light is sweet and it is pleasant for the eyes to see the sun; Rejoice, young man, in your youth and walk in the ways of your heart, but know that for all these God will bring you into judgment; In the morning sow your seed and in the evening do not withhold your hand, for you do not know which will prosper; If clouds are full they empty rain; where the tree falls, north or south, there it lies; He who watches the wind will not sow, and he who regards the clouds will not reap; Youth and the dawn of life (shaharut, 'blackness of hair') are vapor; Graded numerical saying: 'Three things... and four...' (x / x+1).

Only in God's signs, the inexhaustible words, and the five things only God knows: Creating and resurrecting all of you is for God like a single soul; Waves overwhelm the ship like canopies (zulal); If all trees were pens and the sea, replenished by seven more seas, were ink, God's words would not be exhausted; The religion of the fathers invoked, held to or renounced [contrast between the texts]; Whoever rejects false gods (taghut) and believes in God grasps the firmest handhold that never breaks; On the Day no parent can avail his child, nor child his parent; Only God knows when the mountain goats and hinds give birth and counts their months; Seafarers cry to God in a storm; what they do once rescued [divergence between the texts]; Sailors in a storm call on God sincerely, vow thanks, and transgress once saved; Rejecters reply 'we follow what we found our fathers upon'; Sun and moon are subjected, each running to an appointed term; God makes the night pass into the day and the day into the night; and 1 more.

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml): contrast. What the Quran puts in the mouths of the deniers is voiced by Qohelet: Q 23:37 in hiya illā ḥayātunā d-dunyā namūtu wa-naḥyā wa-mā naḥnu bi-mabʿūthīna (after 23:35 idhā mittum wa-kuntum turāban wa-ʿiẓāman) ~ Eccl 3:20 hak-kōl hāyâ min he-ʿāfār wə-hak-kōl šāv ʾel he-ʿāfār, 3:21 mî yôdēaʿ rûaḥ bənê hā-ʾādām hā-ʿōlâ hîʾ lə-māʿlâ. In Ecclesiastes the doubt is wisdom; in the Quran it is the unbelief of the chiefs who 'were given luxury' (atrafnāhum).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Whether those who die and return to dust rise again [contrast between the texts] (weight 6.3); Human comes from dust and returns to dust (weight 5.0). Pair score 11.3.

Only in Injustice, divine judgment, and humans no better than beasts: God tests humans to show them that they are but beasts; man has no advantage over the beast; Who knows whether the spirit of man goes upward and the spirit of the beast goes down to the earth?; In the place of justice there is wickedness and in the place of righteousness wickedness; God will judge the righteous and the wicked, for there is a time for every matter; Whether death is the end: asked, held by sceptics, or answered by resurrection [response between the texts]; One fate (miqreh) befalls the wise and the fool, man and beast alike; Who will bring him to see what will be after him?; There is nothing better than to eat, drink and find enjoyment in one's toil; this is from the hand of God; Do evildoers think God will make them equal to the righteous in life and in death?.

Only in A later generation's messenger, the Cry, and messengers in succession: God sent his messengers one after another; each was denied and each nation became a tale; A people is seized by the Cry (al-ṣayḥa) and made like flood-scum; Earlier messengers were only men who ate food and were not immortal; Hero asks the deity to judge or destroy his opponents; Your dead shall live, their corpses rise; dwellers in the dust shall awake and sing; Destruction follows the people's rejection of a messenger.

Qohelet: miqreh ʾeḥāḏ lāhem kə-môṯ zeh kēn môṯ zeh ... hak-kōl šāḇ ʾel he-ʿāp̄ār; mî yôḏēaʿ rûaḥ bənê hā-ʾāḏām hā-ʿōlâ hîʾ lə-māʿlâ. (mî yôḏēaʿ) the Quran replies that they have no knowledge (ʿilm), only conjecture, and 45:26 affirms the gathering to the Day of Resurrection. evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/08-hb-quran.yaml): parallel. alladhī jamaʿa mālan wa-ʿaddadahu yaḥsabu anna mālahu akhladah; alhākumu t-takāthuru ḥattā zurtumu l-maqābir ~ ʿōšer šāmûr li-vʿālāyw le-rāʿātô ... ka-ʾăšer yāṣāʾ mi-bbeṭen ʾimmô ʿārôm yāšûv ... û-meʾûmāh lōʾ yiśśāʾ baʿămālô: hoarded and counted wealth does not survive the grave. Qohelet draws resignation, the Quran a threat (la-yunbadhanna fī l-ḥuṭama).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Riches kept by their owner to his hurt, lost in a bad venture, so that his son has nothing in hand (weight 6.3). Pair score 6.3.

Only in Bureaucratic oppression, the love of money and wealth that perishes: He will not much remember the days of his life because God keeps him occupied with the joy of his heart; When goods increase, those who eat them increase; the owner only sees them with his eyes; The profit of the land is for all; a king is for (served by) the cultivated field; Sweet is the sleep of the laborer whether he eats little or much, but the surfeit of the rich will not let him sleep; He who loves silver will not be satisfied with silver, nor he who loves abundance with income; If you see oppression of the poor in a province, do not be amazed: a high one watches over a high one, and higher ones over them; 'Naked I came from my mother's womb and naked I shall return there'; What profit (yitron) has a man from all his toil under the sun?; There is nothing better than to eat, drink and find enjoyment in one's toil; this is from the hand of God.

Only in Rivalry, time and the slanderer: Knowledge of certainty ('ilm al-yaqin) and the eye of certainty ('ayn al-yaqin): you will see hell; God's kindled fire rises over the hearts and is closed over them in extended columns; Oath by time or the afternoon (al-'asr): humankind is in loss; Rivalry in piling up (al-takathur) distracts people until they visit the graves; they will be asked about the pleasures; A fire is closed over the damned (mu'sada); Hell given proper names: Laza (scalp-stripper), Saqar (scorcher, leaves nothing), al-Hutama (the crusher), Hawiya (the abyss); Do not go about as a talebearer among your people; Woe to every slanderer and backbiter (humaza lumaza) who amasses and counts wealth, thinking it makes him immortal; Rhetorical formula 'And what will make you know what X is?' (wa ma adraka ma) introducing an eschatological term.

passages.text: אִ֣ישׁ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יִתֶּן ל֣וֹ הָאֱלֹהִ֡ים עֹשֶׁר֩ וּנְכָסִ֨ים וְכָב֜וֹד וְֽאֵינֶ֨נּוּ חָסֵ֥ר לְנַפְשׁ֣וֹ מִכֹּ֣ל אֲשֶׁר יִתְאַוֶּ֗ה וְלֹֽא יַשְׁלִיטֶ֤נּוּ הָֽאֱלֹהִים֙ לֶאֱכֹ֣ל מִמֶּ֔נּוּ כִּ֛י אִ֥ישׁ נָכְרִ֖י יֹֽאכֲלֶ֑נּוּ זֶ֥ה הֶ֛בֶל וָחֳלִ֥י רָ֖ע הֽוּא

passages.note: 'Hevel havalim': vapor of vapors, all is vapor (vanity, futility, transience)
passages.text: כִּֽי בַהֶ֥בֶל בָּ֖א וּבַחֹ֣שֶׁךְ יֵלֵ֑ךְ וּבַחֹ֖שֶׁךְ שְׁמ֥וֹ יְכֻסֶּֽה

passages.note: 'Hevel havalim': vapor of vapors, all is vapor (vanity, futility, transience) (worldly life as play; the hereafter is 'the true life' (al-hayawan))
passages.text: وَمَا هَٰذِهِ ٱلْحَيَوٰةُ ٱلدُّنْيَآ إِلَّا لَهْوٌ وَلَعِبٌ وَإِنَّ ٱلدَّارَ ٱلْءَاخِرَةَ لَهِىَ ٱلْحَيَوَانُ لَوْ كَانُوا۟ يَعْلَمُونَ

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/06-hb-quran.yaml): divergence. Both call this life empty: wa-mā hādhihi l-ḥayātu d-dunyā illā lahwun wa-laʿib vs. mispar yəmê ḥayyê heḇlô wə-yaʿăśēm ka-ṣṣēl. Qohelet ends agnostic, mî yaggîd lā-ʾāḏām mah-yihyeh ʾaḥărâw (who will tell man what comes after him; cf. Eccl 9:5, 9:10, no reckoning in Sheol). The Quran answers: inna d-dāra l-ākhirata la-hiya l-ḥayawān, the next abode is the real life.

Shared motifs, rarest first: This life is fleeting; whether anything real follows it [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); 'Hevel havalim': vapor of vapors, all is vapor (vanity, futility, transience) (weight 5.3). Pair score 12.0.

Only in Wealth unenjoyed, the stillborn better off, desire unfilled: Whatever has come to be has already been named; man cannot dispute with one stronger than he; All man's toil is for his mouth, yet the appetite (nefesh) is never filled; Better the sight of the eyes than the wandering of desire; A man with a hundred children and long life who is unsatisfied and has no burial: the stillborn (nefel) is better off than he; Even if he lived a thousand years twice and saw no good, do not all go to one place?; God gives a man riches, possessions and honor but not the power to enjoy them; a stranger enjoys them; Who will bring him to see what will be after him?; Sufferer wishes he had died in the womb or been a hidden stillborn; Human days on earth are a shadow.

Only in God's earth is wide; every soul tastes death; signs and the secure sanctuary: God made a secure sanctuary (haram amin) while people around are snatched away; Seafarers cry to God in a storm; what they do once rescued [contrast between the texts]; Was not God's earth wide enough for you to emigrate (hijra) in it?; Seafarers cry to God in a storm; what they do once rescued [divergence between the texts]; Sailors in a storm call on God sincerely, vow thanks, and transgress once saved; The life of this world is only amusement and play (lahw wa-la'ib); the abode of the hereafter is the true life; Every soul shall taste death; God provides prey for the lion and food for the raven's young that cry to him; If asked who created heaven and earth and sends rain, the idolaters themselves answer 'God'; Rain from the sky gives life to the earth after its death, a sign of resurrection; Paradise as gardens (of ʿAdn) beneath which rivers flow, where the righteous abide forever.
Wealth unenjoyed, the stillborn better off, desire unfilled: tagged by Claude (model), reading the Hebrew.
God's earth is wide; every soul tastes death; signs and the secure sanctuary: tagged by Claude (model), reading the Arabic.

leads.title: Better-than sayings (name, mourning, end of a thing) ↔ Those who stayed behind, the exempt, and the Bedouin
leads.summary: These two units share 1 motifs: let them laugh a little and weep much.

passages.note: Let them laugh a little and weep much (Weeping preferred to laughter: fa-l-yaḍḥakū qalīlan wa-l-yabkū kathīran vs ṭôb kaʿas miśśᵉḥōq ... lēb ḥăkāmîm bᵉbêt ʾēbel wᵉlēb kᵉsîlîm bᵉbêt śimḥāh. In Eccl it is wisdom; in Q a punishment for the shirkers.)
passages.text: ט֥וֹב כַּ֖עַס מִשְּׂחֹ֑ק כִּֽי בְרֹ֥עַ פָּנִ֖ים יִ֥יטַב לֵֽב

passages.note: Let them laugh a little and weep much (Weeping preferred to laughter: fa-l-yaḍḥakū qalīlan wa-l-yabkū kathīran vs ṭôb kaʿas miśśᵉḥōq ... lēb ḥăkāmîm bᵉbêt ʾēbel wᵉlēb kᵉsîlîm bᵉbêt śimḥāh. In Eccl it is wisdom; in Q a punishment for the shirkers.)
passages.text: לֵ֤ב חֲכָמִים֙ בְּבֵ֣ית אֵ֔בֶל וְלֵ֥ב כְּסִילִ֖ים בְּבֵ֥ית שִׂמְחָֽה

passages.note: Let them laugh a little and weep much
passages.text: فَلْيَضْحَكُوا۟ قَلِيلًا وَلْيَبْكُوا۟ كَثِيرًا جَزَآءًۢ بِمَا كَانُوا۟ يَكْسِبُونَ

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/03-hb-quran.yaml): echo. Weeping preferred to laughter: fa-l-yaḍḥakū qalīlan wa-l-yabkū kathīran vs ṭôb kaʿas miśśᵉḥōq ... lēb ḥăkāmîm bᵉbêt ʾēbel wᵉlēb kᵉsîlîm bᵉbêt śimḥāh. In Eccl it is wisdom; in Q a punishment for the shirkers.
Shared motifs, rarest first: Let them laugh a little and weep much (weight 6.7). Pair score 6.7.

Only in Better-than sayings (name, mourning, end of a thing): Do not be quick to anger, for anger lodges in the bosom of fools; Do not say 'Why were the former days better than these?', for it is not from wisdom you ask this; The end of a thing is better than its beginning; patience is better than pride; Like the crackling of thorns (sirim) under a pot (sir), so is the laughter of the fool; In the day of prosperity be joyful, in the day of adversity consider: God has made the one as well as the other; A good name is better than good oil (shem / shemen), and the day of death than the day of birth; Better to go to the house of mourning than to the house of feasting, for that is the end of all men; the heart of the wise is in the house of mourning; Oppression makes a wise man foolish and a bribe destroys the heart; Vexation is better than laughter, for by sadness of face the heart is made glad; Consider the work of God: who can make straight what he has made crooked?; Wisdom is a shelter (shade) as money is a shelter; wisdom gives life to its possessor; A good name is to be chosen rather than great riches, favor rather than silver and gold; and 1 more.

Only in Those who stayed behind, the exempt, and the Bedouin: The Bedouin (al-a'rab) are harder in unbelief and hypocrisy; Shirkers say 'do not go out in the heat'; hell's fire is hotter; Poor volunteers turn away weeping because the prophet has no mounts for them; Who is excused from going out to war [divergence between the texts]; Even in laughter the heart may ache, and the end of joy is grief; The prophet must never pray over a dead hypocrite or stand at his grave; Catalogue of believers: repenting, worshiping, praising, wandering/fasting (sa'ihun), bowing, prostrating, enjoining right; God uses the unbelievers' wealth and children to punish them in this life; Hypocrites swear excuses and ask permission to stay behind from the campaign; Exemptions from war for a new house, unharvested vineyard, betrothed bride, or faintheartedness; God seals (tab') the hearts of deniers so they do not hear.
Better-than sayings (name, mourning, end of a thing): tagged by Claude (model), reading the Hebrew.

leads.title: Obeying the king, the hour of death and the failure of retribution ↔ The Companions of the Left in smoke and samum; who creates semen, crops, rain and fire?; the hidden Book; the soul at the throat
leads.summary: These two units share 1 motifs: when the soul reaches the throat at death and you look on, god is nearer than you; if you are not to be judged, bring it back!.

passages.note: When the soul reaches the throat at death and you look on, God is nearer than you; if you are not to be judged, bring it back! (No man can hold back the departing spirit: ʾên ʾāḏām šallîṭ bā-rûaḥ li-ḵlôʾ ʾeṯ hā-rûaḥ wə-ʾên šilṭôn bə-yôm ham-māweṯ vs. fa-lawlā idhā balaghati l-ḥulqūm ... fa-lawlā in kuntum ghayra madīnīna tarjiʿūnahā in kuntum ṣādiqīn. Qohelet states it as a limit of human power; the Quran turns it into a challenge: if you are not to be judged, bring the soul back.)
passages.text: אֵ֣ין אָדָ֞ם שַׁלִּ֤יט בָּר֨וּחַ֙ לִכְל֣וֹא אֶת הָר֔וּחַ וְאֵ֤ין שִׁלְטוֹן֙ בְּי֣וֹם הַמָּ֔וֶת וְאֵ֥ין מִשְׁלַ֖חַת בַּמִּלְחָמָ֑ה וְלֹֽא יְמַלֵּ֥ט רֶ֖שַׁע אֶת בְּעָלָֽיו

passages.note: When the soul reaches the throat at death and you look on, God is nearer than you; if you are not to be judged, bring it back!
passages.text: فَلَوْلَآ إِذَا بَلَغَتِ ٱلْحُلْقُومَ

passages.note: When the soul reaches the throat at death and you look on, God is nearer than you; if you are not to be judged, bring it back!
passages.text: وَأَنتُمْ حِينَئِذٍ تَنظُرُونَ

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/07-hb-quran.yaml): parallel. No man can hold back the departing spirit: ʾên ʾāḏām šallîṭ bā-rûaḥ li-ḵlôʾ ʾeṯ hā-rûaḥ wə-ʾên šilṭôn bə-yôm ham-māweṯ vs. fa-lawlā idhā balaghati l-ḥulqūm ... fa-lawlā in kuntum ghayra madīnīna tarjiʿūnahā in kuntum ṣādiqīn. Qohelet states it as a limit of human power; the Quran turns it into a challenge: if you are not to be judged, bring the soul back.
Shared motifs, rarest first: When the soul reaches the throat at death and you look on, God is nearer than you; if you are not to be judged, bring it back! (weight 6.7). Pair score 6.7.

Only in Obeying the king, the hour of death and the failure of retribution: Because sentence (pitgam) against an evil deed is not executed speedily, the heart of men is set to do evil; There are righteous men who receive what the wicked deserve and wicked who receive what the righteous deserve; No man has power over the wind (ruah) to restrain it, nor power over the day of death; there is no discharge in war; Keep the king's command because of the oath of God; who can say to him 'What are you doing?'; I saw the wicked buried with honor, going in and out of the holy place, and praised in the city where they did such things; Who is like the wise and knows the interpretation (pesher) of a thing? Wisdom makes his face shine; Man cannot find out the work that is done under the sun; even if the wise man claims to know, he cannot find it; For everything there is a season and a time for every matter under heaven (birth and death, planting and uprooting, etc.); Who will bring him to see what will be after him?; Wisdom or the fear of YHWH adds days and years of life; the years of the wicked are shortened; Human days on earth are a shadow; There is nothing better than to eat, drink and find enjoyment in one's toil; this is from the hand of God.

Only in The Companions of the Left in smoke and samum; who creates semen, crops, rain and fire?; the hidden Book; the soul at the throat: The damned eat of Zaqqum to fill their bellies and drink boiling water like thirst-crazed camels (al-him); A noble Quran in a hidden Book which none touch but the purified; The 'hospitality' (nuzul) of the deniers is boiling water and roasting in hell; The damned had lived in luxury and persisted in the great sin (al-hinth al-'azim); 'I swear by the positions (setting-places) of the stars, a mighty oath if you knew'; Have you seen the water you drink? Did you send it down from the rain-clouds? We could make it bitter (ujaj); For those brought near: rest (rawh), fragrance (rayhan) and a garden of bliss; The Companions of the Left are in scorching wind (samum), boiling water and the shade of black smoke (yahmum), neither cool nor kind; 'This is the certain truth' (haqq al-yaqin); Have you seen what you sow? Do you make it grow, or are we the grower? We could make it chaff; Fire kindled from a tree that God made grow [divergence between the texts]; The scripture exists with God in the 'Mother of the Book' (umm al-kitab), a heavenly archetype; and 8 more.

leads.title: Time and chance; the poor wise man who saved the city ↔ Desire as god, 'only Time destroys us', and every nation kneeling before its book
leads.summary: These two units share 1 motifs: deniers say there is only this life; we die and live, and only time (al-dahr) destroys us.

passages.note: Deniers say there is only this life; we die and live, and only Time (al-dahr) destroys us (Time as the impersonal power over men: kî ʿēṯ wā-p̄egaʿ yiqreh ʾeṯ kullām (time and chance befall them all) vs. wa-mā yuhlikunā illā d-dahr. Qohelet sets this beside faith in God; the Quran treats it as the deniers' creed.)
passages.text: שַׁ֜בְתִּי וְרָאֹ֣ה תַֽחַת הַשֶּׁ֗מֶשׁ כִּ֣י לֹא֩ לַקַּלִּ֨ים הַמֵּר֜וֹץ וְלֹ֧א לַגִּבּוֹרִ֣ים הַמִּלְחָמָ֗ה וְ֠גַם לֹ֣א לַחֲכָמִ֥ים לֶ֨חֶם֙ וְגַ֨ם לֹ֤א לַנְּבֹנִים֙ עֹ֔שֶׁר וְגַ֛ם לֹ֥א לַיֹּדְעִ֖ים חֵ֑ן כִּי עֵ֥ת וָפֶ֖גַע יִקְרֶ֥ה אֶת כֻּלָּֽם

passages.note: Deniers say there is only this life; we die and live, and only Time (al-dahr) destroys us
passages.text: وَقَالُوا۟ مَا هِىَ إِلَّا حَيَاتُنَا ٱلدُّنْيَا نَمُوتُ وَنَحْيَا وَمَا يُهْلِكُنَآ إِلَّا ٱلدَّهْرُ وَمَا لَهُم بِذَٰلِكَ مِنْ عِلْمٍ إِنْ هُمْ إِلَّا يَظُنُّونَ

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/07-hb-quran.yaml): echo. Time as the impersonal power over men: kî ʿēṯ wā-p̄egaʿ yiqreh ʾeṯ kullām (time and chance befall them all) vs. wa-mā yuhlikunā illā d-dahr. Qohelet sets this beside faith in God; the Quran treats it as the deniers' creed.
Shared motifs, rarest first: Deniers say there is only this life; we die and live, and only Time (al-dahr) destroys us (weight 6.3). Pair score 6.3.

Only in Time and chance; the poor wise man who saved the city: Man does not know his time; like fish caught in a net and birds in a snare, people are trapped in an evil time; A great king besieges a small city; a poor wise man delivers it by his wisdom, yet no one remembers him; The race is not to the swift nor the battle to the strong, nor bread to the wise; time and chance (pega') happen to all; Wisdom is better than might and weapons of war, but one sinner destroys much good; A wise man scales the city of the mighty and brings down its trusted stronghold; 'Better is X than Y' comparative saying (tov ... min).

Only in Desire as god, 'only Time destroys us', and every nation kneeling before its book: God's book speaks against them with truth: 'We used to have transcribed (nastansikh) all that you did'; What God's heavenly book records: names or deeds [divergence between the texts]; Deniers of resurrection say there is only our first death and challenge the prophet to bring back their fathers; To God belongs the grandeur (kibriya') in the heavens and the earth; Whether death is the end: asked, held by sceptics, or answered by resurrection [response between the texts]; On the day of the Hour every community is seen kneeling (jathiya), each called to its book of deeds; Whoever takes his own desire (hawā) as his god; The prophet's mission and the hearers' closed ears, eyes and hearts: caused, sealed, or beyond his cure [divergence between the texts]; God forgets the damned today as they forgot the meeting of this day; Do evildoers think God will make them equal to the righteous in life and in death?; God did not create the heavens and earth and what is between them in play (la'ibin) but in truth; God sets a seal on the unbelievers' hearts and hearing and a covering over their eyes; and 2 more.

leads.title: Ahasuerus's banquets and Queen Vashti's refusal ↔ Solomon, the speech of birds, the ants, the hoopoe and the Queen of Sheba
leads.summary: These two units share 1 motifs: the queen consults her chiefs, who defer to her; she observes that kings who enter a town ruin it and humble its nobles.

passages.note: The queen consults her chiefs, who defer to her; she observes that kings who enter a town ruin it and humble its nobles (yā ayyuhā l-malaʾu aftūnī fī amrī mā kuntu qāṭiʿatan amran ḥattā tashhadūni ~ wa-yyōʾmer ham-melekh la-ḥăkhāmîm yōdʿê hā-ʿittîm: a ruler consults the council before deciding on a crisis involving a queen; in Esther the king about the defiant Vashti, in the Quran the queen herself about Solomon's letter.)
passages.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ לַחֲכָמִ֖ים יֹדְעֵ֣י הָֽעִתִּ֑ים כִּי כֵן֙ דְּבַ֣ר הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ לִפְנֵ֕י כָּל יֹדְעֵ֖י דָּ֥ת וָדִֽין

passages.text: וְהַקָּרֹ֣ב אֵלָ֗יו כַּרְשְׁנָ֤א שֵׁתָר֙ אַדְמָ֣תָא תַרְשִׁ֔ישׁ מֶ֥רֶס מַרְסְנָ֖א מְמוּכָ֑ן שִׁבְעַ֞ת שָׂרֵ֣י פָּרַ֣ס וּמָדַ֗י רֹאֵי֙ פְּנֵ֣י הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ הַיֹּשְׁבִ֥ים רִאשֹׁנָ֖ה בַּמַּלְכֽוּת

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml): echo. yā ayyuhā l-malaʾu aftūnī fī amrī mā kuntu qāṭiʿatan amran ḥattā tashhadūni ~ wa-yyōʾmer ham-melekh la-ḥăkhāmîm yōdʿê hā-ʿittîm: a ruler consults the council before deciding on a crisis involving a queen; in Esther the king about the defiant Vashti, in the Quran the queen herself about Solomon's letter.
Shared motifs, rarest first: The queen consults her chiefs, who defer to her; she observes that kings who enter a town ruin it and humble its nobles (weight 6.7). Pair score 6.7.

Only in Ahasuerus's banquets and Queen Vashti's refusal: Royal decree that every man shall rule in his own house; Merry with wine, the king orders the queen brought in her crown to show her beauty to his guests; A decree written into the laws of Persia and Media cannot be revoked; At the royal banquet drinking is by rule, no one compelled; The disobedient queen is deposed and her royalty given to 'another better than she'; The queen refuses to come at the king's command and the king is enraged; King holds a banquet showing his riches for 180 days; The queen holds a separate banquet for the women; Seven named eunuchs serve the king; Palace garden decorated with fine hangings, marble columns, gold and silver couches and mosaic pavement; Susa the citadel (Shushan ha-birah) as setting; Royal decree sent to each province in its own script and each people in its own language; and 2 more.

Only in Solomon, the speech of birds, the ants, the hoopoe and the Queen of Sheba: Entering Solomon's palace, the queen takes its floor of smooth glass for a pool and bares her legs; The hoopoe returns with sure news from Sabaʾ, knowledge Solomon lacked; Solomon sends the hoopoe to drop his letter before the queen and wait for their reply; Solomon reviews the birds, finds the hoopoe absent and threatens to punish or slaughter it unless it brings a clear excuse; An ʿifrīt of the jinn offers to bring the queen's throne before Solomon rises from his seat; Solomon's letter begins 'In the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate' and demands submission; The queen sends a gift to see what the envoys bring back; Solomon rejects the wealth and threatens invasion; The queen confesses she wronged herself and submits with Solomon to God, Lord of the worlds; Solomon has the queen's throne disguised to test whether she recognizes it; she says 'It is as though it were it'; The queen and her people prostrate to the sun instead of God; Solomon inherits from David (knowledge and kingship); Solomon prays to be inspired to thank God for favor to him and his parents and to be admitted among the righteous; and 22 more.

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/07-hb-quran.yaml): echo. Light going before the faithful on their way: wa-YHWH hōlēḵ lip̄nêhem ... wə-laylâ bə-ʿammûḏ ʾēš lə-hāʾîr lāhem lāleḵeṯ vs. yawma tarā l-muʾminīna wa-l-muʾmināti yasʿā nūruhum bayna aydīhim wa-bi-aymānihim. Israel's pillar of fire leads a whole people through the desert; the Quran's light is each believer's own, on the Day, and cannot be borrowed by the hypocrites (unẓurūnā naqtabis min nūrikum). cf. Matt 25:8-12.
Shared motifs, rarest first: On the day believers' light runs before them and on their right hands (weight 6.3). Pair score 6.3.

Only in Consecration of the firstborn, sign on hand and forehead, Joseph's bones, pillar of cloud and fire: The exodus month is Aviv, the month of ripening grain; Firstborn sons must be redeemed; God leads the people by a roundabout route so they will not see war and turn back; The cloud over Israel in the wilderness: guide or shade [divergence between the texts]; A firstborn donkey is redeemed with a lamb or its neck is broken; The rite shall be a sign on your hand and a memorial between your eyes; Command to tell one's son and grandson of God's deeds in Egypt; A child asks the meaning of a rite and the parent recites the exodus story; Firstborn sons and animals belong to God; Hero makes them swear to carry his bones out of Egypt; Unleavened bread eaten for seven days; God leads the people in a pillar of cloud by day and a pillar of fire by night; and 1 more.

Only in The believers' light, the hypocrites who would borrow it, and the wall with a gate; hearts hardened by long time: Believers must not be like those given the Book before, whose term grew long and whose hearts hardened; The hypocrites beg the believers 'Wait for us, that we may borrow some of your light' and are told 'Go back and seek light'; A wall with a gate is set between them: inside it mercy, outside it, facing, the punishment; The people's hearts are called hard (Arabic q-s-w, Hebrew q-sh-h), or God makes them so [contrast between the texts]; The people's hearts are called hard (Arabic q-s-w, Hebrew q-sh-h), or God makes them so [divergence between the texts]; No ransom (kofer) may be taken for a murderer's life; Each wrongdoer would ransom himself with all that is on earth, if he could; God will remove the heart of stone and give a heart of flesh and a new spirit; Who will lend God a goodly loan (qard hasan), that he may multiply it for him?; Rain from the sky gives life to the earth after its death, a sign of resurrection.

leads.title: The pursuit and the parting of the sea ↔ Moses, the houses as qibla, and Pharaoh's drowning faith
leads.summary: These two units share 5 motifs: pharaoh acknowledges israel's god or his own sin, and what follows, why pharaoh pursues the departing israelites, what becomes of the drowned pharaoh and his army after the sea [divergence between the texts], the king's heart is hardened (by himself or by god) so he refuses to release the people….

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/03-hb-quran.yaml): divergence, echo, parallel. At the sea the pursuers recognise Israel's God: wayyōʾmer miṣrayim ʾānûsāh mippᵉnê yiśrāʾēl kî YHWH nilḥām lāhem vs Pharaoh's āmantu annahu lā ilāha illā lladhī āmanat bihi banū isrāʾīl. Exod gives it to the Egyptians as a group, Q to Pharaoh alone. cf. Pirqe de-R. Eliezer 43 and Mekhilta (Pharaoh survives and repents), outside the canon. Why Pharaoh pursues: in Exod regret at losing the slave labour (mah-zōʾt ʿāśînû kî-šillaḥnû ʾet-yiśrāʾēl mēʿobdēnû); in Q aggression and enmity (fa-atbaʿahum firʿawnu wa-junūduhu baghyan wa-ʿadwan). wa-jāwaznā bi-banī isrāʾīla l-baḥra fa-atbaʿahum firʿawnu ... ḥattā idhā adrakahu l-gharaq vs wayyāšūbû hammayim wayᵉkassû ʾet-hārekeb ... lᵉkōl ḥêl parʿōh. The drowned are seen as a sign afterwards: fa-l-yawma nunajjīka bi-badanika li-takūna li-man khalfaka āyatan vs wayyarʾ yiśrāʾēl ʾet-miṣrayim mēt ʿal-śᵉpat hayyām. Exod shows the Egyptian dead on the shore to Israel then; Q singles out Pharaoh's body, saved from the sea as a sign for later generations.

Shared motifs, rarest first: Pharaoh acknowledges Israel's God or his own sin, and what follows (weight 6.7); Why Pharaoh pursues the departing Israelites (weight 6.7); What becomes of the drowned Pharaoh and his army after the sea [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); The king's heart is hardened (by himself or by God) so he refuses to release the people (weight 4.6); The returning waters drown the pursuing army; not one survives (weight 4.5). Pair score 29.2.

Only in The pursuit and the parting of the sea: God's angel and the cloud pillar move behind the fleeing people to screen them from the pursuers; Israel camps by the sea opposite Baal-zephon, Migdol and Pi-hahiroth; God removes or clogs the wheels of the pursuers' chariots; The rescued people see the enemy dead on the seashore; At the morning watch God looks down from the pillar of fire and cloud and panics the enemy; God sets a trap so the enemy pursues and is destroyed, gaining glory over him; After the deliverance the people believe in God and in Moses his servant; The people say it would be better to serve their oppressors than die in the wilderness; God tells the praying leader: 'Why do you cry to me? Tell the people to go forward'; Who or what parts the sea [divergence between the texts]; Israel's belief or disbelief in Moses after the sea [divergence between the texts]; The king musters his whole force to pursue the departing people; and 16 more.

Only in Moses, the houses as qibla, and Pharaoh's drowning faith: Only some youths (dhurriyya) of Moses' people believed him, fearing Pharaoh; As he drowns Pharaoh declares faith in the God of the Israelites, too late; Pharaoh's body is saved from the sea to be a sign for those after him; Moses prays God to obliterate Pharaoh's wealth and harden their hearts so they do not believe until they see punishment; Moses and Aaron are told to make their people's houses in Egypt a qibla (place/direction of prayer); God's instruction about the Israelites' houses in Egypt before the exodus [divergence between the texts]; Threatened believers say 'to our Lord we return' and pray for patience and to die as muslims; Pharaoh acknowledges Israel's God or his own sin, and what follows [divergence between the texts]; Who throws the staff before Pharaoh and what it becomes; How Moses' own people in Egypt respond to his message [divergence between the texts]; The king confesses he has sinned and that God is righteous; Who causes Pharaoh's refusal: God hardening his heart, or Pharaoh and his people themselves; and 6 more.

Pharaoh leads his people at their head to their end: fa-ttabaʿū amra firʿawna ... yaqdumu qawmahu yawma l-qiyāmati fa-awradahumu n-nāra wa-biʾsa l-wirdu l-mawrūd vs wayyeʾsōr ʾet-rikbô wᵉʾet-ʿammô lāqaḥ ʿimmô wayyiqqaḥ šēš-mēʾôt rekeb. The setting is moved: in Exod he leads them into the sea; in Q he leads them into the fire on the day of resurrection, a fire called a 'watering place' (wird).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Pharaoh goes at the head of his people to their destruction [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7). Pair score 6.7.

Only in The pursuit and the parting of the sea: God's angel and the cloud pillar move behind the fleeing people to screen them from the pursuers; Israel camps by the sea opposite Baal-zephon, Migdol and Pi-hahiroth; God removes or clogs the wheels of the pursuers' chariots; The rescued people see the enemy dead on the seashore; At the morning watch God looks down from the pillar of fire and cloud and panics the enemy; God sets a trap so the enemy pursues and is destroyed, gaining glory over him; After the deliverance the people believe in God and in Moses his servant; The people say it would be better to serve their oppressors than die in the wilderness; God tells the praying leader: 'Why do you cry to me? Tell the people to go forward'; Who or what parts the sea [divergence between the texts]; Israel's belief or disbelief in Moses after the sea [divergence between the texts]; What becomes of the drowned Pharaoh and his army after the sea [divergence between the texts]; and 20 more.

Only in Pharaoh leads his people into the fire; the towns standing and mown: Of the destroyed towns some still stand, some are mown down; On judgment day Pharaoh will lead his people down into the fire, an evil watering place; The gods of a people judged by God cannot help them; 'Far be it from God to do wickedness, from Shaddai to do wrong'; he repays a man according to his deeds; Divine punishment falls on a town by night or while its people take the midday rest; At judgment the associated 'partners' disown their worshipers: 'it was not us you worshiped'.

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/04-hb-quran.yaml): divergence, parallel. wayyābōʾû bənê-yiśrāʾēl bətôk hayyām bayyabbāšâ; fa-ḍrib lahum ṭarīqan fī l-baḥri yabasā: a dry road through the sea, with the cognate root y-b-š / y-b-s. The means differ: Exod has Moses stretch out his hand and YHWH drive the sea back by a strong east wind all night (bərûaḥ qādîm ʿazzâ kol-hallaylâ); Q has God tell Moses to strike a road, with the night departure (asri bi-ʿibādī) and 'fear not being overtaken'. wayyirdəpû miṣrayim ... wayyāšubû hammayim wayəkassû ʾet-hārekeb; fa-atbaʿahum Firʿawnu bi-junūdihi fa-ghashiyahum mina l-yammi mā ghashiyahum: the pursuing army is covered by the sea (ksh / ghšy, 'cover').

Shared motifs, rarest first: The people walk on dry ground through the sea with the waters as a wall on either side [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); King regrets releasing the slaves and pursues them with chariots (weight 6.3); The people walk on dry ground through the sea with the waters as a wall on either side (weight 5.3); The returning waters drown the pursuing army; not one survives (weight 4.5). Pair score 22.8.

Only in The pursuit and the parting of the sea: God's angel and the cloud pillar move behind the fleeing people to screen them from the pursuers; Israel camps by the sea opposite Baal-zephon, Migdol and Pi-hahiroth; God removes or clogs the wheels of the pursuers' chariots; The rescued people see the enemy dead on the seashore; At the morning watch God looks down from the pillar of fire and cloud and panics the enemy; God sets a trap so the enemy pursues and is destroyed, gaining glory over him; After the deliverance the people believe in God and in Moses his servant; The people say it would be better to serve their oppressors than die in the wilderness; God tells the praying leader: 'Why do you cry to me? Tell the people to go forward'; Who or what parts the sea [divergence between the texts]; Israel's belief or disbelief in Moses after the sea [divergence between the texts]; What becomes of the drowned Pharaoh and his army after the sea [divergence between the texts]; and 17 more.

Only in The night departure, the dry road through the sea, the mount and manna: The covenant appointment is at the right (ayman) side of the Mount (al-Ṭūr); A mountain called the mountain of God; Manna named from the people's question 'What is it?' (man hu); Wind brings quail in vast quantity to feed the people.

leads.title: The pursuit and the parting of the sea ↔ Moses and Pharaoh disputing; the magicians; the sea split like mountains
leads.summary: These two units share 9 motifs: how the sea was split for the crossing [divergence between the texts], the king musters his whole force to pursue the departing people, why pharaoh pursues the departing israelites [divergence between the texts], whether those who saw the sea miracle believed [divergence between the texts]….

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml): divergence, parallel. Motive for the pursuit: Exodus gives Pharaoh's regret (mah zōʾt ʿāśînû kî šillaḥnû ʾet Yiśrāʾēl mēʿovdēnû) and God hardening his heart so he will pursue and God be glorified (wə-ḥizzaqtî ʾet lēv Parʿōh wə-rādaf ʾaḥărêhem wə-ʾikkāvədâ bə-Farʿōh); Q 26:52 says only that God warned Moses 'innakum muttabaʿūn', and 26:54-55 gives Pharaoh's contempt (la-shirdhimatun qalīlūna ... la-ghāʾiẓūn). There is no regret over losing slaves and no hardening. fa-arsala Firʿawnu fī l-madāʾini ḥāshirīna ~ wa-yyeʾsōr ʾet rikbô wə-ʾet ʿammô lāqaḥ ʿimmô wa-yyiqqaḥ šēš mēʾôt rekhev bāḥûr: Pharaoh musters his force; Exodus counts chariots, the Quran sends heralds to the cities. qāla aṣḥābu Mūsā innā la-mudrakūna qāla kallā inna maʿiya rabbī sa-yahdīni ~ wə-hinnēh Miṣrayim nōsēaʿ ʾaḥărêhem wa-yyîrəʾû məʾōd ... ʾal tîrāʾû hityaṣṣəvû û-rəʾû ʾet yəšûʿat YHWH: the people see the pursuers and panic, and Moses calms them. In Exodus they complain bitterly (14:11-12); in the Quran they only state 'we are overtaken'. an iḍrib bi-ʿaṣāka l-baḥra fa-nfalaqa ~ hārēm ʾet maṭṭəkā û-nəṭēh ʾet yādəkā ʿal hay-yām û-vəqāʿēhû ... wa-yyôlekh YHWH ʾet hay-yām bə-rûaḥ qādîm ʿazzâ kol hal-laylâ: the split (infalaqa / vāqaʿ) follows the staff in both, but the Quran has Moses strike the sea, and it splits at once; the strong east wind blowing all night is gone. fa-nfalaqa ... wa-anjaynā Mūsā wa-man maʿahu ajmaʿīna ~ wa-yyāvōʾû vənê Yiśrāʾēl bə-tôkh hay-yām bay-yabbāšâ wə-ham-mayim lāhem ḥōmâ: passage through the divided sea; the Quran images the waters as mountains (ṭawd), Exodus as a wall (ḥōmâ). thumma aghraqnā l-ākharīna ~ wa-yyāšuvû ham-mayim wa-yəkhassû ʾet hā-rekhev ... lōʾ nišʾar bāhem ʿad ʾeḥād: the waters return over the pursuers and none survives.

Shared motifs, rarest first: How the sea was split for the crossing [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); The king musters his whole force to pursue the departing people (weight 6.7); Why Pharaoh pursues the departing Israelites [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); Whether those who saw the sea miracle believed [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); 'Stand still and see the salvation of YHWH; YHWH will fight for you' (weight 6.3); King regrets releasing the slaves and pursues them with chariots (weight 6.3); Prophet stretches his staff over the sea and God splits it with a strong east wind (weight 6.0); The people walk on dry ground through the sea with the waters as a wall on either side (weight 5.3); The returning waters drown the pursuing army; not one survives (weight 4.5). Pair score 55.1.

Only in The pursuit and the parting of the sea: God's angel and the cloud pillar move behind the fleeing people to screen them from the pursuers; Israel camps by the sea opposite Baal-zephon, Migdol and Pi-hahiroth; God removes or clogs the wheels of the pursuers' chariots; The rescued people see the enemy dead on the seashore; At the morning watch God looks down from the pillar of fire and cloud and panics the enemy; God sets a trap so the enemy pursues and is destroyed, gaining glory over him; After the deliverance the people believe in God and in Moses his servant; The people say it would be better to serve their oppressors than die in the wilderness; God tells the praying leader: 'Why do you cry to me? Tell the people to go forward'; Who or what parts the sea [divergence between the texts]; Israel's belief or disbelief in Moses after the sea [divergence between the texts]; What becomes of the drowned Pharaoh and his army after the sea [divergence between the texts]; and 12 more.

Only in Moses and Pharaoh disputing; the magicians; the sea split like mountains: Pharaoh calls the Israelites 'a small band' who enrage him; God expelled the Egyptians from gardens, springs, treasures and fine dwellings and made Israel inherit them; The magicians cast their spells swearing 'By the might of Pharaoh'; Moses admits he did the killing while he was 'of those astray' and fled out of fear; Pharaoh reproaches Moses: 'Did we not raise you among us as a child, and you did your deed?'; Pharaoh threatens to imprison Moses if he takes a god other than Pharaoh; Before Pharaoh the staff becomes a manifest great serpent (thuʿbān); Prophet's wonders are imitated by the king's magicians in a contest [divergence between the texts]; The title of God in whose name Moses goes to Pharaoh; Egypt reduced the Israelites to slavery; How a public contest between God's prophet and the king's religious specialists ends [contrast between the texts]; Whose forefathers' God is proclaimed in the Moses story [divergence between the texts]; and 34 more.

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/08-hb-quran.yaml): echo. wa-thiyābaka fa-ṭahhir ~ we-qiddaštām ha-yyôm û-māḥār we-kibbesû śimlōtām. Garment purity at revelation; for the people at Sinai, for the prophet himself in the Quran.
Shared motifs, rarest first: The people wash their garments to prepare for God's appearance (weight 6.7). Pair score 6.7.

Only in Arrival at Sinai, covenant offer and theophany: Israel arrives at Sinai in the third month after leaving Egypt; God carried Israel on eagles' wings; Moses speaks and God answers him with a voice (thunder); God comes to the prophet in a thick cloud so the people may hear; Priests are mentioned before the Aaronic priesthood is instituted; A ram's horn blast signals that the people may go up the mountain; Men must not approach a woman before a holy encounter; God descends or reveals himself on the third day; A boundary is set round the holy mountain; whoever touches it dies; A horn blast at which all tremble [divergence between the texts]; Israel stands beneath the mountain when the covenant is given [divergence between the texts]; Israel is to be a kingdom of priests and a holy nation; and 10 more.

Only in The cloaked one: the call, the opponent, and the nineteen: The people of paradise ask the damned what brought them to hell; they answer: we did not pray, feed the poor, and we denied the day; Those who turn from the reminder are like startled wild asses fleeing from a lion (qaswara); Every soul is held in pledge (rahina) for what it has earned; Each of the deniers wants to be given scrolls unrolled (personally revealed) to him; Over hell are nineteen; its keepers are angels whose number is made a test; God created a man alone, gave him extended wealth and sons present at his side; yet he wants more and stubbornly opposes the signs; The companions of the right (ashab al-yamin, al-maymana) are saved; the companions of the left (al-mash'ama) are damned; The intercession of intercessors will not benefit the damned; no soul has power to help another; Measure for measure: as you have done, so it shall be done to you; your deed returns on your head; You will not will unless God wills; Prophet wraps his face in his mantle on hearing God; An opponent dismisses the revelation as inherited sorcery (sihr yu'thar) or 'only the word of a mortal'; and 6 more.

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/04-hb-quran.yaml): divergence, parallel. Exod: the mother's own plan, after hiding him three months, wattiqqaḥ-lô tēbat gōmeʾ wattaḥmərâ baḥēmār ûbazzāpet ... wattāśem bassûp ʿal-śəpat hayʾōr, set carefully among the reeds. Q: God reveals it to her (idh awḥaynā ilā ummika), iqdhifīhi fī t-tābūti fa-qdhifīhi fī l-yamm fa-l-yulqihi l-yammu bi-s-sāḥil: she throws the box into the river and the river casts it ashore by God's command. Exod: Pharaoh's daughter finds him, takes pity (wattaḥmōl ʿālāyw) and adopts and names him (wayhî-lāh ləbēn wattiqrāʾ šəmô mōšeh). Q: the finder is 'an enemy to me and an enemy to him' (yaʾkhudhhu ʿaduwwun lī wa-ʿaduwwun lah), and the love comes from God, wa-alqaytu ʿalayka maḥabbatan minnī. The naming and the rescuer's compassion are dropped. wattōʾmer ʾăḥōtô ʾel-bat-parʿōh hăʾēlēk wəqārāʾtî lāk ʾiššâ mêneqet min hāʿibriyyōt ... wattiqrāʾ ʾet-ʾēm hayyāled; idh tamshī ukhtuka fa-taqūlu hal adullukum ʿalā man yakfuluh fa-rajaʿnāka ilā ummika kay taqarra ʿaynuhā wa-lā taḥzan. Q gives the motive as the mother's comfort; Exod has the wages (ʾetten ʾet-śəkārēk). wayyak ʾet-hammiṣrî wayyiṭmənēhû baḥôl ... wayyîrāʾ mōšeh ... wayyibraḥ mōšeh mippənê parʿōh wayyēšeb bəʾereṣ-midyān; wa-qatalta nafsan fa-najjaynāka mina l-ghammi wa-fatannāka futūnan fa-labithta sinīna fī ahli Madyan. The killing and the flight to Midian are the same; Q retells them as God rescuing Moses from distress and testing him. Exod makes Moses' fear and Pharaoh's hunt the reason.

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml): divergence. At the water of Midian: Exodus has seven daughters of the priest of Midian (šebaʿ bānôt) who draw water, shepherds who drive them off (wa-ygārəšûm), and Moses who rescues them (wa-yyôšiʿān) and waters their flock. There is no fight with the shepherds. The father: Exodus has a named priest, kōhēn Midyān and Rəʿûʾēl, who scolds his daughters for leaving the stranger and invites him to eat (qirʾen lô wə-yōʾkhal leḥem); the Quran has an unnamed 'very old man' (shaykhun kabīr), no priest, who sends a daughter to pay Moses his wage (li-yajziyaka ajra mā saqayta lanā) and reassures him: lā takhaf najawta mina l-qawmi ẓ-ẓālimīn. The daughters' role: in Exodus they report together to their father, ʾîš Miṣrî hiṣṣîlānû mi-yyad hā-rōʿîm, 'an Egyptian man saved us' (Moses taken for an Egyptian); in the Quran one daughter walks shyly (tamshī ʿalā stiḥyāʾ) to invite him and then advises her father, istaʾjirhu inna khayra mani staʾjarta l-qawiyyu l-amīnu, 'hire him, the best one to hire is the strong and trustworthy'. The marriage: Exodus has wa-yyôʾel Mōše lāševet ʾet hā-ʾîš wa-yyittēn ʾet Ṣippōrâ vittô lə-Mōše, a named bride and no terms; the Quran has an unnamed daughter given under a contract of service, ʿalā an taʾjuranī thamāniya ḥijajin fa-in atmamta ʿashran fa-min ʿindika, eight years or ten if he wishes, sworn before God (wa-llāhu ʿalā mā naqūlu wakīl).

Pair score 39.7.

Only in Birth and rescue of Moses; killing of the Egyptian; flight to Midian; Israel's cry: The foundling's weeping moves the finder to compassion; The hero's parents are introduced anonymously as a Levite man and a Levite woman; Mother sees that her newborn 'is good' (ki tov); Hero names his son for being a stranger in a foreign land; Infant adopted by a royal woman [divergence between the texts]; The groaning of the oppressed rises to God, who hears and remembers his covenant; Hero kills an oppressor beating a kinsman and hides the body in the sand; How Moses learns that his life is sought [divergence between the texts]; How Moses killed the Egyptian [divergence between the texts]; Moses killed a man and God delivered him from distress, then tried him with trials [divergence between the texts]; Who decides that Moses be put on the water [divergence between the texts]; Moses' upbringing in Pharaoh's house [divergence between the texts]; and 20 more.

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml): divergence, parallel. The killing: Exodus has Moses see an Egyptian beating a Hebrew 'of his brothers', look this way and that and see no one (wa-yyifen kōh wā-khōh wa-yyarʾ kî ʾên ʾîš), strike him and hide him in the sand. The Quran has him find two men fighting, one of his party (shīʿa) and one of his enemy; at his kinsman's cry for help he strikes one blow and the man dies (fa-wakazahu Mūsā fa-qaḍā ʿalayhi). There is no looking around and no hiding of the body; the act is unpremeditated. Moral verdict on the killing: Exodus passes none; Moses only fears exposure (wa-yyîrāʾ Mōše wa-yyōʾmar ʾākhēn nôdaʿ had-dāvār). The Quran has Moses judge it at once, hādhā min ʿamali sh-shayṭān ... rabbi innī ẓalamtu nafsī fa-ghfir lī, and God forgives him (fa-ghafara lahu), so Moses is a repentant penitent before he is a prophet. The second day: in Exodus two Hebrews (šənê ʾănāšîm ʿIvrîm) fight, Moses rebukes the guilty one, and that Hebrew retorts mî śāməkhā lə-ʾîš śar wə-šōfēṭ ʿālênû ha-lə-hārəgēnî ʾattâ ʾōmēr ka-ʾăšer hāragtā ʾet ham-Miṣrî. In the Quran the same kinsman again calls for help against an enemy, Moses calls the kinsman 'clearly misguided' (la-ghawiyyun mubīn), and as he moves to strike the enemy he hears a-turīdu an taqtulanī kamā qatalta nafsan bi-l-amsi in turīdu illā an takūna jabbāran fī l-arḍ. 'Prince and judge' becomes 'tyrant' (jabbār). How the danger reaches Moses: Exodus has wa-yyišmaʿ Parʿōh ʾet had-dāvār haz-zeh wa-yvaqqēš lahărōg ʾet Mōše, Pharaoh himself; the Quran has the chiefs plotting (al-malaʾa yaʾtamirūna bika li-yaqtulūka) and an unnamed sympathizer running from the far end of the city to warn him (wa-jāʾa rajulun min aqṣā l-madīnati yasʿā). fa-kharaja minhā khāʾifan yataraqqabu ... wa-lammā tawajjaha tilqāʾa Madyana ~ wa-yyivraḥ Mōše mip-pənê Farʿōh wa-yyēšev bə-ʾereṣ Midyān: flight to Midian (Madyan / Midyān). The Quran adds two prayers (rabbi najjinī ... ʿasā rabbī an yahdiyanī sawāʾa s-sabīl).

Shared motifs, rarest first: How Moses killed the Egyptian [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); How Moses learns that his life is sought [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); Kinsman rebuffs the hero: 'Who made you prince and judge over us?' (weight 6.7); Hero kills an oppressor beating a kinsman and hides the body in the sand (weight 6.7); The retort Moses hears on the day after the killing [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); How Moses' killing of the Egyptian is judged [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.3); Hero flees the king's death sentence to a foreign land (weight 5.8). Pair score 45.5.

Only in Birth and rescue of Moses; killing of the Egyptian; flight to Midian; Israel's cry: The foundling's weeping moves the finder to compassion; The hero's parents are introduced anonymously as a Levite man and a Levite woman; Mother sees that her newborn 'is good' (ki tov); Hero names his son for being a stranger in a foreign land; Infant adopted by a royal woman [divergence between the texts]; The groaning of the oppressed rises to God, who hears and remembers his covenant; Hero drives off shepherds and waters the flock of women at a well; What the Midianite daughters do after Moses helps them [divergence between the texts]; Moses helps the women at the water of Midian [divergence between the texts]; Moses' father-in-law in Midian [divergence between the texts]; Moses killed a man and God delivered him from distress, then tried him with trials [divergence between the texts]; Who decides that Moses be put on the water [divergence between the texts]; and 19 more.

Only in Moses kills the Egyptian, is warned, and flees toward Midian: Moses calls his killing 'the work of Satan' and asks forgiveness, which is granted; A man comes running from the far end of the city to warn the hero that the chiefs plot to kill him; When Moses reached his full strength God gave him judgment and knowledge; Moses killed a man and God delivered him from distress, then tried him with trials.

Who decides to put the child on the water: Exodus has the mother, on her own, hide him three months and, when she can hide him no longer (wə-lōʾ yākhlâ ʿôd haṣṣəfînô), make a papyrus basket sealed with pitch. In the Quran God inspires her (awḥaynā ilā ummi Mūsā): nurse him, cast him into the river when you fear, and 'we will return him to you and make him one of the messengers'. The rescue is announced in advance. fa-alqīhi fī l-yammi ~ wat-tāśem bas-sûf ʿal śəfat hay-yəʾōr: Exodus places him carefully among the reeds at the edge of the Nile (yəʾōr), in a basket (tēvat gōmeʾ) with bitumen and pitch; the Quran says 'cast him into the yamm', with no vessel in this passage, using the word that elsewhere names the sea where Pharaoh drowns. Who finds and adopts him: Pharaoh's daughter (bat Parʿōh), bathing, sees the basket, has pity on the crying child, recognizes him as Hebrew (mī-yaldê hā-ʿIvrîm zeh) and later names him. In the Quran Pharaoh's household picks him up (iltaqaṭahu ālu Firʿawn), and Pharaoh's wife (imraʾat Firʿawn) pleads with Pharaoh: qurratu ʿaynin lī wa-laka lā taqtulūhu ʿasā an yanfaʿanā aw nattakhidhahu waladan. Daughter becomes wife, pity becomes intercession, and the Quran adds the divine irony 'so that he would be an enemy and a grief to them' (28:8). qālat li-ukhtihi quṣṣīhi fa-baṣurat bihi ʿan junubin wa-hum lā yashʿurūna ~ wat-tētaṣṣav ʾăḥōtô mē-rāḥōq lə-dēʿâ mah yyēʿāśeh lô: the sister watches from a distance. In the Quran the mother sends her. The sister's offer: Exodus has hăʾēlēkh wə-qārāʾtî lākh ʾiššâ mêneqet min hā-ʿIvriyyōt on her own initiative; the Quran first has God forbid the other wet-nurses to him (wa-ḥarramnā ʿalayhi l-marāḍiʿa min qablu), then the sister offers a household that will rear him. cf. b. Sotah 12b (Moses refuses Egyptian breasts), outside the HB. Why the child goes back to his mother: Exodus has a paid arrangement with the princess, hêlîkhî ʾet hay-yeled haz-zeh wə-hênîqihû lî wa-ʾănî ʾettēn ʾet śəkhārēkh; the Quran has God keeping his promise, fa-radadnāhu ilā ummihi kay taqarra ʿaynuhā wa-lā taḥzana wa-li-taʿlama anna waʿda llāhi ḥaqqun. The Quran omits the naming and its etymology (Exod 2:10).

evidence.text: Passages are shown for the 10 rarest of 11 shared motifs; the full list follows.

Shared motifs, rarest first: People fear to hear God directly and ask the prophet to mediate (weight 6.3); Honor father and mother, with the promise of long life [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.0); Prohibitions of murder, adultery, theft and false witness [divergence between the texts] (weight 5.8); Prohibition of coveting the neighbor's wife and property (weight 5.8); No other gods before YHWH (weight 5.8); Sabbath rest on the seventh day for all, including servants, animals and strangers (weight 5.6); God visits the fathers' sin on the third and fourth generation, but keeps steadfast love for thousands (weight 5.6); Prohibition of carved images or likenesses of anything for worship (weight 5.6); The Ten Commandments (Decalogue) (weight 5.4); Honor father and mother, with the promise of long life (weight 5.3); Prohibitions of murder, adultery, theft and false witness (weight 5.1). Pair score 62.2.

Only in The Ten Words and the people's fear: God identifies himself as the one who brought Israel out of Egypt, the house of slaves; The people 'see' the voices or thunder at the revelation; Do not take God's name in vain; The prophet approaches the thick darkness where God is; Sexual relations with a neighbor's wife are forbidden [divergence between the texts]; Prohibition of coveting the neighbor's wife and property [divergence between the texts]; Do not kill the soul God has made sacred except by right [divergence between the texts]; No other gods before YHWH [divergence between the texts]; The ground and the reward of the duty to parents [divergence between the texts]; The Sabbath is justified by God's resting on the seventh day of creation; The Sabbath was imposed only on those who differed about it [response between the texts]; The Ten Commandments (Decalogue) [divergence between the texts]; and 3 more.

Only in The Decalogue restated and the people's fear at Horeb: The covenant is made with those alive today, not only with the fathers; Worship of God alone joined to duty to parents [divergence between the texts]; Whether God should speak to the people directly [contrast between the texts]; Mountain burns with fire to the heart of heaven amid darkness and cloud; The people answer as one: all that YHWH has spoken we will do [response between the texts]; Who was present at the revelation on the mountain, and who knows it only by report [contrast between the texts]; God heard as a voice out of fire with no visible form; The people's answer to the covenant ('we hear ...') [response between the texts]; Sabbath grounded in the memory of slavery in Egypt; Believers' confession 'we hear and we obey' (sami'na wa-ata'na); Keep the law, turning neither to the right nor to the left; God gives stone tablets he himself has written.

Only in Al-Lat, al-'Uzza and Manat; angelic intercession; the scrolls of Abraham and Moses; the Lord of Sirius: The three goddesses al-Lat, al-'Uzza and Manat, 'the third, the other', named and rejected; They follow only conjecture (zann), and conjecture avails nothing against the truth; God created the pairs, male and female, from a drop of sperm (nutfa) when it is emitted; A surah ends with the command to prostrate (sajda verse); God destroyed 'Ad 'the first' (implying a second 'Ad); God knew you when he produced you from the earth and when you were embryos in your mothers' bellies; do not claim purity; The idols are only names you and your fathers have named, for which God sent down no authority; God is 'the Lord of Sirius' (al-shi'ra), a star worshipped by some Arabs; Those who avoid the great sins and indecencies, except minor slips (al-lamam), find God's forgiveness wide; To your Lord is the final end (al-muntaha); 'Is the male for you and the female for him? That is an unfair division'; 'Which of your Lord's bounties (ala') will you dispute/deny?'; and 15 more.

leads.summary: These two units share 6 motifs: the ten commandments (decalogue) [divergence between the texts], honor father and mother, with the promise of long life [divergence between the texts], prohibitions of murder, adultery, theft and false witness [divergence between the texts], the ten commandments (decalogue)….

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/02-hb-quran.yaml): divergence. A recited list of commandments compared item by item. Kept: no other gods (allā tushrikū bihi shayʾan = lōʾ yihyeh-ləkhā ʾĕlōhîm ʾăḥērîm), parents, killing, sexual sin, false speech. Omitted: the Sabbath (zākhôr ʾet-yôm haš-šabbāt) and coveting; the image ban is folded into 'associate nothing'. Added: allā taqtulū awlādakum min imlāqin, the orphan's property, full measure and weight, keeping God's covenant. evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/06-hb-quran.yaml): parallel. ʾeṯ-ʾêmāṯî ʾăšallaḥ ləp̄āneyḵā wə-hammōṯî ʾeṯ-kol-hā-ʿām vs. wa-qadhafa fī qulūbihimu r-ruʿb: God's terror (ʾêmâ / ruʿb) sent against the enemy. In Exodus it goes ahead of Israel into Canaan; in the Quran it is cast into the ahl al-kitāb who had sided with the besiegers.
Shared motifs, rarest first: God casts terror (ru'b) into the hearts of the unbelievers (weight 6.3); God sends terror ahead to panic the enemies (weight 6.0). Pair score 12.3.

Only in The angel sent ahead and promises of conquest: The promised borders run from the Red Sea to the Sea of the Philistines and to the River; Obedience is rewarded with health, fertility and full lifespan; Enemies driven out little by little lest wild beasts multiply; Israel must tear down the standing stones of the Canaanite gods; God sends an angel ahead of Israel who bears God's name; Make no covenant with the inhabitants or their gods, who would be a snare; God sends the hornet to drive out the inhabitants.

Only in The confederates besiege Medina; hypocrites and the faithful: Fleeing will not save you from death or killing; you would enjoy life only a little; Hypocrites ask leave to quit the battle line saying 'our houses are exposed', wanting only to flee; Among the believers are men who fulfilled their covenant with God; some have met their end (qada nahbah) and some still wait; In the messenger of God you have an excellent example (uswa hasana); Those who say 'we believe' will not be left untested; God tries them as he tried those before to know the truthful from the liars; In terror eyes swerve and hearts reach the throats; Men leave the battle line to go home, and how that is judged [contrast between the texts]; Book-people who aided the enemy are brought down from their fortresses, terror cast in their hearts; some killed, some captured, their land inherited; God sent a wind and invisible hosts against the confederate armies besieging the believers.

Only in Covenant Code - justice, enemy's animal, sabbatical year, festivals: Return your enemy's stray animal and help his overloaded donkey; Neither favor nor pervert justice for the poor in his lawsuit; Whoever commits a sin and casts it on an innocent bears slander and manifest sin; God does not forbid kindness and justice toward those who did not fight you over religion or expel you; Do not oppress the stranger, for you were strangers in Egypt; The land lies fallow in the seventh year for the poor and wild animals; Do not invoke the names of other gods; Let not hatred of a people move you to injustice; be just; Do not spread false reports or follow the majority to do wrong in court; Who must make pilgrimage to the sanctuary, and how often [divergence between the texts]; Judge fairly, favoring neither the poor nor the great; A bribe blinds the clear-sighted and perverts the words of the righteous; and 1 more.

Only in New tablets, the attributes of mercy and the ritual decalogue: God promises no one will covet the land while the men go up on pilgrimage; The Sabbath must be kept even in plowing and harvest time; Call to the People of the Book to a common word: worship none but God and take none as lords besides him; What the tablets given at Sinai contain [divergence between the texts]; Israel must tear down the standing stones of the Canaanite gods; A firstborn donkey is redeemed with a lamb or its neck is broken; God passes by and proclaims his name and attributes of mercy; A boundary is set round the holy mountain; whoever touches it dies; Whether one person (kin, descendants) bears another's sin [contrast between the texts]; Make no covenant with the inhabitants or their gods, who would be a snare; The prophet intercedes for the people, arguing from God's reputation; How far God's mercy and his punishment extend [divergence between the texts]; and 16 more.

passages.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֶל מֹשֶׁ֗ה עֲלֵ֥ה אֵלַ֛י הָהָ֖רָה וֶהְיֵה שָׁ֑ם וְאֶתְּנָ֨ה לְךָ֜ אֶת לֻחֹ֣ת הָאֶ֗בֶן וְהַתּוֹרָה֙ וְהַמִּצְוָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר כָּתַ֖בְתִּי לְהוֹרֹתָֽם

passages.note: God gives stone tablets he himself has written (alwah, 'we wrote')
passages.text: وَكَتَبْنَا لَهُۥ فِى ٱلْأَلْوَاحِ مِن كُلِّ شَىْءٍ مَّوْعِظَةً وَتَفْصِيلًا لِّكُلِّ شَىْءٍ فَخُذْهَا بِقُوَّةٍ وَأْمُرْ قَوْمَكَ يَأْخُذُوا۟ بِأَحْسَنِهَا سَأُو۟رِيكُمْ دَارَ ٱلْفَٰسِقِينَ

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/03-hb-quran.yaml): divergence, parallel. Moses on the mountain forty: wa-wāʿadnā mūsā thalāthīna laylatan wa-atmamnāhā bi-ʿashrin fa-tamma mīqātu rabbihi arbaʿīna laylatan vs wayᵉhî mōšeh bāhār ʾarbāʿîm yôm wᵉʾarbāʿîm lāylāh. Q counts nights only and builds the forty as an appointment of thirty completed by ten. Deputy left with the people: ukhlufnī fī qawmī wa-aṣliḥ wa-lā tattabiʿ sabīla l-mufsidīn vs wᵉhinnēh ʾahărōn wᵉḥûr ʿimmākem mî-baʿal dᵉbārîm yiggaš ʾălēhem. Q drops Hur, makes Aaron Moses' khalīfa and adds a charge to keep order and not follow the corrupters, which prepares Aaron's innocence in 7:150. God writes the tablets himself, for instruction: wa-katabnā lahu fī l-alwāḥi ... mawʿiẓatan vs lūḥōt hāʾeben wᵉhattôrāh wᵉhammiṣwāh ʾăšer kātabtî lᵉhôrōtām.

Shared motifs, rarest first: Moses leaves a deputy (Aaron, with or without Hur) with the people while he is on the mountain [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); Moses' set period on the mountain is forty (days and nights, or nights) [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); Aaron and Hur left in charge while Moses is on the mountain (weight 6.7); A prophet spends forty days and forty nights in a set period (weight 5.8); God gives stone tablets he himself has written (weight 5.3). Pair score 31.1.

Only in Moses ascends into the cloud for forty days: The cloud covers the mountain six days and God calls on the seventh; God's glory appears as a devouring fire; Joshua serves as Moses' attendant; God sends down his sakina (tranquility, cf. shekhinah) on the prophet and believers.

Only in Forty nights, the request to see God and the tablets: When God manifests himself to the mountain it is crushed to dust; The prophet falls down unconscious at the theophany and repents on waking; The tablets contain an exhortation and an explanation of all things; The appointed time on the mountain is thirty nights completed with ten more, making forty; What the tablets given at Sinai contain [divergence between the texts]; Moses asks to see God, his glory or God himself [divergence between the texts]; A mountain is shattered when God passes by or manifests himself [divergence between the texts]; The prophet asks to see God's glory; What happens after God refuses to be seen by Moses [divergence between the texts]; God answers the prophet's request to see him: 'You will not see me'; Seeing God or breaking through to him brings death; God speaks to the prophet face to face, as a man speaks to his friend; and 2 more.

passages.text: (25:31) וְעָשִׂ֥יתָ מְנֹרַ֖ת זָהָ֣ב טָה֑וֹר מִקְשָׁ֞ה תֵּעָשֶׂ֤ה הַמְּנוֹרָה֙ יְרֵכָ֣הּ וְקָנָ֔הּ גְּבִיעֶ֛יהָ כַּפְתֹּרֶ֥יהָ וּפְרָחֶ֖יהָ מִמֶּ֥נָּה יִהְיֽוּ (25:32) וְשִׁשָּׁ֣ה קָנִ֔ים יֹצְאִ֖ים מִצִּדֶּ֑יהָ שְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה קְנֵ֣י מְנֹרָ֗ה מִצִּדָּהּ֙ הָאֶחָ֔ד וּשְׁלֹשָׁה֙ קְנֵ֣י מְנֹרָ֔ה מִצִּדָּ֖הּ הַשֵּׁנִֽי (25:33) שְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה גְ֠בִעִים מְֽשֻׁקָּדִ֞ים בַּקָּנֶ֣ה הָאֶחָד֮ כַּפְתֹּ֣ר וָפֶרַח֒ וּשְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה גְבִעִ֗ים מְשֻׁקָּדִ֛ים בַּקָּנֶ֥ה הָאֶחָ֖ד כַּפְתֹּ֣ר וָפָ֑רַח כֵּ֚ן לְשֵׁ֣שֶׁת הַקָּנִ֔ים הַיֹּצְאִ֖ים מִן הַמְּנֹרָֽה (25:34) וּבַמְּנֹרָ֖ה אַרְבָּעָ֣ה גְבִעִ֑ים מְשֻׁקָּדִ֔ים כַּפְתֹּרֶ֖יהָ וּפְרָחֶֽיהָ (25:35) וְכַפְתֹּ֡ר תַּחַת֩ שְׁנֵ֨י הַקָּנִ֜ים מִמֶּ֗נָּה וְכַפְתֹּר֙ תַּ֣חַת שְׁנֵ֤י הַקָּנִים֙ מִמֶּ֔נָּה וְכַפְתֹּ֕ר תַּחַת שְׁנֵ֥י הַקָּנִ֖ים מִמֶּ֑נָּה לְשֵׁ֨שֶׁת֙ הַקָּנִ֔ים הַיֹּצְאִ֖ים מִן הַמְּנֹרָֽה (25:36) כַּפְתֹּרֵיהֶ֥ם וּקְנֹתָ֖ם מִמֶּ֣נָּה יִהְי֑וּ כֻּלָּ֛הּ מִקְשָׁ֥ה אַחַ֖ת זָהָ֥ב טָהֽוֹר (25:37) וְעָשִׂ֥יתָ אֶת נֵרֹתֶ֖יהָ שִׁבְעָ֑ה וְהֶֽעֱלָה֙ אֶת נֵ֣רֹתֶ֔יהָ וְהֵאִ֖יר עַל עֵ֥בֶר פָּנֶֽיהָ (25:38) וּמַלְקָחֶ֥יהָ וּמַחְתֹּתֶ֖יהָ זָהָ֥ב טָהֽוֹר (25:39) כִּכָּ֛ר זָהָ֥ב טָה֖וֹר יַעֲשֶׂ֣ה אֹתָ֑הּ אֵ֥ת כָּל הַכֵּלִ֖ים הָאֵֽלֶּה

passages.text: (37:17) וַיַּ֥עַשׂ אֶת הַמְּנֹרָ֖ה זָהָ֣ב טָה֑וֹר מִקְשָׁ֞ה עָשָׂ֤ה אֶת הַמְּנֹרָה֙ יְרֵכָ֣הּ וְקָנָ֔הּ גְּבִיעֶ֛יהָ כַּפְתֹּרֶ֥יהָ וּפְרָחֶ֖יהָ מִמֶּ֥נָּה הָיֽוּ (37:18) וְשִׁשָּׁ֣ה קָנִ֔ים יֹצְאִ֖ים מִצִּדֶּ֑יהָ שְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה קְנֵ֣י מְנֹרָ֗ה מִצִּדָּהּ֙ הָֽאֶחָ֔ד וּשְׁלֹשָׁה֙ קְנֵ֣י מְנֹרָ֔ה מִצִּדָּ֖הּ הַשֵּׁנִֽי (37:19) שְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה גְ֠בִעִים מְֽשֻׁקָּדִ֞ים בַּקָּנֶ֣ה הָאֶחָד֮ כַּפְתֹּ֣ר וָפֶרַח֒ וּשְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה גְבִעִ֗ים מְשֻׁקָּדִ֛ים בְּקָנֶ֥ה אֶחָ֖ד כַּפְתֹּ֣ר וָפָ֑רַח כֵּ֚ן לְשֵׁ֣שֶׁת הַקָּנִ֔ים הַיֹּצְאִ֖ים מִן הַמְּנֹרָֽה (37:20) וּבַמְּנֹרָ֖ה אַרְבָּעָ֣ה גְבִעִ֑ים מְשֻׁ֨קָּדִ֔ים כַּפְתֹּרֶ֖יהָ וּפְרָחֶֽיהָ (37:21) וְכַפְתֹּ֡ר תַּחַת֩ שְׁנֵ֨י הַקָּנִ֜ים מִמֶּ֗נָּה וְכַפְתֹּר֙ תַּ֣חַת שְׁנֵ֤י הַקָּנִים֙ מִמֶּ֔נָּה וְכַפְתֹּ֕ר תַּֽחַת שְׁנֵ֥י הַקָּנִ֖ים מִמֶּ֑נָּה לְשֵׁ֨שֶׁת֙ הַקָּנִ֔ים הַיֹּצְאִ֖ים מִמֶּֽנָּה (37:22) כַּפְתֹּרֵיהֶ֥ם וּקְנֹתָ֖ם מִמֶּ֣נָּה הָי֑וּ כֻּלָּ֛הּ מִקְשָׁ֥ה אַחַ֖ת זָהָ֥ב טָהֽוֹר (37:23) וַיַּ֥עַשׂ אֶת נֵרֹתֶ֖יהָ שִׁבְעָ֑ה וּמַלְקָחֶ֥יהָ וּמַחְתֹּתֶ֖יהָ זָהָ֥ב טָהֽוֹר (37:24) כִּכָּ֛ר זָהָ֥ב טָה֖וֹר עָשָׂ֣ה אֹתָ֑הּ וְאֵ֖ת כָּל כֵּלֶֽיהָ

passages.text: (25:23) וְעָשִׂ֥יתָ שֻׁלְחָ֖ן עֲצֵ֣י שִׁטִּ֑ים אַמָּתַ֤יִם אָרְכּוֹ֙ וְאַמָּ֣ה רָחְבּ֔וֹ וְאַמָּ֥ה וָחֵ֖צִי קֹמָתֽוֹ (25:24) וְצִפִּיתָ֥ אֹת֖וֹ זָהָ֣ב טָה֑וֹר וְעָשִׂ֥יתָ לּ֛וֹ זֵ֥ר זָהָ֖ב סָבִֽיב (25:25) וְעָשִׂ֨יתָ לּ֥וֹ מִסְגֶּ֛רֶת טֹ֖פַח סָבִ֑יב וְעָשִׂ֧יתָ זֵר זָהָ֛ב לְמִסְגַּרְתּ֖וֹ סָבִֽיב (25:26) וְעָשִׂ֣יתָ לּ֔וֹ אַרְבַּ֖ע טַבְּעֹ֣ת זָהָ֑ב וְנָתַתָּ֙ אֶת הַטַּבָּעֹ֔ת עַ֚ל אַרְבַּ֣ע הַפֵּאֹ֔ת אֲשֶׁ֖ר לְאַרְבַּ֥ע רַגְלָֽיו (25:27) לְעֻמַּת֙ הַמִּסְגֶּ֔רֶת תִּהְיֶ֖יןָ הַטַּבָּעֹ֑ת לְבָתִּ֣ים לְבַדִּ֔ים לָשֵׂ֖את אֶת הַשֻּׁלְחָֽן (25:28) וְעָשִׂ֤יתָ אֶת הַבַּדִּים֙ עֲצֵ֣י שִׁטִּ֔ים וְצִפִּיתָ֥ אֹתָ֖ם זָהָ֑ב וְנִשָּׂא בָ֖ם אֶת הַשֻּׁלְחָֽן (25:29) וְעָשִׂ֨יתָ קְּעָרֹתָ֜יו וְכַפֹּתָ֗יו וּקְשׂוֹתָיו֙ וּמְנַקִּיֹּתָ֔יו אֲשֶׁ֥ר יֻסַּ֖ךְ בָּהֵ֑ן זָהָ֥ב טָה֖וֹר תַּעֲשֶׂ֥ה אֹתָֽם (25:30) וְנָתַתָּ֧ עַֽל הַשֻּׁלְחָ֛ן לֶ֥חֶם פָּנִ֖ים לְפָנַ֥י תָּמִֽיד

passages.text: (37:10) וַיַּ֥עַשׂ אֶת הַשֻּׁלְחָ֖ן עֲצֵ֣י שִׁטִּ֑ים אַמָּתַ֤יִם אָרְכּוֹ֙ וְאַמָּ֣ה רָחְבּ֔וֹ וְאַמָּ֥ה וָחֵ֖צִי קֹמָתֽוֹ (37:11) וַיְצַ֥ף אֹת֖וֹ זָהָ֣ב טָה֑וֹר וַיַּ֥עַשׂ ל֛וֹ זֵ֥ר זָהָ֖ב סָבִֽיב (37:12) וַיַּ֨עַשׂ ל֥וֹ מִסְגֶּ֛רֶת טֹ֖פַח סָבִ֑יב וַיַּ֧עַשׂ זֵר זָהָ֛ב לְמִסְגַּרְתּ֖וֹ סָבִֽיב (37:13) וַיִּצֹ֣ק ל֔וֹ אַרְבַּ֖ע טַבְּעֹ֣ת זָהָ֑ב וַיִּתֵּן֙ אֶת הַטַּבָּעֹ֔ת עַ֚ל אַרְבַּ֣ע הַפֵּאֹ֔ת אֲשֶׁ֖ר לְאַרְבַּ֥ע רַגְלָֽיו (37:14) לְעֻמַּת֙ הַמִּסְגֶּ֔רֶת הָי֖וּ הַטַּבָּעֹ֑ת בָּתִּים֙ לַבַּדִּ֔ים לָשֵׂ֖את אֶת הַשֻּׁלְחָֽן (37:15) וַיַּ֤עַשׂ אֶת הַבַּדִּים֙ עֲצֵ֣י שִׁטִּ֔ים וַיְצַ֥ף אֹתָ֖ם זָהָ֑ב לָשֵׂ֖את אֶת הַשֻּׁלְחָֽן (37:16) וַיַּ֜עַשׂ אֶֽת הַכֵּלִ֣ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר עַל הַשֻּׁלְחָ֗ן אֶת קְעָרֹתָ֤יו וְאֶת כַּפֹּתָיו֙ וְאֵת֙ מְנַקִּיֹּתָ֔יו וְאֶת הַקְּשָׂוֺ֔ת אֲשֶׁ֥ר יֻסַּ֖ךְ בָּהֵ֑ן זָהָ֖ב טָהֽוֹר

passages.text: (25:10) וְעָשׂ֥וּ אֲר֖וֹן עֲצֵ֣י שִׁטִּ֑ים אַמָּתַ֨יִם וָחֵ֜צִי אָרְכּ֗וֹ וְאַמָּ֤ה וָחֵ֨צִי֙ רָחְבּ֔וֹ וְאַמָּ֥ה וָחֵ֖צִי קֹמָתֽוֹ (25:11) וְצִפִּיתָ֤ אֹתוֹ֙ זָהָ֣ב טָה֔וֹר מִבַּ֥יִת וּמִח֖וּץ תְּצַפֶּ֑נּוּ וְעָשִׂ֧יתָ עָלָ֛יו זֵ֥ר זָהָ֖ב סָבִֽיב (25:12) וְיָצַ֣קְתָּ לּ֗וֹ אַרְבַּע֙ טַבְּעֹ֣ת זָהָ֔ב וְנָ֣תַתָּ֔ה עַ֖ל אַרְבַּ֣ע פַּעֲמֹתָ֑יו וּשְׁתֵּ֣י טַבָּעֹ֗ת עַל צַלְעוֹ֙ הָֽאֶחָ֔ת וּשְׁתֵּי֙ טַבָּעֹ֔ת עַל צַלְע֖וֹ הַשֵּׁנִֽית (25:13) וְעָשִׂ֥יתָ בַדֵּ֖י עֲצֵ֣י שִׁטִּ֑ים וְצִפִּיתָ֥ אֹתָ֖ם זָהָֽב (25:14) וְהֵֽבֵאתָ֤ אֶת הַבַּדִּים֙ בַּטַּבָּעֹ֔ת עַ֖ל צַלְעֹ֣ת הָאָרֹ֑ן לָשֵׂ֥את אֶת הָאָרֹ֖ן בָּהֶֽם (25:15) בְּטַבְּעֹת֙ הָאָרֹ֔ן יִהְי֖וּ הַבַּדִּ֑ים לֹ֥א יָסֻ֖רוּ מִמֶּֽנּוּ (25:16) וְנָתַתָּ֖ אֶל הָאָרֹ֑ן אֵ֚ת הָעֵדֻ֔ת אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֶתֵּ֖ן אֵלֶֽיךָ

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: A cult object is hammered from a single piece of gold (weight 6.7); A golden cover (kapporet, mercy seat) on top of the ark (weight 6.7); A golden seven-lamp lampstand with almond-blossom cups (weight 6.0); A gold table with the bread of the presence always before God (weight 6.0); The ark of the covenant: a gold-plated acacia chest with rings and poles (weight 5.6); Two golden cherubim face each other with wings spread over the ark (weight 5.4). Pair score 36.4.

Only in Contribution for the sanctuary; ark, cover, table and lampstand: The ark of the covenant: a gold-plated acacia chest with rings and poles [divergence between the texts]; List of precious materials for the sanctuary: metals, dyed yarns, linen, skins, wood, oil, spices, gems; God's voice speaks to Moses from above the ark cover between the two cherubim; The ark's carrying poles must never be removed; God will dwell in the midst of the people in a sanctuary; Exact dimensions in cubits are given for a sacred object of the sanctuary; Covering of tahash skins (an unidentified animal); Materials for the sanctuary come from the free-will gifts of all whose heart moves them; The tablets of the testimony are placed inside the ark; The sanctuary is built after a pattern shown by God on the mountain.

Only in Bezalel makes the ark, table, lampstand and incense altar: Recipe of the holy anointing oil of myrrh, cinnamon, cane, cassia and olive oil; Execution of a divine command is narrated by repeating the command almost verbatim; A small gold-plated altar for burning incense before the veil.

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml): divergence. Exod 25:10, 16 wĕ-ʿāśû ʾărôn ʿăṣê šiṭṭîm ... wĕ-nātattā ʾel hā-ʾārōn ʾēt hā-ʿēdut: the ark made to hold the testimony; Q 2:248 at-tābūt (not ʾārôn; the word is the Aramaic/Hebrew tēbâ-type loan used of Moses' basket in Q 20:39) holding sakīna and relics.

Shared motifs, rarest first: The ark of the covenant: a gold-plated acacia chest with rings and poles [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); The ark of the covenant: a gold-plated acacia chest with rings and poles (weight 5.6). Pair score 12.3.

Only in Contribution for the sanctuary; ark, cover, table and lampstand: A cult object is hammered from a single piece of gold; A golden cover (kapporet, mercy seat) on top of the ark; List of precious materials for the sanctuary: metals, dyed yarns, linen, skins, wood, oil, spices, gems; God's voice speaks to Moses from above the ark cover between the two cherubim; The ark's carrying poles must never be removed; God will dwell in the midst of the people in a sanctuary; Exact dimensions in cubits are given for a sacred object of the sanctuary; Covering of tahash skins (an unidentified animal); Materials for the sanctuary come from the free-will gifts of all whose heart moves them; A golden seven-lamp lampstand with almond-blossom cups; A gold table with the bread of the presence always before God; The tablets of the testimony are placed inside the ark; and 2 more.

Only in Talut (Saul), the ark and Jalut (Goliath): The ark (tabut) returns, carried by angels, containing tranquility (sakina) and relics left by the family of Moses and Aaron; David kills Jalut (Goliath) and is given kingship and wisdom; Were it not for God checking people by means of others, the earth would be corrupted; 'How many a small band has overcome a large one by God's leave'; God chose the king and increased him in knowledge and stature, though he lacked wealth; The people object that the chosen king has no wealth and they have more right to kingship; Before battle the army is tested at a river: whoever drinks is not with the leader, except a handful scooped by hand; What the ark contains [contrast between the texts]; David kills the Philistine giant [divergence between the texts]; A giant taunts Israel and is killed by a hero; A jar of manna preserved before the testimony for future generations; Objection raised against the newly chosen king [divergence between the texts]; and 9 more.

leads.title: Tabernacle curtains, frames and veil ↔ Bezalel appointed; too many gifts; making of the curtains and frames
leads.summary: These two units share 8 motifs: eleven goat-hair curtains form the tent over the tabernacle, an embroidered screen at the entrance of the tent or court, outer coverings of red-dyed ram skins and tahash skins, a middle bar runs through the frames from end to end….

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml): parallel. miṣbāḥun ... yūqadu min shajaratin mubārakatin zaytūnatin ... yakādu zaytuhā yuḍīʾu ~ šemen zayit zākh kātît la-mmāʾôr ləhaʿălōt nēr tāmîd: a lamp lit with olive oil (zayt / zayit, cognate). In Exodus it is the sanctuary lamp tended by Aaron and his sons from evening to morning; in the Quran it is a parable of God's light, set 'in houses God allowed to be raised' where he is praised morning and evening (24:36).
Shared motifs, rarest first: A perpetual lamp fed with pure beaten olive oil (weight 6.3). Pair score 6.3.

Only in Bronze altar, courtyard and lamp oil: Bronze-plated altar of burnt offering with a bronze grating; The altar is hollow, made of boards and carried with poles; The tabernacle court measures 100 by 50 cubits with linen hangings; An altar with horns at its four corners; The sanctuary is built after a pattern shown by God on the mountain.

Only in The Light Verse; the mirage, the dark sea, the praising birds, hail and the creatures: Or like darkness in a deep sea, covered by wave upon wave and cloud above, darkness upon darkness, so one cannot see his own hand; The deeds of unbelievers are like a mirage in a plain that the thirsty takes for water until he reaches it and finds nothing, but finds God there; God is the light of the heavens and the earth; God's light is like a niche holding a lamp in a glass like a glittering star, lit from a blessed olive tree neither of east nor west, whose oil almost glows untouched by fire: light upon light; God sends down hail from mountains in the sky; the flash of his lightning nearly takes away sight; In houses God allowed to be raised, men undistracted by trade glorify him morning and evening; God created every beast from water: some go on their bellies, some on two legs, some on four; Birds with outspread wings glorify God; each knows its prayer and praise; With God is the fountain of life; in his light we see light; A lamp fed directly by an olive tree [divergence between the texts]; A golden lampstand with seven lamps is flanked by two olive trees that pour golden oil through golden pipes; The mirage and the thirsty traveler [divergence between the texts]; and 8 more.
