Only in The glory of God returns to the temple: God's voice (or the sound of his coming) is like the sound of many waters; The divine glory returns to the temple from the east through the east gate; Kings' corpses or memorials (pigre malkehem) beside the temple defile God's holy name; The temple stands on the top of a (very high) mountain whose whole territory is most holy; The temple is called the place of God's throne and the soles of his feet, where he will dwell forever; The prophet is to describe the temple's plan so that Israel will be ashamed of its sins; Fear that the spirit of YHWH will carry the prophet off to an unknown place; The cloud and glory fill the sanctuary so that even the leader cannot enter; The sanctuary is built after a pattern shown by God on the mountain; The prophet falls on his face at the sight of the divine glory.

Only in Do not despair of mercy; the earth in God's grip; the throngs to hell and Garden: The angels are seen surrounding the Throne, glorifying the praise of their Lord; The blessed praise God who gave them the land (ard) as inheritance to settle in the Garden where they will; The Book (record) is laid down, the prophets and witnesses are brought, and judgment is passed with truth; Unbelievers are driven to hell in throngs (zumar) and the godfearing to the Garden in throngs; the gates open and the keepers address each; The keepers of the Garden greet the righteous 'Peace be upon you, you have been good; enter'; Lest a soul say 'Alas for my neglect of God' or 'If only I had another chance (karra)'; If you associate partners with God your deeds will come to nothing; At the first trumpet blast all in heaven and earth swoon (sa'iqa) except whom God wills; at the second they stand looking; On the Day of Resurrection the whole earth is in God's grip and the heavens folded in his right hand; Who holds the keys that open and shut [divergence between the texts]; The keepers of hell ask 'Did not messengers from among you come to you?'; To God belong the keys (maqalid) of the heavens and the earth; and 5 more.

Only in The shut east gate, foreigners excluded, Levites and Zadokite priests: The east gate stays shut forever because YHWH the God of Israel entered by it; The first of the dough (reshit arisot) is given to the priest so that blessing rests on the house; Levites who went astray after idols are demoted to gatekeepers and slaughterers, barred from priestly service; Priests stand as judges in disputes, judging by God's ordinances; Priests may neither shave their heads nor let their hair grow long, but must trim it; Priests serve in linen only, with no wool, and must not gird themselves with anything that causes sweat; Only the prince (nasi) may sit in the shut gate to eat bread before YHWH; No foreigner uncircumcised in heart and flesh may enter the sanctuary; Priestly tribe receives no land: 'I am your portion and inheritance'; Priest may defile himself only for close kin; Priests may not marry a harlot or divorcee; the high priest only a virgin of his people; Priests must take off their holy garments in special chambers before going out to the people, lest the garments transmit holiness; and 5 more.

Only in Prayer not while drunk; bathing and dry ablution: Do not approach prayer while intoxicated, until you know what you say; One in major impurity (junub) must bathe before prayer, except a traveller passing through; Purification after seminal emission or intercourse [divergence between the texts]; Emission of semen makes a man (and his partner) unclean until evening; No wine before approaching God [divergence between the texts]; Without water, purify with clean earth (tayammum), wiping face and hands.

leads.title: The river from the temple and the healing of the sea ↔ The Originator, winged angels, and the two seas

leads.title: The end has come upon the four corners of the land ↔ Pharaoh leads his people into the fire; the towns standing and mown
leads.summary: These two units share 2 motifs: the gods of a people judged by god cannot help them, 'far be it from god to do wickedness, from shaddai to do wrong'; he repays a man according to his deeds.

passages.note: The gods of a people judged by God cannot help them (What they relied on cannot save them on the day of wrath: kaspām ûzᵉhābām lōʾ-yûkal lᵉhaṣṣîlām bᵉyôm ʿebrat YHWH vs fa-mā aghnat ʿanhum ālihatuhum ... wa-mā zādūhum ghayra tatbīb. Ezek speaks of their silver and gold (idols, 7:20), Q of their gods.)
passages.text: כַּסְפָּ֞ם בַּחוּצ֣וֹת יַשְׁלִ֗יכוּ וּזְהָבָם֮ לְנִדָּ֣ה יִֽהְיֶה֒ כַּסְפָּ֨ם וּזְהָבָ֜ם לֹֽא יוּכַ֣ל לְהַצִּילָ֗ם בְּיוֹם֙ עֶבְרַ֣ת יְהוָ֔ה נַפְשָׁם֙ לֹ֣א יְשַׂבֵּ֔עוּ וּמֵעֵיהֶ֖ם לֹ֣א יְמַלֵּ֑אוּ כִּֽי מִכְשׁ֥וֹל עֲוֺנָ֖ם הָיָֽה

passages.note: The gods of a people judged by God cannot help them (The judged people's gods are powerless: fa-mā aghnat ʿanhum ālihatuhumu llatī yadʿūna min dūni llāhi min shayʾin lammā jāʾa amru rabbik vs ûbᵉkol-ʾĕlōhê miṣrayim ʾeʿĕśeh šᵉpāṭîm ʾănî YHWH. In Exod God judges the gods themselves; in Q they merely fail their worshippers.)

Only in The six executioners and the man in linen who marks the foreheads: The angelic agent returns and reports 'I have done as you commanded me'; Divine slaughter is to begin at God's sanctuary, with the elders before the temple; Six men (angelic executioners), each with a weapon of destruction, come from the north gate to slay the city; The destroyer (mashhit) passes over houses marked with blood; The reminder is in honored, exalted, purified scrolls in the hands of noble, righteous scribes (safara); A heavenly man clothed in linen with a scribe's writing kit at his waist; A mark on the faces or foreheads of the faithful [divergence between the texts]; Prophet falls on his face crying 'Ah Lord, will you destroy the whole remnant of Israel?'; The divine glory leaves the temple in stages: from the cherub to the threshold, to the east gate, to the mountain east of the city; Sinners say 'YHWH does not see us; YHWH has forsaken the land'.

Only in Nun: by the pen; the prophet's great character; the swearer, slanderer and base-born man branded on the snout: God threatens: 'We shall brand him on the snout (khurtum)'; The deniers wish the prophet would compromise (tudhin) so they would compromise; The prophet is not mad; he has an unfailing reward and is of a great moral character (khuluq 'azim); Mamzer excluded from the assembly to the tenth generation; Do not obey every contemptible swearer, backbiter going about with slander, hinderer of good, coarse and moreover 'zanim' (base-born, ignoble); The prophet is no soothsayer (kahin), no madman, no poet awaiting the accident of fate; God will put his hook in the enemy king's nose and his bit in his lips and lead him back; Defense of the prophet: there is no madness (jinna) in your companion; he is only a warner; Do not go about as a talebearer among your people; Unbelievers dismiss the revelation as 'tales of the ancients' (asatir al-awwalin) they could equal; A surah opens with isolated letters (huruf muqatta'at) of unexplained meaning, e.g. alif-lam-mim.

Only in Covenant to send away foreign wives; assembly in the rain; list of offenders: The assembly sits trembling in the open square in the winter rains; Mixed marriages have already produced children, who are included in the dismissal; Community covenants to send away all foreign wives and their children; Named individuals are recorded as opposing the assembly's decision; Leader neither eats bread nor drinks water in mourning for the people's sin; Sons of the high priest are among those who married foreign wives; Named list of men who had married foreign wives; Leader makes the priests, Levites and all Israel swear to carry out the reform; Whoever fails to attend loses his property (herem) and is separated from the congregation; Leader prays and confesses weeping, prostrate before the house of God; 'There is still hope for Israel concerning this'; A tribunal of family heads examines each case at appointed times; and 1 more.

Only in Al-Mumtahana: no affection for God's enemies, Abraham's excellent example, examining emigrant women, and the women's pledge: Abraham and those with him are an excellent example: they declared themselves quit of their people and their gods, with enmity until they believe; Except Abraham's saying to his father 'I will ask forgiveness for you, though I have no power for you before God'; They despair of the hereafter as the unbelievers despair of those in the graves; Believers must not take God's enemies, who expelled the prophet, as allies (awliya') or secretly show them affection; Prohibition of killing one's children; Do not hold on to marriage ties with unbelieving women; dowries are reckoned between the communities; Believing women who emigrate are to be examined; if believers, they are not returned to the unbelievers, whose dowries are repaid; The women's pledge (bay'at al-nisa'): not to associate anything with God, steal, commit adultery, kill their children, bring a fabricated slander, or disobey in what is right; Abraham declares to his father and people that he is free of what they worship, except the one who created him; God does not forbid kindness and justice toward those who did not fight you over religion or expel you; Neither your blood-ties nor your children will benefit you on the Day of Resurrection; Mightier towns than the one that drove the prophet out were destroyed; and 3 more.

leads.summary: These two units share 1 motifs: only those who believe, pray and give alms may maintain god's places of worship.

Shared motifs, rarest first: Only those who believe, pray and give alms may maintain God's places of worship (weight 6.7). Pair score 6.7.

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/03-hb-quran.yaml): divergence. Six days of creation, then what God does next: khalaqa s-samāwāti wa-l-arḍa fī sittati ayyāmin thumma stawā ʿalā l-ʿarshi yudabbiru l-amra vs wayᵉkal ʾĕlōhîm bayyôm haššᵉbîʿî mᵉlaʾktô ... wayyišbōt bayyôm haššᵉbîʿî. The seventh day is replaced: Gen has rest (šābat) and a hallowed day; Q has God mounting the Throne and governing, with no rest and no seventh day. God makes the two lights to measure time: jaʿala sh-shamsa ḍiyāʾan wa-l-qamara nūran wa-qaddarahu manāzila li-taʿlamū ʿadada s-sinīna wa-l-ḥisāb vs ʾet-hammāʾôr haggādōl lᵉmemšelet hayyôm wᵉʾet-hammāʾôr haqqāṭōn lᵉmemšelet hallaylāh; wᵉhāyû ... lᵉyāmîm wᵉšānîm. Gen avoids the names sun and moon ('the great light, the small light'); Q names them.

Shared motifs, rarest first: Sun and moon are set to rule day and night and mark signs and seasons [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); Creation is completed in six days [divergence between the texts] (weight 5.8); Creation is completed in six days (weight 5.2); Sun and moon are set to rule day and night and mark signs and seasons (weight 4.7). Pair score 22.4.

Only in Creation in six days and the seventh-day rest: Deity gives names to the elements it creates (day, night, heaven, earth, seas); Deity rests on the seventh day after creating, and sanctifies it; The earth itself is commanded to bring forth plants or animals; Light exists before the sun and moon are made; Humans and animals originally given only plants as food; Creation proceeds by dividing (light/darkness, waters above/below); Deity rests on the seventh day after creating, and sanctifies it [divergence between the texts]; A divine wind or spirit hovers or moves over the primeval waters; God made every living thing from water [divergence between the texts]; God speaks to heavenly beings about making man [divergence between the texts]; The heavens and earth were a closed-up mass (ratq) that God split apart (fatq) [divergence between the texts]; The form God gave humans at creation [divergence between the texts]; and 24 more.

Only in The wise Book, creation, sun and moon, the prayer of paradise: The blessed in paradise cry 'Glory to you, O God', greet with 'Peace' and end with 'Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds'; The damned are given a drink of boiling water (hamim); God made the sun a radiance and the moon a light with measured stations, to count years and reckoning; People marvel that a reminder came through a man from among them; God originates creation and then repeats it (resurrection as re-creation); Opponents call the prophet or his message 'manifest sorcery'; After creating the heavens and earth God established himself on the Throne (istawa 'ala l-'arsh); Intercession avails only for whom God permits; Paradise as gardens (of ʿAdn) beneath which rivers flow, where the righteous abide forever; A surah opens with isolated letters (huruf muqatta'at) of unexplained meaning, e.g. alif-lam-mim.

Pair score 19.4.

Only in Creation in six days and the seventh-day rest: Deity gives names to the elements it creates (day, night, heaven, earth, seas); Deity rests on the seventh day after creating, and sanctifies it; The earth itself is commanded to bring forth plants or animals; Light exists before the sun and moon are made; Humans and animals originally given only plants as food; Creation proceeds by dividing (light/darkness, waters above/below); Deity rests on the seventh day after creating, and sanctifies it [divergence between the texts]; A divine wind or spirit hovers or moves over the primeval waters; God made every living thing from water [divergence between the texts]; The heavens and earth were a closed-up mass (ratq) that God split apart (fatq) [divergence between the texts]; The form God gave humans at creation [divergence between the texts]; Whether humans bear God's likeness, or nothing is like him [contrast between the texts]; and 25 more.

Only in Adam, the angels and Iblis: God teaches Adam all the names and he recites them to the angels, who cannot; The expelled are told 'Go down, enemies to one another' with a dwelling and provision on earth for a time; God announces to the angels he will place a vicegerent (khalifa) on earth; The first man names the animals; Adam receives words from his Lord and God turns to him in forgiveness; Angels object that the new human will corrupt the earth and shed blood while they praise God; Enmity decreed at the expulsion from the garden [divergence between the texts]; The first man's response after the transgression in the garden (blame or repentance) [divergence between the texts]; The first man and the names of the creatures [divergence between the texts]; The tree forbidden to the first humans [divergence between the texts]; The garden given to the first humans to live and eat in [divergence between the texts]; The human condition on earth after the expulsion [divergence between the texts]; and 10 more.

leads.summary: These two units share 2 motifs: whether humans bear god's likeness, or nothing is like him [contrast between the texts], humanity created male and female in one act.

passages.note: Whether humans bear God's likeness, or nothing is like him [contrast between the texts] (In the same breath as the creation of human pairs, opposite statements on likeness to God. evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/03-hb-quran.yaml): divergence, parallel. Who comes: wa-la-qad jāʾat rusulunā ibrāhīma bi-l-bushrā vs wayyērāʾ ʾēlāyw YHWH ... wᵉhinnēh šᵉlōšāh ʾănāšîm. Gen has YHWH himself appear in the form of three men; Q has 'our messengers', with no number and no appearance of God. Abraham at once brings a calf: fa-mā labitha an jāʾa bi-ʿijlin ḥanīdh (roasted) vs ʾel-habbāqār rāṣ ʾabrāhām wayyiqqaḥ ben-bāqār rak wāṭôb ... wayᵉmahēr (both stress haste). Q has no foot-washing, cakes, curds or milk. Reversed: in Gen the guests eat (wayyittēn lipnêhem wᵉhûʾ-ʿōmēd ʿălêhem taḥat hāʿēṣ wayyōʾkēlû); in Q their hands do not reach the food (fa-lammā raʾā aydiyahum lā taṣilu ilayhi nakirahum). cf. Tob 12:19, Gen. Rab. 48:14, b. Bava Metzia 86b (angels only seem to eat), outside the canon. Who is afraid and why: in Q Abraham is afraid because the guests will not eat (wa-awjasa minhum khīfatan qālū lā takhaf); in Gen it is Sarah who is afraid when caught laughing (wattᵉkaḥēš śārāh lēʾmōr lōʾ ṣāḥaqtî kî yārēʾāh). The order and the answer change: in Gen Sarah overhears the promise at the tent door and then laughs inwardly (wattiṣḥaq śārāh bᵉqirbāh), and God rebukes her (lāmmāh zeh ṣāḥăqāh śārāh), she denies it (lōʾ ṣāḥaqtî); in Q she is standing by and laughs first (wa-mraʾatuhu qāʾimatun fa-ḍaḥikat), then receives the tidings, with no rebuke and no denial. ṣḥq / ḍḥk are cognate. The promise of a son: fa-basharnāhā bi-isḥāqa wa-min warāʾi isḥāqa yaʿqūb vs šôb ʾāšûb ʾēlêkā kāʿēt ḥayyāh wᵉhinnēh-bēn lᵉśārāh ʾištekā. It is said to Sarah directly in Q, to Abraham in Gen (Sarah only overhears); Q names Isaac and adds Jacob after him; Gen names no child here and adds a date (lammôʿēd ... kāʿēt ḥayyāh).
Passages are shown for the 10 rarest of 12 shared motifs; the full list follows.

Shared motifs, rarest first: When and why Sarah laughs, and how it is answered [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); Who is afraid during the visit of the heavenly guests, and why [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); Who Abraham's visitors are (weight 6.7); Whether Abraham's heavenly guests eat the meal he serves [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); Doubt voiced at the promise of a son in old age (weight 6.7); A tender calf is slaughtered and served to divine guests (weight 6.3); The old wife overhears the promise of a son at the tent door and laughs (weight 6.3); A divine messenger announces a son to a barren couple [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.0); 'Is anything too wondrous for the LORD?' (weight 6.0); God appears as three men who visit the patriarch (weight 5.8); Patriarch or matriarch laughs at the promise of a child in old age (weight 5.6); Host runs to welcome strangers, washes their feet and feeds them (weight 5.1). Pair score 74.5.

Only in Three visitors at Mamre and the promise of Isaac: Child promised to a woman past childbearing age; The answer given to the old woman's doubt [divergence between the texts]; Heavenly visitors eat a human meal; Doubt voiced at the promise of a son in old age [divergence between the texts]; The aged father asks how he can have a son when his wife is barren and he is very old [divergence between the texts]; Host runs to welcome strangers, washes their feet and feeds them [divergence between the texts]; Who Abraham's visitors are [divergence between the texts]; The patriarch tells his unknown guests 'we are afraid of you' [divergence between the texts]; Patriarch or matriarch laughs at the promise of a child in old age [divergence between the texts]; Sarah's reaction to the announcement of a son [divergence between the texts]; Whether Abraham's heavenly guests eat the meal [divergence between the texts]; Sacred oak or terebinth marks a sanctuary site (Moreh, Mamre); and 1 more.

Only in Abraham's guests, the roasted calf and the laughing wife: Abraham is forbearing, sighing (awwah) and penitent; Abraham's angelic guests do not stretch their hands to the food, and he is afraid; The annunciation names Isaac 'and after Isaac, Jacob'; Promised son born to aged parents at the appointed time; How Abraham learns of Sodom's fate, and his response; How God answers Abraham's plea for the people of Sodom [divergence between the texts]; When and why Sarah laughs, and how it is answered; Hero bargains with God to spare a city for the sake of a few righteous (50 down to 10).

Gen: Abraham runs to meet the three men, bows (wayyištaḥû ʾārṣâ) and serves them a meal, and they eat (wayyōʾkēlû). Q 15: the guests say salāman, and Abraham answers innā minkum wajilūn. Hospitality and a shared meal become fear; there is no meal in this telling. Who doubts. Gen: Sarah, listening at the tent door, laughs (wattiṣḥaq śārâ bəqirbāh ... waʾdōnî zāqēn) and is rebuked: hăyippālēʾ mēYHWH dābār. Q: Abraham himself doubts, a-bashshartumūnī ʿalā an massaniya l-kibaru fa-bima tubashshirūn, and is told fa-lā takun mina l-qāniṭīn. Abraham replies wa-man yaqnaṭu min raḥmati rabbihi illā ḍ-ḍāllūn. Sarah, the laughter and the name Isaac are absent (the son is only ghulām ʿalīm).

leads.title: Three visitors at Mamre and the promise of Isaac ↔ The family of Imran, Mary and Zechariah
leads.summary: These two units share 3 motifs: doubt voiced at the promise of a son in old age [divergence between the texts], a divine messenger announces a son to a barren couple [divergence between the texts], patriarch or matriarch laughs at the promise of a child in old age.

passages.note: Doubt voiced at the promise of a son in old age [divergence between the texts] (Gen 18:12 wa-ttiṣḥaq śārâ bĕ-qirbāh lēʾmōr ʾaḥărê bĕlōtî hāyĕtâ llî ʿednâ wa-ʾdōnî zāqēn: the old wife doubts and laughs, citing her own age and her husband's; Q 3:40 qāla rabbi annā yakūnu lī ghulāmun wa-qad balaghaniya l-kibaru wa-mraʾatī ʿāqirun: the old husband objects, citing his age and his wife's barrenness. The doubt moves from wife to husband, and there is no laughter and no rebuke (contrast Gen 18:13-15): God answers kadhālika llāhu yafʿalu mā yashāʾ, cf. Gen 18:14 ha-yippālēʾ mē-YHWH dābār.)

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/07-hb-quran.yaml): divergence, parallel. Who the visitors are. Genesis: wa-yērāʾ ʾēlâw YHWH bə-ʾēlōnê mamrēʾ ... wə-hinnēh šəlōšâ ʾănāšîm (YHWH appears, as three men; YHWH himself speaks in 18:13). Quran: ḍayfu ibrāhīma l-mukramīn, addressed as ayyuhā l-mursalūn (51:31): honored guests who are 'sent ones', no number, and God is not among them. The welcome. Genesis: Abraham runs to meet them (wa-yyāroṣ liqrāʾṯām), bows to the ground and begs ʾăḏōnāy ʾim nāʾ māṣāʾṯî ḥēn bə-ʿênêḵā, then wa-yəmahēr ʾaḇrāhām hā-ʾōhĕlâ ʾel śārâ. Quran: the guests speak first, fa-qālū salāman qāla salāmun qawmun munkarūn (Abraham returns the greeting and finds them strange), then fa-rāgha ilā ahlihi (he slipped off to his household). Same hurried move to the tent; the bow and the plea are absent, and Abraham's unease (munkarūn) is added. wa-yiqqaḥ ben bāqār raḵ wā-ṭôḇ ... wa-yiqqaḥ ḥemʾâ wə-ḥālāḇ û-ḇen hab-bāqār ... wa-yittēn lip̄nêhem vs. fa-jāʾa bi-ʿijlin samīnin fa-qarrabahu ilayhim. Genesis: a tender, good calf with curds and milk; Quran: a fat calf only. Reversal: in Genesis the visitors eat: wə-hûʾ ʿōmēḏ ʿălêhem taḥaṯ hā-ʿēṣ wa-yyōʾḵēlû. In the Quran they do not: qāla a-lā taʾkulūn, fa-awjasa minhum khīfatan, qālū lā takhaf. The refusal to eat reveals that they are angels and frightens Abraham. cf. Tob 12:19, Gen. Rab. 48:14 and b. Bava Metzia 86b (the angels only seemed to eat), a solution to the same problem; not in the HB. wə-hinnēh ḇēn lə-śārâ ʾištekā; lam-môʿēḏ ʾāšûḇ ʾēleḵā kā-ʿēṯ ḥayyâ û-lə-śārâ ḇēn vs. wa-bashsharūhu bi-ghulāmin ʿalīm. Genesis promises a son to Sarah with a set time; the Quran gives the good news to Abraham of 'a knowing boy', with no time and no name. Sarah's reaction, changed from inner laughter to an open cry. Genesis: wat-tiṣḥaq śārâ bə-qirbāh lēʾmōr ʾaḥărê ḇəlōṯî ... wa-ʾḏōnî zāqēn; God asks lāmmâ zeh ṣāḥăqâ śārâ and she denies it out of fear (lōʾ ṣāḥaqtî kî yārēʾâ). Quran: fa-aqbalati mraʾatuhu fī ṣarratin fa-ṣakkat wajhahā wa-qālat ʿajūzun ʿaqīm (she came forward crying out, struck her face and said 'a barren old woman!'). The messengers answer ka-dhālika qāla rabbuki innahu huwa l-ḥakīmu l-ʿalīm: no rebuke, no denial, no laughter (ṣ-ḥ-q, the pun on Isaac's name, is gone).

Shared motifs, rarest first: The answer given to the old woman's doubt [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); Host runs to welcome strangers, washes their feet and feeds them [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); Whether Abraham's heavenly guests eat the meal [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); Heavenly visitors eat a human meal (weight 6.7); Who Abraham's visitors are [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); Sarah's reaction to the announcement of a son [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); A tender calf is slaughtered and served to divine guests (weight 6.3); The old wife overhears the promise of a son at the tent door and laughs (weight 6.3); A divine messenger announces a son's birth and gives his name (weight 5.2); Host runs to welcome strangers, washes their feet and feeds them (weight 5.1). Pair score 63.0.

Only in Abraham's honored guests, the barren old wife striking her face, the stones of clay for Lot's people; Pharaoh, 'Ad, Thamud and Noah: On 'Ad God sent the barren wind (al-rih al-'aqim), which left everything like rotten bones; Abraham brings a fattened calf but the guests do not eat, and he becomes afraid of them; The honored guests enter saying 'Peace' and Abraham replies 'Peace, strangers (qawm munkarun)'; The guests announce to Abraham a knowing (or wise) son ('alim); Thamud were told 'Enjoy yourselves for a while', defied the command and were seized by the thunderbolt while they looked on; Abraham's wife comes forward crying out, strikes her face and says 'A barren old woman!'; Angels seize the hesitating family by the hand and lead them out; How Abraham learns of Sodom's fate, and his response [divergence between the texts]; Only Lot's household is brought out of the doomed city [divergence between the texts]; In Lot's town only one house of submitters (muslimin) was found, and the believers were brought out; God seized Pharaoh and his hosts and cast them into the sea while he was blameworthy; Pharaoh turned away with his power/pillar (rukn) and called Moses 'a sorcerer or a madman'; and 10 more.

passages.text: וַ֠יָּבֹאוּ שְׁנֵ֨י הַמַּלְאָכִ֤ים סְדֹ֨מָה֙ בָּעֶ֔רֶב וְל֖וֹט יֹשֵׁ֣ב בְּשַֽׁעַר סְדֹ֑ם וַיַּרְא לוֹט֙ וַיָּ֣קָם לִקְרָאתָ֔ם וַיִּשְׁתַּ֥חוּ אַפַּ֖יִם אָֽרְצָה

passages.note: How Lot receives the heavenly guests [divergence between the texts] (Lot's response to the guests is reversed: in Gen he rises to meet them, bows and presses them to stay (wayyāqom liqrāʾtām wayyištaḥû ... wayyipṣar-bām mᵉʾōd ... wayyaʿaś lāhem mišteh); in Q he is distressed and helpless on their account (sīʾa bihim wa-ḍāqa bihim dharʿan wa-qāla hādhā yawmun ʿaṣīb).)
passages.text: וַיֹּ֜אמֶר הִנֶּ֣ה נָּא אֲדֹנַ֗י ס֣וּרוּ נָ֠א אֶל בֵּ֨ית עַבְדְּכֶ֤ם וְלִ֨ינוּ֙ וְרַחֲצ֣וּ רַגְלֵיכֶ֔ם וְהִשְׁכַּמְתֶּ֖ם וַהֲלַכְתֶּ֣ם לְדַרְכְּכֶ֑ם וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ לֹּ֔א כִּ֥י בָרְח֖וֹב נָלִֽין

passages.note: How Lot receives the heavenly guests [divergence between the texts] (Lot's response to the guests is reversed: in Gen he rises to meet them, bows and presses them to stay (wayyāqom liqrāʾtām wayyištaḥû ... wayyipṣar-bām mᵉʾōd ... wayyaʿaś lāhem mišteh); in Q he is distressed and helpless on their account (sīʾa bihim wa-ḍāqa bihim dharʿan wa-qāla hādhā yawmun ʿaṣīb).)
passages.text: وَلَمَّا جَآءَتْ رُسُلُنَا لُوطًا سِىٓءَ بِهِمْ وَضَاقَ بِهِمْ ذَرْعًا وَقَالَ هَٰذَا يَوْمٌ عَصِيبٌ

passages.note: When Lot leaves the city and when the destruction falls [divergence between the texts] (When they leave and when the blow falls: Q, by night, the destruction appointed for morning (bi-qiṭʿin mina l-layli ... inna mawʿidahumu ṣ-ṣubḥu a-laysa ṣ-ṣubḥu bi-qarīb); Gen, the angels hurry him at dawn (kᵉmô haššaḥar ʿālāh wayyāʾîṣû) and the fire falls once the sun has risen and Lot is in Zoar (haššemeš yāṣāʾ ʿal-hāʾāreṣ wᵉlôṭ bāʾ ṣōʿărāh).)
passages.text: וּכְמוֹ֙ הַשַּׁ֣חַר עָלָ֔ה וַיָּאִ֥יצוּ הַמַּלְאָכִ֖ים בְּל֣וֹט לֵאמֹ֑ר קוּם֩ קַ֨ח אֶֽת אִשְׁתְּךָ֜ וְאֶת שְׁתֵּ֤י בְנֹתֶ֨יךָ֙ הַנִּמְצָאֹ֔ת פֶּן תִּסָּפֶ֖ה בַּעֲוֺ֥ן הָעִֽיר

passages.note: When Lot leaves the city and when the destruction falls [divergence between the texts] (When they leave and when the blow falls: Q, by night, the destruction appointed for morning (bi-qiṭʿin mina l-layli ... inna mawʿidahumu ṣ-ṣubḥu a-laysa ṣ-ṣubḥu bi-qarīb); Gen, the angels hurry him at dawn (kᵉmô haššaḥar ʿālāh wayyāʾîṣû) and the fire falls once the sun has risen and Lot is in Zoar (haššemeš yāṣāʾ ʿal-hāʾāreṣ wᵉlôṭ bāʾ ṣōʿărāh).)
passages.text: הַשֶּׁ֖מֶשׁ יָצָ֣א עַל הָאָ֑רֶץ וְל֖וֹט בָּ֥א צֹֽעֲרָה

passages.text: قَالُوا۟ يَٰلُوطُ إِنَّا رُسُلُ رَبِّكَ لَن يَصِلُوٓا۟ إِلَيْكَ فَأَسْرِ بِأَهْلِكَ بِقِطْعٍ مِّنَ ٱلَّيْلِ وَلَا يَلْتَفِتْ مِنكُمْ أَحَدٌ إِلَّا ٱمْرَأَتَكَ إِنَّهُۥ مُصِيبُهَا مَآ أَصَابَهُمْ إِنَّ مَوْعِدَهُمُ ٱلصُّبْحُ أَلَيْسَ ٱلصُّبْحُ بِقَرِيبٍ

passages.note: Only Lot's household is brought out of the doomed city (Lot is told to take his family out: fa-asri bi-ahlika vs qûm qaḥ ʾet-ʾištᵉkā wᵉʾet-šᵉtê bᵉnōtêkā ... pen-tissāpeh baʿăwōn hāʿîr. Gen adds the sons-in-law who think he is joking (wayᵉhî kimṣaḥēq bᵉʿênê ḥătānāyw).)
passages.text: וַיֹּאמְר֨וּ הָאֲנָשִׁ֜ים אֶל ל֗וֹט עֹ֚ד מִֽי לְךָ֣ פֹ֔ה חָתָן֙ וּבָנֶ֣יךָ וּבְנֹתֶ֔יךָ וְכֹ֥ל אֲשֶׁר לְךָ֖ בָּעִ֑יר הוֹצֵ֖א מִן הַמָּקֽוֹם

passages.note: What Lot says to the townsmen (Lot offers his daughters: hāʾulāʾi banātī hunna aṭharu lakum fa-ttaqū llāha wa-lā tukhzūni fī ḍayfī a-laysa minkum rajulun rashīd vs ʾal-nāʾ ʾaḥay tārēʿû hinnēh-nāʾ lî šᵉtê bānôt ... wᵉʿăśû lāhen kaṭṭôb bᵉʿênêkem raq lāʾănāšîm hāʾēl ʾal-taʿăśû dābār. The terms differ: in Gen 'do to them as you please'; in Q 'they are purer for you', with an appeal to fear God and to right-minded men. Exegesis reads Q as lawful marriage.)
passages.text: וַיֹּאמַ֑ר אַל נָ֥א אַחַ֖י תָּרֵֽעוּ

passages.text: הִנֵּה נָ֨א לִ֜י שְׁתֵּ֣י בָנ֗וֹת אֲשֶׁ֤ר לֹֽא יָדְעוּ֙ אִ֔ישׁ אוֹצִֽיאָה נָּ֤א אֶתְהֶן֙ אֲלֵיכֶ֔ם וַעֲשׂ֣וּ לָהֶ֔ן כַּטּ֖וֹב בְּעֵינֵיכֶ֑ם רַ֠ק לָֽאֲנָשִׁ֤ים הָאֵל֙ אַל תַּעֲשׂ֣וּ דָבָ֔ר כִּֽי עַל כֵּ֥ן בָּ֖אוּ בְּצֵ֥ל קֹרָתִֽי

passages.text: وَجَآءَهُۥ قَوْمُهُۥ يُهْرَعُونَ إِلَيْهِ وَمِن قَبْلُ كَانُوا۟ يَعْمَلُونَ ٱلسَّيِّـَٔاتِ قَالَ يَٰقَوْمِ هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ بَنَاتِى هُنَّ أَطْهَرُ لَكُمْ فَٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ وَلَا تُخْزُونِ فِى ضَيْفِىٓ أَلَيْسَ مِنكُمْ رَجُلٌ رَّشِيدٌ

passages.note: Lot's townspeople turn on him (The townsmen besiege Lot's house: wa-jāʾahu qawmuhu yuhraʿūna ilayhi vs nāsabbû ʿal-habbayit minnaʿar wᵉʿad-zāqēn ... hôṣîʾēm ʾēlênû wᵉnēdʿāh ʾōtām. Their answer differs: in Gen they turn on Lot as an alien who plays the judge (hāʾeḥād bāʾ-lāgûr wayyišpōṭ šāpôṭ) and try to break the door; in Q they only say la-qad ʿalimta mā lanā fī banātika min ḥaqqin wa-innaka la-taʿlamu mā nurīd.)
passages.text: טֶרֶם֮ יִשְׁכָּבוּ֒ וְאַנְשֵׁ֨י הָעִ֜יר אַנְשֵׁ֤י סְדֹם֙ נָסַ֣בּוּ עַל הַבַּ֔יִת מִנַּ֖עַר וְעַד זָקֵ֑ן כָּל הָעָ֖ם מִקָּצֶֽה

passages.text: قَالُوا۟ لَقَدْ عَلِمْتَ مَا لَنَا فِى بَنَاتِكَ مِنْ حَقٍّ وَإِنَّكَ لَتَعْلَمُ مَا نُرِيدُ

passages.note: The angels tell Lot who sent them and what they will do [divergence between the texts] (The guests disclose their errand: yā lūṭu innā rusulu rabbika lan yaṣilū ilayka vs kî-mašḥitîm ʾănaḥnû ʾet-hammāqôm hazzeh ... wayᵉšallᵉḥēnû YHWH lᵉšaḥătāh. In Gen the angels first pull Lot inside and strike the mob with blindness (hikkû bassanwērîm); in Q, where Lot wishes for strength or a strong support (law anna lī bikum quwwatan aw āwī ilā ruknin shadīd), only their word assures him.)

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/03-hb-quran.yaml): divergence, parallel. Lot's response to the guests is reversed: in Gen he rises to meet them, bows and presses them to stay (wayyāqom liqrāʾtām wayyištaḥû ... wayyipṣar-bām mᵉʾōd ... wayyaʿaś lāhem mišteh); in Q he is distressed and helpless on their account (sīʾa bihim wa-ḍāqa bihim dharʿan wa-qāla hādhā yawmun ʿaṣīb). The townsmen besiege Lot's house: wa-jāʾahu qawmuhu yuhraʿūna ilayhi vs nāsabbû ʿal-habbayit minnaʿar wᵉʿad-zāqēn ... hôṣîʾēm ʾēlênû wᵉnēdʿāh ʾōtām. Their answer differs: in Gen they turn on Lot as an alien who plays the judge (hāʾeḥād bāʾ-lāgûr wayyišpōṭ šāpôṭ) and try to break the door; in Q they only say la-qad ʿalimta mā lanā fī banātika min ḥaqqin wa-innaka la-taʿlamu mā nurīd. Lot offers his daughters: hāʾulāʾi banātī hunna aṭharu lakum fa-ttaqū llāha wa-lā tukhzūni fī ḍayfī a-laysa minkum rajulun rashīd vs ʾal-nāʾ ʾaḥay tārēʿû hinnēh-nāʾ lî šᵉtê bānôt ... wᵉʿăśû lāhen kaṭṭôb bᵉʿênêkem raq lāʾănāšîm hāʾēl ʾal-taʿăśû dābār. The terms differ: in Gen 'do to them as you please'; in Q 'they are purer for you', with an appeal to fear God and to right-minded men. Exegesis reads Q as lawful marriage. The guests disclose their errand: yā lūṭu innā rusulu rabbika lan yaṣilū ilayka vs kî-mašḥitîm ʾănaḥnû ʾet-hammāqôm hazzeh ... wayᵉšallᵉḥēnû YHWH lᵉšaḥătāh. In Gen the angels first pull Lot inside and strike the mob with blindness (hikkû bassanwērîm); in Q, where Lot wishes for strength or a strong support (law anna lī bikum quwwatan aw āwī ilā ruknin shadīd), only their word assures him. Lot is told to take his family out: fa-asri bi-ahlika vs qûm qaḥ ʾet-ʾištᵉkā wᵉʾet-šᵉtê bᵉnōtêkā ... pen-tissāpeh baʿăwōn hāʿîr. Gen adds the sons-in-law who think he is joking (wayᵉhî kimṣaḥēq bᵉʿênê ḥătānāyw). When they leave and when the blow falls: Q, by night, the destruction appointed for morning (bi-qiṭʿin mina l-layli ... inna mawʿidahumu ṣ-ṣubḥu a-laysa ṣ-ṣubḥu bi-qarīb); Gen, the angels hurry him at dawn (kᵉmô haššaḥar ʿālāh wayyāʾîṣû) and the fire falls once the sun has risen and Lot is in Zoar (haššemeš yāṣāʾ ʿal-hāʾāreṣ wᵉlôṭ bāʾ ṣōʿărāh).

Gen: Lot rises to meet them at the gate, bows, presses them to stay and bakes maṣṣôt. Q: Lot greets them coldly, innakum qawmun munkarūn ('you are strangers'). Hospitality is replaced by unease, as with Abraham. Order reversed. Gen: first the mob (19:4-11), then the angels reveal kî-mašḥitîm ʾănaḥnû ʾet-hammāqôm hazzeh (19:13). evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml): divergence, parallel. The sin: Genesis has one night's event, the townsmen demanding Lot's two guests, hôṣîʾēm ʾēlênû wə-nēdəʿâ ʾōtām; the Quran has a standing practice of the whole people, a-taʾtūna dh-dhukrāna mina l-ʿālamīna wa-tadharūna mā khalaqa lakum rabbukum min azwājikum. The Quran has no guests, angels or hospitality, and Lot preaches as 'their brother' and a trustworthy messenger (26:161-162), which Genesis' Lot never does. la-in lam tantahi yā Lūṭu la-takūnanna mina l-mukhrajīna ~ hāʾeḥād bāʾ lāgûr wa-yyišpōṭ šāfôṭ ʿattâ nāraʿ ləkhā mēhem: the people turn on Lot as an outsider who presumes to judge them; Genesis threatens worse harm than to the guests, the Quran threatens expulsion. Why Lot is saved: Gen 19:29 wa-yyizkōr ʾĕlōhîm ʾet ʾAvrāhām wa-yšallaḥ ʾet Lôṭ, for Abraham's sake, and the angels drag the hesitating family out (wa-yyitmahmāh, 19:16); Q 26:169-170 Lot prays rabbi najjinī wa-ahlī mimmā yaʿmalūna and God saves him and his family in answer, for his own sake. Lot neither hesitates nor depends on Abraham. illā ʿajūzan fī l-ghābirīna ~ wat-tabbēṭ ʾištô mē-ʾaḥărāyw wat-təhî nəṣîv melaḥ: the one family member lost. Genesis names her Lot's wife and says why (she looked back) and how (pillar of salt); the Quran says only 'an old woman among those who stayed behind', with no looking back and no salt. wa-amṭarnā ʿalayhim maṭaran fa-sāʾa maṭaru l-mundharīna ~ wa-YHWH himṭîr ʿal Sədōm ... gofrît wā-ʾēš: the same verb (amṭara / himṭîr); the Quran does not name sulphur and fire, and Sodom is never named.

Shared motifs, rarest first: What the sin of Lot's townsmen was [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); Lot's people threaten to expel him (weight 6.3); The fate of Lot's wife (weight 5.8); Who is saved with the hero from the destruction, and why [divergence between the texts] (weight 5.8); Wife who looks back is turned into a pillar of salt (weight 5.6); The men of Sodom are exceedingly wicked (weight 5.2); God rains sulfur and fire from heaven on cities (weight 4.8); Hero's family saved with him (weight 4.5). Pair score 44.6.

Only in Lot's guests and the destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah: A small town is spared at the refugee's request (Zoar, 'small'); Angels seize the hesitating family by the hand and lead them out; Two angels are received as guests by Lot in Sodom [divergence between the texts]; The angels tell Lot who sent them and what they will do [divergence between the texts]; The angelic guests reveal they are sent against a criminal people [divergence between the texts]; Cities overturned (hafakh) and the plain destroyed [divergence between the texts]; Deniers pray: 'If this is the truth from you, rain stones on us from the sky'; God rains destruction on Lot's town [divergence between the texts]; Command not to look back while fleeing a doomed place [divergence between the texts]; The fate of Lot's wife [divergence between the texts]; God rains sulfur and fire from heaven on cities [divergence between the texts]; Host offers his virgin daughters to the mob to protect his guests [divergence between the texts]; and 34 more.

Only in Lot and his people: Lot's family is saved except an old woman among those who stayed behind; Lot condemns his people for approaching males and leaving the wives God created for them; The town that was rained on with an evil rain (Lot's) is passed by travelers; Formula: 'their brother' (akhūhum) Noah/Hud/Salih/Lot is a trustworthy messenger sent to his people; Refrain closing each episode: 'In that is a sign, yet most of them do not believe; your Lord is the Mighty, the Merciful'.

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml): divergence, parallel. Lot and the guests: Genesis has him rise, bow and press them to stay (wa-yyifṣar bām məʾōd), and he makes a feast with unleavened bread; the Quran has him distressed and helpless on their account, sīʾa bihim wa-ḍāqa bihim dharʿan, until they reassure him, lā takhaf wa-lā taḥzan innā munajjūka. Eager hospitality becomes dismay. innā muhlikū ahli hādhihi l-qaryati inna ahlahā kānū ẓālimīna ... innā munzilūna ʿalā ahli hādhihi l-qaryati rijzan mina s-samāʾi ~ kî mašḥitîm ʾănaḥnû ʾet ham-māqôm haz-zeh ... wa-yšallə ḥēnû YHWH ləšaḥătāh: the messengers declare they are sent to destroy 'this place / this town'. In Genesis they say it to Lot; in the Quran first to Abraham, then to Lot. illā mraʾataka kānat mina l-ghābirīna ~ wat-tabbēṭ ʾištô mē-ʾaḥărāyw wat-təhî nəṣîv melaḥ: the wife's fate is known in advance and told to Abraham and Lot in the Quran; Genesis tells it as her own act during the flight.

Shared motifs, rarest first: How Lot receives the divine messengers [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); God's messengers announce that they are sent to destroy the city (weight 6.7); Two angels are received as guests by Lot in Sodom (weight 6.0); The fate of Lot's wife (weight 5.8); Wife who looks back is turned into a pillar of salt (weight 5.6); The men of Sodom are exceedingly wicked (weight 5.2); God rains sulfur and fire from heaven on cities (weight 4.8). Pair score 40.7.

Only in Lot's guests and the destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah: A small town is spared at the refugee's request (Zoar, 'small'); Angels seize the hesitating family by the hand and lead them out; Two angels are received as guests by Lot in Sodom [divergence between the texts]; The angels tell Lot who sent them and what they will do [divergence between the texts]; The angelic guests reveal they are sent against a criminal people [divergence between the texts]; Cities overturned (hafakh) and the plain destroyed [divergence between the texts]; Deniers pray: 'If this is the truth from you, rain stones on us from the sky'; God rains destruction on Lot's town [divergence between the texts]; Command not to look back while fleeing a doomed place [divergence between the texts]; The fate of Lot's wife [divergence between the texts]; God rains sulfur and fire from heaven on cities [divergence between the texts]; Host offers his virgin daughters to the mob to protect his guests [divergence between the texts]; and 35 more.

Only in Lot and the destruction of his town: The host is troubled and helpless on account of the angelic guests, fearing for them; Lot's people approach men, cut off the road (highway robbery) and commit abominations in their assembly (nadi); Abraham's plea when told that the city of Lot will be destroyed [divergence between the texts]; The sin of Sodom was pride, surfeit of bread and careless ease, not strengthening the hand of the poor and needy; A land will be overthrown like Sodom and Gomorrah and their neighbors, never inhabited; Hero bargains with God to spare a city for the sake of a few righteous (50 down to 10); God appears as three men who visit the patriarch; Deniers dare the prophet: 'Bring us what you threaten, if you are truthful'.

leads.summary: These two units share 1 motifs: two messengers sent to a town are rejected, so god reinforces them with a third.

passages.note: Two messengers sent to a town are rejected, so God reinforces them with a third (Messengers come to a doomed town. Gen: wa-yyāḇōʾû šənê ham-malʾāḵîm sədōmâ, two messengers (the third of Gen 18 stays behind). Q: idh arsalnā ilayhimu thnayni ... fa-ʿazzaznā bi-thālith, two messengers then a third. Lot alone urges his people (qûmû ṣəʾû min-ha-mmāqôm ha-zze) and is mocked (wa-yəhî ḵi-mṣaḥēq); the Quranic man from the city's edge urges yā-qawmi ttabiʿū l-mursalīn. Structural lead only, the town is unnamed in the Quran.)

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/06-hb-quran.yaml): echo. Messengers come to a doomed town. Gen: wa-yyāḇōʾû šənê ham-malʾāḵîm sədōmâ, two messengers (the third of Gen 18 stays behind). Q: idh arsalnā ilayhimu thnayni ... fa-ʿazzaznā bi-thālith, two messengers then a third. Lot alone urges his people (qûmû ṣəʾû min-ha-mmāqôm ha-zze) and is mocked (wa-yəhî ḵi-mṣaḥēq); the Quranic man from the city's edge urges yā-qawmi ttabiʿū l-mursalīn. Structural lead only, the town is unnamed in the Quran.
Shared motifs, rarest first: Two messengers sent to a town are rejected, so God reinforces them with a third (weight 6.7). Pair score 6.7.

Only in Lot's guests and the destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah: A small town is spared at the refugee's request (Zoar, 'small'); Angels seize the hesitating family by the hand and lead them out; Two angels are received as guests by Lot in Sodom [divergence between the texts]; The angels tell Lot who sent them and what they will do [divergence between the texts]; The angelic guests reveal they are sent against a criminal people [divergence between the texts]; Cities overturned (hafakh) and the plain destroyed [divergence between the texts]; Deniers pray: 'If this is the truth from you, rain stones on us from the sky'; God rains destruction on Lot's town [divergence between the texts]; Command not to look back while fleeing a doomed place [divergence between the texts]; The fate of Lot's wife [divergence between the texts]; God rains sulfur and fire from heaven on cities [divergence between the texts]; Host offers his virgin daughters to the mob to protect his guests [divergence between the texts]; and 41 more.

Only in The people of the town, the three messengers and the man who came running: A man comes running from the farthest part of the city urging his people to follow the messengers; The believer is told 'enter the Garden' and says 'Would that my people knew how my Lord forgave me'; The townsfolk say 'we augur ill of you' and threaten to stone the messengers; they reply 'your omen is with you'; No host from heaven was needed: a single Shout (sayha) and they were extinguished; Offender stoned to death by the community; Travel in the land and see the end of those who denied; Intercession avails only for whom God permits; The Prophet asks no wage for the message.

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/07-hb-quran.yaml): divergence, echo. What falls on the city. Genesis: wa-YHWH himṭîr ʿal səḏōm wə-ʿal ʿămōrâ goprîṯ wā-ʾēš mē-ʾēṯ YHWH min haš-šāmāyim (sulfur and fire rained from YHWH). Quran: li-nursila ʿalayhim ḥijāratan min ṭīnin musawwamatan ʿinda rabbika li-l-musrifīn (stones of clay, each marked by your Lord for the transgressors). Fire and sulfur become marked clay stones (cf. Q 11:82 sijjīl). One household rescued. Genesis: ʿōḏ mî ləḵā p̄ōh ḥāṯān û-ḇānêḵā û-ḇənōṯêḵā ... hôṣēʾ min ham-māqôm; the angels seize Lot's hand and his wife's and daughters' (wa-yyaḥăzîqû hā-ʾănāšîm bə-yāḏô ...) because of YHWH's pity (bə-ḥemlaṯ YHWH ʿālâw), and Lot hesitates (wa-yyiṯmahmāh). Quran: fa-akhrajnā man kāna fīhā mina l-muʾminīna fa-mā wajadnā fīhā ghayra baytin mina l-muslimīn. Lot's household is defined by faith (muʾminūn, muslimūn), not kinship; the hesitation, the sons-in-law and the wife's fate (19:26) are not told here. wə-hinnēh ʿālâ qîṭōr hā-ʾāreṣ kə-qîṭōr hak-kiḇšān (Abraham sees the smoke over the plain) vs. wa-taraknā fīhā āyatan li-lladhīna yakhāfūna l-ʿadhāba l-alīm. The aftermath seen by Abraham becomes a lasting sign for later people.

Shared motifs, rarest first: God left in the destroyed city a sign for those who fear the painful punishment (weight 6.7); Only Lot's household is brought out of the doomed city [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); Angels seize the hesitating family by the hand and lead them out (weight 6.7); What falls from heaven on Sodom [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.3); The men of Sodom are exceedingly wicked (weight 5.2); Host runs to welcome strangers, washes their feet and feeds them (weight 5.1); God rains sulfur and fire from heaven on cities (weight 4.8). Pair score 41.4.

Only in Lot's guests and the destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah: A small town is spared at the refugee's request (Zoar, 'small'); Two angels are received as guests by Lot in Sodom [divergence between the texts]; The angels tell Lot who sent them and what they will do [divergence between the texts]; The angelic guests reveal they are sent against a criminal people [divergence between the texts]; Cities overturned (hafakh) and the plain destroyed [divergence between the texts]; Deniers pray: 'If this is the truth from you, rain stones on us from the sky'; God rains destruction on Lot's town [divergence between the texts]; Command not to look back while fleeing a doomed place [divergence between the texts]; The fate of Lot's wife [divergence between the texts]; God rains sulfur and fire from heaven on cities [divergence between the texts]; Host offers his virgin daughters to the mob to protect his guests [divergence between the texts]; Lot's family is saved at the time before dawn (bi-sahar) while a storm of stones (hasib) destroys the rest; and 35 more.

Only in Abraham's honored guests, the barren old wife striking her face, the stones of clay for Lot's people; Pharaoh, 'Ad, Thamud and Noah: On 'Ad God sent the barren wind (al-rih al-'aqim), which left everything like rotten bones; Abraham brings a fattened calf but the guests do not eat, and he becomes afraid of them; The honored guests enter saying 'Peace' and Abraham replies 'Peace, strangers (qawm munkarun)'; The guests announce to Abraham a knowing (or wise) son ('alim); Thamud were told 'Enjoy yourselves for a while', defied the command and were seized by the thunderbolt while they looked on; Abraham's wife comes forward crying out, strikes her face and says 'A barren old woman!'; The answer given to the old woman's doubt [divergence between the texts]; Heavenly visitors eat a human meal; Host runs to welcome strangers, washes their feet and feeds them [divergence between the texts]; How Abraham learns of Sodom's fate, and his response [divergence between the texts]; Who Abraham's visitors are [divergence between the texts]; In Lot's town only one house of submitters (muslimin) was found, and the believers were brought out; and 13 more.

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/07-hb-quran.yaml): parallel. The 'overturned' city: wa-yyahăp̄ōḵ ʾeṯ he-ʿārîm hā-ʾēl wə-ʾēṯ kol hak-kikkār vs. wa-l-muʾtafikata ahwā fa-ghashshāhā mā ghashshā. Both use 'overturn' (h-p-k; ʾ-f-k, al-muʾtafika). The Quran names no city and has it 'hurled down' (ahwā) and covered.
Shared motifs, rarest first: Cities overturned (hafakh) and the plain destroyed (weight 5.6). Pair score 5.6.

Only in Lot's guests and the destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah: A small town is spared at the refugee's request (Zoar, 'small'); Angels seize the hesitating family by the hand and lead them out; Two angels are received as guests by Lot in Sodom [divergence between the texts]; The angels tell Lot who sent them and what they will do [divergence between the texts]; The angelic guests reveal they are sent against a criminal people [divergence between the texts]; Cities overturned (hafakh) and the plain destroyed [divergence between the texts]; Deniers pray: 'If this is the truth from you, rain stones on us from the sky'; God rains destruction on Lot's town [divergence between the texts]; Command not to look back while fleeing a doomed place [divergence between the texts]; The fate of Lot's wife [divergence between the texts]; God rains sulfur and fire from heaven on cities [divergence between the texts]; Host offers his virgin daughters to the mob to protect his guests [divergence between the texts]; and 41 more.

Only in Al-Lat, al-'Uzza and Manat; angelic intercession; the scrolls of Abraham and Moses; the Lord of Sirius: The three goddesses al-Lat, al-'Uzza and Manat, 'the third, the other', named and rejected; They follow only conjecture (zann), and conjecture avails nothing against the truth; God created the pairs, male and female, from a drop of sperm (nutfa) when it is emitted; A surah ends with the command to prostrate (sajda verse); God destroyed 'Ad 'the first' (implying a second 'Ad); God knew you when he produced you from the earth and when you were embryos in your mothers' bellies; do not claim purity; The idols are only names you and your fathers have named, for which God sent down no authority; God is 'the Lord of Sirius' (al-shi'ra), a star worshipped by some Arabs; Those who avoid the great sins and indecencies, except minor slips (al-lamam), find God's forgiveness wide; To your Lord is the final end (al-muntaha); 'Is the male for you and the female for him? That is an unfair division'; 'Which of your Lord's bounties (ala') will you dispute/deny?'; and 15 more.

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/07-hb-quran.yaml): divergence, echo, parallel. The mob blinded at Lot's door. Genesis: ʾayyēh hā-ʾănāšîm ... hôṣîʾēm ʾēlênû wə-nēḏəʿāh ʾōṯām; the angels (hā-ʾănāšîm) strike them bas-sanwērîm and they weary themselves finding the door. Quran: wa-la-qad rāwadūhu ʿan ḍayfihi fa-ṭamasnā aʿyunahum fa-dhūqū ʿadhābī wa-nudhur (God says 'We blotted out their eyes'). The striking passes from the angel-guests to God himself, and the search for the door is dropped. Rescue at daybreak: û-ḵəmô haš-šaḥar ʿālâ wa-yyāʾîṣû ham-malʾāḵîm bə-lôṭ vs. illā āla lūṭin najjaynāhum bi-saḥar (Hebrew šaḥar 'dawn', Arabic saḥar 'the hour before dawn'). Why Lot is saved. Genesis: wa-yyizkōr ʾĕlōhîm ʾeṯ ʾaḇrāhām wa-yšallaḥ ʾeṯ lôṭ mit-tôḵ ha-hăp̄ēḵâ (for Abraham's sake), and earlier bə-ḥemlaṯ YHWH ʿālâw (19:16, God's pity in spite of his delay). Quran: najjaynāhum bi-saḥarin niʿmatan min ʿindinā ka-dhālika najzī man shakar (a favor from us; so we reward whoever is grateful). Rescue for Abraham's merit becomes reward for Lot's own gratitude. goprîṯ wā-ʾēš mē-ʾēṯ YHWH min haš-šāmāyim vs. innā arsalnā ʿalayhim ḥāṣiban (a storm of stones). As in Q 51:33 the Quran's Sodom is stoned, not burned. Lot's warning disbelieved: qûmû ṣəʾû min ham-māqôm haz-zeh kî mašḥîṯ YHWH ʾeṯ hā-ʿîr wa-yhî ḵi-mṣaḥēq bə-ʿênê ḥăṯānâw vs. wa-la-qad andharahum baṭshatanā fa-tamāraw bi-n-nudhur. Genesis: only his sons-in-law, who take it as a joke; Quran: the whole people, who dispute the warnings.

Shared motifs, rarest first: Lot's family is saved at the time before dawn (bi-sahar) while a storm of stones (hasib) destroys the rest (weight 6.7); Who strikes the Sodom mob's eyes [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); What falls from heaven on Sodom [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.3); The righteous man's warning is taken as a joke by his own relatives (weight 6.3); Attackers struck with blindness and cannot find the door (weight 6.3); Townsmen surround the house and demand the male guest for sexual abuse (weight 6.0); Hero's family saved with him [divergence between the texts] (weight 5.4); God rains sulfur and fire from heaven on cities (weight 4.8). Pair score 48.5.

Only in Lot's guests and the destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah: A small town is spared at the refugee's request (Zoar, 'small'); Angels seize the hesitating family by the hand and lead them out; Two angels are received as guests by Lot in Sodom [divergence between the texts]; The angels tell Lot who sent them and what they will do [divergence between the texts]; The angelic guests reveal they are sent against a criminal people [divergence between the texts]; Cities overturned (hafakh) and the plain destroyed [divergence between the texts]; Deniers pray: 'If this is the truth from you, rain stones on us from the sky'; God rains destruction on Lot's town [divergence between the texts]; Command not to look back while fleeing a doomed place [divergence between the texts]; The fate of Lot's wife [divergence between the texts]; God rains sulfur and fire from heaven on cities [divergence between the texts]; Host offers his virgin daughters to the mob to protect his guests [divergence between the texts]; and 34 more.

Only in Refrains over 'Ad, Thamud's she-camel, Lot's guests and Pharaoh; everything by measure; the seat of truth: God's command is but one, like a blink of the eye; The guilty are dragged on their faces into the Fire: 'Taste the touch of Saqar'; The God-fearing are in gardens and a river, in a seat of truth with an all-powerful King; A single Cry (sayha) is sent and they become like the dry stubble of a pen-builder; When they solicited Lot's guests, God obliterated their eyes; 'The host will be routed and turn their backs' (applied to Badr); Everything they did is in the scriptures (zubur); every small and great thing is written down; God created everything by measure/decree (bi-qadar); 'Are your unbelievers better than those, or have you an immunity (bara'a) in the scriptures (zubur)?'; Supernatural being must leave before daybreak; Refrain: 'How then were my punishment and my warnings?' (fa-kayfa kana 'adhabi wa-nudhur); Refrain: 'We have made the Quran easy to remember; is there anyone who will remember?' (fa-hal min muddakir); and 5 more.

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/08-hb-quran.yaml): parallel. wa-l-muʾtafikātu bi-l-khāṭiʾa ... fa-ʿaṣaw rasūla rabbihim fa-akhadhahum ~ wa-yyahăfōk ʾet he-ʿārîm hā-ʾēl: the cities named only as 'the overturned ones'. The Quran gives the reason as disobeying 'the messenger of their Lord'; Genesis gives no messenger to Sodom except the visiting angels.
Shared motifs, rarest first: Cities overturned (hafakh) and the plain destroyed (weight 5.6). Pair score 5.6.

Only in Lot's guests and the destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah: A small town is spared at the refugee's request (Zoar, 'small'); Angels seize the hesitating family by the hand and lead them out; Two angels are received as guests by Lot in Sodom [divergence between the texts]; The angels tell Lot who sent them and what they will do [divergence between the texts]; The angelic guests reveal they are sent against a criminal people [divergence between the texts]; Cities overturned (hafakh) and the plain destroyed [divergence between the texts]; Deniers pray: 'If this is the truth from you, rain stones on us from the sky'; God rains destruction on Lot's town [divergence between the texts]; Command not to look back while fleeing a doomed place [divergence between the texts]; The fate of Lot's wife [divergence between the texts]; God rains sulfur and fire from heaven on cities [divergence between the texts]; Host offers his virgin daughters to the mob to protect his guests [divergence between the texts]; and 41 more.

Only in Al-Haqqa: Thamud and 'Ad, the running ship, the single trumpet blast, the sky split and eight bearing the Throne: 'Ad were destroyed by a furious wind for seven nights and eight days, lying felled like hollow palm trunks; When the water overflowed God carried 'you' in the running ship (al-jariya) as a reminder for retaining ears; That day eight (angels) bear the Throne of your Lord above them; At a single blast on the trumpet, the earth and mountains are lifted and crushed with a single crushing; Thamud were destroyed by the Overwhelming (al-tagiya, the Blast); Rhetorical opening: 'The Reality (al-haqqa)! What is the Reality? And what will make you know what the Reality is?'; When the water overflowed God carried 'you' in the running ship (al-jariya) as a reminder for retaining ears [divergence between the texts]; Four living creatures (hayyot) of human form bear the divine throne [divergence between the texts]; The overturned city (al-mu'tafika, Sodom) God hurled down and covered with what covered it; A roaring cold wind (sarsar) on a day of continuous ill omen plucks men away like trunks of uprooted palms; The sky splits and is frail that day, and the angels are on its borders; When the Event (al-waqi'a) befalls, none can deny it: it abases and exalts; and 4 more.
Lot's guests and the destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah: tagged by Claude (model), reading the Hebrew.
Al-Haqqa: Thamud and 'Ad, the running ship, the single trumpet blast, the sky split and eight bearing the Throne: tagged by Claude (model), reading the Arabic.

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml): divergence. Who knows the names is reversed. Gen 2:19 wa-yyābēʾ ʾel hā-ʾādām lirʾôt mah yyiqrāʾ lô ... wa-yyiqrāʾ hā-ʾādām šēmôt: God brings the animals 'to see what he would call them' and the man invents the names; Q 2:31 wa-ʿallama ādama l-asmāʾa kullahā thumma ʿaraḍahum ʿalā l-malāʾikati: God teaches Adam all the names and displays the creatures to the angels as a test, ending innī aʿlamu ghayba s-samāwāti wa-l-arḍ (2:33). Human initiative before an observing God becomes knowledge given by an all-knowing God, and the scene becomes a contest with the angels. Gen 2:8 gan bĕ-ʿēden miqqedem, 2:16 mi-kkōl ʿēṣ ha-gān ʾākōl tōʾkēl (said to the man alone, before the woman is made); Q 2:35 uskun anta wa-zawjuka l-jannata wa-kulā minhā raghadan ḥaythu shiʾtumā: 'the Garden' with no place in the east, and the permission is given to both (dual) together. Gen 2:17 û-mē-ʿēṣ ha-daʿat ṭôb wā-rāʿ lōʾ tōʾkal mimmennû kî bĕ-yôm ʾăkolkā mimmennû môt tāmût; Q 2:35 wa-lā taqrabā hādhihi sh-shajarata fa-takūnā mina ẓ-ẓālimīn. The tree has no name (no 'knowledge of good and evil'); the sanction is to become wrongdoers, not death.

Shared motifs, rarest first: The garden given to the first humans to live and eat in [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); The tree forbidden to the first humans [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); The first man names the animals (weight 6.7); The first man and the names of the creatures [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); A tree of knowledge whose fruit is forbidden (weight 5.8); God plants a garden (Eden) in the east and places the first human there (weight 5.6). Pair score 38.1.

Only in Second creation account, Eden, and the making of woman: Eating the forbidden fruit is threatened with death; The first human is put in the garden to work and guard it; Man leaves father and mother and cleaves to his wife; they become one flesh; A mist or spring rises from the earth to water the ground; First couple naked and not ashamed; God made a covenant with Adam, but he forgot and lacked resolve [divergence between the texts]; Whether the first couple were naked or clothed before the fall [contrast between the texts]; How the first human's mate is made from the first human [divergence between the texts]; Whether any fruit in the Garden is forbidden [contrast between the texts]; Forming a creature from earth and breathing life into it [divergence between the texts]; Four rivers in the Garden [divergence between the texts]; In the garden Adam will not hunger, be naked, thirst or suffer the sun's heat [divergence between the texts]; and 16 more.

Only in Adam, the angels and Iblis: God teaches Adam all the names and he recites them to the angels, who cannot; The expelled are told 'Go down, enemies to one another' with a dwelling and provision on earth for a time; God announces to the angels he will place a vicegerent (khalifa) on earth; Adam receives words from his Lord and God turns to him in forgiveness; Angels object that the new human will corrupt the earth and shed blood while they praise God; Enmity decreed at the expulsion from the garden [divergence between the texts]; The first man's response after the transgression in the garden (blame or repentance) [divergence between the texts]; God speaks to heavenly beings about making man [divergence between the texts]; The human condition on earth after the expulsion [divergence between the texts]; The office given to humans on earth at creation [divergence between the texts]; The tempter in the garden [divergence between the texts]; Whoever sheds human blood, by man shall his blood be shed, because humans bear God's image; and 7 more.

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/04-hb-quran.yaml): divergence. wayṣaw YHWH ʾĕlōhîm ʿal-hāʾādām ... ûmēʿēṣ haddaʿat ṭôb wārāʿ lōʾ tōʾkal mimmennû kî bəyôm ʾăkolkā mimmennû môt tāmût; wa-la-qad ʿahidnā ilā Ādama min qablu fa-nasiya wa-lam najid lahu ʿazmā. Gen gives a command with a death sanction; Q gives a covenant that Adam forgets. Q frames the fault as forgetting and lack of resolve, and has no death threat. Reversal. Gen: in the garden they are naked and unashamed, wayyihyû šənêhem ʿărûmmîm ... wəlōʾ yitbōšāšû. Q: in the garden Adam is promised he will not be naked, inna laka allā tajūʿa fīhā wa-lā taʿrā. Nakedness is innocence in Gen and a deprivation the garden protects from in Q.

passages.note: How God made the human mate, and for what purpose [divergence between the texts] (Purpose of the mate: Gen ʿēzer kə-neḡdô (a help fit for him), and the woman built from the rib (ha-ṣṣēlāʿ) of the one man. leads.title: Second creation account, Eden, and the making of woman ↔ One soul, the wombs, orphans' property and the bride-gift

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/06-hb-quran.yaml): divergence. Placement of the 'test'. Gen opens with it, wə-hā-ʾĕlōhîm nissâ ʾeṯ-ʾaḇrāhām, so the reader knows from the start that it is a trial. Q names it only after the rescue: inna hādhā la-huwa l-balāʾu l-mubīn. Gen's closing reason, kî ʿattâ yāḏaʿtî kî-yərēʾ ʾĕlōhîm ʾattâ (now I know, 22:12), has no counterpart: in Q God does not come to know. How the command comes. Gen: direct divine speech, qaḥ-nāʾ ʾeṯ-binḵā ... wə-lek-ləḵā ʾel-ʾereṣ ha-mmōriyyâ wə-haʿălēhû šām lə-ʿōlâ (a burnt offering at a named place). Q: a dream reported by the father, innī arā fī l-manāmi annī adhbaḥuka (I see in sleep that I slaughter you), with no place, no mountain and no ʿōlâ. Q's dhabaḥa is cognate with Hebrew zāḇaḥ, while Gen uses ʿōlâ and liš-ḥōṭ (22:10). Who the son is. Gen names him three times over: ʾeṯ-binḵā ʾeṯ-yəḥîḏəḵā ʾăšer-ʾāhaḇtā ʾeṯ-yiṣḥāq. Q has only bi-ghulāmin ḥalīm (a forbearing boy) and announces Isaac only after the episode, wa-basharnāhu bi-Isḥāqa nabiyyan mina ṣ-ṣāliḥīn (37:112). This leaves the victim unnamed, and many exegetes read him as Ishmael. The 'only' (yāḥîḏ) son of Gen is not said. Who speaks, and what the son knows. Gen: Isaac does not know. He asks hinnēh hā-ʾēš wə-hā-ʿēṣîm wə-ʾayyēh ha-śśeh lə-ʿōlâ, and Abraham gives the veiled answer ʾĕlōhîm yirʾeh-lô ha-śśeh ... bənî. Q: the father tells him openly and asks his view, fa-nẓur mādhā tarā, and the son consents, yā-abati fʿal mā tuʾmaru sa-tajidunī in shāʾa llāhu mina ṣ-ṣābirīn. The address pair ʾāḇî / bənî matches yā-abati / yā-bunayya. Isaac's silence becomes the son's active submission. The act. Gen: wood laid on Isaac, fire and knife, an altar built, wa-yyaʿăqōḏ ʾeṯ-yiṣḥāq bənô wa-yyāśem ʾōṯô ʿal-ha-mmizbēaḥ mi-mmaʿal lā-ʿēṣîm, knife raised. Q: fa-lammā aslamā wa-tallahu li-l-jabīn, both 'submitted' and he laid him on his brow. No binding (ʿăqēḏâ), no altar, no wood, no fire and no three-day journey. The decisive word is the dual aslamā (both of them submitted). Who stops it, and why. Gen: wa-yyiqrāʾ ʾēlâw malʾaḵ YHWH min-ha-ššāmayim ... ʾaḇrāhām ʾaḇrāhām wa-yyōʾmer hinnēnî; ʾal-tišlaḥ yāḏəḵā ʾel-ha-nnaʿar, because Abraham fears God. Q: wa-nādaynāhu an yā-Ibrāhīmu qad ṣaddaqta r-ruʾyā. God calls in the first person plural, with no angel and no hinnēnî. The reason is that Abraham has already fulfilled the dream, not a prohibition.

Shared motifs, rarest first: God commands a father to sacrifice his son [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); Who the son to be sacrificed is and how he is named [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); What the son to be sacrificed knows and says [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); Father binds his son on the altar and lifts the knife (weight 6.7); The father lays the son down for the sacrifice [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); What is offered in place of the son, and who provides it [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); A ram caught in a thicket is sacrificed in place of the son (weight 6.7); The reward and blessing after the averted sacrifice [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); An angel calls from heaven to stop the sacrifice at the last moment (weight 6.7); Who stops the sacrifice of the son, and why [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); God commands a father to sacrifice his son (weight 6.7); God tests the patriarch's obedience (weight 6.3); God tests the patriarch's obedience [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.3). Pair score 86.2.

Only in The binding of Isaac (Aqedah): The son to be sacrificed is called the only, beloved son; Place of sacrifice named 'YHWH will see/provide' on the mount of the LORD; Son asks his father where the sacrificial lamb is; The son carries the wood for his own sacrifice; Three-day journey to the mountain of sacrifice; Descendants will possess the gate of their enemies; Called by name, the hero answers 'Here I am' (hineni); All families of the earth will be blessed through the patriarch; God swears by himself; Descendants promised to be as countless as the dust, stars or sand.

Only in Abraham's dream and the near-sacrifice of his son: God ransomed the son with a great sacrifice (dhibh 'azim); When both had submitted he laid him on his forehead (talla-hu li-l-jabin); The father sees in a dream that he is sacrificing his son; The son of the sacrifice is not named; Isaac's birth is announced only after the episode (read as Ishmael by many exegetes); Lot believes in Abraham, who declares 'I am emigrating to my Lord'; The son, consulted by his father, consents: 'Father, do what you are commanded; you will find me patient'; Refrain 'We left for him among later generations: Peace upon X... thus we reward those who do good'; A barren wife is told by a divine messenger that she will bear a son; A divine messenger announces a son's birth and gives his name.

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml): divergence, echo. Q 2:35 wa-lā taqrabā hādhihi sh-shajarata 'do not come near this tree' is God's own wording; in Genesis the extension is the woman's addition: Gen 3:3 lōʾ tōʾkĕlû mimmennû wĕ-lōʾ tiggĕʿû bô 'nor touch it', which God had not said (2:17). Gen 3:1, 3:13 ha-nnāḥāš hāyâ ʿārûm ... ha-nnāḥāš hiššîʾanî: a cunning serpent deceives the woman, who eats first and gives to the man (3:6); Q 2:36 fa-azallahumā sh-shayṭānu ʿanhā: Satan makes both slip (dual). No serpent, no woman eating first, no woman as channel of the sin. Gen 3:23-24 wa-yšallĕḥēhû YHWH ʾĕlōhîm ... wa-ygāreš ʾet hā-ʾādām, with cherubim and a flaming sword guarding the tree of life: God drives the man out; Q 2:36 fa-akhrajahumā mimmā kānā fīhi: Satan is the subject who 'brought them out', then God's ihbiṭū 'go down' (2:36, 2:38), addressed to a plural. No cherubim, no tree of life. Gen 3:15 wĕ-ʾêbâ ʾāšît bênkā û-bên hā-ʾiššâ û-bên zarʿăkā û-bên zarʿāh: enmity between serpent and woman and their offspring; Q 2:36 ihbiṭū baʿḍukum li-baʿḍin ʿaduwwun: 'some of you enemies to others' among those sent down. The same decree of enmity (ʾêbâ / ʿaduww) at the expulsion, with the serpent gone. Gen 3:17-19 ʾărûrâ hā-ʾădāmâ baʿăbûrekā bĕ-ʿiṣṣābôn tōʾkălennâ ... ʿad šûbĕkā ʾel hā-ʾădāmâ: cursed ground, toil and death; Q 2:36 wa-lakum fī l-arḍi mustaqarrun wa-matāʿun ilā ḥīn: on earth an abode and provision for a time. The curses on ground, woman and serpent are left out; the earth is a lodging and a time limit, not a curse. The ending changes. Gen 3:12 hā-ʾiššâ ʾăšer nātattâ ʿimmādî hîʾ nātĕnâ-llî min hā-ʿēṣ wā-ʾōkēl: the man blames the woman (and God who gave her), with no repentance or pardon; Q 2:37 fa-talaqqā ādamu min rabbihi kalimātin fa-tāba ʿalayhi innahu huwa t-tawwābu r-raḥīm: Adam receives words and God turns to him in forgiveness before the descent. The Quran adds a reconciliation Genesis does not have.

Shared motifs, rarest first: The first man's response after the transgression in the garden (blame or repentance) [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); The tempter in the garden [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); Enmity decreed at the expulsion from the garden [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); The human condition on earth after the expulsion [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); First humans expelled from the garden [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.3); God speaks in the plural (us, our) as if to a divine council (weight 6.0); First humans expelled from the garden (weight 6.0); A cunning serpent persuades the woman to eat the forbidden fruit (weight 6.0); A tree of knowledge whose fruit is forbidden (weight 5.8). Pair score 56.8.

Only in The serpent, the eating, the curses and the expulsion: Each accused shifts blame to another (man to woman, woman to serpent); First woman named as mother of all living; God heard walking in the garden in the breeze of the day; Humans gain divine knowledge and God fears they will also gain immortality; Woman punished with pain in childbirth and subordination to husband; The woman eats first and gives the fruit to her husband; Adam receives words from his Lord and God turns to him in forgiveness [divergence between the texts]; Cherubim and a flaming turning sword guard the way to the tree of life; Eating opens their eyes and they know they are naked [divergence between the texts]; How the first couple answer God after eating: shifting the blame or confessing [divergence between the texts]; God makes garments of skin for the first couple; God makes garments of skin for the first couple [divergence between the texts]; and 18 more.

Only in Adam, the angels and Iblis: God teaches Adam all the names and he recites them to the angels, who cannot; The expelled are told 'Go down, enemies to one another' with a dwelling and provision on earth for a time; God announces to the angels he will place a vicegerent (khalifa) on earth; The first man names the animals; Adam receives words from his Lord and God turns to him in forgiveness; Angels object that the new human will corrupt the earth and shed blood while they praise God; The first man and the names of the creatures [divergence between the texts]; The tree forbidden to the first humans [divergence between the texts]; The garden given to the first humans to live and eat in [divergence between the texts]; God speaks to heavenly beings about making man [divergence between the texts]; The office given to humans on earth at creation [divergence between the texts]; Whoever sheds human blood, by man shall his blood be shed, because humans bear God's image; and 4 more.

leads.title: The serpent, the eating, the curses and the expulsion ↔ Adam's forgetting, Iblis, the tree of immortality and the descent
leads.summary: These two units share 11 motifs: eating opens their eyes and they know they are naked [divergence between the texts], the tempter offers 'the tree of immortality and a kingdom that never decays' [divergence between the texts], adam receives words from his lord and god turns to him in forgiveness [divergence between the texts], eating opens their eyes and they know they are naked….

passages.note: Eating opens their eyes and they know they are naked [divergence between the texts] (wattōʾkal wattittēn gam-ləʾîšāh ... wayyōʾkal wattippāqaḥnâ ʿênê šənêhem wayyēdəʿû kî ʿêrummim hēm wayyitpərû ʿălēh təʾēnâ; fa-akalā minhā fa-badat lahumā sawʾātuhumā wa-ṭafiqā yakhṣifāni ʿalayhimā min waraqi l-janna. Gen: wəhannāḥāš hāyâ ʿārûm ... wayyōʾmer ʾel-hāʾiššâ, a clever beast addressing the woman. Q: fa-waswasa ilayhi sh-shayṭānu qāla yā Ādamu, Satan, already marked as enemy after refusing to bow (inna hādhā ʿaduwwun laka wa-li-zawjik), addressing Adam. The serpent and the woman as first addressee drop out. What the tree offers. Gen: knowledge, wihyîtem kēʾlōhîm yōdəʿê ṭôb wārāʿ; immortality belongs to a second tree that God guards, pen-yišlaḥ yādô wəlāqaḥ gam mēʿēṣ haḥayyîm wəʾākal wāḥay ləʿōlām. Gen's two trees merge into one, and the lure becomes eternal life and kingship, not godlike knowledge. wattōʾkal wattittēn gam-ləʾîšāh ... wayyōʾkal wattippāqaḥnâ ʿênê šənêhem wayyēdəʿû kî ʿêrummim hēm wayyitpərû ʿălēh təʾēnâ; fa-akalā minhā fa-badat lahumā sawʾātuhumā wa-ṭafiqā yakhṣifāni ʿalayhimā min waraqi l-janna. Same sequence: eating, exposed nakedness, sewing leaves. Changes: in Gen the woman eats first and hands it on, while Q has both eat and puts the blame on Adam (wa-ʿaṣā Ādamu rabbahu fa-ghawā); fig leaves become just 'leaves of the garden'. Gen goes from the eating straight to curses, ʾărûrâ hāʾădāmâ baʿăbûrekā ... kî-ʿāpār ʾattâ wəʾel-ʿāpār tāšûb, with no repentance and no forgiveness. Adam's sin is forgiven, not cursed, and no death sentence follows. wəʾêbâ ʾāšît bênkā ûbên hāʾiššâ ûbên zarʿăkā ûbên zarʿāh ... wayəšalləḥēhû ... waygāreš ʾet-hāʾādām; qāla hbiṭā minhā jamīʿan baʿḍukum li-baʿḍin ʿaduww. Q's enmity is among those sent down, and Q adds a promise of guidance, fa-immā yaʾtiyannakum minnī hudan fa-mani ttabaʿa hudāya fa-lā yaḍillu wa-lā yashqā.

Only in The serpent, the eating, the curses and the expulsion: Each accused shifts blame to another (man to woman, woman to serpent); First woman named as mother of all living; God heard walking in the garden in the breeze of the day; Humans gain divine knowledge and God fears they will also gain immortality; Woman punished with pain in childbirth and subordination to husband; The woman eats first and gives the fruit to her husband; Cherubim and a flaming turning sword guard the way to the tree of life; Enmity decreed at the expulsion from the garden [divergence between the texts]; How the first couple answer God after eating: shifting the blame or confessing [divergence between the texts]; The first man's response after the transgression in the garden (blame or repentance) [divergence between the texts]; God makes garments of skin for the first couple; God makes garments of skin for the first couple [divergence between the texts]; and 16 more.

Only in Adam's forgetting, Iblis, the tree of immortality and the descent: God made a covenant with Adam, but he forgot and lacked resolve; In the garden Adam will not hunger, be naked, thirst or suffer the sun's heat; Whoever turned from God's reminder is raised blind on judgment day: as he forgot the signs, so he is forgotten; The tempter offers 'the tree of immortality and a kingdom that never decays'; God made a covenant with Adam, but he forgot and lacked resolve [divergence between the texts]; Adam receives words from his Lord and God turns to him in forgiveness; God commands the angels to prostrate to Adam; all do except Iblis, who refuses; Satan whispers (waswasa) to tempt humans; In the garden Adam will not hunger, be naked, thirst or suffer the sun's heat [divergence between the texts]; God plants a garden (Eden) in the east and places the first human there.

passages.note: The ground of a husband's authority over his wife [divergence between the texts] (Gen 3:16 wĕ-ʾel ʾîšēk tĕšûqātēk wĕ-hûʾ yimšol bāk: the husband's rule over the wife as part of the curse after the fall; Q 4:34 ar-rijālu qawwāmūna ʿalā n-nisāʾi bi-mā faḍḍala llāhu baʿḍahum ʿalā baʿḍin wa-bi-mā anfaqū min amwālihim: men are maintainers of women by God's preference and because they spend their wealth. evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/02-hb-quran.yaml): divergence, echo, parallel. A different tempter. Gen: wə-han-nāḥāš hāyāh ʿārûm mik-kōl ḥayyat haś-śādeh, an animal speaking to the woman. Q: fa-waswasa lahumā l-shayṭānu, the devil already expelled in 7:13, whispering to both, and he swears an oath (wa-qāsamahumā innī lakumā la-mina l-nāṣiḥīna). There is no serpent and no curse to crawl on the belly (Gen 3:14). What the tempter promises. Gen: wi-hyîtem kē-ʾlōhîm yōdəʿê ṭôv wā-rāʿ, and God himself confirms the danger: hēn hā-ʾādām hāyāh kə-ʾaḥad mimmennû ... wā-ḥay lə-ʿōlām. Q: mā nahākumā rabbukumā ʿan hādhihi l-shajarati illā an takūnā malakayni aw takūnā mina l-khālidīna. 'Like gods knowing good and evil' becomes 'angels or immortals', a lie (bi-ghurūrin). Q has no divine admission that the humans have become 'like one of us'. Who is tempted and eats first. Gen: the serpent talks to the woman (wa-yyōʾmer ʾel-hā-ʾiššāh), she eats first and gives to her husband (wat-tittēn gam-lə-ʾîšāh ʿimmāh wa-yyōʾkhal). Q uses the dual throughout: wa-zawjuka ... fa-kulā ... wa-lā taqrabā ... waswasa lahumā ... fa-lammā dhāqā l-shajarata. The couple acts together and the woman is not singled out. Gen 3:3, the woman's paraphrase: wə-lōʾ tiggəʿû bô, 'nor touch it', a fence God had not said. Q, God's own command: wa-lā taqrabā hādhihi l-shajarata, 'do not come near'. passages.note: A food taboo of Israel (Jacob) before the Torah [divergence between the texts] (Gen 32:33 ʿal kēn lōʾ yōʾkĕlû bĕnê yiśrāʾēl ʾet gîd ha-nnāšeh ... kî nāgaʿ bĕ-kap yerek yaʿăqōb: the sons of Israel do not eat the sinew because the divine wrestler struck Jacob's thigh, a custom 'to this day'; Q 3:93 kullu ṭ-ṭaʿāmi kāna ḥillan li-banī isrāʾīla illā mā ḥarrama isrāʾīlu ʿalā nafsihi min qabli an tunazzala t-tawrātu: all food was lawful to the Children of Israel except what Israel (Jacob) forbade himself before the Torah. A pre-Sinai food taboo tied to Jacob/Israel in both; in Genesis it comes from God's touch and binds the descendants, in the Quran Israel imposes it on himself, and the point is that the later Torah food laws were not original (fa-ʾtū bi-t-tawrāti fa-tlūhā).)
