Only in One soul, the wombs, orphans' property and the bride-gift: Those who devour orphans' property devour fire into their bellies; Fear God, by whom you ask of one another, and the wombs (kinship ties, al-arḥām); Kin, orphans and the poor present at the division of an estate are given something from it; Property is not handed to the feeble-minded (sufahāʾ); they are fed and clothed from it; Women as well as men receive a fixed share of what parents and kin leave; The husband gives the bride her marriage gift (ṣaduqa, ajr) as her own; she may freely remit part; God hears the cry of the oppressed widow and orphan and punishes measure for measure; How the first woman was made [divergence between the texts]; Do not enter the fields of the fatherless, for their redeemer (go'el) is strong and will plead their cause; A man may marry two, three or four wives, or only one if he fears injustice; A man who seduces an unbetrothed virgin must marry her or pay the bride-price; First woman made from the man's rib or side while he sleeps; and 4 more.

Pair score 38.5.

Only in Generations of Esau, Horite chiefs, kings of Edom: Amalek's ancestor is born to a concubine in Esau's line; Brothers separate because the land cannot support both their herds; While herding his father's asses, a man discovers 'the yemim' in the wilderness (hot springs or mules).

Only in Sons of Ishmael, Keturah and Esau; the Seirite chiefs and kings of Edom: Abraham's sons by the concubine Keturah (Midian, Sheba, Dedan...); Ishmael promised to father twelve princes and a great nation; Ishmael's twelve sons as Arabian tribes (Nebaioth, Kedar, Dumah, Tema...); A lone daughter is named in a male genealogy (Dinah, Serah).

leads.title: Joseph's dreams, the pit and the sale to Egypt ↔ Joseph and his brothers (Surah 12, full read)
leads.summary: These two units share 21 motifs: father rebukes the hero for his dream but keeps it in mind [divergence between the texts], hero bought by an egyptian official [divergence between the texts], hero cast into a pit or well [divergence between the texts], a wild animal is blamed for the hero's death [divergence between the texts]….

Only in Joseph's dreams, the pit and the sale to Egypt: Brothers sit down to eat bread after casting their brother into the pit; Hero's story begins when he is seventeen; Young hero brings bad reports of his brothers to their father; An anonymous man finds the wandering hero in the field and directs him; Dream of the brothers' sheaves bowing to the hero's sheaf; Father believes the hero is dead and refuses comfort; Father rebukes the hero for his dream but keeps it in mind; Father himself sends the hero to his brothers; Evidence presented with the formula 'Please recognize (haker na)' whose is this; Father gives the hero a special garment; Called by name, the hero answers 'Here I am' (hineni).

Only in Joseph and his brothers (Surah 12, full read): Brothers tell their father to ask the town and the caravan to confirm their story; Brothers claim the accused youth's absent brother (the hero) had also stolen before; Famished brothers bring poor goods and ask the disguised hero for alms; The brothers confess 'we were sinners' once the hero is revealed and ask their father to pray for them; Father keeps lamenting his lost son for years until his sons fear he will waste away; The patriarch claims to know from God what his sons do not know; Father promises his repentant sons to ask God's forgiveness for them later; Fleeing the seductress, the hero and the woman find her husband at the door; The bereaved father answers with 'beautiful patience' (sabr jamil) and reliance on God; The hero could not have kept his brother under the king's law, so a stratagem is needed; The hero declares he follows the religion of his fathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob; A camel-load is promised to whoever brings back the missing royal cup, with a guarantor; and 88 more.

Only in Joseph's dreams, the pit and the sale to Egypt: Brothers sit down to eat bread after casting their brother into the pit; Hero's story begins when he is seventeen; Young hero brings bad reports of his brothers to their father; An anonymous man finds the wandering hero in the field and directs him; Hero bought by an Egyptian official [divergence between the texts]; Brothers, out of envy, plot to kill the hero [divergence between the texts]; Hero cast into a pit or well [divergence between the texts]; Dream of the brothers' sheaves bowing to the hero's sheaf; Father believes the hero is dead and refuses comfort; Father believes the hero is dead and refuses comfort [divergence between the texts]; Father loves the hero more than his brothers [divergence between the texts]; Father rebukes the hero for his dream but keeps it in mind; and 10 more.

Only in Joseph in the Quran (Surah 12): Brothers persuade the reluctant father to send the hero with them; Brothers come to their father at night, weeping; God reassures the hero in the pit; Hero reveals himself to the youngest brother first; Father does not believe the brothers' story; Father warns the hero not to tell his dream to his brothers; Hero's garment restores the father's sight; Hero refuses release until his innocence is established; Hero prays to die in submission and join the righteous; Hero preaches monotheism to his fellow prisoners; Hero prays that prison is preferable to sin; The husband recognizes his wife's guilt; and 47 more.

Only in Judah and Tamar: A woman accused of harlotry is sentenced to be burned; Man spills his seed on the ground to avoid raising offspring for his dead brother and is struck dead; God kills a man for unspecified wickedness; A kid of the goats promised as a harlot's hire; Seal, cord and staff left as a pledge, later used as proof of paternity; A roadside harlot referred to as a qedeshah ('consecrated woman'); Midwife ties a scarlet thread on the hand of the twin who emerges first; Man acknowledges the wronged woman: 'She is more righteous than I'; Twins contend at birth over who emerges first; A widow veils herself, sits by the road and is taken for a harlot by her father-in-law; Father-in-law withholds his youngest son from the widow, fearing he too will die; Evidence presented with the formula 'Please recognize (haker na)' whose is this; and 2 more.

Only in Divorce before consummation; the prophet's marriages; the curtain and the cloaks: A wife divorced before consummation owes no waiting period ('idda); give her a gift and release her gracefully; Enter the prophet's houses only when invited to a meal and leave after; ask his wives from behind a curtain (hijab); Special marriage rules for the prophet: lawful wives, captives, named cousins who emigrated, and a woman who gives herself; afterwards no more wives; God and his angels bless (yusalluna 'ala) the prophet; believers are told to bless him and greet him with peace; How a husband sends away a divorced wife (document, gift, waiting period) [divergence between the texts]; Limits on how many wives the leader may take [contrast between the texts]; Limits on how many wives the leader may take [divergence between the texts]; Believing women are to draw their outer cloaks (jalabib) over themselves so they are recognized and not harmed; The prophet's wives are the mothers of the believers and may not be married after him; The way (sunna) of God with those who passed before: you will find no change in God's way; King must not multiply horses, wives or silver and gold, nor return the people to Egypt.

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/04-hb-quran.yaml): divergence, parallel. wayhî YHWH ʾet-yôsēp wayhî ʾîš maṣlîaḥ; wa-ka-dhālika makkannā li-Yūsufa fī l-arḍ ... ātaynāhu ḥukman wa-ʿilmā: God's favor rests on the slave. wa-rāwadathu llatī huwa fī baytihā ʿan nafsihi wa-ghallaqati l-abwāba wa-qālat hayta lak; wattiśśāʾ ʾēšet-ʾădōnāyw ʾet-ʿênêhā ... šikbâ ʿimmî, wəʾên ʾîš mēʾanšê habbayit šām: the master's wife, alone with him in the house. maʿādha llāhi innahu rabbī aḥsana mathwāy; hēn ʾădōnî lōʾ-yādaʿ ʾittî ... wəḥāṭāʾtî lēʾlōhîm: loyalty to the master and to God. Q's rabbī can mean either. Addition. Gen: Joseph refuses at once and every day, wayəmāʾēn ... wəlōʾ-šāmaʿ ʾēlêhā. Q: wa-la-qad hammat bihi wa-hamma bihā lawlā an raʾā burhāna rabbih: he was on the point of yielding, and only God's sign stops him. Reversal of what the garment proves. Gen: she seizes his garment (wattitpəśēhû bəbigdô), he leaves it in her hand, and she keeps it to accuse him (wattannaḥ bigdô ʾeṣlāh). Q: she tears his shirt from behind (qaddat qamīṣahu min dubur), and the tear clears him: in kāna qamīṣuhu qudda min dubur fa-kadhabat. Gen: the master believes his wife, wayyiḥar ʾappô, and jails Joseph at once. Q: the master finds both at the door (wa-alfayā sayyidahā ladā l-bāb), accepts the shirt-test of a witness min ahlihā, and blames her: innahu min kaydikunna inna kaydakunna ʿaẓīm ... wa-staghfirī li-dhanbiki. Gen's ʾîš ʿibrî ... ləṣaḥeq bānû (the foreign slave) is absent.
Passages are shown for the 10 rarest of 13 shared motifs; the full list follows.

Shared motifs, rarest first: The woman falsely accuses the hero of assault [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); Hero's garment becomes evidence in the seduction episode [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); Hero nearly yields but a sign from God stops him [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); Hero thrown into prison [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); God's favor rests on the hero while he is a slave or prisoner (weight 6.0); Hero's garment becomes evidence in the seduction episode (weight 6.0); Hero refuses, citing loyalty to his master and to God (weight 6.0); Seduction attempt when the two are alone in the house (weight 5.8); Hero thrown into prison (weight 5.8); The master's wife tries to seduce the hero (weight 5.8); The woman falsely accuses the hero of assault (weight 5.8); Hero bought by an Egyptian official (weight 5.8); Hero's beauty is remarked on (weight 4.9). Pair score 78.5.

Only in Joseph in Potiphar's house and in prison: The jailer puts all the prisoners in the hero's charge; God blesses a foreigner's house for the sake of the righteous slave; Master entrusts his whole household to the hero.

Only in Joseph and his brothers (Surah 12, full read): Brothers tell their father to ask the town and the caravan to confirm their story; Brothers claim the accused youth's absent brother (the hero) had also stolen before; Famished brothers bring poor goods and ask the disguised hero for alms; The brothers confess 'we were sinners' once the hero is revealed and ask their father to pray for them; Father keeps lamenting his lost son for years until his sons fear he will waste away; The patriarch claims to know from God what his sons do not know; Father promises his repentant sons to ask God's forgiveness for them later; Fleeing the seductress, the hero and the woman find her husband at the door; The bereaved father answers with 'beautiful patience' (sabr jamil) and reliance on God; The hero could not have kept his brother under the king's law, so a stratagem is needed; The hero declares he follows the religion of his fathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob; A camel-load is promised to whoever brings back the missing royal cup, with a guarantor; and 96 more.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: God's favor rests on the hero while he is a slave or prisoner (weight 6.0); Hero's garment becomes evidence in the seduction episode (weight 6.0); Hero refuses, citing loyalty to his master and to God (weight 6.0); Seduction attempt when the two are alone in the house (weight 5.8); Hero thrown into prison (weight 5.8); The master's wife tries to seduce the hero (weight 5.8); The woman falsely accuses the hero of assault (weight 5.8); Hero bought by an Egyptian official (weight 5.8); Hero's beauty is remarked on (weight 4.9). Pair score 51.8.

Only in Joseph in Potiphar's house and in prison: The jailer puts all the prisoners in the hero's charge; God blesses a foreigner's house for the sake of the righteous slave; The woman falsely accuses the hero of assault [divergence between the texts]; Hero's garment becomes evidence in the seduction episode [divergence between the texts]; Hero thrown into prison [divergence between the texts]; Hero nearly yields but a sign from God stops him [divergence between the texts]; Master entrusts his whole household to the hero.

Only in Joseph in the Quran (Surah 12): Brothers persuade the reluctant father to send the hero with them; Brothers come to their father at night, weeping; God reassures the hero in the pit; Hero reveals himself to the youngest brother first; Father does not believe the brothers' story; Father warns the hero not to tell his dream to his brothers; Hero's garment restores the father's sight; Hero refuses release until his innocence is established; Hero prays to die in submission and join the righteous; Hero preaches monotheism to his fellow prisoners; Hero prays that prison is preferable to sin; The husband recognizes his wife's guilt; and 48 more.

leads.title: Cain and Abel ↔ The two sons of Adam, the raven, and whoever saves one life
leads.summary: These two units share 7 motifs: god accepts one brother's offering and rejects the other's [divergence between the texts], what the earth does with the murdered brother: takes in his blood, or hides his corpse [divergence between the texts], a brother kills his brother in the first murder [divergence between the texts], the first murderer's lament after the deed [divergence between the texts]….

passages.note: God accepts one brother's offering and rejects the other's [divergence between the texts] (Gen names Qayin and Hevel, specifies the gifts (pərî hā-ʾădāmāh against bəkhōrôt ṣōʾnô û-mē-ḥelvēhen), and gives no reason for God's choice (wa-yyišaʿ ... lōʾ šāʿāh). Q: the brothers are unnamed (ibnay Ādama), the gifts unspecified (qarrabā qurbānan), and the reason is spoken by the victim: innamā yataqabbalu llāhu mina l-muttaqīna.)

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/02-hb-quran.yaml): divergence. Gen names Qayin and Hevel, specifies the gifts (pərî hā-ʾădāmāh against bəkhōrôt ṣōʾnô û-mē-ḥelvēhen), and gives no reason for God's choice (wa-yyišaʿ ... lōʾ šāʿāh). Q: the brothers are unnamed (ibnay Ādama), the gifts unspecified (qarrabā qurbānan), and the reason is spoken by the victim: innamā yataqabbalu llāhu mina l-muttaqīna. A change of speaker. In Gen, God warns Cain before the murder: lāmmāh ḥārāh lākh ... lap-petaḥ ḥaṭṭāʾt rōvēṣ wə-ʾēlêkhā təšûqātô wə-ʾattāh timšol-bô. In Q God is silent and the victim gives the warning: laʾin basaṭta ilayya yadaka ... mā ana bi-bāsiṭin yadiya ilayka ... innī akhāfu llāha rabba l-ʿālamīna. The crouching desire comes back as fa-ṭawwaʿat lahu nafsuhu qatla akhīhi. MT: wa-yyōʾmer Qayin ʾel-Hevel ʾāḥîw, with the speech missing, then wa-yyāqom ... wa-yyahargēhû. Q supplies the dialogue: qāla la-aqtulannaka, and Abel's reply. Then fa-qatalahu fa-aṣbaḥa mina l-khāsirīna. cf. (not a match) Targum Neofiti and Pseudo-Jonathan Gen 4:8, which also supply a dispute in the field. What the earth does differs. Gen: the ground opens its mouth to take the blood, and the blood cries out (qôl dəmê ʾāḥîkhā ṣōʿăqîm ʾēlay min-hā-ʾădāmāh ... ʾăšer pāṣətāh ʾet-pîhā), so the crime is exposed. Q: God sends a raven digging in the earth (ghurāban yabḥathu fī l-arḍi) to show how to hide (yuwārī) the brother's corpse (sawʾata akhīhi). Gen has no burial; Q has no interrogation ('ê Hevel), curse, wandering or mark. cf. (not a match) Pirqe de-Rabbi Eliezer 21 (raven and burial). The murderer's lament. Gen: gādôl ʿăwōnî minnəśōʾ ... nāʿ wā-nād, a complaint about the punishment. Q: yā waylatā aʿajaztu an akūna mithla hādhā l-ghurābi fa-uwāriya sawʾata akhī fa-aṣbaḥa mina l-nādimīna, shame at being outdone by a raven, and remorse. Q has no punishment on earth; it ends in remorse.

Shared motifs, rarest first: God accepts one brother's offering and rejects the other's [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); What the earth does with the murdered brother: takes in his blood, or hides his corpse [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); A brother kills his brother in the first murder [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); The first murderer's lament after the deed [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); God accepts one brother's offering and rejects the other's (weight 6.7); Before the first murder the killer is warned (by God or by the victim) [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); A brother kills his brother in the first murder (weight 6.3). Pair score 46.4.

Only in Cain and Abel: Murderer evades God's question about his brother's whereabouts; The earth opens its mouth to receive spilled blood; Rivalry between a farmer brother and a shepherd brother; Firstborn animals and their fat offered to God; Exile dwells in the land of Nod east of Eden; God puts a protective sign on a murderer so no one kills him; Murderer condemned to be a restless wanderer, the ground withholding its yield; Sin personified as a beast crouching at the door, desiring the man; What the earth does with the murdered brother: takes in his blood, or hides his corpse [divergence between the texts]; A brother kills his brother in the first murder [divergence between the texts]; Parents' words to God about the child he gave them [divergence between the texts]; The first murderer's lament after the deed [divergence between the texts]; and 8 more.

Only in The earthquake: the earth tells its news: Whoever does an atom's weight (mithqal dharra) of good will see it, and an atom's weight of evil will see it; At the end the earth is stretched out, casts out what is in it (its burdens) and empties itself; Heaven and earth called as witnesses against the people; On that day a great earthquake shakes the land; fish, birds, beasts, creeping things and all humans quake before God, mountains are thrown down and every wall falls.

leads.summary: These two units share 1 motifs: where iron and iron-working come from [divergence between the texts].

passages.note: Where iron and iron-working come from [divergence between the texts] (Where iron comes from. Genesis: tûḇal qayin lōṭēš kol ḥōrēš nəḥōšeṯ û-ḇarzel (iron-working begins with a descendant of Cain, a human culture hero). Quran: wa-anzalnā l-ḥadīda fīhi baʾsun shadīdun wa-manāfiʿu li-n-nās (God sent iron down, with great might and benefits). A human craft from Cain's line becomes God's gift sent down beside the Book and the Balance. cf. 1 Enoch 8:1 (Asael teaches metalworking).)

Genesis: tûḇal qayin lōṭēš kol ḥōrēš nəḥōšeṯ û-ḇarzel (iron-working begins with a descendant of Cain, a human culture hero). Quran: wa-anzalnā l-ḥadīda fīhi baʾsun shadīdun wa-manāfiʿu li-n-nās (God sent iron down, with great might and benefits). A human craft from Cain's line becomes God's gift sent down beside the Book and the Balance. cf. 1 Enoch 8:1 (Asael teaches metalworking).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Where iron and iron-working come from [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7). Pair score 6.7.

Only in Cain's line, the first city, culture heroes and the Song of Lamech: Named ancestors are originators of crafts (herding, music, metalwork); First city built and named after the founder's son; First man to take two wives; Boast-song of Lamech to his wives about killing a man for wounding him; Vengeance multiplied sevenfold (or seventy-sevenfold).

Only in Life like withering plants; the Garden as wide as heaven and earth; every calamity written; iron sent down; Jesus' followers and invented monasticism: The People of the Book should know they have no power over God's bounty; bounty is in God's hand for whom he wills; Believers in the messenger receive a double portion (kiflayn) of God's mercy and a light to walk by; God put compassion and mercy in the hearts of those who followed Jesus; God sent down iron, with mighty force and benefits for people; God gave Jesus son of Mary the Gospel (al-Injil); Worldly life is play, adornment, boasting and rivalry in wealth and children, like rain whose growth pleases the sowers, then withers yellow and becomes chaff; God sent down the Book with the truth and the Balance (al-mizan); Christians are nearest in affection to the believers because they have priests and monks and are not proud; So that you do not grieve over what escapes you nor exult over what he gives you; A double portion (k-p-l) from God [divergence between the texts]; No calamity befalls the earth or yourselves but it is in a Book before God brings it into being; Race to forgiveness and a Garden whose breadth is as the breadth of heaven and earth; and 7 more.

Q makes them two fatayān and drops their offices (śar hammašqîm, śar hāʾôpîm) and the three branches and baskets. Gen: one sentence, hălôʾ lēʾlōhîm pitrōnîm. The dream scene becomes a call to monotheism. fa-yasqī rabbahu khamran wa-ammā l-ākharu fa-yuṣlabu fa-taʾkulu ṭ-ṭayru min raʾsih; wətālâ ʾôtəkā ʿal-ʿēṣ wəʾākal hāʿôp ʾet-bəśārəkā. Q drops the three-day term and the pun yiśśāʾ parʿōh ʾet-rōʾšəkā. Gen: the cupbearer simply forgets, wəlōʾ-zākar ... wayyiškāḥēhû. Only in Joseph in the Quran (Surah 12): Brothers persuade the reluctant father to send the hero with them; Brothers come to their father at night, weeping; God reassures the hero in the pit; Hero reveals himself to the youngest brother first; Father does not believe the brothers' story; Father warns the hero not to tell his dream to his brothers; Hero's garment restores the father's sight; Hero refuses release until his innocence is established; Hero prays to die in submission and join the righteous; Hero preaches monotheism to his fellow prisoners; Hero prays that prison is preferable to sin; The husband recognizes his wife's guilt; and 51 more.

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/04-hb-quran.yaml): divergence, parallel. sabʿa baqarātin simānin yaʾkuluhunna sabʿun ʿijāfun wa-sabʿa sunbulātin khuḍrin wa-ukhara yābisāt; šebaʿ pārôt ... bərîʾōt bāśār / daqqôt bāśār; šebaʿ šibbŏlîm. The dreamer is al-malik in Q, not Pharaoh, although the Moses story in Q has Firʿawn. Gen: kol-ḥarṭummê miṣrayim ... wəʾên-pôtēr ʾôtām: they cannot interpret. Q: they dismiss the dream, aḍghāthu aḥlāmin wa-mā naḥnu bi-taʾwīli l-aḥlāmi bi-ʿālimīn. Gen: Joseph is rushed out at once (wayərîṣuhû min-habbôr waygallaḥ) and interprets before Pharaoh. Q: the freed man (wa-ddakara baʿda umma) goes to Joseph in prison, yā Yūsufu ayyuhā ṣ-ṣiddīq, and Joseph interprets from inside it. Gen: officers collect a fifth (wəḥimmēš ʾet-ʾereṣ miṣrayim) and store bār in the cities. Q: leave the harvest in its ears, fa-dharūhu fī sunbulihi, and Q adds a year of relief that Gen does not have, ʿāmun fīhi yughāthu n-nāsu wa-fīhi yaʿṣirūn. Reversal. Gen: Joseph is hurried from the pit, shaved and changed (wayərîṣuhû ... waygallaḥ wayḥallēp śimlōtāyw). Q: summoned (iʾtūnī bihi), he refuses to leave, irjiʿ ilā rabbika fa-sʾalhu mā bālu n-niswati llātī qaṭṭaʿna aydiyahunn, until the wife confesses, al-āna ḥaṣḥaṣa l-ḥaqq. Gen: Pharaoh appoints him after Joseph advises seeking ʾîš nābôn wəḥākām (ʾattâ tihyeh ʿal-bêtî ... rəʾēh nātattî ʾōtəkā ʿal kol-ʾereṣ miṣrayim), with ring, linen and chariot. Q: Joseph asks for the post himself, ijʿalnī ʿalā khazāʾini l-arḍi innī ḥafīẓun ʿalīm. The king's investiture, the name ṣāpnat paʿnēaḥ and the wife ʾāsnat bat-pôṭî peraʿ (41:45) are left out.
Passages are shown for the 10 rarest of 11 shared motifs; the full list follows.

Shared motifs, rarest first: Plan to store grain in the good years for the famine years [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); Hero placed over the land's storehouses or the kingdom [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); The freed prisoner remembers the hero and recommends him [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); The king's experts cannot interpret the dream [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); Hero refuses release until his innocence is established [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); Plan to store grain in the good years for the famine years (weight 6.0); The freed prisoner remembers the hero and recommends him (weight 6.0); King dreams of seven fat cows eaten by seven lean, and seven green ears and seven dry (weight 6.0); Hero placed over the land's storehouses or the kingdom (weight 5.6); Hero attributes his dream interpretation to God (weight 5.4); The king's experts cannot interpret the dream (weight 5.3). Pair score 67.8.

Only in Pharaoh's dreams and Joseph's elevation: A dream given twice means God has firmly decided and will act soon; Grain stored like the sand of the sea, beyond counting; Hero is thirty when he enters royal service; In a dream the lean devour the fat but remain as lean as before; Prisoner shaved and dressed in new clothes before appearing before the king; Hero names his sons for forgetting his hardship and being fruitful in affliction; A foreign king recognizes 'a man in whom is the spirit of God'; All lands come to Egypt to buy grain from the hero; King gives the foreign hero a new native name; Seven years of plenty followed by seven years of famine; Hero given an Egyptian priest's daughter as wife; King invests the hero with ring, linen and chariot.

Only in Joseph and his brothers (Surah 12, full read): Brothers tell their father to ask the town and the caravan to confirm their story; Brothers claim the accused youth's absent brother (the hero) had also stolen before; Famished brothers bring poor goods and ask the disguised hero for alms; The brothers confess 'we were sinners' once the hero is revealed and ask their father to pray for them; Father keeps lamenting his lost son for years until his sons fear he will waste away; The patriarch claims to know from God what his sons do not know; Father promises his repentant sons to ask God's forgiveness for them later; Fleeing the seductress, the hero and the woman find her husband at the door; The bereaved father answers with 'beautiful patience' (sabr jamil) and reliance on God; The hero could not have kept his brother under the king's law, so a stratagem is needed; The hero declares he follows the religion of his fathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob; A camel-load is promised to whoever brings back the missing royal cup, with a guarantor; and 98 more.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: Plan to store grain in the good years for the famine years (weight 6.0); The freed prisoner remembers the hero and recommends him (weight 6.0); King dreams of seven fat cows eaten by seven lean, and seven green ears and seven dry (weight 6.0); Hero placed over the land's storehouses or the kingdom (weight 5.6); Hero attributes his dream interpretation to God (weight 5.4); The king's experts cannot interpret the dream (weight 5.3). Pair score 34.3.

Only in Pharaoh's dreams and Joseph's elevation: A dream given twice means God has firmly decided and will act soon; Grain stored like the sand of the sea, beyond counting; Hero is thirty when he enters royal service; In a dream the lean devour the fat but remain as lean as before; Prisoner shaved and dressed in new clothes before appearing before the king; Hero names his sons for forgetting his hardship and being fruitful in affliction; A foreign king recognizes 'a man in whom is the spirit of God'; All lands come to Egypt to buy grain from the hero; The king's experts cannot interpret the dream [divergence between the texts]; The freed prisoner remembers the hero and recommends him [divergence between the texts]; Plan to store grain in the good years for the famine years [divergence between the texts]; Hero placed over the land's storehouses or the kingdom [divergence between the texts]; and 5 more.

Only in Joseph in the Quran (Surah 12): Brothers persuade the reluctant father to send the hero with them; Brothers come to their father at night, weeping; God reassures the hero in the pit; Hero reveals himself to the youngest brother first; Father does not believe the brothers' story; Father warns the hero not to tell his dream to his brothers; Hero's garment restores the father's sight; Hero refuses release until his innocence is established; Hero prays to die in submission and join the righteous; Hero preaches monotheism to his fellow prisoners; Hero prays that prison is preferable to sin; The husband recognizes his wife's guilt; and 51 more.

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/04-hb-quran.yaml): divergence, echo. fa-ʿarafahum wa-hum lahu munkirūn; wayyakkirēm wayyitnakkēr ʾălêhem ... wəhēm lōʾ hikkiruhû. Same root n-k-r on both sides, in opposite senses: in Gen Joseph makes himself strange (wayyitnakkēr), in Q the brothers fail to recognize him (munkirūn). Omission of the harshness. Gen: wayədabbēr ʾittām qāšôt, məraggəlîm ʾattem, three days in custody, one brother bound. Q: no spy charge. Joseph is a generous host, a-lā tarawna annī ūfī l-kayla wa-ana khayru l-munzilīn, and the only threat is fa-lā kayla lakum ʿindī. Reversed reaction. Gen: on finding the silver they are terrified, wayyēṣēʾ libbām wayyeḥerdû ... mah-zzōʾt ʿāśâ ʾĕlōhîm lānû. Q: they are glad, yā abānā mā nabghī hādhihi biḍāʿatunā ruddat ilaynā. Q also gives Joseph's motive, laʿallahum yarjiʿūn. Gen: grief and blame, ʾōtî šikkaltem ... lōʾ-yērēd bənî ʿimmākem ... wəhôradtem ʾet-śêbātî bəyāgôn šəʾôlâ. Q: hal āmanukum ʿalayhi illā ka-mā amintukum ʿalā akhīhi min qabl, fa-llāhu khayrun ḥāfiẓan: the father turns to trust in God. Gen: Joseph takes Simeon as hostage on the first journey, wayyiqqaḥ mēʾittām ʾet-šimʿôn wayyeʾĕsōr ʾōtô. Q: on the second journey the eldest stays of his own will after the cup affair, qāla kabīruhum ... fa-lan abraḥa l-arḍa ḥattā yaʾdhana lī abī.
Passages are shown for the 10 rarest of 11 shared motifs; the full list follows.

Shared motifs, rarest first: Their payment is secretly returned in their bags [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); Father refuses at first to send the youngest [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); One brother stays behind in Egypt [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); Hero accuses his brothers of being spies [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); Brothers come for grain and do not recognize the hero (weight 6.0); One brother stays behind in Egypt (weight 6.0); Their payment is secretly returned in their bags (weight 6.0); Hero demands they bring their youngest brother (weight 6.0); Family prostrates before the hero, fulfilling the dream (weight 5.8); A brother or the brothers give the father a pledge for the youngest (weight 5.8); Father refuses at first to send the youngest (weight 5.6). Pair score 67.9.

Only in The brothers' first journey to Egypt: Hero speaks through an interpreter so the others do not know he understands them; Hero swears 'by the life of Pharaoh'; Brothers held in custody for three days; Brothers confess their old crime in front of the victim without knowing he hears them; Hero turns aside or withdraws to weep unseen before his brothers; Hero accuses his brothers of being spies; Father says losing his son will bring his grey hairs down to Sheol in sorrow; Famine forces the family to go down to Egypt.

Only in Joseph and his brothers (Surah 12, full read): Brothers tell their father to ask the town and the caravan to confirm their story; Brothers claim the accused youth's absent brother (the hero) had also stolen before; Famished brothers bring poor goods and ask the disguised hero for alms; The brothers confess 'we were sinners' once the hero is revealed and ask their father to pray for them; Father keeps lamenting his lost son for years until his sons fear he will waste away; The patriarch claims to know from God what his sons do not know; Father promises his repentant sons to ask God's forgiveness for them later; Fleeing the seductress, the hero and the woman find her husband at the door; The bereaved father answers with 'beautiful patience' (sabr jamil) and reliance on God; The hero could not have kept his brother under the king's law, so a stratagem is needed; The hero declares he follows the religion of his fathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob; A camel-load is promised to whoever brings back the missing royal cup, with a guarantor; and 98 more.

Gen: gəbîaʿ hakkesep, the cup in which my lord drinks and wəhûʾ naḥēš yənaḥēš bô (divination), and naḥēš yənaḥēš ʾîš ʾăšer kāmōnî. Q: as-siqāya / ṣuwāʿ al-malik, the king's drinking or measuring vessel, with no divination. Q adds a reward, ḥimlu baʿīrin wa-ana bihi zaʿīm. adhdhana muʾadhdhinun ayyatuhā l-ʿīru innakum la-sāriqūn ... mā kunnā sāriqīn; lāmmâ šillamtem rāʿâ taḥat ṭôbâ ... ḥālîlâ laʿăbādêkā ... wəʾêk nignōb: the pursuit, the charge and the protest of innocence. jazāʾuhu man wujida fī raḥlihi fa-huwa jazāʾuh; ʾăšer yimmāṣēʾ ʾittô ... wāmēt wəgam-ʾănaḥnû nihyeh laʾdōnî laʿăbādîm, reduced to hûʾ yihyeh-llî ʿābed: the brothers pronounce the penalty, the one found with it becomes the slave. fa-badaʾa bi-awʿiyatihim qabla wiʿāʾi akhīhi thumma stakhrajahā min wiʿāʾi akhīh; baggādôl hēḥēl ûbaqqāṭōn killâ wayyimmāṣēʾ haggābîaʿ bəʾamtaḥat binyāmin. Q adds a theological comment: ka-dhālika kidnā li-Yūsuf. Gen: Judah's long plea ends with yēšeb-nāʾ ʿabdəkā taḥat hannaʿar, and it breaks Joseph, wəlōʾ-yākōl yôsēp ləhitʾappēq (45:1), who reveals himself at once. Q: an unnamed fa-khudh aḥadanā makānahu is refused (maʿādha llāhi an naʾkhudha illā man wajadnā matāʿanā ʿindah), and the brothers go home. The revelation comes only on a third journey (12:88-90).

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml): divergence. Tribal oracles become a test of faith; the speaker moves from foretelling to questioning. cf. Gen. Rabbah 98:3 (sons answer with the Shema).

Shared motifs, rarest first: Dying Jacob addresses his sons [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); A dying father gathers his sons to bless them and foretell their destinies (weight 6.3). Pair score 13.0.

Noah and those with him in the ark survive: fa-najjaynāhu wa-man maʿahu fī l-fulki vs wayyiššāʾer ʾak-nōaḥ waʾăšer ʾittô battēbāh; bōʾ-ʾattāh wᵉkol-bêtᵉkā ʾel-hattēbāh. Gen's 'household' (bêt) is 'those with him' (man maʿahu) in Q.

Shared motifs, rarest first: Why God destroyed a generation or a people (weight 6.3); Whether the flood hero speaks to his people before the flood (weight 6.3); Hero's family saved with him (weight 4.5). Pair score 17.1.

Only in The Flood (full read): Clean animals taken aboard by sevens, unclean by pairs; Flood events given exact calendar dates (year of hero's life, month, day); Rain or flood lasts forty days and forty nights; God regrets having made humankind and is grieved in his heart; God himself shuts the vessel's door behind the hero; A dove returns with an olive leaf in its beak; A raven is sent out and does not return (goes to and fro); Seven days pass between the warning or boarding and the onset of the flood; Vessel has several decks, a side door and a roof opening or window; God sends a wind (ruah) over the earth to make the waters subside; Angels object that the new human will corrupt the earth and shed blood while they praise God; When the water overflowed God carried 'you' in the running ship (al-jariya) as a reminder for retaining ears [divergence between the texts]; and 43 more.

Only in Noah's challenge to his people: Prophet challenges the idolaters to call their partners and plot against him without delay; Leader protests he never took so much as a donkey from anyone; A seer faced with payment or worldly gain [contrast between the texts]; God seals (tab') the hearts of deniers so they do not hear; Hero warns or preaches to his people before the flood; Destruction follows the people's rejection of a messenger; The Prophet asks no wage for the message.

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/03-hb-quran.yaml): contrast, divergence, echo, parallel. Noah and his people before the flood: Gen records no word from Noah, only obedience (wayyaʿaś nōaḥ kᵉkōl ʾăšer-ṣiwwāhû YHWH); Q adds a long debate, innī lakum nadhīrun mubīnun an lā taʿbudū illā llāha, with the chiefs' replies (mā narāka illā basharan mithlanā) and their mockery while he builds (sakhirū minhu). Why they drown: Gen, the earth full of violence (kî-mālᵉʾāh hāʾāreṣ ḥāmās mippᵉnêhem); Q, rejecting the messenger and doing wrong (lladhīna ẓalamū innahum mughraqūn), after Noah's preaching. In Gen all flesh perishes (qēṣ kol-bāśār); in Q 'Noah's people'. God tells Noah privately that the others will be destroyed by water: wa-ūḥiya ilā nūḥin annahu lan yuʾmina min qawmika illā man qad āmana ... innahum mughraqūn vs qēṣ kol-bāśār bāʾ lᵉpānay ... hinnî mēbîʾ ʾet-hammabbûl mayim. wa-ṣnaʿi l-fulka bi-aʿyuninā wa-waḥyinā vs ʿăśēh lᵉkā tēbat ʿăṣê-gōper. Gen gives the material, measurements and pitch (6:14-16); Q only 'under our eyes and our inspiration'. The sign that the flood begins: ḥattā idhā jāʾa amrunā wa-fāra t-tannūru (the oven boiled over) vs bayyôm hazzeh nibqᵉʿû kol-maʿyᵉnōt tᵉhôm rabbāh waʾărubbōt haššāmayim niptāḥû, dated to the 17th of the second month of Noah's 600th year. Q has a domestic oven instead of the cosmic deep and the windows of heaven, and no date. cf. b. Sanhedrin 108b (boiling flood waters), outside the canon. min kullin zawjayni thnayni vs šᵉnayim mikkōl ... zākār ûnᵉqēbāh. Q lacks Gen's second rule of seven pairs of clean animals (šibʿāh šibʿāh, Gen 7:2).
Passages are shown for the 10 rarest of 17 shared motifs; the full list follows.

Shared motifs, rarest first: What the flood hero does when the vessel comes to rest (weight 6.7); Vessel comes to rest on a named mountain [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); When and from where the flood waters come (weight 6.7); Which of Noah's household enter the ark and survive [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); How the flood waters are stopped and subside [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); Noah's standing before God: blameless, or in need of forgiveness [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); What God says of later generations after the flood: no repeat, or punishment to come [contrast between the texts] (weight 6.7); Whether and how Noah speaks to God (weight 6.7); Waters rise above the highest mountains (fifteen cubits) (weight 6.7); Why God destroyed a generation or a people (weight 6.3); Whether the flood hero speaks to his people before the flood (weight 6.3); Animals taken aboard in pairs (weight 5.8); Vessel comes to rest on a named mountain (weight 5.4); Deity decides to destroy humankind (weight 5.3); Hero builds a vessel on divine instruction (weight 5.2); Hero privately warned of the coming flood by a deity (weight 5.1); Hero's family saved with him (weight 4.5). Pair score 104.1.

Only in The Flood (full read): Clean animals taken aboard by sevens, unclean by pairs; Flood events given exact calendar dates (year of hero's life, month, day); Rain or flood lasts forty days and forty nights; God regrets having made humankind and is grieved in his heart; God himself shuts the vessel's door behind the hero; A dove returns with an olive leaf in its beak; A raven is sent out and does not return (goes to and fro); Seven days pass between the warning or boarding and the onset of the flood; Vessel has several decks, a side door and a roof opening or window; God sends a wind (ruah) over the earth to make the waters subside; Angels object that the new human will corrupt the earth and shed blood while they praise God; When the water overflowed God carried 'you' in the running ship (al-jariya) as a reminder for retaining ears [divergence between the texts]; and 29 more.

Only in Noah, the boiling oven, the lost son and al-Judi: Embark: 'in the name of God be its sailing and its mooring'; God commands: 'Earth, swallow your water; sky, withhold!' and the water subsides; Noah reminds God that his son is of his family and God's promise is true; The elite scorn the prophet because only the lowest of them follow him; God answers that the drowned son is not of Noah's family: 'he is a deed not righteous'; The prophet's stories are 'tidings of the unseen' unknown to him and his people before; The ark sails through waves like mountains; The prophet's opponents object that only the lowliest follow him; he refuses to drive the believers away; Someone seeks refuge on a mountain and is drowned; A son of Noah is found unworthy, and what follows [divergence between the texts]; The prophet disclaims having God's treasuries, knowing the unseen, or being an angel; A specific sign marks the moment to board; and 12 more.

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml): divergence, parallel. an iṣnaʿi l-fulka bi-aʿyuninā wa-waḥyinā ~ ʿăśē ləkā tēvat ʿăṣê gōfer: God commands the vessel. Genesis gives the wood, pitch and dimensions (6:14-16), the Quran only says it is built 'under our eyes and our revelation'; the ark is fulk, not tēvâ. fa-sluk fīhā min kullin zawjayni thnayni ~ šənayim mi-kkōl tāvîʾ ʾel hat-tēvâ ... zākhār û-nəqēvâ: two of every kind. The Quran omits the sevens of clean animals (Gen 7:2), which prepare Noah's sacrifice. In Genesis Noah never speaks before the flood: wa-yyaʿaś Nōaḥ kə-khōl ʾăšer ṣiwwâ ʾōtô; he is chosen because God saw him righteous (ʾōtəkā rāʾîtî ṣaddîq). In the Quran he is a messenger (arsalnā Nūḥan ilā qawmihi) who preaches 'yā qawmi ʿbudū llāha mā lakum min ilāhin ghayruhu', and the chiefs answer that he is only a man like them, possessed (bihi jinna). Cause of the flood: Gen 6:13 kî mālʾâ hā-ʾāreṣ ḥāmās, the earth filled with violence, and God's own decision (hinnî mašḥîtām); Q 23:26-27: they are drowned for rejecting the messenger (bimā kadhdhabūni ... alladhīna ẓalamū innahum mughraqūn), and Noah asks for it (rabbi nṣurnī). Signal and source: Genesis gives a time (lə-yāmîm ʿôd šivʿâ ʾānōkhî mamṭîr) and waters from the burst springs of the deep and the windows of heaven (nivqəʿû kol maʿyənôt təhôm rabbâ wa-ʾărubbōt haš-šāmayim niftāḥû); the Quran gives a sign, 'when our command comes and the oven boils' (wa-fāra t-tannūr). cf. b. Sanh. 108b (boiling flood waters), outside the HB. Genesis saves the whole household, bōʾ ʾattâ wə-khol bêtəkā ... Nōaḥ û-vānāyw wə-ʾištô û-nəšê vānāyw; the Quran excepts some: wa-ahlaka illā man sabaqa ʿalayhi l-qawlu minhum (the drowned son of 11:42-43), and forbids Noah to plead for the wrongdoers (wa-lā tukhāṭibnī fī lladhīna ẓalamū).

Shared motifs, rarest first: What the flood hero does when the vessel comes to rest [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); When and from where the flood waters come [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); Whether the flood hero speaks to his people before the flood [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.3); Why God destroyed a generation or a people [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.0); Who is saved with the hero from the destruction, and why [divergence between the texts] (weight 5.8); Animals taken aboard in pairs (weight 5.8); Hero builds a vessel on divine instruction (weight 5.2); Hero's family saved with him (weight 4.5). Pair score 46.9.

Only in The Flood (full read): Clean animals taken aboard by sevens, unclean by pairs; Flood events given exact calendar dates (year of hero's life, month, day); Rain or flood lasts forty days and forty nights; God regrets having made humankind and is grieved in his heart; God himself shuts the vessel's door behind the hero; A dove returns with an olive leaf in its beak; A raven is sent out and does not return (goes to and fro); Seven days pass between the warning or boarding and the onset of the flood; Vessel has several decks, a side door and a roof opening or window; God sends a wind (ruah) over the earth to make the waters subside; Angels object that the new human will corrupt the earth and shed blood while they praise God; When the water overflowed God carried 'you' in the running ship (al-jariya) as a reminder for retaining ears [divergence between the texts]; and 38 more.

Only in Noah called a madman; the ark and the boiling oven: God forbids the prophet to address him on behalf of those who did wrong: they will be drowned; The flood hero prays to be landed at a blessed landing place; The prophet's people object that he is only a human like them; had God willed he would have sent angels; A specific sign marks the moment to board; The flood waters are hot or boiling; A member of the hero's family is lost; Hero asks the deity to judge or destroy his opponents; Hero warns or preaches to his people before the flood; Officers call the visiting prophet 'this madman' (meshugga').

passages.note: After Zayd ends his marriage, God marries his former wife to the prophet so believers may marry the ex-wives of adopted sons (A prophet's marriage arranged by God as a public sign: lēḵ qaḥ-ləḵā ʾēšeṯ zənûnîm ... kî-zānōh tizneh hā-ʾāreṣ vs. zawwajnākahā li-kay lā yakūna ʿalā l-muʾminīna ḥaraj. passages.text: תְּחִלַּ֥ת דִּבֶּר יְהוָ֖ה בְּהוֹשֵׁ֑עַ וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֶל הוֹשֵׁ֗עַ לֵ֣ךְ קַח לְךָ֞ אֵ֤שֶׁת זְנוּנִים֙ וְיַלְדֵ֣י זְנוּנִ֔ים כִּֽי זָנֹ֤ה תִזְנֶה֙ הָאָ֔רֶץ מֵֽאַחֲרֵ֖י יְהוָֽה

passages.note: After Zayd ends his marriage, God marries his former wife to the prophet so believers may marry the ex-wives of adopted sons (Zayd is the only Companion named in the Quran)
passages.text: وَإِذْ تَقُولُ لِلَّذِىٓ أَنْعَمَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَأَنْعَمْتَ عَلَيْهِ أَمْسِكْ عَلَيْكَ زَوْجَكَ وَٱتَّقِ ٱللَّهَ وَتُخْفِى فِى نَفْسِكَ مَا ٱللَّهُ مُبْدِيهِ وَتَخْشَى ٱلنَّاسَ وَٱللَّهُ أَحَقُّ أَن تَخْشَىٰهُ فَلَمَّا قَضَىٰ زَيْدٌ مِّنْهَا وَطَرًا زَوَّجْنَٰكَهَا لِكَىْ لَا يَكُونَ عَلَى ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ حَرَجٌ فِىٓ أَزْوَٰجِ أَدْعِيَآئِهِمْ إِذَا قَضَوْا۟ مِنْهُنَّ وَطَرًا وَكَانَ أَمْرُ ٱللَّهِ مَفْعُولًا

In Hosea the marriage is an allegory of Israel's harlotry, in the Quran a legal precedent (amru llāhi mafʿūlā).

leads.summary: These two units share 1 motifs: they will say to the mountains 'cover us' and to the hills 'fall on us'.

passages.note: They will say to the mountains 'Cover us' and to the hills 'Fall on us'
passages.text: וְנִשְׁמְד֞וּ בָּמ֣וֹת אָ֗וֶן חַטַּאת֙ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל ק֣וֹץ וְדַרְדַּ֔ר יַעֲלֶ֖ה עַל מִזְבְּחוֹתָ֑ם וְאָמְר֤וּ לֶֽהָרִים֙ כַּסּ֔וּנוּ וְלַגְּבָע֖וֹת נִפְל֥וּ עָלֵֽינוּ

passages.note: They will say to the mountains 'Cover us' and to the hills 'Fall on us' (law tusawwā bihimu l-arḍ; compare Hos 10:8)
passages.text: يَوْمَئِذٍ يَوَدُّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ وَعَصَوُا۟ ٱلرَّسُولَ لَوْ تُسَوَّىٰ بِهِمُ ٱلْأَرْضُ وَلَا يَكْتُمُونَ ٱللَّهَ حَدِيثًا

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml): parallel. Hos 10:8 wĕ-ʾāmĕrû le-hārîm kassûnû wĕ-la-gĕbāʿôt nipĕlû ʿālênû: they will say to the mountains 'cover us', to the hills 'fall on us'; Q 4:42 yawmaʾidhin yawaddu lladhīna kafarū ... law tusawwā bihimu l-arḍu: on that day the unbelievers will wish the earth were levelled over them. Wish to be buried under the land to escape judgment; Hosea's is the fall of Samaria's shrines, the Quran's the Last Day.
Shared motifs, rarest first: They will say to the mountains 'Cover us' and to the hills 'Fall on us' (weight 6.7). Pair score 6.7.

Only in The luxuriant vine, the calves of Beth-aven, sow righteousness: Israel a luxuriant vine: the more fruit, the more altars and pillars; The idol-priests (kemarim) mourn as the calf is carried off as tribute to Assyria; Sow for yourselves righteousness, reap steadfast love, break up your fallow ground; Thorns and thistles grow up on their altars; Ephraim a trained heifer that loves to thresh, now yoked to plow; Israel's sin recalled as 'the days of Gibeah'; Bethel ('house of God') mocked as Beth-aven ('house of iniquity'); Infants dashed to pieces and pregnant women ripped open in war.

Only in The circle of kindness, misers, and the atom's weight: Misers who urge stinginess and hide what God gave them of his bounty; On that day the disbelievers wish the earth were leveled over them; God does not wrong anyone by an atom's weight (mithqāl dharra); Good works (spending, prayer) done to be seen by people (riyāʾ); God multiplies a good deed (tenfold) while an evil deed is requited only by its like; Love your neighbor as yourself; Kindness to the near neighbor, the distant neighbor, the companion at one's side and the wayfarer; Whoever turns from God's remembrance is assigned a devil as constant companion (qarin), whom he curses at the judgment; On judgment day a witness is brought from every nation, and the Prophet as witness over them; Honor father and mother, with the promise of long life.

leads.summary: These two units share 1 motifs: 'ad grow arrogant: 'who is mightier than us in strength?'.

passages.note: 'Ad grow arrogant: 'Who is mightier than us in strength?' (A boast of one's own strength answered by the maker/made relation: man ashaddu minnā quwwatan ... a-wa-lam yaraw anna llāha lladhī khalaqahum huwa ashaddu minhum quwwatan vs. Assyria's bə-ḵōaḥ yāḏî ʿāśîṯî (by the strength of my hand I did it) answered by hă-yiṯpāʾēr ha-garzen ʿal ha-ḥōṣēḇ bô (shall the axe boast over the one who hews with it?). Isaiah's boaster is God's tool (šēḇeṭ ʾappî, 10:5) used against Israel; 'Ad is a people destroyed for its boast.)

Only in Restoration of Jacob and the taunt over the king of Babylon (Helel son of Dawn): The proud one plans to ascend to heaven, raise his throne above the stars of El and make himself like Elyon; Reversal: Israel will take captive those who captured them and rule over their oppressors; The would-be god is brought down instead to Sheol, to the recesses of the pit (yarkete bor); Strangers (gerim) will join themselves to Israel and cleave to the house of Jacob; 'How you have fallen from heaven, Helel son of Shahar (Shining One, son of Dawn)!' - a star-figure cast down to earth; In the underworld maggots are spread beneath the dead king and worms are his covering; The mount of assembly (har mo'ed) in the recesses of the north (yarkete tsafon), seat of the gods; God cuts off from the enemy 'name and remnant, offspring and posterity'; Sheol below is stirred to meet the arriving tyrant; the shades and dead kings rise from their thrones to greet him: 'you too have become weak like us'; God sweeps the city with the broom of destruction, leaving it to hedgehogs and marshes; Mocking dirge (mashal) over a fallen tyrant: 'How the oppressor has ceased!'; The cypresses and cedars of Lebanon rejoice that no woodcutter comes up since the tyrant fell; and 8 more.

Only in The chosen patriarchs; the Gardens of Eden and the quarrel of the damned: The damned ask 'Why do we not see men we counted among the wicked, whom we mocked?'; The prophet had no knowledge of the Exalted Assembly when they disputed (over Adam); Elisha (al-Yasa') is named among the excellent; Ishmael is named among the chosen prophets; The provision of paradise never runs out; Abraham, Isaac and Jacob are 'possessors of hands and sight' (power and insight); God's choice of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, and what it passes on [divergence between the texts]; A prophet called Dhū l-Kifl is listed among the patient; The Gardens of Eden have their gates opened for the righteous; Paradise has full-breasted companions of equal age (kawa'ib atrab); Whether a prophet has first-hand knowledge of the heavenly council [contrast between the texts]; The damned followers ask double punishment for those who misled them; all get double; and 3 more.

Only in The earth laid waste; the host of heaven imprisoned; YHWH reigns on Zion: The 'city of chaos' (qiryat tohu) is broken; every house shut, joy banished; The earth is polluted under its inhabitants because they transgressed laws and broke the everlasting covenant; a curse devours it; YHWH empties the earth and lays it waste, twisting its surface and scattering its inhabitants: priest as people, master as slave; The earth breaks, splits, totters and reels like a drunkard and sways like a hut; it falls and will not rise; On that day YHWH punishes the host of the height in the height and the kings of the earth, gathering them as prisoners in a pit, shut up and punished after many days; Prophet cries 'razi li, razi li' ('my leanness/my secret is mine'), woe to me, the treacherous deal treacherously; The moon is abashed and the sun ashamed, for YHWH reigns on Mount Zion with glory before his elders; The windows on high are opened and the foundations of the earth shake (flood imagery); Remnant left like gleanings at the olive-beating: two or three berries at the top of the bough; Shed blood pollutes the land and only the killer's blood atones for it; The quake of the Hour: every nursing mother forgets her suckling, every pregnant one miscarries, people seem drunk though not drunk; 'Terror, pit and snare': who flees the terror falls into the pit, who climbs out is caught in the snare; and 1 more.

leads.title: Thanksgiving; the feast on the mountain; death swallowed forever ↔ Deniers demand their fathers; the people of Tubba'; the tree of Zaqqum; silk, brocade and the houris
leads.summary: These two units share 1 motifs: in paradise they taste no death except the first death.

passages.note: In paradise they taste no death except the first death (No more death for the saved: billaʿ ham-māweṯ lā-neṣaḥ ... û-māḥâ ... dimʿâ mēʿal kol pānîm vs. lā yadhūqūna fīhā l-mawta illā l-mawtata l-ūlā. evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/07-hb-quran.yaml): echo. No more death for the saved: billaʿ ham-māweṯ lā-neṣaḥ ... û-māḥâ ... dimʿâ mēʿal kol pānîm vs. lā yadhūqūna fīhā l-mawta illā l-mawtata l-ūlā. Isaiah: death swallowed for all peoples at the mountain feast; Quran: the blessed in the Garden, after their first death.
Shared motifs, rarest first: In paradise they taste no death except the first death (weight 6.7). Pair score 6.7.

Only in Thanksgiving; the feast on the mountain; death swallowed forever: God will swallow up death forever (bila ha-mavet la-netsah); On this mountain YHWH makes for all peoples a feast of rich foods and well-aged wines; God turned the city into a heap, the foreigners' palace never to be rebuilt; strong peoples fear him; God is a stronghold for the poor, refuge from the storm and shade from the heat; The Lord YHWH will wipe away tears from all faces and remove his people's disgrace; Moab trampled like straw in a dung-pit, spreading his hands like a swimmer; 'Behold, this is our God; we waited for him and he saved us'; God swallows the shroud (lot) and veil spread over all peoples.

Only in Deniers demand their fathers; the people of Tubba'; the tree of Zaqqum; silk, brocade and the houris: The Day of Sorting/Decision (yawm al-fasl) is the appointed time for all; The blessed wear fine silk (sundus) and brocade (istabraq), facing one another on couches; God has made the revelation easy in the prophet's own tongue so they may remember; Angels drag the sinner into the midst of hellfire and pour boiling water (hamim) over his head; Death as final, voiced by a sufferer or by deniers of resurrection [divergence between the texts]; Deniers of resurrection say there is only our first death and challenge the prophet to bring back their fathers; In hell the unbelievers are cut garments of fire and boiling water is poured on their heads, melting their insides and skins; The damned man is taunted: 'Taste! leads.title: Song of the strong city; your dead shall live ↔ The Companions of the Cave and al-Raqim (Surah 18:9-31)
leads.summary: These two units share 1 motifs: god lets the people discover the sleepers so they know his promise of resurrection is true.

passages.note: God lets the people discover the sleepers so they know his promise of resurrection is true (lēk ʿammî bōʾ baḥădārêkā ûsgōr dəlātəkā baʿădekā ḥăbî kimʿaṭ-regaʿ ʿad-yaʿăbor-zāʿam, next to hāqîṣû wərannənû šōknê ʿāpār; fa-ʾwū ilā l-kahfi yanshur lakum rabbukum min raḥmatih ... ka-dhālika baʿathnāhum ... li-yaʿlamū anna waʿda llāhi ḥaqq: the faithful hide in a closed place until the wrath passes, beside an awakening of sleepers that points to resurrection. Isa's 'little moment' becomes Q's 309 years, which the sleepers think was 'a day or part of a day' (18:19).)

passages.text: وَإِذِ ٱعْتَزَلْتُمُوهُمْ وَمَا يَعْبُدُونَ إِلَّا ٱللَّهَ فَأْوُۥٓا۟ إِلَى ٱلْكَهْفِ يَنشُرْ لَكُمْ رَبُّكُم مِّن رَّحْمَتِهِۦ وَيُهَيِّئْ لَكُم مِّنْ أَمْرِكُم مِّرْفَقًا

Only in Song of the strong city; your dead shall live: Other lords ruled us; they are dead, they will not live; shades (rephaim) will not rise; their memory is wiped out; God's dew is a 'dew of lights' (tal orot) and the earth will give birth to the shades (rephaim); The earth will disclose the blood shed on it and no longer cover its slain; 'Go, my people, enter your chambers and shut the doors behind you; hide a little moment until the wrath passes'; We were pregnant, we writhed, but gave birth only to wind; we brought no salvation to the earth; God keeps the steadfast mind in perfect peace (shalom shalom) because it trusts in him; 'My soul yearns for you in the night; my spirit within me seeks you at dawn'; 'We have a strong city... Open the gates that the righteous nation that keeps faith may enter'; In Yah YHWH is an everlasting rock (tsur olamim); What the dead say when they wake from the dust [divergence between the texts]; On God's day all that is lofty (cedars of Lebanon, oaks of Bashan, towers, ships of Tarshish) is brought low and God alone exalted; The Gardens of Eden have their gates opened for the righteous; and 7 more.

Only in The Companions of the Cave and al-Raqim (Surah 18:9-31): The companions of the Cave and al-Raqim (an inscription or tablet); The sleepers' dog lies stretching its forelegs at the cave's threshold; The sleepers fear the townspeople will stone them or force them back to their religion; Hell's walls (suradiq) enclose the damned; they are given water like molten metal that scalds faces; People dispute the sleepers' number (three, five or seven, plus their dog); only God knows; In paradise the blessed wear gold bracelets and green silk and brocade, reclining on couches; The prevailing party builds a place of worship over the sleepers; Whoever looked upon the sleepers would flee filled with terror; The sleepers stayed in their cave three hundred years and nine more; One sleeper is sent to town with their silver coin to buy food discreetly; The sleepers seem awake though asleep, and God turns them from side to side; Woken after centuries, the sleepers think they slept a day or part of a day; and 9 more.

leads.title: Woe to Ariel; enemies like a dream; the sealed book; lip service; the potter and the clay ↔ Recite the Book; dispute with the People of the Book; the unlettered prophet
leads.summary: These two units share 1 motifs: the prophet neither recited any scripture nor wrote one with his right hand before the revelation.

passages.note: The prophet neither recited any scripture nor wrote one with his right hand before the revelation (wa-mā kunta tatlū min qablihi min kitābin wa-lā takhuṭṭuhu bi-yamīnika vs. wə-nittan ha-sēp̄er ʿal ʾăšer lōʾ yāḏaʿ sēp̄er ... qərāʾ nāʾ zeh wə-ʾāmar lōʾ yāḏaʿtî sēp̄er. Both speak of one who did not know writing before the book; Isaiah's is a figure of blindness to the vision, the Quran's a proof that the book is not forged (la-rtāba l-mubṭilūn). Lead only; the frequent link of Isa 29:12 to Q 96:1 iqraʾ is later literature.)

leads.summary: These two units share 1 motifs: amassing war horses, and trust in god [contrast between the texts].

Only in Woe to those who go down to Egypt; YHWH like a lion and hovering birds over Zion: Assyria will fall by a sword not of man; YHWH's fire is in Zion and his furnace in Jerusalem; 'Egypt is man and not God, their horses flesh and not spirit'; Like hovering birds YHWH protects Jerusalem; he will 'pass over' (pasoah) and rescue it; YHWH comes down to fight on Mount Zion like a lion growling over its prey, undaunted by the shepherds' shouts; Judah (or allies) put trust in Egypt and Cush for help against Assyria and are put to shame; Idols called 'elilim' ('nothings').

passages.note: God made everything grow in due weight and sends it down only in known measure (wa-anbatnā fīhā min kulli shayʾin mawzūn ... illā bi-qadarin maʿlūm; mî-mādad bəšoʿŏlô mayim ... wəšāqal bappeles hārîm ûgəbāʿôt bəmōʾznāyim: the creator weighs and measures creation (mawzūn and mōʾznayim from cognate roots for weighing). Isa uses it to show the creator's incomparability, Q to show his provision.)

Only in Desire as god, 'only Time destroys us', and every nation kneeling before its book: God's book speaks against them with truth: 'We used to have transcribed (nastansikh) all that you did'; What God's heavenly book records: names or deeds [divergence between the texts]; Deniers of resurrection say there is only our first death and challenge the prophet to bring back their fathers; To God belongs the grandeur (kibriya') in the heavens and the earth; Whether death is the end: asked, held by sceptics, or answered by resurrection [response between the texts]; On the day of the Hour every community is seen kneeling (jathiya), each called to its book of deeds; Deniers say there is only this life; we die and live, and only Time (al-dahr) destroys us; Whoever takes his own desire (hawā) as his god; God forgets the damned today as they forgot the meeting of this day; Do evildoers think God will make them equal to the righteous in life and in death?; God did not create the heavens and earth and what is between them in play (la'ibin) but in truth; God sets a seal on the unbelievers' hearts and hearing and a covering over their eyes; and 1 more.

Only in Ahaz, the Syro-Ephraimite threat and the Immanuel sign: The child will eat curds and honey until he knows to refuse evil and choose good; 'If you do not believe (ta'aminu) you will not be established (te'amenu)': faith as condition of survival; God will whistle for the fly of Egypt and the bee of Assyria to settle in the land; God will shave head, 'hair of the feet' and beard with a razor hired beyond the River (the king of Assyria); King invited to ask any sign 'deep as Sheol or high as heaven' refuses, saying he will not test God; Cultivated land worth a thousand silver reverts to briers and thorns (shamir va-shayit), fit only for grazing and hunting; Enemy kings dismissed as two smoldering stumps of firebrands; Aram (Rezin) and Israel (Pekah) ally to attack Jerusalem and install a puppet king (son of Tabeel); A divine messenger announces a son to a virgin untouched by any man [divergence between the texts]; Before a child knows to refuse evil and choose good (or say 'father, mother') the enemy kings' lands will be deserted; Prophet meets the king at the conduit of the upper pool on the highway of the Fuller's Field; Prophet's child bears a symbolic name that is itself an oracle (Shear-yashuv, Maher-shalal-hash-baz); and 1 more.

Only in The annunciation and the mission of Jesus: Jesus comes confirming the Torah and making lawful some of what was forbidden; God says to Jesus 'I will take you (mutawaffika) and raise you to myself and purify you'; Jesus tells people what they eat and store in their houses; Jesus announced as a word (kalima) from God, named the Messiah, Jesus son of Mary; Forming a creature from earth and breathing life into it [divergence between the texts]; They plotted, and God plotted; God is the best of plotters; The likeness of Jesus with God is as Adam, created from dust by 'Be'; Jesus will speak to people in the cradle and in maturity; Challenge to mutual imprecation (mubahala): gather sons, women and selves and invoke God's curse on the liars; God sent down the Torah (al-Tawrat) and the Gospel (al-Injil) before as guidance; Mary asks how she will have a child when no man has touched her; Jesus asks 'Who are my helpers to God?' and the disciples (hawariyyun) answer 'We are God's helpers'; and 8 more.

Only in Zedekiah's inquiry - the way of life and the way of death: The besieged king sends to ask the prophet to inquire of God, hoping God will do a wonder and make the enemy withdraw; The city is given into the hand of the king of Babylon who will burn it with fire; God himself fights against his own people with outstretched hand and mighty arm, turning their weapons back; Whoever stays in the city will die, but whoever goes out and surrenders to the besiegers will live, his life as spoil; God redeems 'with an outstretched arm' and great judgments; Judgment by the triad sword, famine and pestilence.

Only in The city: the two highways and the steep ascent: The companions of the right (ashab al-yamin, al-maymana) are saved; the companions of the left (al-mash'ama) are damned; A fire is closed over the damned (mu'sada); The steep ascent ('aqaba) is freeing a neck (slave), feeding an orphan relative or a needy man in the dust on a day of hunger; Ground cursed; man must eat by sweat of his brow among thorns and thistles; Ground cursed; man must eat by sweat of his brow among thorns and thistles [divergence between the texts]; Oath by 'this city' (Mecca), the secure city (al-balad al-amin); The fast God chooses is to loose bonds of injustice, free the oppressed, share bread with the hungry and clothe the naked; Oath introduced by the negated formula 'No! I swear by...' (la uqsimu / fa-la uqsimu); Woe to every slanderer and backbiter (humaza lumaza) who amasses and counts wealth, thinking it makes him immortal; Rhetorical formula 'And what will make you know what X is?' God writes on the heart: nāṯattî ʾeṯ tôrāṯî bə-qirbām wə-ʿal libbām ʾeḵtăḇennâ vs. ulāʾika kataba fī qulūbihimu l-īmāna wa-ayyadahum bi-rūḥin minhu. passages.note: A land deed made in a sealed copy and an open copy, witnessed and the silver weighed (Double deed: sealed copy and open copy, witnesses, silver weighed on scales)
passages.text: (32:10) וָאֶכְתֹּ֤ב בַּסֵּ֨פֶר֙ וָֽאֶחְתֹּ֔ם וָאָעֵ֖ד עֵדִ֑ים וָאֶשְׁקֹ֥ל הַכֶּ֖סֶף בְּמֹאזְנָֽיִם (32:11) וָאֶקַּ֖ח אֶת סֵ֣פֶר הַמִּקְנָ֑ה אֶת הֶֽחָת֛וּם הַמִּצְוָ֥ה וְהַחֻקִּ֖ים וְאֶת הַגָּלֽוּי (32:12) וָאֶתֵּ֞ן אֶת הַסֵּ֣פֶר הַמִּקְנָ֗ה אֶל בָּר֣וּךְ בֶּן נֵרִיָּה֮ בֶּן מַחְסֵיָה֒ לְעֵינֵי֙ חֲנַמְאֵ֣ל דֹּדִ֔י וּלְעֵינֵי֙ הָֽעֵדִ֔ים הַכֹּתְבִ֖ים בְּסֵ֣פֶר הַמִּקְנָ֑ה לְעֵינֵי֙ כָּל הַיְּהוּדִ֔ים הַיֹּשְׁבִ֖ים בַּחֲצַ֥ר הַמַּטָּרָֽה (32:13) וָֽאֲצַוֶּה֙ אֶת בָּר֔וּךְ לְעֵינֵיהֶ֖ם לֵאמֹֽר (32:14) כֹּֽה אָמַר֩ יְהוָ֨ה צְבָא֜וֹת אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל לָק֣וֹחַ אֶת הַסְּפָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֡לֶּה אֵ֣ת סֵפֶר֩ הַמִּקְנָ֨ה הַזֶּ֜ה וְאֵ֣ת הֶחָת֗וּם וְאֵ֨ת סֵ֤פֶר הַגָּלוּי֙ הַזֶּ֔ה וּנְתַתָּ֖ם בִּכְלִי חָ֑רֶשׂ לְמַ֥עַן יַעַמְד֖וּ יָמִ֥ים רַבִּֽים

passages.note: A land deed made in a sealed copy and an open copy, witnessed and the silver weighed (Jer 32:10, 12 wā-ʾektōb ba-sseper wā-ʾeḥtōm wā-ʾāʿid ʿēdîm ... lĕʿênê hā-ʿēdîm ha-kkōtĕbîm bĕ-sēper ha-mmiqnâ: a written, sealed deed, with witnesses signing, handed to the scribe Baruch; Q 2:282 idhā tadāyantum bi-daynin ilā ajalin musamman fa-ktubūhu wa-l-yaktub baynakum kātibun bi-l-ʿadli ... wa-stashhidū shahīdayni: write a term debt down, by a just scribe, before two witnesses. A land sale in Jeremiah, a loan in the Quran; the writing is a sign of hope in Jeremiah and a protection against doubt in the Quran (adnā allā tartābū).)

leads.summary: These two units share 1 motifs: who dictated and who wrote down a prophet's book [contrast between the texts].

passages.note: Who dictated and who wrote down a prophet's book [contrast between the texts] (Who dictates to whom: in Jeremiah the prophet dictates and the scribe writes, wa-yyiktōv Bārûkh mip-pî Yirmyāhû ... mip-pîw yiqrāʾ ʾēlay ... wa-ʾănî kōtēv ʿal has-sēfer bad-dəyô; in the opponents' charge the prophet has old tales written down and they are dictated to him (iktatabahā fa-hiya tumlā ʿalayhi bukratan wa-aṣīlan), with helpers (aʿānahu ʿalayhi qawmun ākharūn). evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: The fleeing king is overtaken in the plains of Jericho (weight 6.7); The conqueror leaves the poorest people in the land as vinedressers and farmers (weight 6.7); Jerusalem is breached, captured and burned by the Babylonians (weight 6.7); The captive king's sons are slaughtered before his eyes, then his eyes are put out (weight 6.3); Besieged king flees by night through a gate between the walls and is overtaken (weight 6.3). Only in Fall of Jerusalem; Zedekiah blinded at Riblah; Jeremiah freed; Ebed-melech promised safety: The conquering Babylonian officers, named with their titles (Rab-saris, Rab-mag), sit in the city's Middle Gate; The foreign conqueror orders his officers to look after the prophet and do him no harm; A foreigner who helped the prophet is promised his life will be spared because he trusted God; Captive king taken with hooks and bound in bronze fetters to Babylon; Whoever surrenders to the enemy will live; his life shall be his booty.

Only in Historical appendix: siege, burning of the temple, bronze spoils, deportation numbers, Jehoiachin's release: Precise numbers of deportees for each year of exile; A captive king is released after decades, changes his prison clothes and eats at the foreign king's table; A king 'lifts the head' of a prisoner, releasing and honoring him; The besiegers build a siege wall (dayeq) around the city; Famine becomes severe in the besieged city; there is no bread; The chief priest, second priest and officials are executed by the conqueror at Riblah; The king's mother is named in his regnal formula; The released captive king is given a throne above the other kings in Babylon; The temple of Jerusalem is burned and the city walls broken down; Seven princes or counselors who 'see the king's face' advise the king; A great cast-bronze 'sea' basin rests on twelve bronze oxen facing the four directions in threes; Two named bronze pillars, Jachin and Boaz, before the temple; and 2 more.

leads.title: If you return - circumcise your hearts ↔ Polemic with the People of the Book
leads.summary: These two units share 1 motifs: the people's 'uncircumcised heart' must be humbled.

passages.note: The people's 'uncircumcised heart' must be humbled (Jer 4:4 himmōlû la-YHWH wĕ-hāsīrû ʿorlôt lĕbabkem: call to remove the heart's foreskins; Q 2:88 qulūbunā ghulfun: the hearers claim their hearts are covered.)

passages.note: The people's 'uncircumcised heart' must be humbled (qulubuna ghulf, 'our hearts are uncircumcised/wrapped')

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml): echo. Jer 4:4 himmōlû la-YHWH wĕ-hāsīrû ʿorlôt lĕbabkem: call to remove the heart's foreskins; Q 2:88 qulūbunā ghulfun: the hearers claim their hearts are covered.
Shared motifs, rarest first: The people's 'uncircumcised heart' must be humbled (weight 5.6). Pair score 5.6.

Only in If you return - circumcise your hearts: 'Break up your fallow ground and do not sow among thorns' as a call to repentance; Circumcise the foreskin of your heart; God calls 'Return, faithless children (shuvu banim shovavim), I will heal your faithlessness'; All families of the earth will be blessed through the patriarch.

Only in Polemic with the People of the Book: The love of the calf was made to sink (be drunk) into their hearts; If the next world is yours alone, wish for death: they never will; Enmity to Gabriel and Michael (Mikal) equated with enmity to God; Gabriel (Jibril) brings down the revelation upon the prophet's heart; Some wish to be granted a life of a thousand years; Israel made to drink the golden calf [divergence between the texts]; Worship of God alone joined to duty to parents [divergence between the texts]; Claim that the fire will touch them only for a few numbered days, rebutted; The idol is burned, ground to powder, scattered on water and the people made to drink it; Israel at the mountain says 'we hear and we disobey' (sami'na wa-'asayna); Woe to those who write the book with their own hands and say it is from God, for a small price; Hypocrites profess faith before believers and tell their own 'devils' in private they were only mocking; and 16 more.

leads.title: My bowels, my bowels - the vision of uncreation ↔ Moses asks Pharaoh to hand over God's servants; the sea left parted; heaven did not weep
leads.summary: These two units share 1 motifs: whether heaven and earth mourn a destroyed people [contrast between the texts].

passages.note: Whether heaven and earth mourn a destroyed people [contrast between the texts] (Whether heaven and earth mourn the destroyed. evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/07-hb-quran.yaml): parallel. The ancestors' cult defended against a prophet: lə-qaṭṭēr li-mleḵeṯ haš-šāmayim ... kaʾăšer ʿāśînû ʾănaḥnû wa-ʾăḇōṯênû malḵênû wə-śārênû vs. innā wajadnā ābāʾanā ʿalā ummatin wa-innā ʿalā āthārihim muqtadūn (said by its mutrafūn, the well-off). In both the worship goes to female deities: the Queen of Heaven, and the angels made females (43:19).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Opponents refuse the prophet: 'We found our fathers on a way and follow in their footsteps' (weight 6.7). Pair score 6.7.

Only in The Judeans in Egypt defend their cult of the Queen of Heaven: Worshipers argue their goddess cult brought plenty and abandoning it brought disaster; Women bake cakes bearing the image of the goddess they worship; God swears his name will no longer be invoked in oaths by apostates in a foreign land; God swears by his great name; The prophet ironically tells idolaters to go ahead and fulfill their vows; Judeans settled in Egyptian cities: Migdol, Tahpanhes, Memphis and Pathros; Pharaoh Hophra will be handed over to those who seek his life; Events will show whose word will stand, God's or the people's; The wickedness of the kings of Judah and of their wives; Women burn incense to a goddess, claiming they did so with their husbands' knowledge; Offerings, incense and libations to the 'Queen of Heaven'; God sends his messengers 'rising early and sending' out of compassion; and 2 more.

Only in Ha-Mim: the Mother of the Book, the riding prayer and the 'daughters' of God: When one of them is told of a daughter's birth, his face darkens and he chokes with grief; A formula of praise when mounting ship or beast: 'Glory to him who subjected this to us; we could not have done it'; Long catalogue of women's jewelry and garments (anklets, crescents, amulets, nose-rings, perfume boxes, veils); Whether heavenly beings are God's sons or daughters, or his servants [contrast between the texts]; The religion inherited from the fathers, defended or confessed as lies [divergence between the texts]; The scripture exists with God in the 'Mother of the Book' (umm al-kitab), a heavenly archetype; Oath 'By the clear Book!' opening a surah; God made the earth a cradle (mahd) or bed and laid out paths in it; Polemic against assigning daughters to God (the angels as females) while preferring sons for themselves; If asked who created heaven and earth and sends rain, the idolaters themselves answer 'God'; The revelation is sent down as an Arabic Quran; The people mock God's messengers, despise his words and scoff at his prophets; and 2 more.

passages.note: God takes the souls at death and of those not dead in their sleep; he keeps those decreed to die and sends back the others for a set term (ʾim-yāśîm ʾēlâw libbô rûḥô wə-nišmāṯô ʾēlâw yeʾĕsōp̄ yiḡwaʿ kol-bāśār yaḥad vs. allāhu yatawaffā l-anfusa ḥīna mawtihā ... fa-yumsiku llatī qaḍā ʿalayhā l-mawt: God gathers back the breath or soul, and death follows. Elihu states it as a possibility for all flesh; the Quran describes it as happening every night and at each death.)

Elihu states it as a possibility for all flesh; the Quran describes it as happening every night and at each death.
Shared motifs, rarest first: God takes the souls at death and of those not dead in their sleep; he keeps those decreed to die and sends back the others for a set term (weight 6.3). Pair score 6.3.

Only in Elihu - God cannot do wrong: God shows no partiality to princes, nor regards the rich above the poor, for all are the work of his hands; God shatters the mighty without inquiry and sets others in their place; God keeps a godless man from ruling, that he not ensnare the people; If God gathered his spirit and breath to himself, all flesh would perish together and return to dust; Elihu wishes that Job be tried to the end for answering like wicked men; In a moment they die; at midnight people are shaken and pass away, the mighty removed without a hand; 'Does God pervert justice, does Shaddai pervert right?'; Man is abominable and corrupt, drinking iniquity like water; 'Does not the ear test words as the palate tastes food?'; The sufferer is accused of multiplying words without knowledge; 'Why do you hide your face and count me as your enemy?'; 'Can a man be of use to God? Is it gain to Shaddai if you are righteous?'; and 3 more.

Only in The prophet's mortality; souls taken in sleep; intercession belongs to God: When God alone is mentioned the hearts of unbelievers shrink with aversion; at mention of others they rejoice; All intercession belongs to God; 'You will die and they will die', said to the prophet; Death described as sleep: 'lest I sleep the sleep of death'; Given a blessing, man says 'I was given it only because of my knowledge'; it is a trial; An earthful of gold would not be accepted as ransom from one who dies unbelieving; If asked who created heaven and earth and sends rain, the idolaters themselves answer 'God'; When harm touches people they turn to God; when he gives them relief a party of them associates partners again.

Only in Elihu on God's justice and suffering as discipline: Who has prescribed God's way, or who can say 'You have done wrong'?; Affliction is God's instruction: he opens the sufferer's ear through suffering so he may turn back; God shows no partiality and takes no bribe.

Only in Owner of sovereignty: On the day each soul finds what good and evil it did present before it, wishing a far distance from its evil; Believers may not take unbelievers as allies, unless guarding against them (tuqat); God warns you of himself (yuhadhdhirukum allahu nafsahu); God makes night enter day and day night, brings the living from the dead and the dead from the living; O God, owner of sovereignty, you give it to whom you will and take it from whom you will; you exalt and abase; God changes times and seasons, deposes kings and sets up kings; The Most High rules the kingdom of men, gives it to whom he wills and sets over it the lowliest of men; God provides for whom he wills without reckoning (bi-ghayri hisab); Hymn of reversals: the barren bears seven, the mighty broken, the poor raised from the dung-heap.
