Only in Elihu's hymn on rain, thunder, snow and the storm: Golden splendor comes out of the north as God's awesome majesty; God's booth or canopy (sukkah) is made of thunderclouds and darkness; In the winter storm God seals up every man's hand (stops human work) so all may know him; The number of God's years cannot be searched out; Ice and frozen waters are produced by the breath of God; God beat out the skies hard as a molten mirror of cast metal; God draws up drops of water which distill as rain from his mist (evaporation and rainfall cycle); Storm-wind comes out of a chamber (heder) and cold from the scattering winds; God speaks to the snow 'Fall on the earth' and commands the downpour; Thunder is the roaring voice of God; God sends the winds as heralds before his mercy and sends down pure water from the sky.

Only in The Light Verse; the mirage, the dark sea, the praising birds, hail and the creatures: Or like darkness in a deep sea, covered by wave upon wave and cloud above, darkness upon darkness, so one cannot see his own hand; The deeds of unbelievers are like a mirage in a plain that the thirsty takes for water until he reaches it and finds nothing, but finds God there; God is the light of the heavens and the earth; God's light is like a niche holding a lamp in a glass like a glittering star, lit from a blessed olive tree neither of east nor west, whose oil almost glows untouched by fire: light upon light; God sends down hail from mountains in the sky; the flash of his lightning nearly takes away sight; In houses God allowed to be raised, men undistracted by trade glorify him morning and evening; God created every beast from water: some go on their bellies, some on two legs, some on four; Birds with outspread wings glorify God; each knows its prayer and praise; With God is the fountain of life; in his light we see light; A lamp fed directly by an olive tree [divergence between the texts]; A golden lampstand with seven lamps is flanked by two olive trees that pour golden oil through golden pipes; The mirage and the thirsty traveler [divergence between the texts]; and 8 more.

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/07-hb-quran.yaml): echo, parallel. Abraham's father served other gods: teraḥ ʾăḇî ʾaḇrāhām ... wa-yaʿaḇḏû ʾĕlōhîm ʾăḥērîm; wā-ʾeqqaḥ ʾeṯ ʾăḇîḵem ʾeṯ ʾaḇrāhām mē-ʿēḇer han-nāhār vs. wa-idh qāla ibrāhīmu li-abīhi wa-qawmihi innanī barāʾun mimmā taʿbudūn. Changed actor: in Joshua it is God who 'takes' Abraham away from his father's land and gods; in the Quran Abraham himself declares himself free (barāʾ) of his father's worship. Choosing the one God against the fathers' gods: wə-hāsîrû ʾeṯ ʾĕlōhîm ʾăšer ʿāḇəḏû ʾăḇôṯêḵem ... wə-ʾānōḵî û-ḇêṯî naʿăḇōḏ ʾeṯ YHWH vs. innanī barāʾun mimmā taʿbudūn illā lladhī faṭaranī fa-innahu sa-yahdīn. Joshua's 'I and my house' becomes Abraham's personal confession to his own father.
Shared motifs, rarest first: The people are told to choose this day whom they will serve (weight 6.7); Hero's father makes, sells or worships idols (weight 4.8). Pair score 11.5.

Only in Covenant at Shechem; 'choose this day whom you will serve'; deaths of Joshua and Eleazar: God set darkness between Israel and the pursuing Egyptians; A priest is buried on the hill belonging to his son; Leader warns: you cannot serve YHWH, for he is a holy and jealous God; Joshua buried at Timnath-serah/heres north of Mount Gaash; The words of a covenant are written in a book of the law of God; Repeated mutual disavowal: 'I do not worship what you worship, nor do you worship what I worship'; 'to you your religion and to me mine'; The people are made witnesses against themselves to their choice; God was pleased with the believers when they pledged allegiance to the prophet under the tree (Bay'at al-Ridwan); Quraysh's security pact (ilaf) and caravan journeys of winter and summer; they should worship the Lord of this House who fed and secured them; A great stone set up as a witness because it has heard all God's words; God turned Balaam's curse into a blessing; Isaac given, and Jacob in addition as an extra gift (nāfila) [divergence between the texts]; and 9 more.

Only in Abraham disowns his father's worship; the great man of the two towns; silver roofs; the devil-companion: The damned wishes that between him and his companion lay 'the distance of the two easts'; But for fear all would become one community, God would give unbelievers houses with silver roofs, stairways, doors, couches and gold ornament; Abraham declares to his father and people that he is free of what they worship, except the one who created him; How Abraham parts from his father and his father's land or gods [divergence between the texts]; God expands provision (rizq) for whom he wills and restricts it; Lying on ivory beds eating lambs and calves, improvising on the harp like David, drinking wine from bowls and anointing with finest oils; What is given in this life is passing enjoyment (mata'); what is with God is better and more lasting; Opponents ask why the revelation was not sent down to some great man of the two towns; The wealth of the wicked: a scandal to be explained, or worthless enjoyment [divergence between the texts]; Abraham's confession is left as an enduring word among his descendants ('aqib); Whoever turns from God's remembrance is assigned a devil as constant companion (qarin), whom he curses at the judgment; The prophet cannot make the dead or deaf hear, nor guide the blind; and 2 more.

Only in Annunciation of Samson's birth to Manoah's wife: Divine messenger ascends to heaven in the flame of the altar; Divine visitor refuses the meal offered him and redirects it to God as an offering; Pregnant mother told to abstain from wine and unclean food for the child's sake; Divine being refuses to tell his name, calling it wonderful or secret; God's spirit appears to a woman in the form of a well-proportioned man; Witness fears he will die because he has seen God or an angel; Child consecrated as a nazirite from the womb, his hair never to be cut; Spirit of God rushes upon a man, giving him strength or ecstasy.

Only in The family of Imran, Mary and Zechariah: Angels call to Zechariah while he stands praying in the sanctuary, announcing John (Yahya); John (Yahya) foretold as noble, chaste (hasur) and a prophet, confirming a word from God; Angels tell Mary that God chose and purified her above the women of the worlds; Mother names her daughter Mary and commits her and her offspring to God's protection from the accursed Satan; Mother who vowed her unborn child finds she has borne a girl: 'the male is not like the female'; Sign given to the doubting father: he will not speak to people for three days except by gestures; Zechariah is made Mary's guardian; Prophet promises a childless woman with an old husband a son 'at this season next year'; God chose Adam, Noah, the family of Abraham and the family of Imran over the worlds; Doubt voiced at the promise of a son in old age [divergence between the texts]; The family of Amram / Imran and Miriam / Maryam [divergence between the texts]; Mother vows her (unborn) child to God's service [divergence between the texts]; and 11 more.

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/04-hb-quran.yaml): parallel. Same sequence: the young man destroys his father's people's cult objects unseen (wayyaʿaś lāylâ / baʿda an tuwallū mudbirīn), and the townsmen ask who did it, mî ʿāśâ haddābār hazzeh ... gidʿôn ben-yôʾāš ʿāśâ / man faʿala hādhā bi-ālihatinā ... samiʿnā fatan yadhkuruhum yuqālu lahu Ibrāhīm. Gideon acts on God's command (wayyōʾmer lô YHWH); Abraham on his own oath (ta-llāhi la-akīdanna aṣnāmakum). The same argument from the idol's helplessness: ʾim-ʾĕlōhîm hûʾ yāreb lô kî nātaṣ ʾet-mizbəḥô, 'if he is a god let him contend for himself'; bal faʿalahu kabīruhum hādhā fa-sʾalūhum in kānū yanṭiqūn, 'ask them, if they can speak'. In Judg the idolatrous father Joash says it to protect his son; in Q Abraham says it to shame the people, and they are turned on their heads (nukisū ʿalā ruʾūsihim).

Shared motifs, rarest first: Hero blames the largest idol for the destruction (weight 6.0); Hero smashes or burns idols (weight 5.6); Hero's father makes, sells or worships idols [divergence between the texts] (weight 5.4); Hero's father makes, sells or worships idols (weight 4.8). Pair score 21.8.

Only in Gideon pulls down his father's Baal altar; Jerubbaal; the fleece signs: A fleece is left on the threshing floor as a sign: wet when the ground is dry, then dry when it is wet; If he is a god, let him defend himself; A person receives a new name commemorating his deed; A seven-year-old bull is sacrificed on wood of the felled Asherah; The townsmen demand the death of the one who destroyed their god's altar; The idolatrous father threatens to stone his son and banishes him [contrast between the texts]; If he is a god, let him defend himself [divergence between the texts]; The called one asks for a sign that it is God who speaks [divergence between the texts]; The called one asks for a sign that it is God who speaks; Spirit of God rushes upon a man, giving him strength or ecstasy.

Only in Abraham breaks the idols and is cast into the fire: Abraham and Lot are rescued to the land God blessed for all peoples; God commands the fire: 'Be coolness and peace upon Abraham'; Abraham and Lot are rescued to the land God blessed for all peoples [divergence between the texts]; The fire does not harm the hero [divergence between the texts]; Isaac given, and Jacob in addition as an extra gift (nāfila); Isaac given, and Jacob in addition as an extra gift (nāfila) [divergence between the texts]; The fire does not harm the hero; The made idol cannot move from its place, speak or answer and save those who cry to it; Hero thrown into a fire or furnace by a king or people; The men of Sodom are exceedingly wicked.

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/06-hb-quran.yaml): parallel. A son destroys the cult objects of his father's house and the townsmen demand his death. Judg: wə-hārastā ʾeṯ-mizbaḥ ha-bbaʿal ʾăšer lə-ʾāḇîḵā ... hôṣēʾ ʾeṯ-binḵā wə-yāmōṯ; Joash answers ʾim-ʾĕlōhîm hûʾ yāreḇ lô (if Baal is a god let him fight for himself). Q: idh qāla li-abīhi wa-qawmihi mādhā taʿbudūn ... fa-rāgha ʿalayhim ḍarban bi-l-yamīn ... qālū bnū lahu bunyānan fa-alqūhu fī l-jaḥīm. In Judges the father defends the son by mocking the god; in the Quran the son mocks (mā lakum lā tanṭiqūn) and the father is the idolater.
Shared motifs, rarest first: Hero smashes or burns idols (weight 5.6); Hero's father makes, sells or worships idols (weight 4.8). Pair score 10.4.

Only in Gideon pulls down his father's Baal altar; Jerubbaal; the fleece signs: A fleece is left on the threshing floor as a sign: wet when the ground is dry, then dry when it is wet; If he is a god, let him defend himself; A person receives a new name commemorating his deed; A seven-year-old bull is sacrificed on wood of the felled Asherah; The townsmen demand the death of the one who destroyed their god's altar; The idolatrous father threatens to stone his son and banishes him [contrast between the texts]; If he is a god, let him defend himself [divergence between the texts]; Hero blames the largest idol for the destruction; The called one asks for a sign that it is God who speaks [divergence between the texts]; The called one asks for a sign that it is God who speaks; Hero's father makes, sells or worships idols [divergence between the texts]; Spirit of God rushes upon a man, giving him strength or ecstasy.

Only in Abraham, the stars, the smashed idols and the fire: Abraham glances at the stars and says 'I am sick', so his people leave him behind; Abraham asks the idols 'Will you not eat? Why do you not speak?' and strikes them with his right hand; The people build a structure (bunyan) and cast Abraham into the blaze, but God makes them the lowest; Abraham looks at the stars, and why [divergence between the texts]; 'Do you worship what you carve, when God created you and what you make?'; Hero reasons from the stars, moon and sun to the one God; Hero thrown into a fire or furnace by a king or people; Idols of wood and stone that cannot see, hear, eat or smell.

Only in The three who were left behind; every step recorded: The three who stayed behind are forgiven after the earth grew narrow for them and they found no refuge but God; Every thirst, fatigue, hunger, step and valley crossed in God's cause is written as a good deed; Not all should go out; a party from each group should stay to gain understanding of religion and warn; Distress is a narrow place and God's rescue gives breadth (tsar / merhav; daqa / rahuba); The believers' pride in their great numbers avails nothing and the earth grows narrow for them (Hunayn).

passages.note: Only four foods are forbidden: carrion, blood, swine and what is offered to other than God [contrast between the texts] (Q restricts the forbidden to four, innamā ḥarrama ʿalaykumu l-maytata wa-d-dama wa-laḥma l-khinzīri wa-mā uhilla li-ghayri llāhi bih. Lev 11 forbids many species and treats contact with nəbēlâ as defiling (hannōgēaʿ bənibəlātāh yiṭmāʾ ... wəhāʾōkēl minnibəlātāh yəkabbēs bəgādāyw). Q explains the longer Jewish list as a special burden: wa-ʿalā lladhīna hādū ḥarramnā mā qaṣaṣnā ʿalayka min qabl. Lev's carrion rule (purification, not a ban on eating) also differs from Q's maytah.)

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml): divergence, parallel. Lev 18:7-17 ʿerwat ... lōʾ tĕgallēh: mother, father's wife, sister and half-sister, granddaughter, aunts, uncle's wife, daughter-in-law, brother's wife, a woman with her daughter; Q 4:23 ḥurrimat ʿalaykum ummahātukum wa-banātukum wa-akhawātukum wa-ʿammātukum wa-khālātukum wa-banātu l-akhi wa-banātu l-ukhti wa-ummahātukumu llātī arḍaʿnakum wa-akhawātukum mina r-raḍāʿa ...: mothers, daughters, sisters, aunts, nieces, nursing mothers and milk sisters, mothers-in-law, stepdaughters, sons' wives. Shared core; the Quran adds daughters and nieces (not named in Lev 18) and milk kinship (absent from the HB), and drops the uncle's wife and the brother's wife (Lev 18:14, 16). Formula: 'uncover nakedness' vs 'forbidden to you'. Lev 18:8 ʿerwat ʾēšet ʾābîkā lōʾ tĕgallēh ʿerwat ʾābîkā hîʾ; Q 4:22 wa-lā tankiḥū mā nakaḥa ābāʾukum mina n-nisāʾi illā mā qad salaf innahu kāna fāḥishatan: do not marry your fathers' wives, 'except what is past'. The Quran adds an amnesty for unions made before the law. Lev 18:18 wĕ-ʾiššâ ʾel ʾăḥōtāh lōʾ tiqqāḥ liṣrōr ... bĕ-ḥayyêhā: do not take a woman's sister as a rival 'while she lives'; Q 4:23 wa-an tajmaʿū bayna l-ukhtayni illā mā qad salaf: do not combine two sisters, except what is past. The motive 'as a rival' is dropped, and an amnesty for the past is added.

Shared motifs, rarest first: Marrying two sisters [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); A man may not marry his wife's sister as a rival while the wife lives (weight 6.7); List of forbidden close-kin unions ('uncovering nakedness') [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); A man must not take his father's wife (uncover his father's skirt) (weight 6.0); List of forbidden close-kin unions ('uncovering nakedness') (weight 6.0). Pair score 32.1.

Only in Forbidden sexual unions; the land vomits out its inhabitants: Sexual relations of a man or a woman with an animal are forbidden; Marrying or lying with a brother's wife is forbidden; Do not follow the practices of Egypt where you lived or of Canaan where you are going; The land, defiled by abominations, vomits out its inhabitants; The person who does God's statutes shall live by them; Lying with a male as with a woman is forbidden; Whether a man may marry his son's (or adopted son's) wife [divergence between the texts]; Sexual relations with a neighbor's wife are forbidden; Zihar: a husband declaring his wife 'like my mother's back'; she is not his mother, the saying is false and abhorrent; Giving one's offspring to Molech is forbidden and punished; Intercourse with a menstruating woman is forbidden.

Only in Inheriting women, the dowry, and the forbidden degrees: A husband exchanging one wife for another may not take back anything he gave, even a qinṭār; God wishes to lighten your burden, for the human was created weak; It is forbidden to inherit women against their will or to hold them back to recover gifts; One who cannot afford a free wife may marry a believing slave woman with her people's leave; Foster mothers and foster sisters by nursing are forbidden in marriage; A married slave woman who commits indecency receives half the punishment of a free woman; Man who lies with a slave woman designated to another man: inquiry and guilt offering, not death, because she is not free; The husband gives the bride her marriage gift (ṣaduqa, ajr) as her own; she may freely remit part; Married women are forbidden except those one's right hand possesses (captives); What becomes of a dead man's widow within his family [contrast between the texts]; A man must marry his dead brother's widow to raise seed for the brother; Hero marries two sisters.

leads.title: Graduated purification offering and the guilt (asham) offering ↔ The debt verse
leads.summary: These two units share 1 motifs: a witness who hears a public adjuration and withholds testimony bears guilt.

passages.note: A witness who hears a public adjuration and withholds testimony bears guilt (qol alah, public curse on withholders)
passages.text: וְנֶ֣פֶשׁ כִּֽי תֶחֱטָ֗א וְשָֽׁמְעָה֙ ק֣וֹל אָלָ֔ה וְה֣וּא עֵ֔ד א֥וֹ רָאָ֖ה א֣וֹ יָדָ֑ע אִם ל֥וֹא יַגִּ֖יד וְנָשָׂ֥א עֲוֺנֽוֹ

passages.note: A witness who hears a public adjuration and withholds testimony bears guilt (witnesses must not refuse; concealing testimony makes the heart sinful)
passages.text: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓا۟ إِذَا تَدَايَنتُم بِدَيْنٍ إِلَىٰٓ أَجَلٍ مُّسَمًّى فَٱكْتُبُوهُ وَلْيَكْتُب بَّيْنَكُمْ كَاتِبٌۢ بِٱلْعَدْلِ وَلَا يَأْبَ كَاتِبٌ أَن يَكْتُبَ كَمَا عَلَّمَهُ ٱللَّهُ فَلْيَكْتُبْ وَلْيُمْلِلِ ٱلَّذِى عَلَيْهِ ٱلْحَقُّ وَلْيَتَّقِ ٱللَّهَ رَبَّهُۥ وَلَا يَبْخَسْ مِنْهُ شَيْـًٔا فَإِن كَانَ ٱلَّذِى عَلَيْهِ ٱلْحَقُّ سَفِيهًا أَوْ ضَعِيفًا أَوْ لَا يَسْتَطِيعُ أَن يُمِلَّ هُوَ فَلْيُمْلِلْ وَلِيُّهُۥ بِٱلْعَدْلِ وَٱسْتَشْهِدُوا۟ شَهِيدَيْنِ مِن رِّجَالِكُمْ فَإِن لَّمْ يَكُونَا رَجُلَيْنِ فَرَجُلٌ وَٱمْرَأَتَانِ مِمَّن تَرْضَوْنَ مِنَ ٱلشُّهَدَآءِ أَن تَضِلَّ إِحْدَىٰهُمَا فَتُذَكِّرَ إِحْدَىٰهُمَا ٱلْأُخْرَىٰ وَلَا يَأْبَ ٱلشُّهَدَآءُ إِذَا مَا دُعُوا۟ وَلَا تَسْـَٔمُوٓا۟ أَن تَكْتُبُوهُ صَغِيرًا أَوْ كَبِيرًا إِلَىٰٓ أَجَلِهِۦ ذَٰلِكُمْ أَقْسَطُ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ وَأَقْوَمُ لِلشَّهَٰدَةِ وَأَدْنَىٰٓ أَلَّا تَرْتَابُوٓا۟ إِلَّآ أَن تَكُونَ تِجَٰرَةً حَاضِرَةً تُدِيرُونَهَا بَيْنَكُمْ فَلَيْسَ عَلَيْكُمْ جُنَاحٌ أَلَّا تَكْتُبُوهَا وَأَشْهِدُوٓا۟ إِذَا تَبَايَعْتُمْ وَلَا يُضَآرَّ كَاتِبٌ وَلَا شَهِيدٌ وَإِن تَفْعَلُوا۟ فَإِنَّهُۥ فُسُوقٌۢ بِكُمْ وَٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ وَيُعَلِّمُكُمُ ٱللَّهُ وَٱللَّهُ بِكُلِّ شَىْءٍ عَلِيمٌ

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml): parallel. Lev 5:1 wĕ-šāmĕʿâ qôl ʾālâ wĕ-hûʾ ʿēd ʾô rāʾâ ʾô yādāʿ ʾim lôʾ yaggîd wĕ-nāśāʾ ʿăwōnô: a witness who keeps silent bears guilt; Q 2:282-283 wa-lā yaʾba sh-shuhadāʾu idhā mā duʿū ... wa-lā taktumū sh-shahādata wa-man yaktumhā fa-innahu āthimun qalbuhu: witnesses must not refuse when called, and whoever hides testimony has a sinful heart. Guilt on the witness (ʿāwōn) vs sin in the heart (āthimun qalbuhu).
Shared motifs, rarest first: A witness who hears a public adjuration and withholds testimony bears guilt (weight 6.3). Pair score 6.3.

Only in Graduated purification offering and the guilt (asham) offering: The poorest bring a flour sin offering without oil or frankincense; One is guilty even for a sin committed without knowing; Restitution to the wronged person precedes the atonement offering; Sacrilege (me'ilah) against the holy things of YHWH; Touching an unclean carcass or human impurity makes one guilty; Defrauding a neighbor with a false oath is a trespass against God; The priest pinches off the bird's head with his fingernail (melikah); Expiation in steps according to what one can afford [divergence between the texts]; The guilt offering is a ram assessed in silver shekels; The priest burns a handful as the token or 'memorial' portion (azkarah); Liability for oaths spoken thoughtlessly [contrast between the texts]; The priest makes atonement and the sinner is forgiven; and 8 more.

Only in The debt verse: A debt for a fixed term must be written by a just scribe, dictated by the debtor or his guardian; Two male witnesses, or one man and two women so that if one errs the other reminds her; On a journey without a scribe a pledge in hand (rihan maqbuda) is taken; A land deed made in a sealed copy and an open copy, witnessed and the silver weighed; How many witnesses are required [divergence between the texts]; No one put to death on the testimony of a single witness.

leads.title: Graduated purification offering and the guilt (asham) offering ↔ Oaths, divorce, nursing and widowhood
leads.summary: These two units share 2 motifs: liability for oaths spoken thoughtlessly [contrast between the texts], a rash oath spoken thoughtlessly requires atonement.

Shared motifs, rarest first: Those who do not prostrate when the scripture is recited to them are rebuked (a prostration verse) [contrast between the texts] (weight 6.7). Pair score 6.7.

Only in Ezra reads the Torah at the Water Gate; the day declared holy; Sukkot restored: Assembly answers the blessing 'Amen, Amen' with uplifted hands and prostrates; Festival booths built on rooftops, in courtyards and in public squares; Leaders forbid weeping and mourning because the day is holy; 'The joy of the LORD is your strength'; Studying the Torah, the leaders find a forgotten commandment written in it; Levites explain the Torah reading so the people understand it; When the reader opens the scroll all the people stand up; On the holy day the people eat, drink and send portions to those who have nothing; Reader stands on a wooden tower made for the purpose, flanked by named men; The people gather 'as one man' to Jerusalem; An eighth day of solemn assembly ('atseret) closes the seven-day festival; Fruit of a goodly tree, palm fronds, leafy boughs and brook willows taken for the festival; and 5 more.

Only in The splitting: the book in the right hand: O man, you are toiling laboriously toward your Lord, and you will meet him; 'You will surely ride (pass through) stage upon stage' (tabaqan 'an tabaq); Whoever is given his book in his right hand has an easy reckoning; whoever is given it behind his back cries for destruction; Sky and earth 'listen to their Lord' (adhinat) and are made to obey at the end; Those who do not prostrate when the scripture is recited to them are rebuked (a prostration verse); At the end the earth is stretched out, casts out what is in it (its burdens) and empties itself; At the end the sky is split, cleft or opened (infatarat, inshaqqat, furijat); Oath introduced by the negated formula 'No! I swear by...' (la uqsimu / fa-la uqsimu); A series of oaths by natural phenomena (dawn, night, day, sun, moon, sky, earth, stars, winds) opens or punctuates a passage; God keeps a book in which names are written and from which sinners are blotted.

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml): echo, parallel. Neh 9:18-19 ʿāśû lāhem ʿēgel massēkâ ... wĕ-ʾattâ bĕ-raḥămêkā ha-rabbîm lōʾ ʿăzabtām: the people (not Aaron) made the calf and God, ʾĕlôah sĕlîḥôt (9:17), did not abandon them; Q 2:51-52 ittakhadhtumu l-ʿijla ... thumma ʿafawnā ʿankum. The Nehemiah recital and the Quran tell the calf alike, against Exod 32. Neh 9:26 wĕ-ʾet nĕbîʾêkā hārāgû ʾăšer hēʿîdû bām; Q 2:61 wa-yaqtulūna n-nabiyyīna bi-ghayri l-ḥaqqi: Israel killed the prophets. Neh confesses it in the first person plural; the Quran says it of them in the third person as the cause of humiliation and wrath (ḍuribat ʿalayhimu dh-dhillatu ... wa-bāʾū bi-ghaḍabin). Neh 9:17 wa-yyittĕnû rōʾš lāšûb lĕ-ʿabdūtām: the people want to go back to slavery in Egypt; Q 2:61 ihbiṭū miṣran fa-inna lakum mā saʾaltum: Moses retorts 'go down to Egypt (or: a town), you shall have what you asked'. The wish to return is turned into an ironic command.

Shared motifs, rarest first: People propose appointing a leader to go back to Egypt (weight 6.3); God leads the people in a pillar of cloud by day and a pillar of fire by night (weight 5.1); Israel killed the prophets who warned them (weight 5.1); People make a molten calf while the leader is on the mountain (weight 4.7). Pair score 21.2.

Only in Fast of the twenty-fourth and the Levites' historical confession: God found Abraham's heart faithful (ne'eman) before him; God chose Abram, brought him out of Ur of the Chaldeans and renamed him Abraham; Call to bless God 'from everlasting to everlasting'; God's ordinances are those 'which a man shall do and live by them'; 'You give life to them all' - God sustains all creation; God gave his good spirit to instruct the people in the wilderness; Levites stand on a platform and cry out to God with a loud voice; A quarter of the day spent reading the Torah and a quarter confessing and bowing; God made known his holy Sabbath at Sinai; The seed of Israel separate themselves from all foreigners; Drowned enemies sink like a stone or like lead in mighty waters; Closing doxology: glory to your Lord, Lord of might, above what they describe; peace on the messengers; praise to God, Lord of the worlds; and 14 more.

Only in Exodus, the calf and the wilderness: Israelites who demanded to see God are struck by a thunderbolt and then raised after their death; Who or what parts the sea [divergence between the texts]; Israel's belief or disbelief in Moses after the sea [divergence between the texts]; The cloud over Israel in the wilderness: guide or shade [divergence between the texts]; Longing for fish, cucumbers, melons, leeks, onions and garlic of Egypt; Longing for fish, cucumbers, melons, leeks, onions and garlic of Egypt [divergence between the texts]; God's pardon after the golden calf [divergence between the texts]; People make a molten calf while the leader is on the mountain [divergence between the texts]; The killing of Israelites after the golden calf [divergence between the texts]; Wind brings quail in vast quantity to feed the people [divergence between the texts]; Humans seeing God [contrast between the texts]; Israel told to enter the town's gate prostrating and say 'hitta' (remission); the wrongdoers change the word; and 14 more.

Same image: Neh 9:26 wa-yyašlikû ʾet tôrātĕkā ʾaḥărê gawwām 'they cast your Torah behind their back'; Q 2:101 nabadha farīqun mina lladhīna ūtū l-kitāba kitāba llāhi warāʾa ẓuhūrihim 'a party of those given the Book cast God's Book behind their backs'. evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml): divergence. Num 11:31-33 wĕ-rûaḥ nāsaʿ mēʾēt YHWH wa-yyāgoz śalwîm ... ha-bbāśār ʿôdennû bên šinnêhem ... wa-yyak YHWH bā-ʿām: quail given in anger, and a plague while the meat is in their teeth; Q 2:57 wa-anzalnā ʿalaykumu l-manna wa-s-salwā kulū min ṭayyibāti mā razaqnākum: quail as plain provision ('eat of the good things'), with no craving and no plague. Num 11:5 zākarnû ʾet ha-ddāgâ ... ʾēt ha-qqiššuʾîm wĕ-ʾēt hā-ʾăbaṭṭiḥîm wĕ-ʾet he-ḥāṣîr wĕ-ʾet ha-bbĕṣālîm wĕ-ʾet ha-ššûmîm; Q 2:61 baqlihā wa-qiththāʾihā wa-fūmihā wa-ʿadasihā wa-baṣalihā. Three cognates (qiššuʾîm / qiththāʾ, bĕṣālîm / baṣal, šûmîm / fūm). Changed: in Numbers the craving is for meat (mî yaʾăkilēnû bāśār, 11:4) and the food is remembered from Egypt; in the Quran the complaint is 'one food' (lan naṣbira ʿalā ṭaʿāmin wāḥidin), fish and meat are absent, lentils are added. The outcome changes too: plague in Num 11:33; in Q ihbiṭū miṣran fa-inna lakum mā saʾaltum, and humiliation.

Shared motifs, rarest first: Wind brings quail in vast quantity to feed the people [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); Longing for fish, cucumbers, melons, leeks, onions and garlic of Egypt [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); Longing for fish, cucumbers, melons, leeks, onions and garlic of Egypt (weight 6.7); Wind brings quail in vast quantity to feed the people (weight 5.8); The people grumble against their leaders about food or water (weight 5.1). Pair score 30.9.

Only in Taberah, the craving, the seventy elders and the quail: Fire from God burns part of the camp for complaint; Spirit rests on people and they prophesy (ecstatically); A 'rabble' or mixed crowd among the people instigates sin; Leader refuses to silence prophets outside the sanctioned place: 'would all were prophets'; Bird-meat as desired food: punished or granted [contrast between the texts]; Leader doubts God can supply; God replies 'Is my hand too short?' [divergence between the texts]; Craved food granted, then plague strikes while meat is still in their mouths; Leader protests he did not conceive or bear the people to carry them like a nurse; Exhausted leader asks God to kill him; Manna described: like coriander seed, look of bdellium, taste of oil cakes, falls with the dew; Seventy elders of Israel accompany or assist the prophet [divergence between the texts]; Some of the spirit on the leader is taken and placed on others; and 4 more.

Only in Exodus, the calf and the wilderness: Israelites who demanded to see God are struck by a thunderbolt and then raised after their death; Who or what parts the sea [divergence between the texts]; Israel's belief or disbelief in Moses after the sea [divergence between the texts]; The cloud over Israel in the wilderness: guide or shade [divergence between the texts]; God's pardon after the golden calf [divergence between the texts]; People make a molten calf while the leader is on the mountain [divergence between the texts]; The killing of Israelites after the golden calf [divergence between the texts]; Humans seeing God [contrast between the texts]; People propose appointing a leader to go back to Egypt; Israel told to enter the town's gate prostrating and say 'hitta' (remission); the wrongdoers change the word; Ruler orders the killing of male infants [divergence between the texts]; Moses strikes the rock for water [divergence between the texts]; and 13 more.

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/06-hb-quran.yaml): parallel. wə-nəṯattem ʾeṯ-naḥălāṯô li-šʾērô ha-qqārōḇ ʾēlâw mi-mmišpaḥtô ... lə-ḥuqqaṯ mišpāṭ vs. wa-ulū l-arḥāmi baʿḍuhum awlā bi-baʿḍin fī kitābi llāh: inheritance goes by nearness of blood as written law. The Quran adds that it comes before the bond of faith and emigration (mina l-muʾminīna wa-l-muhājirīn).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Blood relatives are nearer to one another (in inheritance) in God's book (weight 6.3). Pair score 6.3.

Only in Daughters of Zelophehad; Moses views the land; Joshua commissioned: Petition so that a dead man's name not be lost from his clan; Leader ordains his successor by laying hands and sharing his 'splendor' (hod); Decisions sought through the priest's Urim; God addressed as 'God of the spirits of all flesh'; Statutory order of inheritance: son, daughter, brothers, father's brothers, nearest kin [divergence between the texts]; Rules for who inherits and in what order or share [divergence between the texts]; Whether and how daughters inherit [divergence between the texts]; Statutory order of inheritance: son, daughter, brothers, father's brothers, nearest kin; Leader defers an unprecedented legal case to a divine oracle; Leader shown the whole land from a mountaintop but may not enter; Daughters petition and win the right to inherit when there is no son; Prayer that the people not be 'like sheep without a shepherd'; and 1 more.

Only in Two hearts, zihar, adopted sons, and the prophet's wives as mothers: God took a solemn covenant (mithaq) from the prophets: Muhammad, Noah, Abraham, Moses and Jesus son of Mary; Adopted sons are not one's sons; call them by their fathers' names, or as brothers in religion and clients; God has not put two hearts inside any man; The prophet's wives are the mothers of the believers and may not be married after him; Whether an adopted or fostered child counts as one's own child [contrast between the texts]; Zihar: a husband declaring his wife 'like my mother's back'; she is not his mother, the saying is false and abhorrent.

leads.summary: These two units share 4 motifs: rules for who inherits and in what order or share [divergence between the texts], whether and how daughters inherit [divergence between the texts], statutory order of inheritance: son, daughter, brothers, father's brothers, nearest kin, daughters petition and win the right to inherit when there is no son.

passages.note: Rules for who inherits and in what order or share [divergence between the texts] (Num 27:8-11 ʾîš kî yāmût û-bēn ʾên lô wĕ-haʿăbartem ʾet naḥălātô lĕ-bittô wĕ-ʾim ʾên lô bat ... lĕ-ʾeḥāyw ... la-ʾăḥê ʾābîw ... li-šʾērô ha-qqārōb: a chain of single heirs: son, else daughter, else brothers, father's brothers, nearest kin; Q 4:11-12 li-dh-dhakari mithlu ḥaẓẓi l-unthayayn ... wa-li-abawayhi li-kulli wāḥidin minhumā s-sudusu ... wa-lakum niṣfu mā taraka azwājukum: fixed fractional shares for several heirs at once, daughters with sons, parents, and spouses (absent from Num 27), siblings only for the kalāla. A sequence of exclusive heirs becomes a set of simultaneous shares. The Quran begins yūṣīkumu llāhu 'God charges you' (cf. ḥuqqat mišpāṭ, 27:11).)

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml): divergence. Num 27:8-11 ʾîš kî yāmût û-bēn ʾên lô wĕ-haʿăbartem ʾet naḥălātô lĕ-bittô wĕ-ʾim ʾên lô bat ... lĕ-ʾeḥāyw ... la-ʾăḥê ʾābîw ... li-šʾērô ha-qqārōb: a chain of single heirs: son, else daughter, else brothers, father's brothers, nearest kin; Q 4:11-12 li-dh-dhakari mithlu ḥaẓẓi l-unthayayn ... wa-li-abawayhi li-kulli wāḥidin minhumā s-sudusu ... wa-lakum niṣfu mā taraka azwājukum: fixed fractional shares for several heirs at once, daughters with sons, parents, and spouses (absent from Num 27), siblings only for the kalāla. A sequence of exclusive heirs becomes a set of simultaneous shares. The Quran begins yūṣīkumu llāhu 'God charges you' (cf. ḥuqqat mišpāṭ, 27:11). Num 27:7-8 kēn bĕnôt ṣĕlopḥād dōbĕrōt ... û-bēn ʾên lô wĕ-haʿăbartem ʾet naḥălātô lĕ-bittô: daughters inherit only when there is no son, after a petition; Q 4:11 fa-in kunna nisāʾan fawqa thnatayni fa-lahunna thuluthā mā taraka wa-in kānat wāḥidatan fa-lahā n-niṣf: daughters always inherit, alongside sons at half a son's share, and alone take a half or two-thirds.

Shared motifs, rarest first: Rules for who inherits and in what order or share [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); Whether and how daughters inherit [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.3); Statutory order of inheritance: son, daughter, brothers, father's brothers, nearest kin (weight 6.3); Daughters petition and win the right to inherit when there is no son (weight 5.8). Pair score 25.0.

Only in Daughters of Zelophehad; Moses views the land; Joshua commissioned: Petition so that a dead man's name not be lost from his clan; Leader ordains his successor by laying hands and sharing his 'splendor' (hod); Decisions sought through the priest's Urim; God addressed as 'God of the spirits of all flesh'; Statutory order of inheritance: son, daughter, brothers, father's brothers, nearest kin [divergence between the texts]; Blood relatives are nearer to one another (in inheritance) in God's book; Leader defers an unprecedented legal case to a divine oracle; Leader shown the whole land from a mountaintop but may not enter; Prayer that the people not be 'like sheep without a shepherd'; The great leader is denied entry into the promised land for a lapse.

Only in The fixed shares of inheritance: Shares are distributed only after a bequest (waṣiyya) and debts are paid; Inheritance fixed in fractions (one half, a third, a quarter, a sixth, an eighth, two-thirds); Husband and wife inherit fixed shares from each other; Three named daughters (Jemimah, Keziah, Keren-happuch), the most beautiful in the land, inherit among their brothers; Who receives a double share of inheritance [divergence between the texts]; One who dies without parent or child (kalāla): brothers and sisters inherit fixed shares; A son (or brother) inherits the share of two daughters (or sisters); 'These are the bounds (hudud) of God; do not approach (or transgress) them'; Paradise as gardens (of ʿAdn) beneath which rivers flow, where the righteous abide forever.

In Numbers Moses takes the case to God and God approves the daughters; in the Quran the woman herself complains to God, God has heard, and the ruling on ẓihār follows. Only in The suspected adulteress and the bitter water: Suspected wife's offering is barley flour without oil or frankincense, a 'meal offering of jealousy'; Ordeal curse: the guilty woman's belly swells and her thigh falls; Person responds to an imprecation with 'Amen, amen'; Holy water in an earthen vessel mixed with dust from the sanctuary floor; Husband who brings an ordeal accusation is free of guilt whatever the result; Woman cleared by the ordeal will bear children; A 'spirit of jealousy' comes over a husband who suspects his wife; Priest unbinds the accused woman's hair before God; Written curses are wiped into water that the accused then drinks; Challenge to mutual imprecation (mubahala): gather sons, women and selves and invoke God's curse on the liars; An oath before God settles a suspicion that cannot be proven.

Only in Edom's crimes against Jacob and the Day of YHWH: Edom condemned for violence against its brother Jacob in the day of Jerusalem's fall; Exiles of Jerusalem in Sepharad and of Israel as far as Zarephath will repossess the land; The enemy stands at the crossroads to cut off and hand over the fleeing survivors; Prohibition of gloating over, looting or handing over one's brother on the day of his calamity; The house of Jacob will be fire and the house of Esau stubble consumed without survivor; On Mount Zion there will be escape (peletah) and holiness in the coming judgment; Saviors ascend Mount Zion to judge Mount Esau, and the kingship shall be YHWH's; Conquerors cast lots over a captured city or its nobles; The wicked should drink of the wrath (cup) of Shaddai.

Only in The cloaked one: the call, the opponent, and the nineteen: The people of paradise ask the damned what brought them to hell; they answer: we did not pray, feed the poor, and we denied the day; Those who turn from the reminder are like startled wild asses fleeing from a lion (qaswara); Every soul is held in pledge (rahina) for what it has earned; Each of the deniers wants to be given scrolls unrolled (personally revealed) to him; Over hell are nineteen; its keepers are angels whose number is made a test; God created a man alone, gave him extended wealth and sons present at his side; yet he wants more and stubbornly opposes the signs; The companions of the right (ashab al-yamin, al-maymana) are saved; the companions of the left (al-mash'ama) are damned; The intercession of intercessors will not benefit the damned; no soul has power to help another; The people wash their garments to prepare for God's appearance; You will not will unless God wills; Prophet wraps his face in his mantle on hearing God; An opponent dismisses the revelation as inherited sorcery (sihr yu'thar) or 'only the word of a mortal'; and 5 more.

Only in Sayings on honest scales, generosity and the fate of the wicked: A city exults at the prosperity of the righteous and shouts for joy when the wicked perish; Like a gold ring in a pig's snout is a beautiful woman without discretion; The people curse him who withholds grain, but blessing is on the head of him who sells it; He who troubles his household will inherit the wind; He who trusts in riches falls; the righteous sprout like green leaves; If the righteous is repaid on earth, how much more the wicked and the sinner; The fruit of the righteous is a tree of life and the wise man 'takes souls' (wins people); Treasures of wickedness do not profit, but righteousness (tsedaqah) delivers from death; The righteous is rescued from trouble and the wicked goes in his place (as his ransom); The rich man thinks his garden will never perish and the Hour will never come; One scatters and yet increases; the generous soul is made fat and who waters will be watered; Pride goes before destruction and a haughty spirit before stumbling; and 6 more.

Only in Shu'ayb and Midian: The prophet forbids his people to lie in wait on every road, threatening and turning people from God's way; The prophet turns from his destroyed people: 'I conveyed the message and advised you'; The elite threaten the prophet and believers: expulsion unless they return to the old religion; A people is destroyed by an earthquake/tremor (al-rajfa); The chiefs (al-mala') of the prophet's people accuse him of error or folly and reject him; The destroyed are as if they had never lived in their land; Morning finds the destroyed lying prostrate (jathimin) in their dwellings; Prophet's refrain to his people: 'Worship God; you have no god other than him'.

passages.note: He who is gracious to the poor lends to YHWH, and he will repay him (Prov 19:17 malwēh YHWH ḥônēn dāl û-gĕmūlô yĕšallem lô: who is kind to the poor lends to YHWH, who repays; Q 2:245 man dhā lladhī yuqriḍu llāha qarḍan ḥasanan fa-yuḍāʿifahu lahu aḍʿāfan kathīratan: lend God a goodly loan and he multiplies it many times. The Quran drops the poor as the go-between (the loan is given to God directly, by context for fighting in his way, 2:244) and raises repayment to manifold increase.)

passages.note: Whatever misfortune strikes people is for what their own hands have earned, though God pardons much (ʾiwwelet ʾāḏām təsallēp̄ darkô wə-ʿal YHWH yizʿap̄ libbô (a man's folly ruins his way, and his heart rages against YHWH) vs. wa-mā aṣābakum min muṣībatin fa-bi-mā kasabat aydīkum wa-yaʿfū ʿan kathīr. Both place the blame on man, not God; the Quran adds that God pardons much.)

Both place the blame on man, not God; the Quran adds that God pardons much.
Shared motifs, rarest first: Whatever misfortune strikes people is for what their own hands have earned, though God pardons much (weight 6.7). Pair score 6.7.

Only in Sayings on the poor, the king's wrath and the sluggard: A man's folly ruins his way and his heart rages against YHWH; A son who ruins his father and chases away his mother brings shame; He who finds a wife finds a good thing and obtains favor from YHWH; a prudent wife is from YHWH; Giving as a loan to God, repaid by him [divergence between the texts]; The king's wrath is like the growling of a young lion; his favor like dew on the grass; A quarrelsome wife is like a continual dripping (of a leaking roof); The sluggard buries his hand in the dish and will not even bring it back to his mouth; Strike a scoffer and the simple will learn prudence; The poor is hated even by his neighbor, but the rich has many friends; A rod is for the back of the fool (the senseless); The slow to anger is better than a mighty man, and he who rules his spirit than he who takes a city; Wisdom or the fear of YHWH adds days and years of life; the years of the wicked are shortened; and 6 more.

Only in Israel's covenant and twelve chiefs; the Christians' forgotten portion: A messenger comes after an interval (fatra) without messengers; The Messenger makes clear much of the scripture they used to hide; Israel called sons of God [response between the texts]; God cast enmity and hatred among them until the day of resurrection; They forgot a portion of what they were reminded of; Those who say 'God is the Messiah son of Mary' have disbelieved; The people's hearts are called hard (Arabic q-s-w, Hebrew q-sh-h), or God makes them so; God raised twelve chieftains (nuqabāʾ) from Israel when taking their covenant; Israel called sons of God; Accusation that some People of the Book distort (yuharrifuna) God's word after understanding it; Twelve men sent to scout the promised land.

Shared motifs, rarest first: He who increases wealth by interest and usury gathers it for one who is gracious to the poor (weight 6.3); Do not charge interest to the poor of my people (weight 5.8). Pair score 12.1.

Only in Sayings on torah, rulers, usury and confession: A man burdened with the blood of a life will flee to the pit; let no one support him; He who conceals his transgressions will not prosper, but he who confesses and forsakes them will obtain mercy; A faithful man has many blessings, but he who hastens to be rich will not go unpunished; When a land transgresses it has many rulers; with a man of understanding it endures; A poor man who oppresses the poor is like a beating rain that leaves no food; When the wicked rise men hide themselves; when they perish the righteous increase; He who turns his ear from hearing the torah, even his prayer is an abomination; He who robs his father or mother and says 'It is no transgression' is companion to a destroyer; Those who forsake the torah praise the wicked; those who keep the torah contend with them; The wicked flee when no one pursues, but the righteous are bold as a lion; A wicked ruler over a poor people is a roaring lion and a charging bear; He who gives to the poor will not lack, but he who hides his eyes will get many curses; and 6 more.

Only in Usury: God blots out usury and makes charity grow; A debtor in hardship is given respite until ease; remitting it as charity is better; Trade is like usury, they say; but God permitted trade and forbade usury (riba); Those who consume usury rise like one driven mad by Satan's touch; Those who do not give up usury are warned of war from God and his messenger; they keep their principal; Whether obligations differ toward insiders and outsiders [contrast between the texts]; Relief of debtors: release or respite [divergence between the texts]; To whom and how widely the ban on interest applies [divergence between the texts]; Lending at interest or increase to a poor brother is forbidden.

passages.text: מִ֤י עָלָֽה שָׁמַ֨יִם וַיֵּרַ֡ד מִ֤י אָֽסַף ר֨וּחַ בְּחָפְנָ֡יו מִ֤י צָֽרַר מַ֨יִם בַּשִּׂמְלָ֗ה מִ֭י הֵקִ֣ים כָּל אַפְסֵי אָ֑רֶץ מַה שְּׁמ֥וֹ וּמַֽה שֶּׁם בְּ֝נ֗וֹ כִּ֣י תֵדָֽע

passages.note: Who has gone up to heaven and come down, gathered the wind in his fists, wrapped the waters in a garment? What is his name and his son's name?
passages.text: أَوْ يَكُونَ لَكَ بَيْتٌ مِّن زُخْرُفٍ أَوْ تَرْقَىٰ فِى ٱلسَّمَآءِ وَلَن نُّؤْمِنَ لِرُقِيِّكَ حَتَّىٰ تُنَزِّلَ عَلَيْنَا كِتَٰبًا نَّقْرَؤُهُۥ قُلْ سُبْحَانَ رَبِّى هَلْ كُنتُ إِلَّا بَشَرًا رَّسُولًا

passages.note: Opponents nearly lure the prophet into inventing something else; God makes him firm (kol-ʾimrat ʾĕlôah ṣərûpâ ... ʾal-tôsp ʿal-dəbārāyw pen-yôkîaḥ bəkā wəniḵzābtā; wa-in kādū la-yaftinūnaka ʿani lladhī awḥaynā ilayka li-taftariya ʿalaynā ghayrahu ... idhan la-adhaqnāka ḍiʿfa l-ḥayāti wa-ḍiʿfa l-mamāt: adding one's own words to God's word is threatened with exposure and punishment.)

passages.note: Opponents nearly lure the prophet into inventing something else; God makes him firm

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/04-hb-quran.yaml): echo. mî ʿālâ-šāmayim wayyērad ... mah-ššəmô ûmah-šem-bənô kî tēdāʿ; aw tarqā fī s-samāʾi wa-lan nuʾmina li-ruqiyyika ḥattā tunazzila ʿalaynā kitāban naqraʾuh ... hal kuntu illā basharan rasūlā: going up to heaven and coming back down is beyond any mortal. Agur asks it of God (and his son's name); the Meccans demand it of the prophet, who answers that he is only human. Cf. 17:111, lam yattakhidh waladan. kol-ʾimrat ʾĕlôah ṣərûpâ ... ʾal-tôsp ʿal-dəbārāyw pen-yôkîaḥ bəkā wəniḵzābtā; wa-in kādū la-yaftinūnaka ʿani lladhī awḥaynā ilayka li-taftariya ʿalaynā ghayrahu ... idhan la-adhaqnāka ḍiʿfa l-ḥayāti wa-ḍiʿfa l-mamāt: adding one's own words to God's word is threatened with exposure and punishment.

(weight 6.7); Opponents nearly lure the prophet into inventing something else; God makes him firm (weight 6.3). Pair score 13.0.

Only in Words of Agur son of Yakeh, confession of ignorance and prayer: Do not add to his words lest he rebuke you and you be found a liar; Every word of God is refined (tested); he is a shield to those who take refuge in him; Riddle question about God (the creator): 'What is his name, and what is the name of his son?'; Prayer for two things: keep falsehood far and give neither poverty nor riches, only my allotted bread, lest I deny God or steal; The sage declares himself more brutish than any man, without human understanding or knowledge of the Holy One; Sayings attributed to Agur son of Yakeh, an oracle (massa) addressed to Ithiel and Ucal; If they own heaven and earth, let them ascend by the cords or ways (asbab) to heaven.

Only in Near compromise, prayer times, the praised station, the spirit, the challenge and the demanded signs (Surah 17:73-100): Were angels walking the earth, God would have sent them an angel as messenger; The creator of heavens and earth is able to create the like of them (resurrection argument); The astray are gathered on their faces, blind, dumb and deaf; Opponents demand a spring gushing from the earth or a garden of palms and vines with rivers; Opponents demand that the prophet have a house of gold ornament; Opponents demand that the sky fall on them in pieces or God and the angels appear; Whenever the fire of hell abates, God increases its blaze; Even owning the treasuries of God's mercy, humans would hold back for fear of spending; Keep vigil (tahajjud) with recitation in part of the night as an extra devotion; The prophet may be raised to a 'praised station' (maqam mahmud), later read as intercession; Prayer: 'Lord, make my entrance and my exit true and grant me a helping authority'; Prayer is fixed from the sun's decline to the dark of night, with the dawn recitation; and 9 more.

Q: wa-waṣṣaynā l-insāna bi-wālidayhi ... wa-in jāhadāka ʿalā an tushrika bī ... fa-lā tuṭiʿhumā wa-ṣāḥibhumā fī d-dunyā maʿrūfan. The duty to parents is commanded by God, not by the father, and it stops where the parents urge shirk. The mother's part is grounded in pregnancy and two years of nursing (waḥnan ʿalā waḥnin wa-fiṣāluhu fī ʿāmayn), not in her tôrâ.

Shared motifs, rarest first: How far a child must obey father and mother [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); 'Hear, my son, your father's instruction and do not forsake your mother's teaching (torah)' (weight 6.3). Pair score 13.0.

Only in Proverbs 6:20-35, commandment as lamp; adultery as fire in the bosom: 'The commandment is a lamp and the teaching (torah) is light; reproofs of discipline are the way of life'; Can a man carry fire in his bosom and his clothes not burn, or walk on coals and his feet not be scorched? So is adultery; A prostitute costs a loaf of bread, but another man's wife hunts the precious life; The jealous husband shows no mercy on the day of vengeance and will accept no ransom (kofer) or bribe for adultery; When you walk it will lead you, when you lie down it will watch over you, when you wake it will talk with you; A starving thief is not despised, yet when caught he repays sevenfold, giving all the wealth of his house; Sexual relations with a neighbor's wife are forbidden; The Torah contains guidance and light; Bind the teachings around your neck (or fingers) and write them on the tablet of your heart; Warning against the 'strange woman' (ishah zarah / nokhriyyah) with smooth words.

Only in Luqman's advice to his son: Do not turn your cheek away from people in scorn or walk proudly on the earth; be modest in your walk; Associating partners with God (shirk) is a tremendous wrong; Lower your voice: the most repugnant of voices is the braying of donkeys; Luqman, a sage given wisdom by God, instructs his son; The mother carried the child in weakness upon weakness and his weaning is in two years; Even a deed the weight of a mustard seed, hidden in a rock or in heaven or earth, God will bring it forth; A community that enjoins the good and forbids the evil (al-amr bil-ma'ruf); How to treat close kin who urge one to worship other gods [contrast between the texts]; Children must treat parents well but must not obey them if they press them to associate partners with God; Whether the heavens rest on pillars [divergence between the texts]; God raised the heavens without pillars that you can see; God set firm mountains on the earth lest it sway with people; and 4 more.

passages.note: God stretches out the heavens like a tent curtain (Ps 104:2 nôṭeh šāmayim ka-yrîʿâ 'stretches out the heavens like a tent curtain'; Q 2:22 jaʿala lakumu l-arḍa firāshan wa-s-samāʾa bināʾan: earth a spread bed, sky a built canopy. Textile tent vs built structure; in the Quran both are made 'for you' (lakum).)

passages.note: God visits the earth with rain, softens it with showers, and crowns the year with harvest (Ps 104:13-14 mašqeh hārîm mē-ʿăliyyôtāyw ... lĕhôṣîʾ leḥem min hā-ʾāreṣ; Q 2:22 wa-anzala mina s-samāʾi māʾan fa-akhraja bihi mina th-thamarāti rizqan lakum: rain from above brings out food from the earth (hôṣîʾ / akhraja).)

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml): divergence, echo, parallel. Ps 104:13-14 mašqeh hārîm mē-ʿăliyyôtāyw ... lĕhôṣîʾ leḥem min hā-ʾāreṣ; Q 2:22 wa-anzala mina s-samāʾi māʾan fa-akhraja bihi mina th-thamarāti rizqan lakum: rain from above brings out food from the earth (hôṣîʾ / akhraja). Ps 104:2 nôṭeh šāmayim ka-yrîʿâ 'stretches out the heavens like a tent curtain'; Q 2:22 jaʿala lakumu l-arḍa firāshan wa-s-samāʾa bināʾan: earth a spread bed, sky a built canopy. Textile tent vs built structure; in the Quran both are made 'for you' (lakum). Ps 104:29-30 tōsēp rûḥām yigwāʿûn ... tĕšallaḥ rûḥăkā yibbārēʾûn: God takes breath and creatures die, sends his spirit and they are created, a cycle within nature; Q 2:28 kuntum amwātan fa-aḥyākum thumma yumītukum thumma yuḥyīkum thumma ilayhi turjaʿūn: the same give-and-take of life told of each person and closed by resurrection and return to God.

Shared motifs, rarest first: God takes life and gives it again [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); God stretches out the heavens like a tent curtain (weight 6.3); God visits the earth with rain, softens it with showers, and crowns the year with harvest (weight 5.3). Pair score 18.3.

Only in Psalm 104, the great creation hymn (cf. the Great Hymn to the Aten): When God takes away their breath creatures die and return to dust; when he sends his spirit they are created; Hymn praising God as creator, describing the ordering of the cosmos and its creatures; Each creature has its God-given habitat: birds in cedars, stork in junipers, ibex in mountains, hyrax in rocks; God rejoices in his works; Leviathan was formed to sport in the sea, or for God to play with; God sends forth his spirit and renews the face of the earth; At God's rebuke and thunder the primeval waters flee from the mountains to their appointed place; God gives wine to gladden the heart of man, oil to make his face shine and bread to sustain him; Self-exhortation 'Bless YHWH, O my soul'; God makes the clouds his chariot and walks on the wings of the wind; All in heaven and earth ask of him; every day he is engaged in some affair (kull yawm huwa fi sha'n); God looks at the earth and it trembles, touches the mountains and they smoke; and 38 more.

Only in Call to worship the Creator; the challenge; paradise and the gnat: God is not ashamed to strike a parable of a gnat or something smaller; Fruits in paradise resemble those of earth: 'this is what we were given before'; A challenge to rivals to prove a divine claim [divergence between the texts]; The people break the covenant God made with them; Humans were dead, given life, will die and be given life again (two deaths, two lives); Hell's fire has men and stones as its fuel; The blessed have purified spouses (azwaj mutahhara) in paradise; God summons the coastlands and nations (and their gods) to a court trial to argue their case; God fashions seven heavens; Inimitability challenge: produce a surah like it, calling on your own witnesses (tahaddi); God opens his good storehouse, the heavens, to give rain; Paradise as gardens (of ʿAdn) beneath which rivers flow, where the righteous abide forever.

leads.title: Psalm 104, the great creation hymn (cf. the Great Hymn to the Aten) ↔ Patience, Safa and Marwa, signs of creation
leads.summary: These two units share 3 motifs: ships go to and fro on the great sea, catalogue of signs: heavens and earth, alternation of night and day, ships, rain reviving dead earth, beasts, winds, clouds, rain from the sky gives life to the earth after its death, a sign of resurrection.

passages.note: Ships go to and fro on the great sea

passages.note: Ships go to and fro on the great sea

passages.note: Catalogue of signs: heavens and earth, alternation of night and day, ships, rain reviving dead earth, beasts, winds, clouds (Same inventory in nearly the same order: heavens, waters and clouds (Ps 104:3 ha-śśām ʿābîm rĕkûbô), rain watering the earth (104:13), moon and sun, darkness and night (104:19-20 tāšet ḥōšek wî-hî lāylâ), the many creatures (104:24 mālĕʾâ hā-ʾāreṣ qinyānekā), ships (104:26 šām ʾŏniyyôt yĕhallēkûn); Q 2:164 khalqi s-samāwāti wa-l-arḍi wa-khtilāfi l-layli wa-n-nahāri wa-l-fulki llatī tajrī fī l-baḥri ... min māʾin fa-aḥyā bihi l-arḍa ... wa-baththa fīhā min kulli dābbatin wa-taṣrīfi r-riyāḥi wa-s-saḥāb. The psalm praises (mah rabbû maʿăśêkā); the Quran presents the list as signs for those who reason (la-āyātin li-qawmin yaʿqilūn).)

leads.title: Psalm 104, the great creation hymn (cf. the Great Hymn to the Aten) ↔ New moons, fighting and the pilgrimage rites
leads.summary: These two units share 2 motifs: the new moons are time markers for people and for the pilgrimage, sun and moon are set to rule day and night and mark signs and seasons.

passages.note: The new moons are time markers for people and for the pilgrimage (Ps 104:19 ʿāśâ yārēaḥ lĕ-môʿădîm: the moon made for appointed times (festivals); Q 2:189 yasʾalūnaka ʿani l-ahillati qul hiya mawāqītu li-n-nāsi wa-l-ḥajj: the new moons are fixed times for people and for the pilgrimage. môʿădîm / mawāqīt, both from roots for 'appointed time'.)

passages.note: God made the night a garment, sleep a rest, and the day a rising (nushūr) (jaʿala lakumu l-layla libāsan wa-n-nawma subātan wa-jaʿala n-nahāra nushūran ~ yēṣēʾ ʾādām lə-foʿŏlô wə-laʿăvōdātô ʿădê ʿārev: the day for going out to work after the night; the Quran calls the daily rising nushūr, the word for resurrection.)

passages.note: A solid firmament (raqia) separates upper waters from lower waters (marajā l-baḥrayni hādhā ʿadhbun furātun wa-hādhā milḥun ujājun wa-jaʿala baynahumā barzakhan ~ wî-hî mavdîl bên mayim lā-māyim: God sets a barrier dividing two bodies of water. passages.note: Rain from the sky gives life to the earth after its death, a sign of resurrection (Ps 104:30 tĕšallaḥ rûḥăkā yibbārēʾûn û-tĕḥaddēš pĕnê ʾădāmâ; Q 2:164 wa-mā anzala llāhu mina s-samāʾi min māʾin fa-aḥyā bihi l-arḍa baʿda mawtihā: the earth renewed by God's spirit vs revived by rain after its death.)

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml): echo. arsala r-riyāḥa bushran bayna yaday raḥmatihi ~ ʿōśeh malʾākhāyw rûḥôt: winds sent as messengers (arsala / malʾākh); in the Quran they bring news of the coming rain. jaʿala lakumu l-layla libāsan wa-n-nawma subātan wa-jaʿala n-nahāra nushūran ~ yēṣēʾ ʾādām lə-foʿŏlô wə-laʿăvōdātô ʿădê ʿārev: the day for going out to work after the night; the Quran calls the daily rising nushūr, the word for resurrection.

Shared motifs, rarest first: God made the night a garment, sleep a rest, and the day a rising (nushūr) (weight 6.3); God makes winds his messengers (angels) and flaming fire his ministers (weight 5.8); A solid firmament (raqia) separates upper waters from lower waters (weight 5.6); God sends the winds as heralds before his mercy and sends down pure water from the sky (weight 5.4); Sun and moon are set to rule day and night and mark signs and seasons (weight 4.7); Rain from the sky gives life to the earth after its death, a sign of resurrection (weight 4.4). Pair score 32.3.

Only in Psalm 104, the great creation hymn (cf. the Great Hymn to the Aten): When God takes away their breath creatures die and return to dust; when he sends his spirit they are created; Hymn praising God as creator, describing the ordering of the cosmos and its creatures; Each creature has its God-given habitat: birds in cedars, stork in junipers, ibex in mountains, hyrax in rocks; God rejoices in his works; Leviathan was formed to sport in the sea, or for God to play with; God sends forth his spirit and renews the face of the earth; At God's rebuke and thunder the primeval waters flee from the mountains to their appointed place; God gives wine to gladden the heart of man, oil to make his face shine and bread to sustain him; Self-exhortation 'Bless YHWH, O my soul'; God makes the clouds his chariot and walks on the wings of the wind; All in heaven and earth ask of him; every day he is engaged in some affair (kull yawm huwa fi sha'n); God takes life and gives it again [divergence between the texts]; and 35 more.

Only in The moving shadow, the night garment, the two seas and the constellations: God extends the shadow, makes the sun its guide, then draws it back gently; God created humans from water and gave them kinship by blood and by marriage; Told to prostrate to the Merciful, the pagans ask 'What is al-Raḥmān?'; What God does after creating in six days [divergence between the texts]; Worship of the constellations or zodiac signs (mazzalot); God has inscribed a circle on the face of the waters at the boundary between light and darkness; As a sign the shadow goes back ten steps on the stairway (dial) of Ahaz; God set constellations (buruj) in the sky and adorned it for beholders; God the Ever-Living, the Self-Subsisting (al-hayy al-qayyum); God let loose the two seas, one sweet, one salt, with a barrier (barzakh) and partition between them; Creation is completed in six days; After creating the heavens and earth God established himself on the Throne (istawa 'ala l-'arsh); and 1 more.

leads.title: Psalm 104, the great creation hymn (cf. the Great Hymn to the Aten) ↔ The litany 'Is there a god with God?' and the unseen

leads.title: Psalm 104, the great creation hymn (cf. the Great Hymn to the Aten) ↔ God's earth is wide; every soul tastes death; signs and the secure sanctuary
leads.summary: These two units share 2 motifs: god provides prey for the lion and food for the raven's young that cry to him, rain from the sky gives life to the earth after its death, a sign of resurrection.

passages.note: God provides prey for the lion and food for the raven's young that cry to him (kullām ʾēleykā yəśabbērûn lāṯēṯ ʾoḵlām bə-ʿittô ... tip̄taḥ yāḏəkā yiśbəʿûn ṭôḇ vs. Allāhu yarzuquhā ... yabsuṭu r-rizqa li-man yashāʾ: the open hand of Ps 104 becomes God 'spreading' provision for whom he wills.)
passages.text: כֻּ֭לָּם אֵלֶ֣יךָ יְשַׂבֵּר֑וּן לָתֵ֖ת אָכְלָ֣ם בְּעִתּֽוֹ

passages.note: God provides prey for the lion and food for the raven's young that cry to him (kullām ʾēleykā yəśabbērûn lāṯēṯ ʾoḵlām bə-ʿittô ... tip̄taḥ yāḏəkā yiśbəʿûn ṭôḇ vs. Allāhu yarzuquhā ... yabsuṭu r-rizqa li-man yashāʾ: the open hand of Ps 104 becomes God 'spreading' provision for whom he wills.)

leads.summary: These two units share 1 motifs: catalogue of signs: heavens and earth, alternation of night and day, ships, rain reviving dead earth, beasts, winds, clouds.

The psalm praises (mah rabbû maʿăśêkā); the Quran presents the list as signs for those who reason (la-āyātin li-qawmin yaʿqilūn).)

Only in Moses, the houses as qibla, and Pharaoh's drowning faith: Only some youths (dhurriyya) of Moses' people believed him, fearing Pharaoh; As he drowns Pharaoh declares faith in the God of the Israelites, too late; Pharaoh's body is saved from the sea to be a sign for those after him; Moses prays God to obliterate Pharaoh's wealth and harden their hearts so they do not believe until they see punishment; What becomes of the drowned Pharaoh and his army after the sea [divergence between the texts]; Moses and Aaron are told to make their people's houses in Egypt a qibla (place/direction of prayer); God's instruction about the Israelites' houses in Egypt before the exodus [divergence between the texts]; Threatened believers say 'to our Lord we return' and pray for patience and to die as muslims; Why Pharaoh pursues the departing Israelites; Pharaoh acknowledges Israel's God or his own sin, and what follows; Pharaoh acknowledges Israel's God or his own sin, and what follows [divergence between the texts]; Who throws the staff before Pharaoh and what it becomes; and 9 more.

Only in Psalm 105, historical hymn from the patriarchs through Joseph and the exodus: Egypt rejoiced when Israel left, for dread of them had fallen on it; God turned the Egyptians' hearts to hate his people and deal craftily with them; Joseph's feet were hurt in fetters and his neck (nefesh) put in iron until his word came true; God sent a man ahead of them: Joseph, sold as a slave; Joseph was to bind the king's princes at will and teach his elders wisdom; At the exodus not one among the tribes stumbled (or was feeble); God calls the patriarchs his 'anointed ones' and 'prophets' and rebukes kings for their sake ('Touch not my anointed'); God opened the rock and waters gushed and ran as a river in the desert; The ancestors were few in number, sojourners wandering from nation to nation; The chain of patriarchs to whom revelation or covenant passed [divergence between the texts]; The number of signs or plagues in Egypt [divergence between the texts]; A palpable darkness covers the land for three days; and 29 more.

Only in Joseph and his brothers (Surah 12, full read): Brothers tell their father to ask the town and the caravan to confirm their story; Brothers claim the accused youth's absent brother (the hero) had also stolen before; Famished brothers bring poor goods and ask the disguised hero for alms; The brothers confess 'we were sinners' once the hero is revealed and ask their father to pray for them; Father keeps lamenting his lost son for years until his sons fear he will waste away; The patriarch claims to know from God what his sons do not know; Father promises his repentant sons to ask God's forgiveness for them later; Fleeing the seductress, the hero and the woman find her husband at the door; The bereaved father answers with 'beautiful patience' (sabr jamil) and reliance on God; The hero could not have kept his brother under the king's law, so a stratagem is needed; The hero declares he follows the religion of his fathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob; A camel-load is promised to whoever brings back the missing royal cup, with a guarantor; and 105 more.

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/02-hb-quran.yaml): divergence. A short plague list. Q: fa-arsalnā ʿalayhimu l-ṭūfāna wa-l-jarāda wa-l-qummala wa-l-ḍafādiʿa wa-l-dama āyātin mufaṣṣalātin, five plagues. Ps 105: hāfakh ʾet-mêmêhem lə-dām ... šāraṣ ʾarṣām ṣəfardəʿîm ... ʿārōv kinnîm ... ʾarbeh. Q's last three, qummal, ḍafādiʿ, dam (lice, frogs, blood), are Exodus's first three (dām, ṣəfardəʿîm, kinnîm) in reverse order. Q adds ṭūfān, which is in no HB list, and leaves out the death of the firstborn (Ps 105:36).

Shared motifs, rarest first: A poetic list of the Egyptian plagues differs in number and order from Exodus [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); The dust of the earth becomes lice on man and beast (weight 6.3); Frogs swarm out of the river into houses, beds, ovens and kneading-troughs (weight 6.0); A poetic list of the Egyptian plagues differs in number and order from Exodus (weight 6.0); Nile water is turned to blood (weight 5.8); The king's heart is hardened (by himself or by God) so he refuses to release the people [divergence between the texts] (weight 5.6); Locusts brought by an east wind devour all vegetation left after the hail (weight 5.6); The king's heart is hardened (by himself or by God) so he refuses to release the people (weight 4.6). Pair score 46.5.

Only in Psalm 105, historical hymn from the patriarchs through Joseph and the exodus: Egypt rejoiced when Israel left, for dread of them had fallen on it; God turned the Egyptians' hearts to hate his people and deal craftily with them; Joseph's feet were hurt in fetters and his neck (nefesh) put in iron until his word came true; God sent a man ahead of them: Joseph, sold as a slave; Joseph was to bind the king's princes at will and teach his elders wisdom; At the exodus not one among the tribes stumbled (or was feeble); God calls the patriarchs his 'anointed ones' and 'prophets' and rebukes kings for their sake ('Touch not my anointed'); God opened the rock and waters gushed and ran as a river in the desert; The ancestors were few in number, sojourners wandering from nation to nation; The chain of patriarchs to whom revelation or covenant passed [divergence between the texts]; The number of signs or plagues in Egypt [divergence between the texts]; A palpable darkness covers the land for three days; and 25 more.

Only in Moses before Pharaoh, the magicians and the plagues: Pharaoh's people are struck with years of drought and lack of fruits before the plagues; Enemies attribute their misfortune to the prophet as a bad omen (tatayyur); their omen is with God; The magicians' spell bewitches the people's eyes and terrifies them; The magicians offer the prophet to throw first; he tells them to throw; Pharaoh is said to have his own gods, whom Moses would make him abandon; One of the Egyptian plagues is a flood (tufan); The tyrant threatens to cut off hands and feet on opposite sides and crucify the converts; The king's courtiers advise him how to deal with the prophet and his people [contrast between the texts]; Rulers fear that a people will leave the land, or drive them out of it [divergence between the texts]; The court magicians ask the king for a reward if they win and are promised closeness; Magicians fail to imitate a wonder and confess 'This is the finger of God'; Magicians fail to imitate a wonder and confess 'This is the finger of God' [divergence between the texts]; and 17 more.

Same catalogue of limbs and senses: a-lahum arjulun yamshūna bihā am lahum aydin yabṭishūna bihā am lahum aʿyunun yubṣirūna bihā am lahum ādhānun yasmaʿūna bihā vs peh lāhem ... ʿênayim lāhem wᵉlōʾ yirʾû ʾoznayim lāhem wᵉlōʾ yišmāʿû ... yᵉdêhem wᵉlōʾ yᵉmîšûn raglêhem wᵉlōʾ yᵉhallēkû. Ps states it; Q puts it as rhetorical questions; tarāhum yanẓurūna ilayka wa-hum lā yubṣirūn (7:198) matches ʿênayim lāhem wᵉlōʾ yirʾû. (weight 6.7); Idols of wood and stone that cannot see, hear, eat or smell (weight 5.0). Pair score 18.4.

passages.note: Death described as sleep: 'lest I sleep the sleep of death' (sleep as a temporary taking of the soul)
passages.text: ٱللَّهُ يَتَوَفَّى ٱلْأَنفُسَ حِينَ مَوْتِهَا وَٱلَّتِى لَمْ تَمُتْ فِى مَنَامِهَا فَيُمْسِكُ ٱلَّتِى قَضَىٰ عَلَيْهَا ٱلْمَوْتَ وَيُرْسِلُ ٱلْأُخْرَىٰٓ إِلَىٰٓ أَجَلٍ مُّسَمًّى إِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ لَءَايَٰتٍ لِّقَوْمٍ يَتَفَكَّرُونَ

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/06-hb-quran.yaml): echo. hāʾîrâ ʿênay pen-ʾîšan ha-mmāweṯ vs. allāhu yatawaffā l-anfusa ḥīna mawtihā wa-llatī lam tamut fī manāmihā: sleep and death set side by side. Shared motifs, rarest first: Death described as sleep: 'lest I sleep the sleep of death' (weight 6.7). Pair score 6.7.

leads.title: Psalm 130, out of the depths ↔ The heirs of the Book, the Gardens of Eden and the cries of the damned
leads.summary: These two units share 1 motifs: if god took people to task for what they earned he would not leave a creature on the earth's back, but he defers them to a set term.

passages.note: If God took people to task for what they earned he would not leave a creature on the earth's back, but he defers them to a set term (ʾim-ʿăwōnôṯ tišmār-yāh ʾăḏōnāy mî yaʿămōḏ vs. wa-law yuʾākhidhu llāhu n-nāsa bi-mā kasabū mā taraka ʿalā ẓahrihā min dābbatin: if God kept strict account no one would survive. The psalm goes on to forgiveness (kî-ʿimməḵā ha-ssəlîḥâ); the Quran to a deferral until an appointed term (yuʾakhkhiruhum ilā ajalin musammā).

leads.summary: These two units share 1 motifs: the believers are nothing but brothers, so make peace between your brothers.

The psalm praises brothers living in unity; the Quran makes the faithful brothers and orders reconciliation.
Shared motifs, rarest first: The believers are nothing but brothers, so make peace between your brothers (weight 6.7). Pair score 6.7.

Only in Psalm 133, brothers dwelling together, oil and dew: 'How good and pleasant when brothers dwell together in unity'; Like the dew of Hermon descending on the mountains of Zion, where God commanded blessing, life forever; Unity likened to the fine oil on the head running down the beard of Aaron onto the collar of his robes; Superscription 'A song of ascents' (shir ha-ma'alot), Ps 120-134.

Only in Al-Hujurat: lowering voices, verifying reports, reconciling believers, backbiting and the peoples and tribes: Those who call the prophet from outside his private chambers (hujurat) lack understanding; they should wait until he comes out; They count their submission a favor to the prophet; rather God has done them a favor in guiding them; Let no people mock another, nor women other women, nor defame one another or insult with nicknames; If two groups of believers fight, make peace between them; fight the one that transgresses until it returns to God's command; The bedouin say 'we believe'; rather say 'we have submitted (aslamna)', for faith has not yet entered your hearts; One origin (one father, one pair, one God) as ground for conduct toward others [divergence between the texts]; Believers must not put themselves before God and his messenger, nor raise their voices above the prophet's or shout to him; Humanity created from a male and a female and made into peoples (shu'ub) and tribes to know one another; the noblest is the most pious; 'Have we not all one father? Has not one God created us? Why do we deal treacherously with one another?'; Slander or gossip pictured as eating [divergence between the texts]; If a corrupt person brings you news, verify it lest you harm a people in ignorance and come to regret it; Avoid suspicion, spying and backbiting: would one of you like to eat the flesh of his dead brother?; and 4 more.

leads.summary: These two units share 1 motifs: if the sea were ink for god's words it would run dry before they ran out, even with another sea.

Only in Psalm 145, acrostic praise of the King (Ashrei): YHWH upholds all who fall and raises up all who are bowed down; An alphabetic acrostic lacks one letter of the alphabet; God's mercy encompasses all things; Praise (hamd) belongs to God, Lord of the worlds (rabb al-alamin); What the fathers told is to be passed on so that coming generations will tell their children; All creatures look to God to give their food in due season; he opens his hand and they are satisfied; All flesh, or all nations, come to God to pray or worship; YHWH is near to all who call on him in truth; God called al-Rahman and al-Rahim (the Merciful, the Compassionate), paired names from the root r-h-m (womb, mercy); Formula of divine attributes: slow to anger, abundant in mercy, visits iniquity to fourth generation; The poem is an alphabetic acrostic (lines or stanzas begin with successive letters).

Only in Al-Mulk: death and life as test, seven flawless heavens, stars as missiles against devils, hell nearly bursting with rage: 'Blessed is he in whose hand is the dominion (al-mulk)'; 'Does he who created not know?' He is the Subtle, the Aware; The damned say: 'Had we listened or reasoned, we would not be among the companions of the Blaze'; As each group is thrown in, the keepers of hell ask 'Did no warner come to you?' and they admit it did; God created seven heavens in layers (tibaqan); look again and again, you will see no flaw or rift; your sight returns dazzled and weary; God adorned the lowest heaven with lamps and made them missiles (rujum) against the devils; I set before you life and death, blessing and curse: choose life [divergence between the texts]; God created heaven and earth to test which of you is best in deeds; God, who fashions the hearts of all and observes all their deeds, looks down from his dwelling; When the damned are cast in they hear hell gasping/roaring as it boils, nearly bursting with rage; God built the sky and adorned it, and it has no rifts (furuj); The stars fight from their courses against the enemy; and 3 more.

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml): echo. Interest decides who stays near God.
Shared motifs, rarest first: Do not charge interest to the poor of my people (weight 5.8). Pair score 5.8.

Only in Psalm 15 - who may dwell on your holy mountain: The righteous keeps his oath even to his own hurt and does not change; The righteous does not slander with his tongue or take up reproach against his neighbor; Entrance liturgy: 'Who may dwell on your holy mountain?' answered by a list of ethical qualifications; God shows no partiality and takes no bribe; Psalm superscription ascribes the poem to David (le-david).

Only in Psalm 150, everything that breathes, praise Yah: Catalogue of instruments for praise: shofar, harp, lyre, timbrel, dance, strings, pipe (ugav), sounding and clashing cymbals; God praised in his sanctuary and in the firmament (raqia) of his might; God's name praised with dance (mahol), timbrel and lyre; Blow the shofar at the new moon and at the full moon (keseh) on our feast day; A doxology ('Blessed be YHWH ... Amen and amen') closes one of the five books of Psalms; The cultic cry 'Hallelu-Yah' (praise Yah) closes or opens a psalm.
