evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/07-hb-quran.yaml): echo. Joy at the right hand: tôḏîʿēnî ʾōraḥ ḥayyîm śōḇaʿ śəmāḥôṯ ʾeṯ pāneyḵā nəʿimôṯ bî-mînəḵā neṣaḥ vs. fa-aṣḥābu l-maymana mā aṣḥābu l-maymana; wa-aṣḥābu l-yamīni mā aṣḥābu l-yamīn. The psalm's delights are at God's right hand; in the Quran the blessed are the people of the right (yamīn / yāmîn).
Shared motifs, rarest first: God shows the path of life; fullness of joy in his presence, pleasures at his right hand forever (weight 6.7). Pair score 6.7.

Only in Psalm 16 - YHWH my portion; not abandoned to Sheol: I have set YHWH always before me; he is at my right hand; Obscure reference to 'the holy ones who are in the land' and 'the mighty ones'; My kidneys (inner self) instruct me in the night; God will not abandon the speaker's soul to Sheol nor let his faithful one see the pit; The measuring lines have fallen for me in pleasant places; a goodly inheritance; The speaker will not pour the blood libations of other gods' followers nor take their names on his lips; YHWH is my allotted portion and my cup; you hold my lot; Superscription contains an obscure musical or liturgical term (neginot, nehilot, sheminit, gittit, alamot, shiggayon, maskil, miktam, shoshannim...); Psalm superscription ascribes the poem to David (le-david).

Only in Al-Waqi'a: the Event that abases and exalts; the three classes; the Foremost, the Companions of the Right and their Garden: In paradise they have the flesh of fowl as they desire; Immortal youths (wildan mukhalladun) circulate with goblets, ewers and a cup from a flowing spring; God created (the companions) anew and made them virgins, loving, of equal age; The Foremost are a multitude of the earlier generations and a few of the later; In paradise they hear no idle talk or sin, only the saying 'Peace, peace'; The Companions of the Right are among thornless lote trees (sidr makhdud) and layered talh (acacia/banana) with extended shade and poured water; Humanity sorted into three classes: Companions of the Right, Companions of the Left, and the Foremost (al-sabiqun) brought near; Bird-meat as desired food: punished or granted [contrast between the texts]; The earth is shaken violently and the mountains crumbled into scattered dust (haba'); Whether any fruit in the Garden is forbidden [contrast between the texts]; Abundant fruit in paradise, neither cut off (seasonless) nor forbidden; Into how many groups humankind is sorted at the end [divergence between the texts]; and 11 more.

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml): echo. allāhu nūru s-samāwāti wa-l-arḍi ... wa-man lam yajʿali llāhu lahu nūran fa-mā lahu min nūrin ~ kî ʾattâ tāʾîr nērî YHWH ʾĕlōhay yaggîha ḥoškî: God gives light to the one in darkness. The Psalm is one speaker's trust; the Quran has God as the light of the cosmos and denies light to those he does not light. yuzjī saḥāban ... wa-yunazzilu mina s-samāʾi min jibālin fīhā min baradin ... yakādu sanā barqihi yadhhabu bi-l-abṣāri ~ ḥeškat mayim ʿăvê šəḥāqîm ... ʿāvāw ʿāvərû bārād wə-gaḥălê ʾēš ... û-vərāqîm rāv: dark clouds, hail (barad / bārād) and lightning (barq / bārāq). Ps 18 is a theophany coming to rescue the king, the Quran a sign of God's ordinary governance.
Shared motifs, rarest first: God is called the speaker's lamp who lights his darkness (weight 6.3); God sends hail mingled with fire and thunder from heaven (weight 5.8). Pair score 12.1.

Only in Psalm 18 - David's song of deliverance and the storm theophany: God makes darkness his hiding place and dark waters and clouds his canopy; The king gives thanks for God's deliverance from all his enemies (song also in 2 Sam 22); At God's rebuke the channels of the sea are seen and the foundations of the world laid bare; 'Who is God except YHWH, and who is a rock besides our God?'; God reaches from on high and draws the sufferer out of many waters; Enemies beaten fine as dust and trampled like mire of the streets; Foreigners come cringing and trembling to submit to the king; God answers the distressed when he calls and removes the evil; God hears the cry from his (heavenly) temple; God shows himself loyal to the loyal and crooked to the crooked; God rides on a cherub and flies on the wings of the wind; God trains the king's hands for war so his arms bend a bow of bronze; and 13 more.

Only in The Light Verse; the mirage, the dark sea, the praising birds, hail and the creatures: Or like darkness in a deep sea, covered by wave upon wave and cloud above, darkness upon darkness, so one cannot see his own hand; The deeds of unbelievers are like a mirage in a plain that the thirsty takes for water until he reaches it and finds nothing, but finds God there; God is the light of the heavens and the earth; God's light is like a niche holding a lamp in a glass like a glittering star, lit from a blessed olive tree neither of east nor west, whose oil almost glows untouched by fire: light upon light; God sends down hail from mountains in the sky; the flash of his lightning nearly takes away sight; In houses God allowed to be raised, men undistracted by trade glorify him morning and evening; God created every beast from water: some go on their bellies, some on two legs, some on four; Birds with outspread wings glorify God; each knows its prayer and praise; With God is the fountain of life; in his light we see light; A lamp fed directly by an olive tree [divergence between the texts]; A golden lampstand with seven lamps is flanked by two olive trees that pour golden oil through golden pipes; The mirage and the thirsty traveler [divergence between the texts]; and 7 more.

evidence.text: Passages are shown for the 10 rarest of 14 shared motifs; the full list follows.

Shared motifs, rarest first: Egypt is called 'the tents of Ham' or 'the land of Ham' (weight 6.3); Moses was given nine clear signs [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.3); Swarms (arov) of insects or wild beasts fill the houses of Egypt (weight 6.3); Quail come up in the evening and cover the camp (weight 6.0); Frogs swarm out of the river into houses, beds, ovens and kneading-troughs (weight 6.0); God kills every firstborn of the land, from the king's heir to the lowest servant and cattle (weight 6.0); Water brought out of a rock by the leader's rod (weight 6.0); A poetic list of the Egyptian plagues differs in number and order from Exodus (weight 6.0); God rains bread from heaven to feed the people in the desert (weight 6.0); Nile water is turned to blood (weight 5.8); God sends hail mingled with fire and thunder from heaven (weight 5.8); Psalm retells Israel's sacred history (patriarchs, Egypt, wilderness, conquest) as instruction or praise (weight 5.6); Locusts brought by an east wind devour all vegetation left after the hail (weight 5.6); God leads the people in a pillar of cloud by day and a pillar of fire by night (weight 5.1). Pair score 82.6.

Only in Psalm 78, Asaph's historical recital from Egypt to David: God sends a band (mishlahat) of 'evil angels' (mal'akhei ra'im) to execute his wrath; Manna called 'bread of the mighty ones' (lehem abbirim), i.e. food of angels; God struck his enemies backward/in the rear (read by rabbis as the Philistines' hemorrhoids); The exodus wonders are located in 'the field of Zoan' (Tanis); The Lord awakes as from sleep like a warrior shouting from wine; God remembers that humans are flesh, a breath that passes and does not return; God rejected the tent of Joseph and tribe of Ephraim and chose Judah and Mount Zion; In the catastrophe young men are consumed by fire, maidens have no wedding song, widows do not lament; God built his sanctuary like the heights (or heavens) and like the earth founded forever; God took David from the sheepfolds, from following the nursing ewes, to shepherd his people; The ark of God is captured by enemies; God commanded the skies and opened the doors (or windows) of heaven; and 27 more.

Only in Psalm 105, historical hymn from the patriarchs through Joseph and the exodus: Egypt rejoiced when Israel left, for dread of them had fallen on it; God turned the Egyptians' hearts to hate his people and deal craftily with them; Joseph's feet were hurt in fetters and his neck (nefesh) put in iron until his word came true; God sent a man ahead of them: Joseph, sold as a slave; Joseph was to bind the king's princes at will and teach his elders wisdom; At the exodus not one among the tribes stumbled (or was feeble); God calls the patriarchs his 'anointed ones' and 'prophets' and rebukes kings for their sake ('Touch not my anointed'); God opened the rock and waters gushed and ran as a river in the desert; The ancestors were few in number, sojourners wandering from nation to nation; The chain of patriarchs to whom revelation or covenant passed [divergence between the texts]; The number of signs or plagues in Egypt [divergence between the texts]; A palpable darkness covers the land for three days; and 19 more.

Only in Twelve tribes, twelve springs, and the word changed at the gate: Twelve springs gush from the struck rock, one drinking place for each tribe; Among Moses' people is a community that guides by the truth and acts justly by it; Prophet strikes a rock and water flows out for the people [divergence between the texts]; The wrongdoers replace the word they were told with another, and a plague falls from heaven; Israel told to enter the town's gate prostrating and say 'hitta' (remission); the wrongdoers change the word; Twelve sons of the patriarch listed by their mothers; Twelve springs in the wilderness [divergence between the texts]; Prophet strikes a rock and water flows out for the people; Oasis with twelve springs and seventy palm trees.

Hearing and sight belong to their maker: amman yamliku s-samʿa wa-l-abṣāra vs hănōṭaʿ ʾōzen hălōʾ yišmāʿ ʾim-yōṣēr ʿayin hălōʾ yabbîṭ. Ps argues that God therefore sees; Q that God, not the partners, owns these faculties.
Shared motifs, rarest first: Argument: He who planted the ear, does he not hear? He who formed the eye, does he not see? (weight 6.3). Pair score 6.3.

Only in Psalm 94, God of vengeance; he who planted the ear: Invocation 'God of vengeance, shine forth; rise up, judge of the earth'; The wicked kill the widow, the stranger and the orphan; Happy is the man whom God disciplines and teaches from his Torah; The wicked ask 'How does God know? Is there knowledge in the Most High?'; The underworld called Dumah, the land of silence; God made human hearing and sight: so God sees and hears, or the senses themselves testify [divergence between the texts]; Vengeance and recompense are mine; Lament question 'How long, O God?' / 'Why have you rejected us forever?'; Those who dig a pit or spread a net for the righteous fall into it themselves; God called rock, fortress, refuge, stronghold or tower of strength.

Only in Who provides and who restores creation; the challenge of the surah: The resurrected feel they had stayed only an hour of a day; The gods are challenged to declare the former things or the things to come so that we may know they are gods; they are nothing; The idol cannot speak to its worshipers or guide them; The Quran confirms what was before it and details the Book; God brings the living out of the dead and the dead out of the living; Inimitability challenge: produce a surah like it, calling on your own witnesses (tahaddi); A foolish people who have eyes but do not see and ears but do not hear; God originates creation and then repeats it (resurrection as re-creation).

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: A specific sign marks the moment to board (weight 6.3); The flood waters are hot or boiling (weight 6.0); Animals taken aboard in pairs (weight 5.8); A member of the hero's family is lost (weight 5.8); Hero builds a vessel on divine instruction (weight 5.2); Hero warns or preaches to his people before the flood (weight 5.2); Hero's family saved with him (weight 4.5). Pair score 38.7.

Only in Noah, the boiling oven, the lost son and al-Judi: Embark: 'in the name of God be its sailing and its mooring'; God commands: 'Earth, swallow your water; sky, withhold!' and the water subsides; Noah reminds God that his son is of his family and God's promise is true; The elite scorn the prophet because only the lowest of them follow him; God answers that the drowned son is not of Noah's family: 'he is a deed not righteous'; The prophet's stories are 'tidings of the unseen' unknown to him and his people before; The ark sails through waves like mountains; What the flood hero does when the vessel comes to rest; What God says of later generations after the flood: no repeat, or punishment to come [contrast between the texts]; How the flood waters are stopped and subside [divergence between the texts]; The prophet's opponents object that only the lowliest follow him; he refuses to drive the believers away; Someone seeks refuge on a mountain and is drowned; and 22 more.

Only in Noah called a madman; the ark and the boiling oven: God forbids the prophet to address him on behalf of those who did wrong: they will be drowned; The flood hero prays to be landed at a blessed landing place; What the flood hero does when the vessel comes to rest [divergence between the texts]; When and from where the flood waters come [divergence between the texts]; The prophet's people object that he is only a human like them; had God willed he would have sent angels; Whether the flood hero speaks to his people before the flood [divergence between the texts]; Why God destroyed a generation or a people [divergence between the texts]; Who is saved with the hero from the destruction, and why [divergence between the texts]; Hero asks the deity to judge or destroy his opponents; Officers call the visiting prophet 'this madman' (meshugga').

passages.text: وَلَمَّا جَآءَ أَمْرُنَا نَجَّيْنَا شُعَيْبًا وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ مَعَهُۥ بِرَحْمَةٍ مِّنَّا وَأَخَذَتِ ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا۟ ٱلصَّيْحَةُ فَأَصْبَحُوا۟ فِى دِيَٰرِهِمْ جَٰثِمِينَ

passages.text: كَأَن لَّمْ يَغْنَوْا۟ فِيهَآ أَلَآ إِنَّ ثَمُودَا۟ كَفَرُوا۟ رَبَّهُمْ أَلَا بُعْدًا لِّثَمُودَ

passages.text: وَلَمَّا جَآءَ أَمْرُنَا نَجَّيْنَا شُعَيْبًا وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ مَعَهُۥ بِرَحْمَةٍ مِّنَّا وَأَخَذَتِ ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا۟ ٱلصَّيْحَةُ فَأَصْبَحُوا۟ فِى دِيَٰرِهِمْ جَٰثِمِينَ

passages.text: وَإِلَىٰ ثَمُودَ أَخَاهُمْ صَٰلِحًا قَالَ يَٰقَوْمِ ٱعْبُدُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ مَا لَكُم مِّنْ إِلَٰهٍ غَيْرُهُۥ هُوَ أَنشَأَكُم مِّنَ ٱلْأَرْضِ وَٱسْتَعْمَرَكُمْ فِيهَا فَٱسْتَغْفِرُوهُ ثُمَّ تُوبُوٓا۟ إِلَيْهِ إِنَّ رَبِّى قَرِيبٌ مُّجِيبٌ

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: A people is destroyed by the Shout / Blast (al-sayha) (weight 6.7); Refrain 'away with...' (bu'dan li-) the destroyed people (weight 6.0); The destroyed are as if they had never lived in their land (weight 5.8); Morning finds the destroyed lying prostrate (jathimin) in their dwellings (weight 5.6); Prophet's refrain to his people: 'Worship God; you have no god other than him' (weight 5.2). Pair score 29.2.

Only in Salih, the she-camel and the Shout: The people tell their prophet he had been their hope before this; After the crime the people are given three days' enjoyment in their homes before destruction; The people hamstring (slaughter) God's she-camel and so seal their doom; A she-camel of God is given as a sign; she must be left to graze unharmed; Unbelievers defend their practice as what they found their fathers doing; First human shaped from dust, clay or soil.

Only in Shu'ayb - measures, the prayer that commands, the clan: The people mock: 'Does your prayer command you that we abandon our fathers' gods or our way with our wealth?'; The prophet does not wish to do himself what he forbids them; he wants only reform; What God leaves you (baqiyyat Allah) is better than dishonest gain; Only the prophet's clan keeps the people from stoning him; Prophet tells deniers 'Wait, I too am waiting'; Roll call of destroyed peoples: Noah's, Ad, Thamud, Abraham's people, Midian and the overturned cities; Honest balances, weights, ephah and hin are commanded.

leads.title: Man from black mud, jinn from scorching fire, and Iblis's refusal (Surah 15:26-50) ↔ Iblis's threat to bridle Adam's offspring; sea peril; the honored children of Adam (Surah 17:61-72)
leads.summary: These two units share 6 motifs: the expelled devil vows to lie in wait on the straight path and mislead humanity, satan has no authority over god's sincere servants, only over those who follow him, god commands the angels to prostrate before the first man, and they do, the devil asks for and is granted respite until the day the dead are raised….

passages.text: فَأَزَلَّهُمَا ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ عَنْهَا فَأَخْرَجَهُمَا مِمَّا كَانَا فِيهِ وَقُلْنَا ٱهْبِطُوا۟ بَعْضُكُمْ لِبَعْضٍ عَدُوٌّ وَلَكُمْ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ مُسْتَقَرٌّ وَمَتَٰعٌ إِلَىٰ حِينٍ

passages.note: A cunning serpent persuades the woman to eat the forbidden fruit (the tempter is al-shaytan, no serpent)
passages.text: فَوَسْوَسَ لَهُمَا ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ لِيُبْدِىَ لَهُمَا مَا وُۥرِىَ عَنْهُمَا مِن سَوْءَٰتِهِمَا وَقَالَ مَا نَهَىٰكُمَا رَبُّكُمَا عَنْ هَٰذِهِ ٱلشَّجَرَةِ إِلَّآ أَن تَكُونَا مَلَكَيْنِ أَوْ تَكُونَا مِنَ ٱلْخَٰلِدِينَ

passages.note: God commands the angels to prostrate before the first man, and they do
passages.text: وَإِذْ قُلْنَا لِلْمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ ٱسْجُدُوا۟ لِءَادَمَ فَسَجَدُوٓا۟ إِلَّآ إِبْلِيسَ أَبَىٰ وَٱسْتَكْبَرَ وَكَانَ مِنَ ٱلْكَٰفِرِينَ

passages.note: God commands the angels to prostrate before the first man, and they do
passages.text: وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنَٰكُمْ ثُمَّ صَوَّرْنَٰكُمْ ثُمَّ قُلْنَا لِلْمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ ٱسْجُدُوا۟ لِءَادَمَ فَسَجَدُوٓا۟ إِلَّآ إِبْلِيسَ لَمْ يَكُن مِّنَ ٱلسَّٰجِدِينَ

passages.note: A tree of knowledge whose fruit is forbidden ('this tree', unnamed)
passages.text: وَقُلْنَا يَٰٓـَٔادَمُ ٱسْكُنْ أَنتَ وَزَوْجُكَ ٱلْجَنَّةَ وَكُلَا مِنْهَا رَغَدًا حَيْثُ شِئْتُمَا وَلَا تَقْرَبَا هَٰذِهِ ٱلشَّجَرَةَ فَتَكُونَا مِنَ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ

passages.note: A tree of knowledge whose fruit is forbidden ('this tree', unnamed; do not even approach it)
passages.text: وَيَٰٓـَٔادَمُ ٱسْكُنْ أَنتَ وَزَوْجُكَ ٱلْجَنَّةَ فَكُلَا مِنْ حَيْثُ شِئْتُمَا وَلَا تَقْرَبَا هَٰذِهِ ٱلشَّجَرَةَ فَتَكُونَا مِنَ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ

passages.note: A tree of knowledge whose fruit is forbidden ('this tree', unnamed; do not even approach it)
passages.text: فَدَلَّىٰهُمَا بِغُرُورٍ فَلَمَّا ذَاقَا ٱلشَّجَرَةَ بَدَتْ لَهُمَا سَوْءَٰتُهُمَا وَطَفِقَا يَخْصِفَانِ عَلَيْهِمَا مِن وَرَقِ ٱلْجَنَّةِ وَنَادَىٰهُمَا رَبُّهُمَآ أَلَمْ أَنْهَكُمَا عَن تِلْكُمَا ٱلشَّجَرَةِ وَأَقُل لَّكُمَآ إِنَّ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنَ لَكُمَا عَدُوٌّ مُّبِينٌ

passages.note: The devil (Iblis) alone refuses to bow to the first man
passages.text: وَإِذْ قُلْنَا لِلْمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ ٱسْجُدُوا۟ لِءَادَمَ فَسَجَدُوٓا۟ إِلَّآ إِبْلِيسَ أَبَىٰ وَٱسْتَكْبَرَ وَكَانَ مِنَ ٱلْكَٰفِرِينَ

passages.note: The devil (Iblis) alone refuses to bow to the first man
passages.text: وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنَٰكُمْ ثُمَّ صَوَّرْنَٰكُمْ ثُمَّ قُلْنَا لِلْمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ ٱسْجُدُوا۟ لِءَادَمَ فَسَجَدُوٓا۟ إِلَّآ إِبْلِيسَ لَمْ يَكُن مِّنَ ٱلسَّٰجِدِينَ

passages.note: The devil (Iblis) alone refuses to bow to the first man
passages.text: قَالَ مَا مَنَعَكَ أَلَّا تَسْجُدَ إِذْ أَمَرْتُكَ قَالَ أَنَا۠ خَيْرٌ مِّنْهُ خَلَقْتَنِى مِن نَّارٍ وَخَلَقْتَهُۥ مِن طِينٍ

passages.note: God plants a garden (Eden) in the east and places the first human there (al-janna; no location)
passages.text: وَقُلْنَا يَٰٓـَٔادَمُ ٱسْكُنْ أَنتَ وَزَوْجُكَ ٱلْجَنَّةَ وَكُلَا مِنْهَا رَغَدًا حَيْثُ شِئْتُمَا وَلَا تَقْرَبَا هَٰذِهِ ٱلشَّجَرَةَ فَتَكُونَا مِنَ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ

passages.note: God plants a garden (Eden) in the east and places the first human there (dwell in the garden; no east, no name Eden here)
passages.text: وَيَٰٓـَٔادَمُ ٱسْكُنْ أَنتَ وَزَوْجُكَ ٱلْجَنَّةَ فَكُلَا مِنْ حَيْثُ شِئْتُمَا وَلَا تَقْرَبَا هَٰذِهِ ٱلشَّجَرَةَ فَتَكُونَا مِنَ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: First humans expelled from the garden [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.3); First humans expelled from the garden (weight 6.0); A cunning serpent persuades the woman to eat the forbidden fruit (weight 6.0); God commands the angels to prostrate before the first man, and they do (weight 5.8); A tree of knowledge whose fruit is forbidden (weight 5.8); The devil (Iblis) alone refuses to bow to the first man (weight 5.8); God plants a garden (Eden) in the east and places the first human there (weight 5.6). Pair score 41.2.

Only in Adam, the angels and Iblis: God teaches Adam all the names and he recites them to the angels, who cannot; The expelled are told 'Go down, enemies to one another' with a dwelling and provision on earth for a time; God announces to the angels he will place a vicegerent (khalifa) on earth; The first man names the animals; Adam receives words from his Lord and God turns to him in forgiveness; Angels object that the new human will corrupt the earth and shed blood while they praise God; Enmity decreed at the expulsion from the garden [divergence between the texts]; The first man's response after the transgression in the garden (blame or repentance) [divergence between the texts]; The first man and the names of the creatures [divergence between the texts]; The tree forbidden to the first humans [divergence between the texts]; The garden given to the first humans to live and eat in [divergence between the texts]; God speaks to heavenly beings about making man [divergence between the texts]; and 6 more.

Only in The prostration to Adam, Iblis' refusal and the fall: Man and wife are addressed, tempted and eat together; the woman is not singled out; The first humans are sent down to earth to live and enjoy provision for a time; The devil will come at humans from before, behind, right and left; The first couple confess 'we have wronged ourselves' and ask God's forgiveness; On the earth humans live, in it they die, and from it they will be brought out; The tempter claims the tree is forbidden only lest the couple become angels or immortals; The tempter swears an oath to the first couple that he is their sincere adviser; God vows to fill hell with the devil and all who follow him; Satan whispers (waswasa) to tempt humans; God casts the proud being out from the mountain of God and destroys him from among the stones of fire, hurling him to earth before kings; How the first couple answer God after eating: shifting the blame or confessing [divergence between the texts]; God gives the adversary (Satan) leave to act against humans; and 15 more.

leads.title: Exodus, the calf and the wilderness ↔ Twelve tribes, twelve springs, and the word changed at the gate
leads.summary: These two units share 5 motifs: prophet strikes a rock and water flows out for the people, israel told to enter the town's gate prostrating and say 'hitta' (remission); the wrongdoers change the word, twelve springs in the wilderness [divergence between the texts], oasis with twelve springs and seventy palm trees….

passages.note: Prophet strikes a rock and water flows out for the people
passages.text: وَإِذِ ٱسْتَسْقَىٰ مُوسَىٰ لِقَوْمِهِۦ فَقُلْنَا ٱضْرِب بِّعَصَاكَ ٱلْحَجَرَ فَٱنفَجَرَتْ مِنْهُ ٱثْنَتَا عَشْرَةَ عَيْنًا قَدْ عَلِمَ كُلُّ أُنَاسٍ مَّشْرَبَهُمْ كُلُوا۟ وَٱشْرَبُوا۟ مِن رِّزْقِ ٱللَّهِ وَلَا تَعْثَوْا۟ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ مُفْسِدِينَ

passages.note: Prophet strikes a rock and water flows out for the people
passages.text: وَقَطَّعْنَٰهُمُ ٱثْنَتَىْ عَشْرَةَ أَسْبَاطًا أُمَمًا وَأَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَىٰ مُوسَىٰٓ إِذِ ٱسْتَسْقَىٰهُ قَوْمُهُۥٓ أَنِ ٱضْرِب بِّعَصَاكَ ٱلْحَجَرَ فَٱنۢبَجَسَتْ مِنْهُ ٱثْنَتَا عَشْرَةَ عَيْنًا قَدْ عَلِمَ كُلُّ أُنَاسٍ مَّشْرَبَهُمْ وَظَلَّلْنَا عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلْغَمَٰمَ وَأَنزَلْنَا عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلْمَنَّ وَٱلسَّلْوَىٰ كُلُوا۟ مِن طَيِّبَٰتِ مَا رَزَقْنَٰكُمْ وَمَا ظَلَمُونَا وَلَٰكِن كَانُوٓا۟ أَنفُسَهُمْ يَظْلِمُونَ

passages.note: Israel told to enter the town's gate prostrating and say 'hitta' (remission); the wrongdoers change the word

passages.note: Israel told to enter the town's gate prostrating and say 'hitta' (remission); the wrongdoers change the word
passages.text: فَبَدَّلَ ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا۟ قَوْلًا غَيْرَ ٱلَّذِى قِيلَ لَهُمْ فَأَنزَلْنَا عَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا۟ رِجْزًا مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ بِمَا كَانُوا۟ يَفْسُقُونَ

passages.note: Israel told to enter the town's gate prostrating and say 'hitta' (remission); the wrongdoers change the word
passages.text: وَإِذْ قِيلَ لَهُمُ ٱسْكُنُوا۟ هَٰذِهِ ٱلْقَرْيَةَ وَكُلُوا۟ مِنْهَا حَيْثُ شِئْتُمْ وَقُولُوا۟ حِطَّةٌ وَٱدْخُلُوا۟ ٱلْبَابَ سُجَّدًا نَّغْفِرْ لَكُمْ خَطِيٓـَٰٔتِكُمْ سَنَزِيدُ ٱلْمُحْسِنِينَ

passages.note: Twelve springs in the wilderness [divergence between the texts] (Exod 15:27 wa-yyābōʾû ʾêlimâ wĕ-šām šĕtêm ʿeśrēh ʿênōt mayim wĕ-šibʿîm tĕmārîm: twelve springs at the oasis of Elim; Q 2:60 fa-nfajarat minhu thnatā ʿashrata ʿaynan qad ʿalima kullu unāsin mashrabahum: twelve springs (cognate numeral + ʿayin) burst from the struck rock, one per tribe. The Elim springs are moved into the rock miracle; the seventy palms are dropped.)
passages.text: وَإِذِ ٱسْتَسْقَىٰ مُوسَىٰ لِقَوْمِهِۦ فَقُلْنَا ٱضْرِب بِّعَصَاكَ ٱلْحَجَرَ فَٱنفَجَرَتْ مِنْهُ ٱثْنَتَا عَشْرَةَ عَيْنًا قَدْ عَلِمَ كُلُّ أُنَاسٍ مَّشْرَبَهُمْ كُلُوا۟ وَٱشْرَبُوا۟ مِن رِّزْقِ ٱللَّهِ وَلَا تَعْثَوْا۟ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ مُفْسِدِينَ

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: Condemned believers tell the tyrant 'decree what you will; you can only decree for this worldly life' (weight 6.7); The magicians' ropes and staffs appear by sorcery to be moving like snakes (weight 6.7); Pharaoh threatens the converted magicians with cutting off hands and feet on opposite sides and crucifixion (on palm trunks) (weight 6.7); The defeated magicians fall prostrate and declare faith in the Lord of Moses and Aaron (weight 6.3); King defies the prophet: 'Who is YHWH that I should obey him?' (weight 6.3); The prophet's staff-serpent swallows the magicians' staff-serpents (weight 6.0); Prophet delivers God's demand 'Let my people go that they may serve me' (weight 5.4); Prophet's wonders are imitated by the king's magicians in a contest (weight 5.1). Only in Moses and Aaron before Pharaoh; the contest with the magicians: The contest with the magicians is set for a festival day (yawm al-zīna) at forenoon with the people assembled; From the earth humans were created, into it they return, and from it they are brought forth again; Formula: 'Peace be on whoever follows the guidance'; Pharaoh asks about the fate of former generations; the answer: their knowledge is with God in a book; The prophets are told to speak to the tyrant with gentle words, that he may take heed or fear; The defeated magicians fall prostrate and declare faith in the Lord of Moses and Aaron [divergence between the texts]; King defies the prophet: 'Who is YHWH that I should obey him?' [divergence between the texts]; God made the earth a cradle (mahd) or bed and laid out paths in it; Prophet delivers God's demand 'Let my people go that they may serve me' [divergence between the texts]; The prophet's staff-serpent swallows the magicians' staff-serpents [divergence between the texts]; In hell the damned neither die nor live; The king's heart is hardened (by himself or by God) so he refuses to release the people [divergence between the texts]; and 3 more.

Only in Moses and Pharaoh disputing; the magicians; the sea split like mountains: Pharaoh calls the Israelites 'a small band' who enrage him; God expelled the Egyptians from gardens, springs, treasures and fine dwellings and made Israel inherit them; The magicians cast their spells swearing 'By the might of Pharaoh'; Moses admits he did the killing while he was 'of those astray' and fled out of fear; Pharaoh reproaches Moses: 'Did we not raise you among us as a child, and you did your deed?'; Pharaoh threatens to imprison Moses if he takes a god other than Pharaoh; Before Pharaoh the staff becomes a manifest great serpent (thuʿbān); Prophet's wonders are imitated by the king's magicians in a contest [divergence between the texts]; The title of God in whose name Moses goes to Pharaoh; Egypt reduced the Israelites to slavery; How a public contest between God's prophet and the king's religious specialists ends [contrast between the texts]; The king musters his whole force to pursue the departing people; and 35 more.

passages.note: Whether the flood hero speaks to his people before the flood [divergence between the texts] (In Genesis Noah never speaks before the flood: wa-yyaʿaś Nōaḥ kə-khōl ʾăšer ṣiwwâ ʾōtô; he is chosen because God saw him righteous (ʾōtəkā rāʾîtî ṣaddîq). In the Quran he is a messenger (arsalnā Nūḥan ilā qawmihi) who preaches 'yā qawmi ʿbudū llāha mā lakum min ilāhin ghayruhu', and the chiefs answer that he is only a man like them, possessed (bihi jinna).)

passages.note: Lot's people threaten to expel him

passages.note: Lot's people threaten to expel him
passages.text: فَمَا كَانَ جَوَابَ قَوْمِهِۦٓ إِلَّآ أَن قَالُوٓا۟ أَخْرِجُوٓا۟ ءَالَ لُوطٍ مِّن قَرْيَتِكُمْ إِنَّهُمْ أُنَاسٌ يَتَطَهَّرُونَ

passages.text: وَأَمْطَرْنَا عَلَيْهِم مَّطَرًا فَسَآءَ مَطَرُ ٱلْمُنذَرِينَ

passages.note: The town that was rained on with an evil rain (Lot's) is passed by travelers
passages.text: وَأَمْطَرْنَا عَلَيْهِم مَّطَرًا فَسَآءَ مَطَرُ ٱلْمُنذَرِينَ

passages.note: The fate of Lot's wife (illā ʿajūzan fī l-ghābirīna ~ wat-tabbēṭ ʾištô mē-ʾaḥărāyw wat-təhî nəṣîv melaḥ: the one family member lost. Genesis names her Lot's wife and says why (she looked back) and how (pillar of salt); the Quran says only 'an old woman among those who stayed behind', with no looking back and no salt.)

passages.text: فَأَنجَيْنَٰهُ وَأَهْلَهُۥٓ إِلَّا ٱمْرَأَتَهُۥ قَدَّرْنَٰهَا مِنَ ٱلْغَٰبِرِينَ

passages.text: إِلَّا عَجُوزًا فِى ٱلْغَٰبِرِينَ

passages.text: فَأَنجَيْنَٰهُ وَأَهْلَهُۥٓ إِلَّا ٱمْرَأَتَهُۥ قَدَّرْنَٰهَا مِنَ ٱلْغَٰبِرِينَ

passages.text: ثُمَّ دَمَّرْنَا ٱلْءَاخَرِينَ

passages.note: Hero's family saved with him
passages.text: فَنَجَّيْنَٰهُ وَأَهْلَهُۥٓ أَجْمَعِينَ

passages.note: Hero's family saved with him
passages.text: فَأَنجَيْنَٰهُ وَأَهْلَهُۥٓ إِلَّا ٱمْرَأَتَهُۥ قَدَّرْنَٰهَا مِنَ ٱلْغَٰبِرِينَ

Only in Lot and the people who expel the pure: Lot's people mock his family as 'people who keep themselves pure' and order their expulsion; What Lot says to the townsmen [divergence between the texts]; Lot's townspeople turn on him [divergence between the texts].

leads.title: Moses and Pharaoh disputing; the magicians; the sea split like mountains ↔ Ta Sin; Moses at the fire, the jann-staff and the nine signs
leads.summary: These two units share 5 motifs: why pharaoh and egypt refuse despite the signs [divergence between the texts], moses' hand turned white as a sign [divergence between the texts], prophet's hand turns leprous, white as snow, and is restored as a sign, a staff thrown down becomes a serpent and turns back into a staff….

passages.note: Why Pharaoh and Egypt refuse despite the signs [divergence between the texts] (Pharaoh's response to the sign: Exod 7:13 wa-yyeḥĕzaq lēv Parʿōh wə-lōʾ šāmaʿ ʾălēhem ka-ʾăšer dibber YHWH, the heart hardened as God foretold (God hardens it himself at 14:4, 14:8); Q 26:49 has no hardening and no divine agency, only Pharaoh's rage: āmantum lahu qabla an ādhana lakum innahu la-kabīrukumu lladhī ʿallamakumu s-siḥra, with a threat of amputation and crucifixion.)
passages.text: قَالَ ءَامَنتُمْ لَهُۥ قَبْلَ أَنْ ءَاذَنَ لَكُمْ إِنَّهُۥ لَكَبِيرُكُمُ ٱلَّذِى عَلَّمَكُمُ ٱلسِّحْرَ فَلَسَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ لَأُقَطِّعَنَّ أَيْدِيَكُمْ وَأَرْجُلَكُم مِّنْ خِلَٰفٍ وَلَأُصَلِّبَنَّكُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ

passages.note: Why Pharaoh and Egypt refuse despite the signs [divergence between the texts] (Why Egypt refuses: Exod 8:15 the magicians admit ʾeṣbaʿ ʾĕlōhîm hîʾ, yet wa-yyeḥĕzaq lēv Parʿōh ... ka-ʾăšer dibber YHWH, the heart is hardened as God foretold; Q 27:14 wa-jaḥadū bihā wa-staiqanathā anfusuhum ẓulman wa-ʿuluwwan, they rejected the signs though inwardly convinced, out of wrongdoing and arrogance. Refusal by God's design becomes knowing, self-chosen denial.)
passages.text: وَجَحَدُوا۟ بِهَا وَٱسْتَيْقَنَتْهَآ أَنفُسُهُمْ ظُلْمًا وَعُلُوًّا فَٱنظُرْ كَيْفَ كَانَ عَٰقِبَةُ ٱلْمُفْسِدِينَ

passages.note: Moses' hand turned white as a sign [divergence between the texts] (wa-nazaʿa yadahu fa-idhā hiya bayḍāʾu li-n-nāẓirīna ~ wə-hinnēh yādô məṣōraʿat ka-ššāleg: the white hand. In Exodus it is leprous (məṣōraʿat), shown to Moses at the bush and meant for the Israelites (4:8-9, 4:30); in the Quran it is simply 'white for the beholders', shown to Pharaoh and his court, with no disease.)
passages.text: وَنَزَعَ يَدَهُۥ فَإِذَا هِىَ بَيْضَآءُ لِلنَّٰظِرِينَ

passages.note: Moses' hand turned white as a sign [divergence between the texts] (wa-adkhil yadaka fī jaybika takhruj bayḍāʾa min ghayri sūʾin ~ hāvēʾ nāʾ yādəkā bə-ḥêqekā ... wə-hinnēh yādô məṣōraʿat ka-ššāleg: hand into the bosom (jayb / ḥêq) and out white. The Quran's 'without evil' (min ghayri sūʾ) excludes exactly what Exodus says, that the hand was leprous (məṣōraʿat), and needs no second step of restoring it (4:7).)
passages.text: وَأَدْخِلْ يَدَكَ فِى جَيْبِكَ تَخْرُجْ بَيْضَآءَ مِنْ غَيْرِ سُوٓءٍ فِى تِسْعِ ءَايَٰتٍ إِلَىٰ فِرْعَوْنَ وَقَوْمِهِۦٓ إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوا۟ قَوْمًا فَٰسِقِينَ

passages.note: Prophet's hand turns leprous, white as snow, and is restored as a sign
passages.text: وَنَزَعَ يَدَهُۥ فَإِذَا هِىَ بَيْضَآءُ لِلنَّٰظِرِينَ

passages.note: Prophet's hand turns leprous, white as snow, and is restored as a sign (into his bosom (jayb), white without evil)
passages.text: وَأَدْخِلْ يَدَكَ فِى جَيْبِكَ تَخْرُجْ بَيْضَآءَ مِنْ غَيْرِ سُوٓءٍ فِى تِسْعِ ءَايَٰتٍ إِلَىٰ فِرْعَوْنَ وَقَوْمِهِۦٓ إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوا۟ قَوْمًا فَٰسِقِينَ

passages.note: A staff thrown down becomes a serpent and turns back into a staff
passages.text: فَأَلْقَىٰ عَصَاهُ فَإِذَا هِىَ ثُعْبَانٌ مُّبِينٌ

passages.note: A staff thrown down becomes a serpent and turns back into a staff
passages.text: وَأَلْقِ عَصَاكَ فَلَمَّا رَءَاهَا تَهْتَزُّ كَأَنَّهَا جَآنٌّ وَلَّىٰ مُدْبِرًا وَلَمْ يُعَقِّبْ يَٰمُوسَىٰ لَا تَخَفْ إِنِّى لَا يَخَافُ لَدَىَّ ٱلْمُرْسَلُونَ

passages.note: Prophet's wonders are imitated by the king's magicians in a contest
passages.text: قَالَ لِلْمَلَإِ حَوْلَهُۥٓ إِنَّ هَٰذَا لَسَٰحِرٌ عَلِيمٌ

passages.note: Prophet's wonders are imitated by the king's magicians in a contest
passages.text: يُرِيدُ أَن يُخْرِجَكُم مِّنْ أَرْضِكُم بِسِحْرِهِۦ فَمَاذَا تَأْمُرُونَ

passages.note: Prophet's wonders are imitated by the king's magicians in a contest (fa-lammā jāʾathum āyātunā mubṣiratan qālū hādhā siḥrun mubīnun ~ wa-yyiqrāʾ gam Parʿōh la-ḥăkhāmîm wə-la-mkhaššəfîm wa-yyaʿăśû gam hēm ... bə-lahăṭêhem kēn: Pharaoh's side treats the signs as magic; Exodus shows it by having the magicians copy them, the Quran by having Pharaoh's people call them 'clear sorcery'.)
passages.text: فَلَمَّا جَآءَتْهُمْ ءَايَٰتُنَا مُبْصِرَةً قَالُوا۟ هَٰذَا سِحْرٌ مُّبِينٌ

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: Why Pharaoh and Egypt refuse despite the signs [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.0); Moses' hand turned white as a sign [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.0); Prophet's hand turns leprous, white as snow, and is restored as a sign (weight 5.6); A staff thrown down becomes a serpent and turns back into a staff (weight 5.4); Prophet's wonders are imitated by the king's magicians in a contest (weight 5.1). Pair score 28.1.

Only in Moses and Pharaoh disputing; the magicians; the sea split like mountains: Pharaoh calls the Israelites 'a small band' who enrage him; God expelled the Egyptians from gardens, springs, treasures and fine dwellings and made Israel inherit them; The magicians cast their spells swearing 'By the might of Pharaoh'; Moses admits he did the killing while he was 'of those astray' and fled out of fear; Pharaoh reproaches Moses: 'Did we not raise you among us as a child, and you did your deed?'; Pharaoh threatens to imprison Moses if he takes a god other than Pharaoh; Before Pharaoh the staff becomes a manifest great serpent (thuʿbān); Prophet's wonders are imitated by the king's magicians in a contest [divergence between the texts]; The title of God in whose name Moses goes to Pharaoh; Egypt reduced the Israelites to slavery; How a public contest between God's prophet and the king's religious specialists ends [contrast between the texts]; The king musters his whole force to pursue the departing people; and 38 more.

Only in Ta Sin; Moses at the fire, the jann-staff and the nine signs: At the fire the voice proclaims 'Blessed is he who is in the fire and those around it'; God described as the one who dwells in the bush (seneh); How God names himself to Moses from the fire [divergence between the texts]; Moses was given nine clear signs; The number of signs or plagues in Egypt [divergence between the texts]; The thrown staff quivers like a jānn (small snake) and Moses turns and flees without looking back; Why Moses approaches the fire [divergence between the texts]; Moses flees from his staff turned serpent, and God's response [divergence between the texts]; Traveling with his family, the prophet sees a fire and goes to bring back a brand or find guidance there; God appears in a bush that burns without being consumed; A poetic list of the Egyptian plagues differs in number and order from Exodus; God addresses the hero with 'Fear not' in a vision; and 2 more.

leads.title: Moses and Pharaoh disputing; the magicians; the sea split like mountains ↔ The fire on the side of the Mount; the call from the tree; Aaron as helper
leads.summary: These two units share 7 motifs: moses' fear of being killed, on returning, for the egyptian's death [divergence between the texts], moses' hand turned white as a sign [divergence between the texts], aaron's role beside moses and how he is appointed [divergence between the texts], prophet's hand turns leprous, white as snow, and is restored as a sign….

passages.note: Moses' fear of being killed, on returning, for the Egyptian's death [divergence between the texts] (Fear of being killed for the old killing: in Exodus God removes it by fact, kî mētû kol hā-ʾănāšîm ham-məvaqšîm ʾet nafšekā; in the Quran Moses raises it himself (wa-lahum ʿalayya dhanbun fa-akhāfu an yaqtulūni), and God answers with his presence, 'kallā ... innā maʿakum mustamiʿūn'.)
passages.text: وَلَهُمْ عَلَىَّ ذَنۢبٌ فَأَخَافُ أَن يَقْتُلُونِ

passages.note: Moses' fear of being killed, on returning, for the Egyptian's death [divergence between the texts] (Fear of being killed for the old killing: in Exodus God removes it by fact, kî mētû kol hā-ʾănāšîm ham-məvaqšîm ʾet nafšekā; in the Quran Moses raises it himself (wa-lahum ʿalayya dhanbun fa-akhāfu an yaqtulūni), and God answers with his presence, 'kallā ... innā maʿakum mustamiʿūn'.)
passages.text: قَالَ كَلَّا فَٱذْهَبَا بِـَٔايَٰتِنَآ إِنَّا مَعَكُم مُّسْتَمِعُونَ

passages.note: Moses' fear of being killed, on returning, for the Egyptian's death [divergence between the texts] (rabbi innī qataltu minhum nafsan fa-akhāfu an yaqtulūni ~ kî mētû kol hā-ʾănāšîm ham-məvaqšîm ʾet nafšekā: the old killing as an obstacle to going back. In Exodus God removes it unasked, in the Quran Moses raises it at the call.)
passages.text: قَالَ رَبِّ إِنِّى قَتَلْتُ مِنْهُمْ نَفْسًا فَأَخَافُ أَن يَقْتُلُونِ

passages.note: Moses' hand turned white as a sign [divergence between the texts] (wa-nazaʿa yadahu fa-idhā hiya bayḍāʾu li-n-nāẓirīna ~ wə-hinnēh yādô məṣōraʿat ka-ššāleg: the white hand. In Exodus it is leprous (məṣōraʿat), shown to Moses at the bush and meant for the Israelites (4:8-9, 4:30); in the Quran it is simply 'white for the beholders', shown to Pharaoh and his court, with no disease.)
passages.text: وَنَزَعَ يَدَهُۥ فَإِذَا هِىَ بَيْضَآءُ لِلنَّٰظِرِينَ

passages.note: Moses' hand turned white as a sign [divergence between the texts] (Two signs, not three, and no leprosy: Exodus gives staff, leprous hand (məṣōraʿat ka-ššāleg), and a third sign held in reserve, Nile water turned to blood (wə-hāyû lə-dām bay-yabbāšet), meant for doubting Israelites; the Quran has fa-dhānika burhānāni min rabbika ilā Firʿawna wa-malaʾihi, two proofs aimed at Pharaoh, the hand white 'without evil' (min ghayri sūʾ), and adds 'draw your arm to your side against fear'.)

passages.note: Aaron's role beside Moses and how he is appointed [divergence between the texts] (God's answer to Moses' reluctance: wa-yyiḥar ʾap YHWH bə-Mōše ... hălōʾ ʾAhărōn ʾāḥîkā ... wə-ʾattâ tihyeh lô lēʾlōhîm (anger; Aaron as mouth, Moses as God to him) ~ qāla kallā fa-dhhabā bi-āyātinā innā maʿakum mustamiʿūna: no anger and no 'as God'; both are sent as equals (fa-dhhabā, dual).)
passages.text: وَيَضِيقُ صَدْرِى وَلَا يَنطَلِقُ لِسَانِى فَأَرْسِلْ إِلَىٰ هَٰرُونَ

passages.text: قَالَ كَلَّا فَٱذْهَبَا بِـَٔايَٰتِنَآ إِنَّا مَعَكُم مُّسْتَمِعُونَ

passages.note: Aaron's role beside Moses and how he is appointed [divergence between the texts] (Aaron's eloquence: in Exodus Moses says he is heavy of mouth, and God, angry, proposes Aaron himself: wa-yyiḥar ʾap YHWH bə-Mōše ... yādaʿtî kî dabbēr yədabbēr hûʾ ... wə-śamtā ʾet had-dəvārîm bə-fîw. In the Quran Moses proposes him, wa-akhī Hārūnu huwa afṣaḥu minnī lisānan fa-arsilhu maʿiya ridʾan yuṣaddiqunī, and God agrees without anger: sa-nashuddu ʿaḍudaka bi-akhīka. Aaron is a supporting witness (ridʾ, yuṣaddiqunī), not a mouth for Moses as God.)
passages.text: وَأَخِى هَٰرُونُ هُوَ أَفْصَحُ مِنِّى لِسَانًا فَأَرْسِلْهُ مَعِىَ رِدْءًا يُصَدِّقُنِىٓ إِنِّىٓ أَخَافُ أَن يُكَذِّبُونِ

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: Moses' fear of being killed, on returning, for the Egyptian's death [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.3); Moses' hand turned white as a sign [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.0); Aaron's role beside Moses and how he is appointed [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.0); Prophet's hand turns leprous, white as snow, and is restored as a sign (weight 5.6); Prophet protests he is heavy of mouth and tongue or 'uncircumcised of lips' (weight 5.6); An eloquent brother is appointed to speak for the hero, who is 'as God' to him (weight 5.6); A staff thrown down becomes a serpent and turns back into a staff (weight 5.4). Pair score 40.5.

Only in Moses and Pharaoh disputing; the magicians; the sea split like mountains: Pharaoh calls the Israelites 'a small band' who enrage him; God expelled the Egyptians from gardens, springs, treasures and fine dwellings and made Israel inherit them; The magicians cast their spells swearing 'By the might of Pharaoh'; Moses admits he did the killing while he was 'of those astray' and fled out of fear; Pharaoh reproaches Moses: 'Did we not raise you among us as a child, and you did your deed?'; Pharaoh threatens to imprison Moses if he takes a god other than Pharaoh; Before Pharaoh the staff becomes a manifest great serpent (thuʿbān); Prophet's wonders are imitated by the king's magicians in a contest [divergence between the texts]; The title of God in whose name Moses goes to Pharaoh; Egypt reduced the Israelites to slavery; How a public contest between God's prophet and the king's religious specialists ends [contrast between the texts]; The king musters his whole force to pursue the departing people; and 36 more.

Only in The fire on the side of the Mount; the call from the tree; Aaron as helper: Moses says his brother Aaron is more eloquent of tongue and asks for him as a helper to confirm him; Moses is called from the tree on the right bank of the valley, in the blessed spot; God calls Moses from the fire, from a bush or a tree [divergence between the texts]; Prophet lodges in 'the cave' on Horeb, the mountain of God; Where and how Moses comes to the place of his call [divergence between the texts]; The thrown staff quivers like a jānn (small snake) and Moses turns and flees without looking back; Moses flees from his staff turned serpent, and God's response [divergence between the texts]; Traveling with his family, the prophet sees a fire and goes to bring back a brand or find guidance there; A shepherd tending flocks comes to the mountain of God and is called; God appears in a bush that burns without being consumed.
Moses and Pharaoh disputing; the magicians; the sea split like mountains: tagged by Claude (model), reading the Arabic.

leads.title: Ta Sin; Moses at the fire, the jann-staff and the nine signs ↔ The fire on the side of the Mount; the call from the tree; Aaron as helper
leads.summary: These two units share 7 motifs: the thrown staff quivers like a jānn (small snake) and moses turns and flees without looking back, traveling with his family, the prophet sees a fire and goes to bring back a brand or find guidance there, moses flees from his staff turned serpent, and god's response [divergence between the texts], moses' hand turned white as a sign [divergence between the texts]….

passages.note: Traveling with his family, the prophet sees a fire and goes to bring back a brand or find guidance there (jadhwa min al-nār, 'a firebrand', that you may warm yourselves)
passages.text: فَلَمَّا قَضَىٰ مُوسَى ٱلْأَجَلَ وَسَارَ بِأَهْلِهِۦٓ ءَانَسَ مِن جَانِبِ ٱلطُّورِ نَارًا قَالَ لِأَهْلِهِ ٱمْكُثُوٓا۟ إِنِّىٓ ءَانَسْتُ نَارًا لَّعَلِّىٓ ءَاتِيكُم مِّنْهَا بِخَبَرٍ أَوْ جَذْوَةٍ مِّنَ ٱلنَّارِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَصْطَلُونَ

passages.note: Moses flees from his staff turned serpent, and God's response [divergence between the texts] (fa-lammā raʾāhā tahtazzu ka-annahā jānnun wallā mudbiran wa-lam yuʿaqqib ~ wa-yhî lə-nāḥāš wa-yyānās Mōše mippānāyw: Moses flees from his transformed staff in both. Exodus then has God order him to grasp the snake by the tail (šəlaḥ yādəkā wə-ʾĕḥōz bi-znāvô); the Quran has God reassure him: yā Mūsā lā takhaf innī lā yakhāfu ladayya l-mursalūna.)
passages.text: وَأَلْقِ عَصَاكَ فَلَمَّا رَءَاهَا تَهْتَزُّ كَأَنَّهَا جَآنٌّ وَلَّىٰ مُدْبِرًا وَلَمْ يُعَقِّبْ يَٰمُوسَىٰ لَا تَخَفْ إِنِّى لَا يَخَافُ لَدَىَّ ٱلْمُرْسَلُونَ

passages.note: Moses flees from his staff turned serpent, and God's response [divergence between the texts] (As at Q 27:10: wa-yyānās Mōše mip-pānāyw ~ wallā mudbiran wa-lam yuʿaqqib; Exodus' command to seize the snake's tail (wə-ʾĕḥōz bi-znāvô) becomes yā Mūsā aqbil wa-lā takhaf innaka mina l-āminīn, 'come forward and do not fear, you are safe'.)
passages.text: وَأَنْ أَلْقِ عَصَاكَ فَلَمَّا رَءَاهَا تَهْتَزُّ كَأَنَّهَا جَآنٌّ وَلَّىٰ مُدْبِرًا وَلَمْ يُعَقِّبْ يَٰمُوسَىٰٓ أَقْبِلْ وَلَا تَخَفْ إِنَّكَ مِنَ ٱلْءَامِنِينَ

passages.note: Moses' hand turned white as a sign [divergence between the texts] (wa-adkhil yadaka fī jaybika takhruj bayḍāʾa min ghayri sūʾin ~ hāvēʾ nāʾ yādəkā bə-ḥêqekā ... wə-hinnēh yādô məṣōraʿat ka-ššāleg: hand into the bosom (jayb / ḥêq) and out white. evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: The thrown staff quivers like a jānn (small snake) and Moses turns and flees without looking back (weight 6.7); Traveling with his family, the prophet sees a fire and goes to bring back a brand or find guidance there (weight 6.3); Moses flees from his staff turned serpent, and God's response [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.3); Moses' hand turned white as a sign [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.0); God appears in a bush that burns without being consumed (weight 6.0); Prophet's hand turns leprous, white as snow, and is restored as a sign (weight 5.6); A staff thrown down becomes a serpent and turns back into a staff (weight 5.4). Pair score 42.3.

Only in Ta Sin; Moses at the fire, the jann-staff and the nine signs: At the fire the voice proclaims 'Blessed is he who is in the fire and those around it'; God described as the one who dwells in the bush (seneh); How God names himself to Moses from the fire [divergence between the texts]; Moses was given nine clear signs; The number of signs or plagues in Egypt [divergence between the texts]; Why Moses approaches the fire [divergence between the texts]; Why Pharaoh and Egypt refuse despite the signs [divergence between the texts]; A poetic list of the Egyptian plagues differs in number and order from Exodus; God addresses the hero with 'Fear not' in a vision; Prophet's wonders are imitated by the king's magicians in a contest; The king's heart is hardened (by himself or by God) so he refuses to release the people; A surah opens with isolated letters (huruf muqatta'at) of unexplained meaning, e.g. alif-lam-mim.

Only in The fire on the side of the Mount; the call from the tree; Aaron as helper: Moses says his brother Aaron is more eloquent of tongue and asks for him as a helper to confirm him; Moses is called from the tree on the right bank of the valley, in the blessed spot; God calls Moses from the fire, from a bush or a tree [divergence between the texts]; Prophet lodges in 'the cave' on Horeb, the mountain of God; Where and how Moses comes to the place of his call [divergence between the texts]; Moses' fear of being killed, on returning, for the Egyptian's death [divergence between the texts]; A shepherd tending flocks comes to the mountain of God and is called; Aaron's role beside Moses and how he is appointed [divergence between the texts]; An eloquent brother is appointed to speak for the hero, who is 'as God' to him; Prophet protests he is heavy of mouth and tongue or 'uncircumcised of lips'.

Shared motifs, rarest first: Mary asks how she will have a child when no man has touched her (weight 6.7); Jesus will speak to people in the cradle and in maturity (weight 6.7); The newborn speaks (weight 5.8); God creates by saying to a thing 'Be' and it is (kun fa-yakun) (weight 5.6). Pair score 24.7.

Only in The annunciation and the mission of Jesus: Deity breathes the breath of life into the first human's nostrils; Child makes birds from clay that come alive; Jesus asks 'Who are my helpers to God?' and the disciples (hawariyyun) answer 'We are God's helpers'; They plotted, and God plotted; God is the best of plotters; First human shaped from dust, clay or soil; Jesus heals the born-blind and the leper and raises the dead by God's leave; The likeness of Jesus with God is as Adam, created from dust by 'Be'; Jesus comes confirming the Torah and making lawful some of what was forbidden; God says to Jesus 'I will take you (mutawaffika) and raise you to myself and purify you'; Jesus tells people what they eat and store in their houses; Jesus announced as a word (kalima) from God, named the Messiah, Jesus son of Mary; Challenge to mutual imprecation (mubahala): gather sons, women and selves and invoke God's curse on the liars; Prophet is taken up alive to heaven in a whirlwind; God sent down the Torah (al-Tawrat) and the Gospel (al-Injil) before as guidance.

Only in Mary, the spirit in human form, the birth under the palm, the speaking infant (Surah 19:16-40): A divine messenger announces a son to a virgin untouched by any man; Mother gives birth alone in a remote place; The Day of Regret (yawm al-hasra) when the matter is decided; God's spirit appears to a woman in the form of a well-proportioned man; The prophet child is dutiful to his parent(s), not an arrogant tyrant; God answers doubt: 'It is easy for me; I created you before when you were nothing'; God gives life and death and is the inheritor of the earth and all on it; Denial that God has taken a son (walad); God does not beget and was not begotten; Jesus says 'worship God, my Lord and your Lord'; The infant Jesus declares himself God's servant, given the Book and made a prophet; 'That is Jesus son of Mary, the word of truth about which they dispute'; Labor pains drive the mother to the trunk of a palm tree; Mary is addressed as 'sister of Aaron'; Mary withdraws from her family to an eastern place behind a screen; A spring or stream appears for the mother; The mother returns with the child and her people accuse her of an enormity; In labor the mother wishes she had died before this and been utterly forgotten; A palm tree provides food to the mother; 'Peace on him the day he was born, the day he dies and the day he is raised alive'; The factions differ among themselves about Jesus; God breathed of his spirit into the woman who guarded her chastity; A voice from beneath her consoles the mother: 'do not grieve'; Mother keeps a vow of silence; Refrain 'And mention in the Book ...' introducing a series of prophet portraits; The woman seeks refuge in God from the mysterious visitor.

Only in Lot's old woman; Jonah and the fish: The fish casts the prophet onto a barren shore while he is sick; Jonah ran away (abaqa, as a runaway slave) to the laden ship; Had Jonah not been among those who glorify God he would have stayed in the fish's belly until the Day of Resurrection; Jonah is sent to a hundred thousand or more; they believe and are granted enjoyment for a while; The hearers pass by the ruins of Lot's people morning and night; Nineveh has more than 120,000 people who do not know their right hand from their left; The fate of Lot's wife [divergence between the texts]; The city to which Jonah is sent believes and is spared [divergence between the texts]; Jonah flees by ship [divergence between the texts]; Sailors cast lots to learn on whose account the disaster has come, and the lot falls on the prophet; Sailors cast lots to learn on whose account the disaster has come, and the lot falls on the prophet [divergence between the texts]; God makes a plant (qiqayon, gourd or castor) grow overnight to shade the prophet; and 4 more.

Only in Do you have a book or oaths binding God?; the shin laid bare; the companion of the fish; the evil eye: Do not be like the companion of the fish (sahib al-hut, Jonah) who cried out while choking with grief; God leads the deniers on step by step (istidraj) from where they do not know, and grants them respite; his plan is firm; Had not grace from his Lord reached him he would have been cast onto the barren shore blameworthy; but his Lord chose him and made him righteous; On the day when the shin is laid bare (yukshafu 'an saq) and they are called to prostrate but cannot; The unbelievers almost make the prophet slip with their (evil) eyes when they hear the reminder; Do they possess the Unseen (al-ghayb) so they write it down?; At God's command the fish vomits the prophet onto dry land [divergence between the texts]; 'Are your unbelievers better than those, or have you an immunity (bara'a) in the scriptures (zubur)?'; The prophet is bitterly angry that God has spared the sinners; The prophet is bitterly angry that God has spared the sinners [divergence between the texts]; The word of God comes to the prophet a second time with the same commission; No messenger came to earlier peoples without being called 'a sorcerer or a madman', as if they had bequeathed the charge to one another; and 3 more.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: The blessed recline on couches set in rows (or face to face) (weight 6.7); Youths (ghilman) like hidden pearls go round serving them (weight 6.7); Abundant fruit in paradise from which the blessed eat (weight 6.0); The blessed are paired with wide-eyed maidens (hur 'in) (weight 6.0); The effects of wine and of the cup: mockery, madness, or none [contrast between the texts] (weight 5.8). Pair score 31.1.

Only in The Garden: offspring joined with parents, the cup without idle talk, youths like pearls; the run of 'or...?' challenges: The blessed question each other and recall that they used to be fearful among their families, and God saved them from the scorching wind (samum); In paradise they pass a cup to one another in which is no idle talk (laghw) or sin; If they saw a fragment of the sky falling they would say 'heaped-up clouds'; Glorify God when you rise, in the night, and at the retreat of the stars (dawn); Do they have a ladder (sullam) by which they eavesdrop on heaven? Let their listener bring clear proof; 'Be patient for your Lord's judgment, for you are under our eyes'; Were they created from nothing, or are they the creators? Did they create the heavens and earth?; Do they possess the Unseen (al-ghayb) so they write it down?; Dream of a ladder or stairway reaching heaven with angels ascending and descending; 'Eat and drink with relish for what you used to do'; A ladder (sullam / sullām) reaching from earth to heaven [divergence between the texts]; Believers' offspring who followed them in faith are joined with them in paradise, without loss of reward; each is pledged for what he earned; and 9 more.

Only in Al-Waqi'a: the Event that abases and exalts; the three classes; the Foremost, the Companions of the Right and their Garden: In paradise they have the flesh of fowl as they desire; Immortal youths (wildan mukhalladun) circulate with goblets, ewers and a cup from a flowing spring; God created (the companions) anew and made them virgins, loving, of equal age; The Foremost are a multitude of the earlier generations and a few of the later; In paradise they hear no idle talk or sin, only the saying 'Peace, peace'; The Companions of the Right are among thornless lote trees (sidr makhdud) and layered talh (acacia/banana) with extended shade and poured water; Humanity sorted into three classes: Companions of the Right, Companions of the Left, and the Foremost (al-sabiqun) brought near; Bird-meat as desired food: punished or granted [contrast between the texts]; The earth is shaken violently and the mountains crumbled into scattered dust (haba'); Whether any fruit in the Garden is forbidden [contrast between the texts]; Abundant fruit in paradise, neither cut off (seasonless) nor forbidden; Into how many groups humankind is sorted at the end [divergence between the texts]; and 7 more.

leads.title: The prostration to Adam, Iblis' refusal and the fall ↔ Man from black mud, jinn from scorching fire, and Iblis's refusal (Surah 15:26-50)
leads.summary: These two units share 5 motifs: the expelled devil vows to lie in wait on the straight path and mislead humanity, god commands the angels to prostrate before the first man, and they do, the devil asks for and is granted respite until the day the dead are raised, the devil (iblis) alone refuses to bow to the first man….

passages.text: قَالَ فَبِمَآ أَغْوَيْتَنِى لَأَقْعُدَنَّ لَهُمْ صِرَٰطَكَ ٱلْمُسْتَقِيمَ

passages.note: The expelled devil vows to lie in wait on the straight path and mislead humanity ('because you led me astray' (bi-mā aghwaytanī) I will adorn things on earth for them)
passages.text: قَالَ رَبِّ بِمَآ أَغْوَيْتَنِى لَأُزَيِّنَنَّ لَهُمْ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ وَلَأُغْوِيَنَّهُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: The expelled devil vows to lie in wait on the straight path and mislead humanity (weight 6.3); God commands the angels to prostrate before the first man, and they do (weight 5.8); The devil asks for and is granted respite until the day the dead are raised (weight 5.8); The devil (Iblis) alone refuses to bow to the first man (weight 5.8); First human shaped from dust, clay or soil (weight 4.6). Pair score 28.2.

Only in The prostration to Adam, Iblis' refusal and the fall: Man and wife are addressed, tempted and eat together; the woman is not singled out; The first humans are sent down to earth to live and enjoy provision for a time; The devil will come at humans from before, behind, right and left; The first couple confess 'we have wronged ourselves' and ask God's forgiveness; On the earth humans live, in it they die, and from it they will be brought out; The tempter claims the tree is forbidden only lest the couple become angels or immortals; The tempter swears an oath to the first couple that he is their sincere adviser; God vows to fill hell with the devil and all who follow him; Satan whispers (waswasa) to tempt humans; God casts the proud being out from the mountain of God and destroys him from among the stones of fire, hurling him to earth before kings; How the first couple answer God after eating: shifting the blame or confessing [divergence between the texts]; God gives the adversary (Satan) leave to act against humans; and 17 more.

Only in Man from black mud, jinn from scorching fire, and Iblis's refusal (Surah 15:26-50): The pious are in gardens and springs, entering in peace and security; Hell has seven gates, each with an assigned portion of the damned; The jinn were created before humans from smokeless or scorching fire; In paradise no fatigue touches them and they are never expelled from it; God removes all rancor from the hearts of those in paradise; Deity breathes the breath of life into the first human's nostrils [divergence between the texts]; Satan has no authority over God's sincere servants, only over those who follow him; God expels Iblis as accursed (rajim) with a curse until the Day of Judgment; Deity breathes the breath of life into the first human's nostrils.

leads.title: The prostration to Adam, Iblis' refusal and the fall ↔ Adam's forgetting, Iblis, the tree of immortality and the descent
leads.summary: These two units share 9 motifs: satan whispers (waswasa) to tempt humans, eating opens their eyes and they know they are naked, enmity between the serpent's seed and the woman's seed: head bruised, heel struck [divergence between the texts], fig leaves sewn into coverings….

passages.note: Satan whispers (waswasa) to tempt humans
passages.text: فَوَسْوَسَ لَهُمَا ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ لِيُبْدِىَ لَهُمَا مَا وُۥرِىَ عَنْهُمَا مِن سَوْءَٰتِهِمَا وَقَالَ مَا نَهَىٰكُمَا رَبُّكُمَا عَنْ هَٰذِهِ ٱلشَّجَرَةِ إِلَّآ أَن تَكُونَا مَلَكَيْنِ أَوْ تَكُونَا مِنَ ٱلْخَٰلِدِينَ

passages.note: Satan whispers (waswasa) to tempt humans
passages.text: فَوَسْوَسَ إِلَيْهِ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ قَالَ يَٰٓـَٔادَمُ هَلْ أَدُلُّكَ عَلَىٰ شَجَرَةِ ٱلْخُلْدِ وَمُلْكٍ لَّا يَبْلَىٰ

passages.note: Eating opens their eyes and they know they are naked (saw'at)
passages.text: فَوَسْوَسَ لَهُمَا ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ لِيُبْدِىَ لَهُمَا مَا وُۥرِىَ عَنْهُمَا مِن سَوْءَٰتِهِمَا وَقَالَ مَا نَهَىٰكُمَا رَبُّكُمَا عَنْ هَٰذِهِ ٱلشَّجَرَةِ إِلَّآ أَن تَكُونَا مَلَكَيْنِ أَوْ تَكُونَا مِنَ ٱلْخَٰلِدِينَ

passages.note: Eating opens their eyes and they know they are naked (saw'at)
passages.text: فَدَلَّىٰهُمَا بِغُرُورٍ فَلَمَّا ذَاقَا ٱلشَّجَرَةَ بَدَتْ لَهُمَا سَوْءَٰتُهُمَا وَطَفِقَا يَخْصِفَانِ عَلَيْهِمَا مِن وَرَقِ ٱلْجَنَّةِ وَنَادَىٰهُمَا رَبُّهُمَآ أَلَمْ أَنْهَكُمَا عَن تِلْكُمَا ٱلشَّجَرَةِ وَأَقُل لَّكُمَآ إِنَّ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنَ لَكُمَا عَدُوٌّ مُّبِينٌ

passages.note: Eating opens their eyes and they know they are naked
passages.text: فَأَكَلَا مِنْهَا فَبَدَتْ لَهُمَا سَوْءَٰتُهُمَا وَطَفِقَا يَخْصِفَانِ عَلَيْهِمَا مِن وَرَقِ ٱلْجَنَّةِ وَعَصَىٰٓ ءَادَمُ رَبَّهُۥ فَغَوَىٰ

passages.note: Enmity between the serpent's seed and the woman's seed: head bruised, heel struck [divergence between the texts] (Gen: wə-ʾêvāh ʾāšît bênkhā û-vên hā-ʾiššāh û-vên zarʿăkhā û-vên zarʿāh, enmity set by God between serpent and woman and their seed. Only in The prostration to Adam, Iblis' refusal and the fall: Man and wife are addressed, tempted and eat together; the woman is not singled out; The first humans are sent down to earth to live and enjoy provision for a time; The devil will come at humans from before, behind, right and left; The first couple confess 'we have wronged ourselves' and ask God's forgiveness; On the earth humans live, in it they die, and from it they will be brought out; The tempter claims the tree is forbidden only lest the couple become angels or immortals; The tempter swears an oath to the first couple that he is their sincere adviser; God vows to fill hell with the devil and all who follow him; God casts the proud being out from the mountain of God and destroys him from among the stones of fire, hurling him to earth before kings; How the first couple answer God after eating: shifting the blame or confessing [divergence between the texts]; God gives the adversary (Satan) leave to act against humans; Sinner hides from God, who calls 'Where are you?' [divergence between the texts]; and 13 more.

Only in Adam's forgetting, Iblis, the tree of immortality and the descent: God made a covenant with Adam, but he forgot and lacked resolve; In the garden Adam will not hunger, be naked, thirst or suffer the sun's heat; Whoever turned from God's reminder is raised blind on judgment day: as he forgot the signs, so he is forgotten; The tempter offers 'the tree of immortality and a kingdom that never decays'; God made a covenant with Adam, but he forgot and lacked resolve [divergence between the texts]; Adam receives words from his Lord and God turns to him in forgiveness; Adam receives words from his Lord and God turns to him in forgiveness [divergence between the texts]; God commands the angels to prostrate to Adam; all do except Iblis, who refuses; Eating opens their eyes and they know they are naked [divergence between the texts]; In the garden Adam will not hunger, be naked, thirst or suffer the sun's heat [divergence between the texts]; The tempter offers 'the tree of immortality and a kingdom that never decays' [divergence between the texts]; A tree whose fruit gives eternal life.

leads.title: Six days, the Throne, winds and rain as proof of resurrection ↔ The moving shadow, the night garment, the two seas and the constellations
leads.summary: These two units share 5 motifs: god sends the winds as heralds before his mercy and sends down pure water from the sky, after creating the heavens and earth god established himself on the throne (istawa 'ala l-'arsh), creation is completed in six days, sun and moon are set to rule day and night and mark signs and seasons….

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: The defeated magicians fall prostrate and declare faith in the Lord of Moses and Aaron (weight 6.3); Prophet delivers God's demand 'Let my people go that they may serve me' [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.3); The prophet's staff-serpent swallows the magicians' staff-serpents [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.3); The prophet's staff-serpent swallows the magicians' staff-serpents (weight 6.0); The king's heart is hardened (by himself or by God) so he refuses to release the people [divergence between the texts] (weight 5.6); Prophet delivers God's demand 'Let my people go that they may serve me' (weight 5.4); Prophet's wonders are imitated by the king's magicians in a contest (weight 5.1); The king's heart is hardened (by himself or by God) so he refuses to release the people (weight 4.6). Pair score 45.6.

Only in Moses before Pharaoh, the magicians and the plagues: Pharaoh's people are struck with years of drought and lack of fruits before the plagues; Enemies attribute their misfortune to the prophet as a bad omen (tatayyur); their omen is with God; The magicians' spell bewitches the people's eyes and terrifies them; The magicians offer the prophet to throw first; he tells them to throw; Pharaoh is said to have his own gods, whom Moses would make him abandon; One of the Egyptian plagues is a flood (tufan); The tyrant threatens to cut off hands and feet on opposite sides and crucify the converts; The king's courtiers advise him how to deal with the prophet and his people [contrast between the texts]; Rulers fear that a people will leave the land, or drive them out of it [divergence between the texts]; The court magicians ask the king for a reward if they win and are promised closeness; Magicians fail to imitate a wonder and confess 'This is the finger of God'; Magicians fail to imitate a wonder and confess 'This is the finger of God' [divergence between the texts]; and 17 more.

Only in Moses and Aaron before Pharaoh; the contest with the magicians: The contest with the magicians is set for a festival day (yawm al-zīna) at forenoon with the people assembled; From the earth humans were created, into it they return, and from it they are brought forth again; Formula: 'Peace be on whoever follows the guidance'; Pharaoh asks about the fate of former generations; the answer: their knowledge is with God in a book; The prophets are told to speak to the tyrant with gentle words, that he may take heed or fear; The defeated magicians fall prostrate and declare faith in the Lord of Moses and Aaron [divergence between the texts]; The magicians' ropes and staffs appear by sorcery to be moving like snakes; Condemned believers tell the tyrant 'decree what you will; you can only decree for this worldly life'; Pharaoh threatens the converted magicians with cutting off hands and feet on opposite sides and crucifixion (on palm trunks); King defies the prophet: 'Who is YHWH that I should obey him?' [divergence between the texts]; God made the earth a cradle (mahd) or bed and laid out paths in it; King defies the prophet: 'Who is YHWH that I should obey him?'; and 3 more.

leads.title: Moses before Pharaoh, the magicians and the plagues ↔ Moses and Pharaoh disputing; the magicians; the sea split like mountains
leads.summary: These two units share 8 motifs: the court magicians ask the king for a reward if they win and are promised closeness, the defeated magicians fall prostrate and declare faith in the lord of moses and aaron, the prophet's staff-serpent swallows the magicians' staff-serpents, prophet's hand turns leprous, white as snow, and is restored as a sign….

passages.note: A poetic list of the Egyptian plagues differs in number and order from Exodus (Two short plague lists that differ from Exodus. Ps: wa-yyahăfōkh lə-dām yəʾōrêhem ... ʿārōv ... û-ṣəfardēaʿ ... la-ḥāsîl yəvûlām wî-gîʿām lā-ʾarbeh; yahărōg bab-bārād gafnām. Q: al-ṭūfāna wa-l-jarāda wa-l-qummala wa-l-ḍafādiʿa wa-l-dama. leads.title: Noah warns his people ↔ Noah, the boiling oven, the lost son and al-Judi
leads.summary: These two units share 5 motifs: the chiefs (al-mala') of the prophet's people accuse him of error or folly and reject him, hero warns or preaches to his people before the flood, prophet's refrain to his people: 'worship god; you have no god other than him', destruction follows the people's rejection of a messenger….

passages.note: The chiefs (al-mala') of the prophet's people accuse him of error or folly and reject him ('we see you in manifest error')
passages.text: قَالَ ٱلْمَلَأُ مِن قَوْمِهِۦٓ إِنَّا لَنَرَىٰكَ فِى ضَلَٰلٍ مُّبِينٍ

passages.note: The chiefs (al-mala') of the prophet's people accuse him of error or folly and reject him ('only a human like us')
passages.text: فَقَالَ ٱلْمَلَأُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ مِن قَوْمِهِۦ مَا نَرَىٰكَ إِلَّا بَشَرًا مِّثْلَنَا وَمَا نَرَىٰكَ ٱتَّبَعَكَ إِلَّا ٱلَّذِينَ هُمْ أَرَاذِلُنَا بَادِىَ ٱلرَّأْىِ وَمَا نَرَىٰ لَكُمْ عَلَيْنَا مِن فَضْلٍۭ بَلْ نَظُنُّكُمْ كَٰذِبِينَ

leads.summary: أَمْن (ʾamn, “security”) occurs in 5 verses; 3 of them (60%) are in the Abraham narrative, which is 3% of the Quran, across 2 surahs. The more common same-gloss word مُؤْمِن (muʾmin, 193 verses) has only 3% of its verses there.

passages.text: وَإِذْ جَعَلْنَا ٱلْبَيْتَ مَثَابَةً لِّلنَّاسِ وَأَمْنًا وَٱتَّخِذُوا۟ مِن مَّقَامِ إِبْرَٰهِۦمَ مُصَلًّى وَعَهِدْنَآ إِلَىٰٓ إِبْرَٰهِۦمَ وَإِسْمَٰعِيلَ أَن طَهِّرَا بَيْتِىَ لِلطَّآئِفِينَ وَٱلْعَٰكِفِينَ وَٱلرُّكَّعِ ٱلسُّجُودِ

وَإِذَا جَآءَهُمْ أَمْرٌ مِّنَ ٱلْأَمْنِ أَوِ ٱلْخَوْفِ أَذَاعُوا۟ بِهِۦ وَلَوْ رَدُّوهُ إِلَى ٱلرَّسُولِ وَإِلَىٰٓ أُو۟لِى ٱلْأَمْرِ مِنْهُمْ لَعَلِمَهُ ٱلَّذِينَ يَسْتَنۢبِطُونَهُۥ مِنْهُمْ وَلَوْلَا فَضْلُ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ وَرَحْمَتُهُۥ لَٱتَّبَعْتُمُ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنَ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا
وَكَيْفَ أَخَافُ مَآ أَشْرَكْتُمْ وَلَا تَخَافُونَ أَنَّكُمْ أَشْرَكْتُم بِٱللَّهِ مَا لَمْ يُنَزِّلْ بِهِۦ عَلَيْكُمْ سُلْطَٰنًا فَأَىُّ ٱلْفَرِيقَيْنِ أَحَقُّ بِٱلْأَمْنِ إِن كُنتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ
ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَلَمْ يَلْبِسُوٓا۟ إِيمَٰنَهُم بِظُلْمٍ أُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ لَهُمُ ٱلْأَمْنُ وَهُم مُّهْتَدُونَ

وَعَدَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ مِنكُمْ وَعَمِلُوا۟ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ لَيَسْتَخْلِفَنَّهُمْ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ كَمَا ٱسْتَخْلَفَ ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِهِمْ وَلَيُمَكِّنَنَّ لَهُمْ دِينَهُمُ ٱلَّذِى ٱرْتَضَىٰ لَهُمْ وَلَيُبَدِّلَنَّهُم مِّنۢ بَعْدِ خَوْفِهِمْ أَمْنًا يَعْبُدُونَنِى لَا يُشْرِكُونَ بِى شَيْـًٔا وَمَن كَفَرَ بَعْدَ ذَٰلِكَ فَأُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلْفَٰسِقُونَ

passages.text: فَأَزَلَّهُمَا ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ عَنْهَا فَأَخْرَجَهُمَا مِمَّا كَانَا فِيهِ وَقُلْنَا ٱهْبِطُوا۟ بَعْضُكُمْ لِبَعْضٍ عَدُوٌّ وَلَكُمْ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ مُسْتَقَرٌّ وَمَتَٰعٌ إِلَىٰ حِينٍ
قُلْنَا ٱهْبِطُوا۟ مِنْهَا جَمِيعًا فَإِمَّا يَأْتِيَنَّكُم مِّنِّى هُدًى فَمَن تَبِعَ هُدَاىَ فَلَا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ

وَإِذْ قُلْتُمْ يَٰمُوسَىٰ لَن نَّصْبِرَ عَلَىٰ طَعَامٍ وَٰحِدٍ فَٱدْعُ لَنَا رَبَّكَ يُخْرِجْ لَنَا مِمَّا تُنۢبِتُ ٱلْأَرْضُ مِنۢ بَقْلِهَا وَقِثَّآئِهَا وَفُومِهَا وَعَدَسِهَا وَبَصَلِهَا قَالَ أَتَسْتَبْدِلُونَ ٱلَّذِى هُوَ أَدْنَىٰ بِٱلَّذِى هُوَ خَيْرٌ ٱهْبِطُوا۟ مِصْرًا فَإِنَّ لَكُم مَّا سَأَلْتُمْ وَضُرِبَتْ عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلذِّلَّةُ وَٱلْمَسْكَنَةُ وَبَآءُو بِغَضَبٍ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ ذَٰلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمْ كَانُوا۟ يَكْفُرُونَ بِـَٔايَٰتِ ٱللَّهِ وَيَقْتُلُونَ ٱلنَّبِيِّۦنَ بِغَيْرِ ٱلْحَقِّ ذَٰلِكَ بِمَا عَصَوا۟ وَّكَانُوا۟ يَعْتَدُونَ

ثُمَّ قَسَتْ قُلُوبُكُم مِّنۢ بَعْدِ ذَٰلِكَ فَهِىَ كَٱلْحِجَارَةِ أَوْ أَشَدُّ قَسْوَةً وَإِنَّ مِنَ ٱلْحِجَارَةِ لَمَا يَتَفَجَّرُ مِنْهُ ٱلْأَنْهَٰرُ وَإِنَّ مِنْهَا لَمَا يَشَّقَّقُ فَيَخْرُجُ مِنْهُ ٱلْمَآءُ وَإِنَّ مِنْهَا لَمَا يَهْبِطُ مِنْ خَشْيَةِ ٱللَّهِ وَمَا ٱللَّهُ بِغَٰفِلٍ عَمَّا تَعْمَلُونَ
قَالَ فَٱهْبِطْ مِنْهَا فَمَا يَكُونُ لَكَ أَن تَتَكَبَّرَ فِيهَا فَٱخْرُجْ إِنَّكَ مِنَ ٱلصَّٰغِرِينَ
قَالَ ٱهْبِطُوا۟ بَعْضُكُمْ لِبَعْضٍ عَدُوٌّ وَلَكُمْ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ مُسْتَقَرٌّ وَمَتَٰعٌ إِلَىٰ حِينٍ
قِيلَ يَٰنُوحُ ٱهْبِطْ بِسَلَٰمٍ مِّنَّا وَبَرَكَٰتٍ عَلَيْكَ وَعَلَىٰٓ أُمَمٍ مِّمَّن مَّعَكَ وَأُمَمٌ سَنُمَتِّعُهُمْ ثُمَّ يَمَسُّهُم مِّنَّا عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ
قَالَ ٱهْبِطَا مِنْهَا جَمِيعًۢا بَعْضُكُمْ لِبَعْضٍ عَدُوٌّ فَإِمَّا يَأْتِيَنَّكُم مِّنِّى هُدًى فَمَنِ ٱتَّبَعَ هُدَاىَ فَلَا يَضِلُّ وَلَا يَشْقَىٰ

passages.text: وَإِذْ قَالَ إِبْرَٰهِيمُ لِأَبِيهِ ءَازَرَ أَتَتَّخِذُ أَصْنَامًا ءَالِهَةً إِنِّىٓ أَرَىٰكَ وَقَوْمَكَ فِى ضَلَٰلٍ مُّبِينٍ

وَجَٰوَزْنَا بِبَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ ٱلْبَحْرَ فَأَتَوْا۟ عَلَىٰ قَوْمٍ يَعْكُفُونَ عَلَىٰٓ أَصْنَامٍ لَّهُمْ قَالُوا۟ يَٰمُوسَى ٱجْعَل لَّنَآ إِلَٰهًا كَمَا لَهُمْ ءَالِهَةٌ قَالَ إِنَّكُمْ قَوْمٌ تَجْهَلُونَ
وَإِذْ قَالَ إِبْرَٰهِيمُ رَبِّ ٱجْعَلْ هَٰذَا ٱلْبَلَدَ ءَامِنًا وَٱجْنُبْنِى وَبَنِىَّ أَن نَّعْبُدَ ٱلْأَصْنَامَ
وَتَٱللَّهِ لَأَكِيدَنَّ أَصْنَٰمَكُم بَعْدَ أَن تُوَلُّوا۟ مُدْبِرِينَ
قَالُوا۟ نَعْبُدُ أَصْنَامًا فَنَظَلُّ لَهَا عَٰكِفِينَ

passages.text: وَإِذْ قَالَ مُوسَىٰ لِقَوْمِهِۦٓ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَأْمُرُكُمْ أَن تَذْبَحُوا۟ بَقَرَةً قَالُوٓا۟ أَتَتَّخِذُنَا هُزُوًا قَالَ أَعُوذُ بِٱللَّهِ أَنْ أَكُونَ مِنَ ٱلْجَٰهِلِينَ
قَالُوا۟ ٱدْعُ لَنَا رَبَّكَ يُبَيِّن لَّنَا مَا هِىَ قَالَ إِنَّهُۥ يَقُولُ إِنَّهَا بَقَرَةٌ لَّا فَارِضٌ وَلَا بِكْرٌ عَوَانٌۢ بَيْنَ ذَٰلِكَ فَٱفْعَلُوا۟ مَا تُؤْمَرُونَ
قَالُوا۟ ٱدْعُ لَنَا رَبَّكَ يُبَيِّن لَّنَا مَا لَوْنُهَا قَالَ إِنَّهُۥ يَقُولُ إِنَّهَا بَقَرَةٌ صَفْرَآءُ فَاقِعٌ لَّوْنُهَا تَسُرُّ ٱلنَّٰظِرِينَ

قَالَ إِنَّهُۥ يَقُولُ إِنَّهَا بَقَرَةٌ لَّا ذَلُولٌ تُثِيرُ ٱلْأَرْضَ وَلَا تَسْقِى ٱلْحَرْثَ مُسَلَّمَةٌ لَّا شِيَةَ فِيهَا قَالُوا۟ ٱلْـَٰٔنَ جِئْتَ بِٱلْحَقِّ فَذَبَحُوهَا وَمَا كَادُوا۟ يَفْعَلُونَ

وَقَالَ ٱلْمَلِكُ إِنِّىٓ أَرَىٰ سَبْعَ بَقَرَٰتٍ سِمَانٍ يَأْكُلُهُنَّ سَبْعٌ عِجَافٌ وَسَبْعَ سُنۢبُلَٰتٍ خُضْرٍ وَأُخَرَ يَابِسَٰتٍ يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلْمَلَأُ أَفْتُونِى فِى رُءْيَٰىَ إِن كُنتُمْ لِلرُّءْيَا تَعْبُرُونَ

يُوسُفُ أَيُّهَا ٱلصِّدِّيقُ أَفْتِنَا فِى سَبْعِ بَقَرَٰتٍ سِمَانٍ يَأْكُلُهُنَّ سَبْعٌ عِجَافٌ وَسَبْعِ سُنۢبُلَٰتٍ خُضْرٍ وَأُخَرَ يَابِسَٰتٍ لَّعَلِّىٓ أَرْجِعُ إِلَى ٱلنَّاسِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَعْلَمُونَ

وَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْكُمْ فِيمَا عَرَّضْتُم بِهِۦ مِنْ خِطْبَةِ ٱلنِّسَآءِ أَوْ أَكْنَنتُمْ فِىٓ أَنفُسِكُمْ عَلِمَ ٱللَّهُ أَنَّكُمْ سَتَذْكُرُونَهُنَّ وَلَٰكِن لَّا تُوَاعِدُوهُنَّ سِرًّا إِلَّآ أَن تَقُولُوا۟ قَوْلًا مَّعْرُوفًا وَلَا تَعْزِمُوا۟ عُقْدَةَ ٱلنِّكَاحِ حَتَّىٰ يَبْلُغَ ٱلْكِتَٰبُ أَجَلَهُۥ وَٱعْلَمُوٓا۟ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَعْلَمُ مَا فِىٓ أَنفُسِكُمْ فَٱحْذَرُوهُ وَٱعْلَمُوٓا۟ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَفُورٌ حَلِيمٌ

وَوَٰعَدْنَا مُوسَىٰ ثَلَٰثِينَ لَيْلَةً وَأَتْمَمْنَٰهَا بِعَشْرٍ فَتَمَّ مِيقَٰتُ رَبِّهِۦٓ أَرْبَعِينَ لَيْلَةً وَقَالَ مُوسَىٰ لِأَخِيهِ هَٰرُونَ ٱخْلُفْنِى فِى قَوْمِى وَأَصْلِحْ وَلَا تَتَّبِعْ سَبِيلَ ٱلْمُفْسِدِينَ
يَٰبَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ قَدْ أَنجَيْنَٰكُم مِّنْ عَدُوِّكُمْ وَوَٰعَدْنَٰكُمْ جَانِبَ ٱلطُّورِ ٱلْأَيْمَنَ وَنَزَّلْنَا عَلَيْكُمُ ٱلْمَنَّ وَٱلسَّلْوَىٰ

leads.title: yastaḥāi: a live word concentrated in Moses
leads.summary: يَسْتَحْىِۦ (yastaḥāi, “live”) occurs in 8 verses; 5 of them (62%) are in the Moses narrative, which is 7% of the Quran, across 4 surahs. The more common same-gloss word سَكَنَ (sakana, 15 verses) has only 13% of its verses there.

lexical.gloss: to live, whether literally or figuratively (H2421, possible cognate)

passages.text: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يَسْتَحْىِۦٓ أَن يَضْرِبَ مَثَلًا مَّا بَعُوضَةً فَمَا فَوْقَهَا فَأَمَّا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ فَيَعْلَمُونَ أَنَّهُ ٱلْحَقُّ مِن رَّبِّهِمْ وَأَمَّا ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ فَيَقُولُونَ مَاذَآ أَرَادَ ٱللَّهُ بِهَٰذَا مَثَلًا يُضِلُّ بِهِۦ كَثِيرًا وَيَهْدِى بِهِۦ كَثِيرًا وَمَا يُضِلُّ بِهِۦٓ إِلَّا ٱلْفَٰسِقِينَ
وَإِذْ نَجَّيْنَٰكُم مِّنْ ءَالِ فِرْعَوْنَ يَسُومُونَكُمْ سُوٓءَ ٱلْعَذَابِ يُذَبِّحُونَ أَبْنَآءَكُمْ وَيَسْتَحْيُونَ نِسَآءَكُمْ وَفِى ذَٰلِكُم بَلَآءٌ مِّن رَّبِّكُمْ عَظِيمٌ

وَقَالَ ٱلْمَلَأُ مِن قَوْمِ فِرْعَوْنَ أَتَذَرُ مُوسَىٰ وَقَوْمَهُۥ لِيُفْسِدُوا۟ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ وَيَذَرَكَ وَءَالِهَتَكَ قَالَ سَنُقَتِّلُ أَبْنَآءَهُمْ وَنَسْتَحْىِۦ نِسَآءَهُمْ وَإِنَّا فَوْقَهُمْ قَٰهِرُونَ
وَإِذْ أَنجَيْنَٰكُم مِّنْ ءَالِ فِرْعَوْنَ يَسُومُونَكُمْ سُوٓءَ ٱلْعَذَابِ يُقَتِّلُونَ أَبْنَآءَكُمْ وَيَسْتَحْيُونَ نِسَآءَكُمْ وَفِى ذَٰلِكُم بَلَآءٌ مِّن رَّبِّكُمْ عَظِيمٌ

وَإِذْ قَالَ مُوسَىٰ لِقَوْمِهِ ٱذْكُرُوا۟ نِعْمَةَ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ إِذْ أَنجَىٰكُم مِّنْ ءَالِ فِرْعَوْنَ يَسُومُونَكُمْ سُوٓءَ ٱلْعَذَابِ وَيُذَبِّحُونَ أَبْنَآءَكُمْ وَيَسْتَحْيُونَ نِسَآءَكُمْ وَفِى ذَٰلِكُم بَلَآءٌ مِّن رَّبِّكُمْ عَظِيمٌ
إِنَّ فِرْعَوْنَ عَلَا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ وَجَعَلَ أَهْلَهَا شِيَعًا يَسْتَضْعِفُ طَآئِفَةً مِّنْهُمْ يُذَبِّحُ أَبْنَآءَهُمْ وَيَسْتَحْىِۦ نِسَآءَهُمْ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ مِنَ ٱلْمُفْسِدِينَ

يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ لَا تَدْخُلُوا۟ بُيُوتَ ٱلنَّبِىِّ إِلَّآ أَن يُؤْذَنَ لَكُمْ إِلَىٰ طَعَامٍ غَيْرَ نَٰظِرِينَ إِنَىٰهُ وَلَٰكِنْ إِذَا دُعِيتُمْ فَٱدْخُلُوا۟ فَإِذَا طَعِمْتُمْ فَٱنتَشِرُوا۟ وَلَا مُسْتَـْٔنِسِينَ لِحَدِيثٍ إِنَّ ذَٰلِكُمْ كَانَ يُؤْذِى ٱلنَّبِىَّ فَيَسْتَحْىِۦ مِنكُمْ وَٱللَّهُ لَا يَسْتَحْىِۦ مِنَ ٱلْحَقِّ وَإِذَا سَأَلْتُمُوهُنَّ مَتَٰعًا فَسْـَٔلُوهُنَّ مِن وَرَآءِ حِجَابٍ ذَٰلِكُمْ أَطْهَرُ لِقُلُوبِكُمْ وَقُلُوبِهِنَّ وَمَا كَانَ لَكُمْ أَن تُؤْذُوا۟ رَسُولَ ٱللَّهِ وَلَآ أَن تَنكِحُوٓا۟ أَزْوَٰجَهُۥ مِنۢ بَعْدِهِۦٓ أَبَدًا إِنَّ ذَٰلِكُمْ كَانَ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ عَظِيمًا
فَلَمَّا جَآءَهُم بِٱلْحَقِّ مِنْ عِندِنَا قَالُوا۟ ٱقْتُلُوٓا۟ أَبْنَآءَ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ مَعَهُۥ وَٱسْتَحْيُوا۟ نِسَآءَهُمْ وَمَا كَيْدُ ٱلْكَٰفِرِينَ إِلَّا فِى ضَلَٰلٍ

leads.title: Who are the Quran's Sabians?
leads.summary: The Quran names the Sabians (al-Ṣābiʾūn) beside Jews and Christians. Candidates include the Mandaeans, the pagans of Harran, and Elchasaite baptists.

passages.text: (2:62) إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَٱلَّذِينَ هَادُوا۟ وَٱلنَّصَٰرَىٰ وَٱلصَّٰبِـِٔينَ مَنْ ءَامَنَ بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلْيَوْمِ ٱلْءَاخِرِ وَعَمِلَ صَٰلِحًا فَلَهُمْ أَجْرُهُمْ عِندَ رَبِّهِمْ وَلَا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ (5:69) إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَٱلَّذِينَ هَادُوا۟ وَٱلصَّٰبِـُٔونَ وَٱلنَّصَٰرَىٰ مَنْ ءَامَنَ بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلْيَوْمِ ٱلْءَاخِرِ وَعَمِلَ صَٰلِحًا فَلَا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ (22:17) إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَٱلَّذِينَ هَادُوا۟ وَٱلصَّٰبِـِٔينَ وَٱلنَّصَٰرَىٰ وَٱلْمَجُوسَ وَٱلَّذِينَ أَشْرَكُوٓا۟ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَفْصِلُ بَيْنَهُمْ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَىْءٍ شَهِيدٌ
